- Models: BERT-base-uncased and RoBERTa-base, fine-tuned per task. Single RTX A6000 24GB suffices.
- Activation linearization: f_act(x) ≈ θ ⊙ x with θ_t = f_act(x^t)/x^t. Approximate but the sum-of-decomposed-vectors recovers the original activation exactly.
- LayerNorm decomposition: lifted from Kobayashi 2021 — re-expressed as a linear function g_{x⁺}(z_{i⇐k}) per token plus a single bias vector γ. Includes the LN bias β (which Kobayashi/Modarressi previously dropped).
- AbsDot weights: ω_k = |b · z^ℓ_{i⇐k,NoBias}| / Σ_k|b · z^ℓ_{i⇐k,NoBias}|. Splits each bias across inputs by alignment with the token's no-bias contribution.
- Faithfulness eval: 0%, 10%, 20%, …, 90% perturbation rates; replace tokens with [MASK] (not delete) to keep input on-distribution.
- Integrated Gradients baseline: step size 0.1, L2-norm of gradient as scalar attribution.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Smallest possible cross-check on cached prefill activations**: use a *gradient × input* approximation of token attribution on the L19 prefill activation projected onto DoM. We have cached `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` activations + the fitted DoM probe. Compute ∂(prefill_activation · DoM)/∂(input_embedding) ⊙ input_embedding for each problem, summed per input token. Then compute attribution-entropy per problem and compare D-bucket vs A-bucket distributions. This is *not* DecompX (less faithful) but is the cheapest probe of the F-2 / F-7 refutation hypotheses, ~30 min on cached NPZs. If the entropy distributions overlap substantially, the refutations don't fire and we don't need full DecompX.
- The DecompX headline (AOPC on SST-2 = 0.627 vs ALTI 0.416) is an encoder-classification claim and not directly replicable in our pipeline.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2402.13212** — already TRIGGERED in our P11-FE4 (mid-generation features for D-bucket). Connection: D-bucket characterisation via per-token attributions is a natural hybrid of FE4 and the DecompX import.
- **Kobayashi et al. 2021 ("Incorporating Residual and Normalization Layers into Analysis of Masked Language Models")** — NOT in graph. Recommend admission. Foundational for the LN-decomposition lemma DecompX uses; it is the actual lift point if we port to Qwen.
- **Modarressi et al. 2022 (GlobEnc)** — NOT in graph. Recommend admission. Direct predecessor to DecompX; if we settle for "good enough" attribution and skip FFN, we're effectively running GlobEnc.
- **Ferrando et al. 2022 (ALTI)** — NOT in graph. Recommend admission. The "norm-then-rollout" baseline DecompX outperforms; competitive method we'd need to cite.
- **Geva et al. 2021/2022 (FFN as key-value memory)** — NOT in graph. Recommend admission if we ever pursue FFN-level attribution for H-13. Strongly relevant if FFN dominates the prefill DoM signal (refutation #3 above).
- **Mohebbi et al. 2023 (Value Zeroing)** — NOT in graph; cited by DecompX as a nominally-faithful alternative to rollout. Worth admitting if we develop our own decoder-side attribution method — Value Zeroing is the cheapest baseline (no propagation, just per-layer ablation).

## 2306.03819 — LEACE: Perfect Linear Concept Erasure (Belrose, Schneider-Joseph, Ravfogel, Cotterell, Raff, Biderman, 2023)

**Relevance:** LEACE is the closed-form, minimum-damage linear-concept-erasure operator. Our F-2 / F-3 / F-9 findings all rest on linear-probe geometry of L19 prefill activations; LEACE provides the strictest available **null** for those findings (what does the probe see when the linear-readable correctness subspace is surgically deleted with minimum collateral damage?). The paper's "concept scrubbing" multi-layer procedure is also the natural causal-test counterpart to our existing correlational DoM probe — it converts a "DoM finds X" claim into an interventional "the model relies on X at every layer" test. Pythia + LLaMA results (160M → 30B) transfer architecturally to Qwen-2.5-1.5B / 7B; the application point (input of each transformer block, post-LN) is identical to Pathway 11's existing extraction hooks.

**Key claim we tested:** Concepts that are linearly-readable in residual-stream features can be perfectly and surgically erased in closed form, and the erasure inflicts much less collateral LM damage than INLP / SAL / RLACE.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** We have not yet applied LEACE to our cached L19 prefill features. The single highest-leverage 20-minute experiment is fitting LEACE on `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` features with K=1 correctness as Z and recomputing post-scrub DoM AUROC against the 0.7731 baseline (FE73). The full concept-scrubbing causal test (FE76) is blocked on H100 pod time.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE101, P11-FE102, P11-FE103, P11-FE104, H-92, H-93; complements P11-FE3 (activation-patching causal test of F-2).

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **LEACE closed-form projection** — P\* = I − W⁺ P\_{WΣ\_XZ} W, where W = (Σ\_XX^{1/2})⁺. Computed from feature covariance Σ\_XX and feature-concept cross-covariance Σ\_XZ. Pip-installable via `concept-erasure`.
  *Replication cost*: <10 min CPU on cached prefill\_L19 NPZ for one (model, layer, label) triple.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — it's the missing strict-null for F-2, F-3, F-9. Highest-leverage import in this brief.
- **Concept scrubbing (Algorithm 1)** — fit LEACE at layer ℓ, apply, propagate to ℓ+1, refit, repeat for all transformer blocks (post-layernorm at each block input). Sequential because intervention at ℓ shifts the distribution at ℓ+k.
  *Replication cost*: ~1h H100 per (model, label) for full residual-stream pass on Qwen 1.5B (28 layers); needs forward hooks.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** but only after the single-layer LEACE result; this is the multi-layer test of "is correctness representation distributed across the residual stream or localized at L19?"
- **Bits-per-byte perplexity evaluation post-erasure** — measure LM degradation after erasing the concept, distinguishes surgical from collateral damage. (Pythia 160M no-intervention 0.90 → LEACE POS-scrubbed 2.79; random projection 0.99.)
  *Replication cost*: ~30min H100 for a single Qwen 1.5B post-scrub LM eval on a held-out chunk of MATH-500 prompts.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — directly measures whether scrubbing correctness-from-L19 wrecks downstream MATH performance, which would be a positive *causal* result.
- **Comparison to mean ablation / SAL / INLP / RLACE** — paper ranks LEACE > RLACE ≈ LEACE in fidelity but ~100× faster; INLP drops 360 dims, LEACE drops 17. Useful as a methodological yardstick if we ever publish steering comparisons.
  *Replication cost*: medium; INLP/RLACE are open-sourced.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **no** — outside scope; we'd just cite the paper's findings.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Linear guardedness" as a formal property** — concept Z is linearly guarded in features X iff every linear classifier on X performs at chance on Z. This is a stricter, testable analog of the informal "the model doesn't represent X" claim that pops up in our F-2 / F-3 framings.
- **Minimum-damage erasure as a Pareto frontier** — LEACE is not just "an erasure method" but the *closed-form optimum* on the (linear erasure × min L2 perturbation) frontier across all inner-product-induced norms. Reusable framing for any future steering / refusal-probe work where damage-vs-effect tradeoffs matter (intersects H-1, H-12, H-13).
- **Concept scrubbing as a counterfactual on the residual stream** — running scrubbing layer-by-layer is operationally a counterfactual model "what does this network do when concept Z is linearly absent everywhere?" This is the missing intervention for any of our findings that currently rest on correlational probes (F-2, F-7, F-9).

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **The Pile validation split** — used for POS-erasure perplexity. Open / HF. Applicable? **partially** — only if we want LM-perplexity sanity checks under scrubbing, not for MATH-500 reasoning evaluation.
- **RedPajama validation split** — same role as Pile for LLaMA. Open / HF. Applicable? **no** — orthogonal to our pipeline.
- **De-Arteaga Bias-in-Bios (binary gender × profession)** — used for BERT bias-removal demo. Open. Applicable? **no** — off-topic for MATH/correctness.
- **Universal Dependencies (English, SpaCy auto-annotated)** — for POS labels. Open. Applicable? **no** — off-topic.

(No new dataset to admit; methodology is the entire reusable contribution for us.)

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Reference implementation: `pip install concept-erasure` (https://github.com/EleutherAI/concept-erasure).
- LEACE fits in O(d²) memory and a single matrix square root + pseudoinverse — trivial on cached NPZs.
- Concept-scrubbing application point in transformers: **input of each transformer block, immediately after layernorm** (Section 6.1). Same hook point as Pathway 11's L-by-L extraction; the existing forward-hook scaffolding is directly reusable.
- Pythia + LLaMA tested across full size range (160M → 30B); residual-stream post-LN application transfers cleanly to Qwen-2.5-1.5B / 7B.
- Reported numerical sensitivity: low — closed-form, no training instability. Random-projection control to distinguish "concept removed" from "any projection breaks LM".
- Hyperparameter knob: rank of the cross-covariance Σ\_XZ. For binary correctness label, rank ≤ 1 — single-direction erasure, equivalent to debiasing along the DoM direction *with* whitening (this is the key delta vs. naive subtract-the-mean-direction).

### Replicable intermediates

- **`pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`** caches Qwen-1.5B prefill features at multiple layers including L19 with K=1 correctness labels. We can fit LEACE on the train fold of these features in <10 min CPU and compute the post-LEACE DoM AUROC. If 0.7731 → 0.5 ± noise, the linear-erasure null is the *strict* lower bound for F-2 — this is the single highest-leverage 20-minute experiment in this brief.
- **`scratch/pathway10_temporal_and_verifier_results.json`** has prefill DoM and final-token DoM directions; we can compute the rank-1 LEACE-projected final-token DoM AUROC after prefill-DoM scrubbing as the F-3 subspace-orthogonality test.
- **CoE-60 cached features (Pathway 9)** — fit LEACE on L19, transform L19 features, recompute CoE-60 trajectory features and refit the CoE-60 probe. Tests F-9 directly.
- **No fresh data or new model run required** for the three highest-leverage replications above.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2306.03341 (Inference-Time Intervention, Li et al., NeurIPS 2023)** — already in graph (status: graphed). LEACE is the **closed-form, minimum-damage** counterpart to ITI's mass-mean direction; both target the same residual-stream object. Worth a comparative note in PAPER\_INDEX entries for both.
- **2410.13640 (Chain-of-Embedding, Wang ICLR 2025)** — already in graph (status: graphed; PARTIALLY CONFIRMED). The F-9 LEACE-scrub experiment directly arbitrates the CoE-60 vs single-L19-DoM redundancy claim.
- **2509.11569 (D²HScore)** — already in graph; provides another label-free probe candidate against which a LEACE-scrubbed null can be measured.
- **2004.07667 (Ravfogel et al., INLP)** — **NOT in graph**; recommend admission. Cited as LEACE's main iterated-projection baseline; we'd want it on the bench when comparing erasure methods.
- **2201.12091 (Ravfogel et al., R-LACE)** — **NOT in graph**; recommend admission. The gradient-based adversarial erasure method that LEACE matches in fidelity at ~100× speedup; still relevant if we ever need stronger erasure on a non-binary concept (e.g., difficulty bucket).

## 2308.08742 — PMET: Precise Model Editing in a Transformer (Li et al., AAAI 2024)

**Relevance:** Sharpens the MHSA-as-extractor / FFN-as-store dichotomy from Geva et al. 2021/2023 into a concrete editing recipe and presents the cleanest existing per-layer empirical analysis of where in a transformer FFN hidden states stabilize (L15/28 in GPT-J). The protocol — per-layer cosine + top-50 Jaccard (vocab-projected) similarity of last-token hidden states before vs after each Transformer Component — is directly portable to our MATH-500 prefill activations and gives us a tool for distinguishing "knowledge axis" from "extraction-pattern axis" at L19. Connects to F-2 (prefill DoM AUROC), F-3 (prefill/final orthogonality), F-9 (CoE redundancy), H-1 (DoM steering), H-13 (head-level attribution).

**Key claim we tested:** FFN hidden states stabilize past a critical layer while MHSA hidden states keep churning; therefore correctness/knowledge probes at "post-stabilization" layers should localize to the FFN-output component, not the MHSA-output component or the residual stream as a whole. Applied to F-2: our prefill L19 DoM should split into a strong FFN-only AUROC and a weak MHSA-only AUROC.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** Pending FE8742 (per-layer FFN-stabilization scan on Qwen) + FE8743 (component-decomposed L19 DoM AUROC). The methodology transfers cleanly; the empirical question of whether the GPT-J pattern holds in Qwen-2.5-1.5B is open. PMET also offers a concrete prediction we have not yet examined for F-3 (orthogonality should disappear in the FFN-only component, since FFN converges to a "specific direction").

**Related experiments:** P11-FE105 (per-layer FFN-stabilization), P11-FE106 (component-decomposed L19 AUROC), P11-FE107 (MHSA-out vs FFN-out DoM steering), P11-FE108 (component-decomposed CoE), H-94, H-95, H-96.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Per-layer hidden-state cosine + Jaccard top-k vocab projection (PMET Section "Investigating MHSA and FFN")** — for each layer l, take last-token hidden states h^{l-1} and a^l (after MHSA) and m^l (after FFN), compute (a) cos(h^{l-1}, a^l) and cos(h^{l-1}, m^l), (b) project all three into vocab space via the unembedding matrix, take top-50 tokens, compute Jaccard similarity J_50(T(h), T(a)). Average across N factual queries; plot per-layer.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute` NPZs if MHSA-out and FFN-out streams are saved; ~3h H100 to re-extract per-component streams if not.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — directly answers "where in Qwen-2.5-1.5B does FFN stabilize?", which gates Refutations 1–3 and is a perimeter test for using L19 as the canonical DoM layer.

- **TC (Transformer Component) hidden-state perturbation** — add learnable parameters δ_a, δ_m to a^L and m^L respectively, optimize via KL + cross-entropy loss to memorize target knowledge.
  *Replication cost*: 4h H100 to port from PMET's GitHub (https://github.com/xpq-tech/PMET) onto Qwen-2.5-1.5B.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **maybe** — full PMET editing is overkill for our use case, but the δ_a / δ_m optimization framework is the cleanest existing implementation of "intervention on MHSA-out vs FFN-out" and could be borrowed for H-1.

- **Square-root residual spread** — when distributing a target intervention across critical layers, scale R^l = (V_1 - W_0 K_1) / sqrt(L - l + 1) instead of even spread. Improves reliability at cost of specificity.
  *Replication cost*: trivial code change (1 line).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes if we ever do multi-layer steering** — direct improvement over uniform per-layer DoM injection in P10 v2 steering experiments.

- **MHSA vs FFN ablation by output-weight masking** — to test whether MHSA stores knowledge, additionally update W^l_O_MHSA via the same loss; observe specificity drop. Diagnostic for "is component X causally involved in this task?"
  *Replication cost*: 2h H100 if porting PMET infra; trivially cheap as a forward-pass-only zero-ablation diagnostic (~30min CPU).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — diagnostic for D-bucket: zero-ablate MHSA-out at L19 on D-bucket vs A-bucket, see whose accuracy collapses harder.

- **Last-token-as-knowledge-summary protocol** — use the residual stream at the last token of a factual query as the canonical representation of the query's knowledge. Foundational assumption for all of PMET's analysis.
  *Replication cost*: zero — already our canonical protocol for prefill DoM extraction.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: already running this.

### Approaches & framings

- **Information-flow decomposition of the residual stream into MHSA + FFN + residual contributions.** PMET's central conceptual move: stop treating h^l as a unified hidden state, decompose into a^l + m^l + h^{l-1}. This intersects every F-N/H-N that currently treats L19 prefill as a single direction (F-2, F-3, F-7, F-9, H-1). Adopting this decomposition would give us a sharper attribution toolkit and a cleaner reformulation of "what is the prefill DoM."

- **MHSA-as-extractor / FFN-as-store dichotomy.** This is the dominant model-editing-literature framing (Geva et al. 2021/2022/2023; ROME; MEMIT). It's not novel to PMET, but PMET sharpens it into "MHSA weights need *not* update on new knowledge — only the directions of its hidden states matter." For us, this predicts: prefill DoM-as-correctness should localize to FFN-out at L19 if the picture is right; deviation indicates either (a) correctness is not factual-recall, or (b) the dichotomy doesn't hold for Qwen-2.5-1.5B.

- **Knowledge-clue / knowledge-point subject-centric model editing.** Less directly relevant — they're framing model editing around subject-relation-object triples and noting that current methods break ripple effects (Cohen et al. 2023, RIPPLEEDITS). This framing is orthogonal to MATH-500 reasoning. Cited only.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **COUNTERFACT** — 21,919 factual triples designed for counterfactual editing (Meng et al. 2022a). Public, BSD license. **Applicable? no** — it's factual recall, not multi-step reasoning; doesn't intersect MATH-500 or our 1024-tok prefill regime.

- **zsRE (Zero-Shot Relation Extraction)** — Levy et al. 2017, ~10K relation triples. Public. **Applicable? no** — same reason.

- **1209 factual statements** subset (Meng et al. 2022a) — used by PMET for the per-layer cosine/Jaccard analysis. **Applicable? maybe** — could be reused as a factual-knowledge-baseline alongside MATH-500 to test whether the prefill DoM lights up on factual recall vs reasoning. ~1h to re-extract Qwen-2.5-1.5B activations on these 1209 statements.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **Code repo**: https://github.com/xpq-tech/PMET — has the δ_a / δ_m optimization implemented for GPT-J and GPT-NeoX. Likely adaptable to Qwen.
- **Critical layer set R**: PMET uses MEMIT's set R = {3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8} for GPT-J (early layers!) — i.e., they edit *early* FFNs even though their analysis says MHSA-stabilization happens around layer 15. The argument is that early FFNs serve as "key-value memories" and editing them is more efficient (Meng et al. 2022b). For our work, if we adopt PMET's framework, the natural Qwen analog is editing early FFNs (L3–L8 say), not L19. This is a non-obvious gotcha.
- **Loss balance hyperparameters**: μ (KL weight) and φ (1/P, prefix averaging weight) — set via grid search per dataset.
- **MHSA + FFN are parallel, not sequential, in GPT-J / GPT-NeoX**: the formula is h^l = h^{l-1} + a^l + m^l with a^l and m^l computed *in parallel* from γ(h^{l-1}). Qwen-2.5-1.5B uses *sequential* MHSA → residual → FFN → residual (Llama-style). The PMET decomposition still applies, but the per-layer dynamics will differ — when porting their analysis, we need to extract pre-MHSA, post-MHSA-pre-FFN, and post-FFN streams as three distinct snapshots, not two.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Per-layer cosine + top-50 Jaccard analysis of last-token hidden states across MHSA and FFN components on Qwen-2.5-1.5B.** Use the cached `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute` MATH-500 prefill activations *if* MHSA-out and FFN-out streams were saved. Verify by inspecting the NPZ schema in `DATA_MANIFEST.md`. If only the post-residual stream was saved, this is *not* a free sanity check — needs ~3h H100 to re-extract with hooks at MHSA-out and FFN-out.
- **L19 component-decomposed DoM AUROC**. Same prerequisite: needs MHSA-out and FFN-out at L19 cached. If saved, a 30-min CPU job suffices. If not, ~3h H100 to re-extract.
- **Reasonable cheap proxy without re-extraction**: read off `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json` for any per-layer DoM AUROCs already computed (across L0–L27). If the curve has a discontinuity around the FFN-stabilization layer (PMET predicts a transition somewhere in L13–L17 for Qwen), that supports PMET's framing without component-level decomposition.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2210.07229** (MEMIT, Meng et al. 2022b) — NOT in graph; recommend admission. PMET's direct predecessor; defines the optimization-based mass-editing framework PMET extends. Without MEMIT in the graph, PMET's contribution is hard to interpret.
- **2202.05262** (ROME, Meng et al. 2022a, "Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT") — not checked here; recommend `query.py paper 2202.05262` to verify. If absent, foundational mechanistic-interpretability paper that should be admitted; it's the source of "FFN as key-value memories" applied to factual editing.
- **2304.14767** (Geva et al. 2023, "Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in AutoRegressive Language Models") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Source of the "MHSA extracts subject attributes" finding PMET cites; directly relevant to H-13 (head-level attribution).
- **2304.00740** (Hernandez, Li, Andreas 2023, "Inspecting and Editing Knowledge Representations") — NOT in graph; recommend admission for H-12 (label-free probes) and H-13 (knowledge-rep editing).
- **2211.00593** (Wang et al., IOI circuit) — already in graph (status: graphed). PMET cites it for MHSA-redundancy results. Already linked to H-13.
- **2211.03495** (Hassid et al., "How much does attention actually attend?") — not checked here; recommend admission. Key precedent for MHSA-redundancy claims; would corroborate or refute PMET's "general extraction patterns" framing.
- **2306.03341** (Inference-Time Intervention, Li et al.) — already in graph (status: CONTRADICTED). PMET's δ_a perturbation is conceptually identical to ITI's per-head additive intervention but applied at residual level. The ITI failure mode (we contradicted them on assuming static directions) directly predicts a failure mode for PMET-style δ_a steering applied to dynamic correctness signals.

## 2308.10248 — Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering (Turner, Thiergart, Leech, Udell, Vazquez, Mini, MacDiarmid, 2023)

**Relevance:** ActAdd is the foundational contrastive activation-addition method and the direct unsupervised cousin of our F-2 supervised DoM. Single layer, single position (a=1), single contrast pair, scalar coefficient c<15 — and SOTA on sentiment + detoxification. Critically constrains how we frame F-2 (predictive direction) and F-3 (prefill/final orthogonality), and is the unavoidable baseline H-1 must beat. Their mid-layer-optimal finding across three model families is also a precise probe of whether our L19 layer choice is correctness-prediction-optimal vs steering-optimal.

**Key claim we tested:** A single contrast-pair direction at one mid-layer, injected at one position, durably steers downstream generation across many tokens.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — pending FE71 (single-vector ActAdd at L19 on MATH-500), FE72 (cosine/AUROC head-to-head with F-2 supervised DoM), and FE73 (layer sweep). Refutation 1 above is the central question: can a fixed-position direction transfer through F-3's orthogonality? Refutation 2 asks whether F-7's "collective signature" survives an ActAdd-style 1-pair recovery test.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE109, P11-FE110, P11-FE111, P10-FE9, H-1, H-97, H-98, H-99

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **ActAdd / contrastive activation addition** — `h^l ← h^l + c·(h₊^l − h₋^l)` at fixed layer `l`, fixed position `a=1`, scalar `c<15`. *Replication cost*: 30 min on cached Qwen-1.5B prefill extractor + a generation pass. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — it's the canonical baseline for any steering experiment in this repo and we don't have it implemented.
- **Sequence-alignment padding for contrast pairs** — pad `p₊` and `p₋` to equal length so position-aligned subtraction is well-defined. *Replication cost*: trivial. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — adopting this convention before P10/P11 steering experiments avoids an avoidable confound.
- **Coefficient sweep `c ∈ [3,20]`** — small grid search per task. *Replication cost*: linear in #generations. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes, embedded in P11-FE109.
- **Layer sweep at coarse stride** — Turner et al. tested `l ∈ [6,24]` on a 48-layer model, found mid optimal. *Replication cost*: cheap on cached states, expensive on generation. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — relevant to F-2's layer choice.
- **Off-target capability evaluation via ConceptNet (LAMA, n=29,774)** — measure P@K for unrelated factual completion to detect collateral damage. *Replication cost*: 1 hr H100 per intervention. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — H-1 needs an off-target check before any accuracy claim is taken seriously.
- **Perplexity ratio on OpenWebText, partitioned by topical relevance** — separate "wedding-related" and "wedding-unrelated" subsets to show selective effect. *Replication cost*: 1 hr CPU per intervention. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — adapt to "math-related" / "math-unrelated" splits as steering side-effect probe.
- **KL-divergence drift between steered and baseline distributions** — token-level distribution comparison. *Replication cost*: trivial alongside generation. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — cheap supplementary metric for any H-1 result.

### Approaches & framings

- **Linear representation hypothesis as a *causal* claim, not just predictive** — Turner et al. argue that activation steering only works if features are encoded as linear directions *and* the residual stream supports compositional add-ons. Our F-2/F-3 work treats DoM as a probe (predictive); ActAdd reframes the same direction as a causal lever. This is the bridge to H-1's steering claim.
- **"Forward passes compose despite no training for it"** — the paper's mechanistic explanation. Implication for us: if our F-3 orthogonality is real, then either (a) ActAdd-style composition would *fail* on Qwen-1.5B math (interesting!) or (b) composition succeeds but not through the DoM directions we measured (also interesting).
- **Gradient-free, single-pair, training-free** — establishes a price-floor for any "calibration via probing" claim: if a 1-pair ActAdd matches a supervised probe, the supervision was wasted compute.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **IMDb sentiment** — n=1000 prompts, public, HF. Applicable? no — we're math-correctness focused, not sentiment.
- **RealToxicityPrompts** — n=1000, HF. Applicable? no — orthogonal task.
- **ConceptNet (LAMA)** — n=29,774 sentences, public, HF. Applicable? yes — natural off-target probe for any MATH-500 steering experiment (does the intervention break general factual recall?).
- **OpenWebText** — public, HF. Applicable? yes — perplexity-ratio side-effect probe for H-1.
- **Wedding-topic generation prompts** — small custom set, in paper's appendix. Applicable? no — toy task.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Pad contrast prompts to equal length before subtraction; misaligned positions destroy the signal.
- Inject at *one* position (default a=1, the BOS-adjacent slot) — not every position.
- Coefficient typically `c < 15`; degeneration ("steering off the manifold") above that.
- Mid-layer is consistently optimal across GPT-2-XL, OPT, LLaMA-3 — not last layer.
- Algorithm 1 in the paper is the canonical pseudocode; one-page implementation.
- Reference implementation: https://github.com/montemac/activation_additions (verify before relying).

### Replicable intermediates

- **Cosine of ActAdd-vector with our supervised L19 prefill DoM** — pure numpy on `pathway11_h100/` cached states + a tiny extractor pass for the contrast pair, ~10 min CPU. If cos > 0.5, F-2's "supervised DoM" is essentially recovering an ActAdd-style direction; if cos ≈ 0, the two directions are doing different things and both are interesting.
- **AUROC of ActAdd-vector projection on cached MATH-500 prefill states** — same script, ~10 min CPU. Direct head-to-head with F-2's 0.7731.
- **Layer sweep of ActAdd-vector AUROC across L0–L27** — uses cached Stage 2 per-layer NPZs if extant; 1 hr CPU. Tests refutation 4 and probes whether L19 is correctness-optimal or steering-optimal.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2306.03341** (Inference-Time Intervention, Li et al.) — already in graph (status: graphed, CONTRADICTED in PAPER_INDEX). Direct sibling: ITI uses mass-mean instead of contrast-pair, applies per-head instead of per-layer. Refutation 1 above is the same flavor as our existing ITI critique.
- **2406.11717** (Arditi et al., refusal direction) — already in graph (status: graphed). Single-direction-mediates-behavior precedent; provides the strongest a-priori case for refutation 1's "ActAdd should work on MATH-500 correctness" hypothesis.
- **2310.01405** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Zou et al. "Representation Engineering" — direct follow-up to ActAdd, generalizes contrastive-pair to LAT (Linear Artificial Tomography), tests on honesty/morality/utility — would let us check whether ActAdd's mid-layer-optimum / fixed-position findings persist under their broader formalism.
- **2502.05206** (search guess; if not the right ID skip) — NOT in graph; only flag if it's the "ITI v2 / Activation Patching for math" paper. Skip if uncertain.

## 2310.03716 — A Long Way to Go: Investigating Length Correlations in RLHF (Singhal, Goyal, Xu, Durrett, 2024)

**Relevance:** RLHF/preference-modeling paper, not a hidden-state or
reasoning paper. Useful to topo-confidence as a methodology import: the
NRG (Non-length Reward Gain) decomposition recipe and the LPPO adversarial
baseline directly apply to any probe-style AUROC headline (F-2, F-8, F-9).
The paper's central lesson — "complex evaluations can collapse to simple
length-correlated baselines, and the field rarely audits for this" — is
the same lesson encoded by H-15 (length-band PR control for F-4) and now
extended to F-2 and F-8 via P11-FE112 / FE84 / FE85.

**Key claim we tested:** A length-only baseline reproduces most of an
RLHF win-rate gain (LPPO 56% vs PPO 58% on WebGPT, 64% vs 63% on RLCD).
NRG (within-length-bucket reward gain / overall ∆R) is 2% on WebGPT,
27% on RLCD. Translated to our setting: the analogous claim would be
"length-only AUROC reproduces most of the prefill-DoM AUROC headline".

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — P11-FE112 / FE84 / FE85 are queued. Until
they run, the paper's threat to F-2 / F-8 / F-9 is hypothetical. The
admission-time framing ("feature-level analogue of F-9 — corroborated_by")
should be downgraded once the experiments run, because the paper's recipe
is a *threat* to F-2/F-8/F-9 rather than evidence for them.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE112, P11-FE113, P11-FE114, H-15, H-100.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **NRG (Non-length Reward Gain) decomposition** — split a metric into
  within-bucket gain (length-bucketed, weighted by bin size) and
  across-bucket gain. Direct port: split prefill-DoM AUROC into
  within-length-bucket discrimination + across-length-bucket
  discrimination contributions.
  *Replication cost:* 30 min CPU on cached `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes — it's a direct NRG-for-AUROC adaptation.
- **Length-only adversarial reward (LPPO)** — define a metric using only
  the suspected confound, see how much of the headline it reproduces.
  Port: train a univariate logistic regression on `prompt_token_count`
  for K=1 correctness, report AUROC against the 0.7731 baseline.
  *Replication cost:* 20 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes — adversarial baseline for F-2.
- **Length heuristic agreement** — accuracy of always-pick-the-longer-output.
  Port to our regime: accuracy of "always-correct-on-the-shorter-prompt"
  as a baseline.
  *Replication cost:* 5 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes, as part of FE83 below.
- **Length-balancing of preference data (BAL)** — subsample so paired
  length-differences are symmetric in 10-token bins. Port: length-balance
  MATH-500 problems (subsample to flatten the length distribution),
  recompute F-2 / F-8.
  *Replication cost:* 30 min CPU + reduces effective N (probably 250–350
  problems out of 500).
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes.
- **Confidence-based truncation (C-TR)** — use data cartography to
  identify low-confidence training examples, train only on those.
  Port: identify low-DoM-confidence MATH-500 problems, see whether
  AUROC is recoverable on the low-confidence subset alone.
  *Replication cost:* 30 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* probably no — low-priority diagnostic.
- **Reward Data Augmentation (R-DA)** — random pairing of prompts
  to break feature reliance. Doesn't have a clean port to our setting
  (we're not training a reward model).
  *Replication cost:* n/a.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* no — no analogous training stage.
- **Training-dynamics confidence cartography (Swayamdipta et al.)** —
  track per-example confidence across epochs to find easy/hard
  examples. We don't train probes for many epochs, but the
  cross-fold (5-fold OOF) confidence variance is a cheap analogue.
  *Replication cost:* 20 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* maybe — only if FE83/FE84 above show
  length confounds, then this is the next diagnostic.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Shallow-feature dominance over complex-feature evaluation"** —
  the paper's central frame. Maps directly onto F-2 / F-8 / F-9 as a
  refutation pattern. Implication for the project: every probe-style
  AUROC headline should be paired with a shallow-feature LR baseline
  before it goes into FINDINGS.md.
- **"NRG ratio as the discriminating metric"** — instead of asking "is
  the metric good?", ask "what fraction of the metric is attributable
  to the simple feature alone?" This frames the validate_claims.py
  91-claim invariant differently: the invariant guards numerical
  reproducibility, not feature-attribution validity. NRG-style
  audits would be a separate axis of validation.
- **"Reward models as the locus of bias"** — the paper localizes the
  length bias to reward modeling, not PPO optimization. Translated to
  our setting: bias would localize to the labeling pipeline (K=1
  correctness, PROOF-format dependent), not to the geometric extraction.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **WebGPT** — 19.6K examples, mean 169 tokens. Open-domain QA, human
  labels. License: research-only via OpenAI WebGPT release. Applicable?
  no — long-form QA, not math reasoning.
- **Stack** — 100K StackExchange Q&A pairs with upvote-derived
  preferences, mean 236 tokens. HF available. Applicable? no.
- **RLCD** — 40K helpfulness multi-turn dialog with synthetic
  preferences, mean 45 tokens. HF available. Applicable? no.
- **AlpacaFarm simulated preferences** — 12 OpenAI-API "annotators"
  voting on outputs. Closed-API, costs API credits. Applicable? no
  for our setting (we have ground-truth correctness labels, not
  preferences).

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Llama-7B base, LoRA rank 16, TRL implementation, λ=0.04 baseline KL
  coefficient.
- LPPO target lengths: 156 (WebGPT), 120 (RLCD), 250 (Stack) — set as
  hyperparameter to "allow desired increases without becoming too long".
- Length penalty `R' = R + (1 − len(y)/N) σ` where σ is moving-average
  batch reward standard deviation.
- 20-token bucket size for length stratification (Figure 3, Table 1)
  — small enough that buckets contain meaningful data, large enough to
  smooth noise. For MATH-500 prompts (typically 50–500 tokens), 50-token
  buckets seem more appropriate.
- Reward model "confidence" computed per training example as `R(x, y+) −
  R(x, y−)` averaged over epochs 2..E (epoch 1 excluded for noise).
- Convergence note: stricter length penalties cause training divergence
  — calibration is delicate.

- **Length-balanced subset re-eval of F-8.** Subsample MATH-500 to
  flatten the prompt-length distribution; recompute selective-prediction

- **Shallow-feature LR baseline.** Train LR on (prompt token count, #

## 2310.04861 — Uncovering hidden geometry in Transformers via disentangling position and context (Song & Zhong, 2024)

**Relevance:** This paper is foundational for our entire residual-stream-geometry program because it provides a clean ANOVA-style decomposition `h_{c,t} = μ + pos_t + ctx_c + resid_{c,t}` that empirically separates *positional structure* from *content structure* in the hidden states of GPT-2, BERT, BLOOM, and Llama-2. Three of our top findings (F-1 universal breathing, F-3 prefill/final DoM orthogonality at cos 0.046, F-10 PH = Gaussian null) are vulnerable to the same methodological gap: we never subtracted the smooth, low-rank positional basis before measuring "content geometry." The paper's empirical incoherence range (0.039–0.190) brackets our F-3 number exactly, raising the prior that F-3 is a baseline pos↔ctx incoherence artifact rather than evidence of two distinct computations.

**Key claim we tested:** Hidden states factorize into incoherent positional and contextual subspaces, with the positional basis carrying ~10–12 effective dimensions, smooth/spiral structure, and 0.66–0.84 relative norm — and these structural facts are robust across architectures, datasets, and even random-token OOD inputs. *In our terms:* much of what we have been measuring as "computational geometry" may be the smooth positional spiral plus token-level content, with no extra "topology" signal in the residual.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** No replication yet. We have proposed P11-FE115–FE83 and H-101, H-102 as the cross-checks. The most direct refutation test (P11-FE115, ~2h CPU) is whether `cos(prefill_DoM_resid, final_DoM_resid)` after pos-subtraction stays at 0.046 or jumps to >0.30. If the latter, F-3's "two circuits" framing collapses and our narrative on prefill-vs-final DoM needs full revision.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE115, P11-FE116, P11-FE117, P11-FE118, H-101, H-102 (all proposed in this brief); EXP-026 (F-10 baseline), EXP-037 (F-2 baseline), EXP-031/032/040 (F-1 breathing baseline).

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Mean-based 4-component decomposition (`h_{c,t} = μ + pos_t + ctx_c + resid_{c,t}`)** — Compute global mean over (c,t), per-position mean, per-context mean, residual is whatever's left. Implementation in 6.4K-sample Colab notebook; runs in minutes on GPU.
  *Replication cost*: 1–2 hours CPU on cached P11 NPZs (one full pass over residual streams).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **YES** — this is the headline tool the paper offers and directly enables Refutations #1–#3.

- **Positional-basis rank estimate via Donoho ScreeNOT (Donoho, Gavish, Romanov 2023)** — singular-value thresholding under correlated noise; gives integer rank for `P = [pos_1, …, pos_T]`.
  *Replication cost*: <30 min CPU. ScreeNOT has a reference implementation.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **YES** if we want to defend or refute F-1 quantitatively.

- **2D discrete cosine transform (DCT) on positional Gram matrix** — `Ĝ = F̃ G F̃^T`, low-frequency energy concentration as a smoothness measure. Used to compute their "ratio explained by low-freq K=10" 99.5% number.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (<5 min).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **YES** as a quick smoothness check on Qwen positional basis.

- **QK matrix decomposition into 4 constituents (`pos-pos`, `pos-cvec`, `cvec-pos`, `cvec-cvec`)** — given the mean-decomposition of embeddings, decompose `h^T W^q (W^k)^T h'` additively. Visualizes which constituent dominates each attention head.
  *Replication cost*: 2–4 hours on cached attention matrices, layer 19 of Qwen 1.5B.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **YES** — directly motivates H-13 and H-21 attribution.

- **Low-rank-plus-diagonal-plus-noise decomposition of `W = W^q (W^k)^T`** — `W ≈ V L V^T + D + noise` where V are top-K right singular vectors of P. Denoising via threshold-zeroing off-diagonal entries rotated by V.
  *Replication cost*: 1–2 hours.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **MAYBE** — interpretive, lower priority than the embedding decomposition.

- **Cosine-similarity-based incoherence measurement** — `max_{t,c} |⟨pos_t/||pos_t||, ctx_c/||ctx_c||⟩|`.
  *Replication cost*: minutes once decomposition is done.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **YES** — direct number for refutation #1.

- **Length-generalization arithmetic stress test (4-layer 4-head NanoGPT trained on `a+b=c` digit strings)** — compares smoothness on language vs arithmetic data.
  *Replication cost*: ~2h GPU to retrain.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **NO** — orthogonal to our agenda; we only care about MATH-500-style natural text.

### Approaches & framings

- **ANOVA framing of hidden states.** Position and context are factors/treatments; embedding is the response variable; mean effects are pos_t and ctx_c. This is a clean alternative ontology to "everything is geometry of correctness." Forces us to ask: which of our findings live in residual (after subtracting both means), vs. are inherited from pos/ctx mean structure?

- **Incoherence-as-factorization-enabling.** Theorem 2 says kernels factorize multiplicatively when bases are incoherent. This is a mechanistic reason to *expect* near-orthogonality between any two functionally-distinct residual-stream subspaces — making F-3's 0.046 a baseline phenomenon, not evidence.

- **Smoothness as a "blessing of natural language."** Language data induces smooth positional basis; arithmetic data does not. This intersects H-2 (breathing on short CoT) and H-3 (breathing on code generation): if breathing is partly positional-spiral driven, code (less smooth than prose, more smooth than arithmetic) may show *intermediate* breathing amplitude. Provides a free contrast condition.

- **Rotated-singular-vector denoising for weight matrices.** Idea that `V^T W V` reveals interpretable low-rank structure aligned with the positional basis is a generic interpretability tool, applicable to any layer's QK matrix.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **OpenWebText** — multi-billion-token web corpus, HF-accessible, MIT-license; used as in-distribution baseline for GPT-2/BERT/BLOOM/Llama-2 in Tables 1–2. Applicable? **YES** — useful as a "natural language" baseline if we want to compute pos_t reference on a corpus matched to typical pretraining.

- **WikiText (likely WikiText-103)** — HF-accessible, Creative Commons. Applicable? **YES** — same reasoning as OpenWebText.

- **GitHub data** — code corpus, accessibility unspecified (likely scraped). Applicable? **MAYBE** — relevant for H-3 (breathing on code) if we want a "less-smooth-than-prose" data point.

- **Tiny Shakespeare (NanoGPT)** — public domain, trivial size. Applicable? **NO** — toy data, not relevant to MATH-500 regime.

- **Random-token sequences** — synthetic. Applicable? **YES (as control)** — already partially used by us in EXP-041; paper's prediction (positional basis preserved on random tokens) is a sharp control we should re-verify.

- **Addition arithmetic strings (`a+b=c`, digit length 5–10)** — synthetic. Applicable? **NO** — arithmetic-only, off-MATH-500-distribution.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **Code repo:** https://github.com/JiajunSong629/uncover-hidden-geometry (full implementation, reproducibility plots, additional measurements).
- **Colab notebook:** https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1ubsJQvLkOSQtiU8LoBA_79t1bd5-5ihi (GPT-2 reproduction, ~minutes on free GPU).
- **Sample size:** C = 6.4K input sequences; T = 128 context length used in Figure 2 visualization.
- **Top-K for V (right singular vectors of P):** K ≈ 20 in QK denoising.
- **Models tested with full decomposition:** GPT-2 (small), BERT, BLOOM, Llama-2 (size unspecified; likely 7B), NanoGPT.
- **Rank estimator:** Donoho et al. 2023 "ScreeNOT: Exact MSE-optimal singular value thresholding in correlated noise" (Annals of Statistics 51:1, 122–148).
- **Anisotropy caveat (§2 "Some exceptions"):** in last few layers embeddings tend to be anisotropic and pos basis may collapse to lower dim; relevant for our L19+ analyses on Qwen since L19/28 ≈ 68% depth.
- **BERT shows higher-frequency positional patterns** (different training, MLM not autoregressive) — useful caveat if we ever extend to encoder-only models.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Quick check (≤2h CPU):** load P11 1024-tok cached residual streams (`pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json` companion NPZs); compute μ, pos_t, ctx_c, resid_{c,t} per layer for L19+. Measure: (a) rank of P via ScreeNOT, (b) `cos(pos_t1, pos_t2)` heatmap vs our DoM cosine matrix, (c) `cos(prefill_DoM, final_DoM)` after subtracting pos_t — direct test of refutation #1.
- **Direct sanity check:** for our F-3 number 0.046, project the prefill-DoM and final-DoM directions onto span(P) (positional subspace) and span(P)^⊥ (non-positional subspace). If both DoMs are mostly in span(P), F-3's "two distinct circuits" is hollow.
- **F-1 quick-cross-check:** participation ratio of `resid_{c,t}` (post pos+ctx subtraction) at every position; compare to raw breathing curve.
- **F-10 retest:** rerun pathway 9 PH pipeline (`pathway9/results/exp3a_gaussian_null_v2.json` regeneration) on `resid_{c,t}` instead of raw L19 hidden states.

### Cross-paper signals

## 2310.06824 — The Geometry of Truth: Emergent Linear Structure in LLM Representations of True/False Datasets (Marks & Tegmark, COLM 2024)

**Relevance:** Foundational reference for the "linear truth direction" framing that motivates F-2 and F-8. The paper introduces mass-mean (difference-in-mean) probing as a stronger alternative to logistic regression for *causal* purposes — at scale, MM probes match LR/CCS for classification (≥95% AUROC on transfer in some conditions for LLaMA-2-13B/70B) but identify directions that are 3–5× more causally implicated under the §6 NIE protocol (e.g. 0.85 vs 0.18 for cities+neg_cities at LLaMA-2-13B). It also documents two phenomena directly relevant to our pipeline: (a) layer-wise rotation of paired truth axes (antipodal → orthogonal → aligned across layers of LLaMA-2-13B) which provides an alternative interpretation of our F-3 cos(·)=0.046 finding, and (b) token-position contamination at non-summarization tokens, which casts doubt on our prefill[-1] extraction choice.

**Key claim we tested:** "Difference-in-mean (mass-mean) is a strong probe for linear truth representations and identifies directions that are causally implicated, not merely predictive." Our F-2 already operationalizes the predictive half on MATH-500 correctness (AUROC 0.7731). The causal half — the part Marks & Tegmark argue is the load-bearing claim — is currently untested in our pipeline.

**Our result:** **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED** Predictive half: F-2 corroborates that raw difference-in-mean is a useful probe at small scale (Qwen-2.5-1.5B, AUROC 0.7731). Causal half: untested; FE75 / H-105 are queued to measure NIE on MATH-500. Methodology gaps identified: (i) we use raw DoM, not Σ⁻¹-corrected mass-mean (FE74 / H-104); (ii) we lack a paired contrast training set, which the paper shows is decisive for NIE (FE77); (iii) F-3's orthogonality may be a layer-15-specific snapshot of a rotation (FE73 / H-103); (iv) prefill[-1] may be the wrong token position vs end-of-statement punctuation (FE76).

**Related experiments:** P11-FE119, P11-FE120, P11-FE121, P11-FE122, P11-FE123, H-103, H-104, H-105; depends on F-2, F-3, F-8; informs F-1.

**Status:** PARTIALLY CONFIRMED

### Methodologies extracted

- **Mass-mean probe (raw `p_mm`)** — direction θ = μ⁺ − μ⁻ where μ are class-conditional means; classification via σ(θᵀx) with bias chosen so probe value matches mean labels.
  *Replication cost*: 10 min CPU on cached L19 prefill activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — this is essentially what F-2 already does, but worth checking our pipeline matches the paper's normalization (Marks & Tegmark center activations and use unbiased probes).

- **IID mass-mean probe (`p_mm^iid` = Σ⁻¹·(μ⁺−μ⁻))** — covariance-corrected difference-in-mean, equivalent to Fisher LDA under homoscedasticity (App. F proof).
  *Replication cost*: 20 min CPU (need Σ from full training fold; small numerical-stability work for high-dim Σ inversion).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly addresses Refutation 2.

- **Activation patching for causal localization** — cache activations on `pT`; replay model on `pF` swapping `h[i,ℓ](pF) → h[i,ℓ](pT)` at one (position, layer) pair; measure log P(TRUE) − log P(FALSE) shift.
  *Replication cost*: ~2h H100 per (model, layer-grid, position-grid) on 20 prompts. Already partially implemented for our few-shot setup.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — would let us localize where in the residual stream MATH-500 correctness is *causally* encoded vs merely *predictable*. Currently F-2 only does the prediction half.

- **PCA visualization of class-conditional clusters** — center activations per dataset; plot top-2 PCs colored by truth label.
  *Replication cost*: 5 min CPU per layer.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — sanity check on whether L19 actually has a linear truth axis (vs DoM AUROC working via cumulative non-linear effects).

- **Causal NIE protocol** — normalize θ so probe assigns θ a "δ-mean shift" worth one class swap; intervene additively at all group-(b) positions; measure log-prob difference shift.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min H100 per probe per dataset.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — our H-1 currently lacks a NIE-style metric, only behavioural accuracy. Adopting NIE makes us comparable to this paper.

- **Contrastive dataset construction** — paired (s, ¬s) statements with `not` insertion; logical conjunctions/disjunctions of true/false elements; structurally controlled negation as a non-truth feature.
  *Replication cost*: 2h to draft a "negated MATH" or "wrong-answer-paired-with-right-answer" dataset.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — key gap; addresses Refutation 3 directly.

- **`likely` distractor dataset** — non-factual generations whose final token is the most-or-100th-most-likely completion; tests whether truth probes are picking up text plausibility instead.
  *Replication cost*: 4h for MATH-style analogue (e.g. plausible-but-wrong final answer tokens vs correct).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — interesting control for "does prefill DoM track *answer plausibility* rather than *correctness*?"

### Approaches & framings

- **Truth as direction, not as classifier** — emphasis on the *direction* identified, with classification accuracy treated as one of two complementary metrics (the other being causal NIE). Reframes our F-2 result: AUROC is the cheap half; the causal half is missing.
- **Hierarchical layer-wise abstraction** — features become "more abstract" with depth; small-model truth probes pick up surface features while large-model probes pick up abstract truth. Implies our F-1 dimensional-breathing may be a small-model phenomenon at 1.5B that is qualitatively different from what 7B is doing.
- **Group-(b) summarization** — clause-ending punctuation tokens are the canonical residence of full-statement features, not the final content token. Reframes our prefill[-1] choice — we should examine whether the prefill template ends in punctuation or not.
- **Salience-based mis-alignment model** — when a non-truth feature `f⁻` is salient on D but anti-correlates with truth on D′, PCA shows orthogonal/antipodal separation; this is a *prediction* about which datasets will mis-generalize. Useful framing for understanding F-7's D-bucket: D-bucket may be a region where a feature `f⁻` (correlated with correctness on our train fold) flips sign.
- **Calibrated few-shot as a baseline** — they use 1-shot prompts and a probability-difference threshold (calibrated so 50% of statements are labelled true); we should adopt this as our verifier-prompt baseline rather than uncalibrated zero-shot.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **cities** — 1496 rows, "The city of [X] is in [Y]." Hugging Face / GitHub (saprmarks/geometry-of-truth), free. Applicable? no — wrong domain (geographical facts, not math).
- **neg_cities** — 1496 rows, negations of cities. Same source. Applicable? no — same reason; useful only as methodology template.
- **sp_en_trans** + **neg_sp_en_trans** — 354 rows each, Spanish-English translation T/F. Applicable? no — wrong domain.
- **larger_than** + **smaller_than** — 1980 rows each, "X is larger than Y." HF/GitHub, free. Applicable? *partially* — closest to MATH in being numerical; useful as a probe-transfer test of "does our MATH DoM transfer to simple numerical comparisons?"
- **cities_cities_conj** + **cities_cities_disj** — 1500 rows each, logical compositions. Applicable? no.
- **companies_true_false** (1200; from Azaria & Mitchell) — Applicable? no.
- **common_claim_true_false** (4450; from Casper et al.) — Applicable? no.
- **counterfact_true_false** (31960; from Meng et al. ROME) — Applicable? *maybe* — large-scale factual T/F probe-transfer benchmark; could test whether MATH-trained DoM identifies a generic truth direction or only a math-correctness direction.
- **likely** (10000) — non-factual generations, final-token plausibility. HF, free. Applicable? *yes (as control)* — directly addresses "is prefill DoM picking up plausibility instead of correctness?"

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Models: LLaMA-2 (7B, 13B, 70B). All open-weight.
- Layer choice: most-downstream group-(b) hidden state — for 13B, this is layer 15 over the EOS punctuation token; for 70B, the rule is more context-dependent (App. B). For Qwen-2.5-1.5B (28 layers), the analogue is roughly layer 17–20 — overlaps with our L19 choice.
- Train/test split: random 80/20 within each dataset; if test-set ≠ train-set, full test-set is used.
- Activations are *centered* (subtract per-dataset mean) before probing; probes are *unbiased*.
- For mass-mean probing, paper uses `p_mm` for OOD test sets but `p_mm^iid` for IID test sets — pipeline-level distinction we currently elide.
- NIE normalization: choose θ scale such that `p(μ⁻ + θ) = p(μ⁺)`. Important for H-1 — without this, magnitude is arbitrary.
- Code/data: https://github.com/saprmarks/geometry-of-truth (MIT-style license inferred from public release).
- Calibrated few-shot: pick threshold so half of statements get labelled true, "improves performance by a few percentage points" — methodology gotcha for verifier baselines.
- Footnote 3 warning: representations *over the final content token* show token-identity clusters in PCA, not truth — implies our current "prefill[-1]" extraction is not necessarily the right token position.

### Replicable intermediates

- **(a) Layer-sweep of cos(prefill_DoM, final_DoM)** at every Qwen-2.5-1.5B layer using the existing Stage 2 cached activations (if all layers were dumped) or via a fresh forward pass (~30 min H100). Tests Refutation 1.
- **(b) Σ⁻¹ correction on existing L19 DoM** — load cached prefill activations, compute Σ on the training fold, project DoM through Σ⁻¹, recompute 5-fold OOF AUROC. ~20 min CPU. Tests Refutation 2.
- **(c) PCA visualization of L19 prefill activations colored by correctness** — confirms whether the truth axis is actually *visible* in top-2 PCs at 1.5B scale. ~5 min CPU. Tests Refutation 5.
- **(d) Re-extract DoM at the period-before-"Solution"** if our prompt template has one — rerun AUROC. ~30 min H100 + 5 min CPU. Tests Refutation 4.
- **(e) NIE for the existing L19 prefill DoM on a 50-problem MATH-500 subset** — single steering experiment with the §6 normalization. ~1 h H100. Tests Refutation 3 / H-1 readiness.

Marks & Tegmark §1.1 / §6 explicitly compare causal protocol to Li et al. and claim improvement via OOD evaluation. Strengthens the case that our F-3-style "rotating direction" finding generalizes.
