Cited by 2402.11917 as the closest prior work on probing internal reasoning trees in language models. Directly motivates our F-2 probing methodology — should be triaged as a foundational mechanistic-interp paper for our pipeline.
- **2209.11895** (Olsson et al., "In-context learning and induction heads") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. The paper builds *deduction heads* as a generalization of induction heads. Foundational reference; should be a `:Method` node (induction head) used by many graphed papers.
- **2310.06824** (Marks & Tegmark, "Geometry of truth") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Cited by 2402.11917 for linear-representation methodology; directly relevant to F-2 framing of "directional probe carries truth signal."
- **2310.10348** (Syed/Rager/Conmy, "Attribution patching outperforms automated circuit discovery") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Cheaper alternative to causal scrubbing; relevant to scaling our circuit-attribution work to 28-layer Qwen.
- **2304.14997** (Conmy et al., "Towards automated circuit discovery / ACDC") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Same motivation as above; foundational tooling for any P12-style mechanistic pathway.
- **2401.12947** (Zhang et al., "Transformer-based models are not yet perfect at learning to emulate structural recursion") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Cited as evidence for the L−1 depth bound and shortcut-solution claim. Directly bears on our refutation #2.
- **2309.16588** (Darcet et al., "Vision transformers need registers") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Source of the "register token" framing the paper imports; provides independent CV-side evidence for the working-memory mechanism. Strong cross-modal corroboration if path merging holds in Qwen.
- **2310.02226** (Goyal et al., "Think before you speak: pause tokens") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Provides downstream-task evidence for register-token-like mechanisms in language models, not just toy synthetic settings.

## 2402.13212 — Soft Self-Consistency Improves Language Model Agents (Wang, Prasad, Stengel-Eskin, Bansal, 2024)

**Relevance:** Replaces self-consistency's majority-vote scoring with `f({P_LM(y_i | y<i, x)})` for `f ∈ {min, mean, product}`. The relevance to our project is *not* the agent-task headline numbers (Bash 30.0, WebShop 46.0, ALFWorld 25.2 SR with CodeLlama-34B at k=10) but the **principle**: a near-zero-cost output-side scalar is a strong correctness ranker. Our pipeline's headline AUROC = 0.7731 (F-2) and selective-prediction = 71.6% at coverage 0.5 (F-8) have never been benchmarked against this baseline. Their finding that AUROC and ECE *don't* correlate with SOFT-SC's selection success rate (r = -0.55 for AUROC on Bash) is also a methodological warning for how F-2 and F-8 are framed.

**Key claim we tested:** Mean / min / product over output token probabilities is sufficient to rank candidate trajectories for selection — no hidden-state probing required. Calibration metrics (ECE, AUROC) are not the right yardstick for selection performance; ranking quality is.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** Sequence-likelihood baseline (FE71) vs F-2's prefill DoM AUROC = 0.7731 has not been run. If the baseline matches or beats DoM, F-2/F-8 are downgraded; if not, F-2 captures information beyond output likelihoods. Adaptive-stopping comparison (FE72) vs H-19's C_exact verification routing is the second-most-leveraged test.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE181 (sequence-likelihood AUROC vs prefill DoM), P11-FE182 (adaptive-stopping routing vs C_exact), P11-FE183 (F-3 orthogonality reduction), P11-FE184 (D-bucket likelihood signature), H-148, H-149, H-150, H-151.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Mean / min / product token-probability aggregation as a confidence score** — `score(y) = f({P_LM(y_i | y<i, x)})`, with `f ∈ {min, mean, product}`. Choice of `f` is dev-set tuned (mean for Bash and ALFWorld; min for WebShop). *Replication cost*: ≤ 1h CPU if log-probs are stored alongside K=1 answers (otherwise re-extract during a forward pass over the 500 problems — small GPU, ~1h). *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — direct competitor to F-2, never baselined.
- **Adaptive stopping by cumulative min-probability threshold** — sample one trajectory at a time, stop when cumulative min-prob ≥ τ. Threshold chosen on dev set. *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU on existing K=8 generations (just simulate the early-stop). *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — natural cheap baseline for H-19.
- **Verbalized vs. logit-based confidence head-to-head** — prompt the model to verbalize a confidence score, use it for selection; compared against logit-based score. Logit-based wins by 2.4% on Bash at k=10. *Replication cost*: ~2h H100 (need to regenerate with verbalize-confidence prompt suffix). *We'd plausibly run this*: **maybe** — mostly relevant if we ever need to rank without logit access.
- **Black-box rescoring via small open-source scorer** — run black-box LLM (GPT-4) for generations, then a smaller open-source LLM for log-prob scoring of those generations. *Replication cost*: not directly applicable to our pipeline — we run open-source models end-to-end. *We'd plausibly run this*: **no**.
- **Cross-aggregation comparison** — they tune `f` over `{min, mean, product}`. Worth doing all three rather than picking one; min and product behave very differently on long answers. *Replication cost*: free given the mean computation. *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes**.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Voting fails when the action space is sparse; soft scoring rescues sample efficiency."** Reframes SC's failure mode: not "votes are noisy" but "exact match is the wrong relation in large action spaces." MATH-500 has a smaller action space (numerical answers, often integers) so this concern is less acute — but the *general* lesson generalizes: any task where the model emits long generations whose surface forms vary should prefer continuous scoring. Intersects F-9 (CoE redundancy with DoM) by suggesting an even simpler continuous score.
- **"Calibration metrics measure absolute probability quality; selection needs ranking quality."** This is the most actionable framing. Our entire pipeline (F-2, F-8) is reported in AUROC and selective-prediction accuracy — both ranking-flavored, but our narrative reads as if AUROC is a calibration-style virtue. SOFT-SC says: don't conflate. Could clean up how F-2 and F-8 are positioned in the next writeup.
- **"Black-box generation + open-source scoring as a deployment pattern."** Not directly used by us, but a reusable framing: if any verifier ever uses a different model than the generator, the relationship between scorer-fit-to-generator and ranking quality matters.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **Bash (Yang et al. 2023)** — 200 user queries (50 dev / 150 test), success rate measured by execution. License: open. *Applicable*: **no** to MATH-500 directly, **yes** as a sanity check for whether our selective-prediction story extends to non-math agent tasks (would feed H-3 code-generation breathing).
- **WebShop (Yao et al. 2022, 50-query subset following Zhou et al. 2023)** — simulated shopping environment, 1.18M products. *Applicable*: **no** to current pipeline.
- **ALFWorld (Shridhar et al. 2021, 134 unseen tasks)** — text-game household chores. *Applicable*: **no** to current pipeline.
- **No math benchmark** — they cite chain-of-thought (Wei et al. 2022) and self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) but do not run on math reasoning. The headline empirics are agent-task-only.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Aggregation `f ∈ {min, mean, product}` should be tuned per dataset on a dev split. **Don't pre-commit to one.** They use mean for Bash/ALFWorld and min for WebShop.
- For the adaptive variant they use **min-probability cumulative score** (not mean) to compare against threshold τ; threshold tuned on dev.
- They observe that the relevant calibration *non-correlation* (with AUROC) is driven by ranking-vs-calibration distinction; concretely, log-prob ordering is preserved under monotone calibration transforms but ECE/AUROC are not invariant.
- Verbalized confidence is reliably worse than logit confidence (Bash, k=10: 27.6 ± 2.0 vs 30.0 ± 2.4). Don't bother with verbalized-confidence ablations as a primary path.
- Code: https://github.com/HanNight/soft_self_consistency (Apache-style — verify before reuse).
- Models actually used: CodeLlama-7B/13B/34B/70B, Mistral-7B, GPT-3.5/GPT-4. None overlap with our Qwen-2.5 / DeepSeek-R1-Distill stack, so direct numbers are not transferable; only the *method* is.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Mean / min / product log-prob over K=1 generations vs F-2's prefill DoM AUROC.** If `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` cached the per-problem K=1 generation strings, one quick re-forward pass gets us per-token log-probs; if it cached log-probs, this is pure CPU. Compute the three aggregations and compute AUROC against the same labels used for F-2. Direct refutation test for **Refutation #1**.
- **Adaptive-stopping simulation on K=8 generations.** If `pathway11_h100/` has K=8 generations cached, simulate "stop at K' < 8 when min-prob > τ" by sweeping τ on the dev split. Plot accuracy vs average-K against H-19's C_exact baseline. Direct test for **Refutation #4**.
- **cos(mean-log-prob, prefill_DoM_score) and cos(mean-log-prob, final_DoM_score) on the 500 MATH-500 problems.** Refutation #3 — settles whether F-3's orthogonality survives once we condition on the output-likelihood signal.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2203.11171** — Wang et al. self-consistency (the paper SOFT-SC extends). Already in graph (status: **REPLICATED + EXTENDED** in our PAPER_INDEX). SOFT-SC cites it as the direct ancestor.
- **2306.03341** — Inference-Time Intervention (Li et al.). Already in graph (status: **CONTRADICTED partial**). Not directly cited by SOFT-SC but in the same "rescore/rerank using model-internal information" family.
- **2410.13640** — Chain-of-Embedding (Wang ICLR 2025). Already in graph (status: **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED / CONTRADICTED**). SOFT-SC's mean-log-prob is a strict simplification of CoE's trajectory-level scoring; cross-paper question worth flagging.
- **2402.03744** — INSIDE / EigenScore. Already in graph (status: **CITED ONLY**). Same "score generations using a continuous internal-state signal" family; SOFT-SC operates one layer further out (output probs only).
- Aggarwal et al. 2023 (Adaptive-Consistency) — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Direct adaptive-stopping baseline; relevant for H-19. arxiv id 2305.11860 (verify).
- Lin et al. 2022 verbalized confidence — NOT in graph; weak relevance only.
- none other worth flagging.

## 2402.15610 — Selective "Selective Prediction": Reducing Unnecessary Abstention in Vision-Language Reasoning (Srikanth et al., 2024)

**Relevance:** VLM selective-prediction paper; not directly on-pathway for our text-CoT pipeline, but provides a clean methodological alternative to F-8's binary probe-driven selective prediction. Specifically reframes selective prediction as a 3-state policy (commit/abstain/gather more), with empirical evidence from VQAv2/A-OKVQA that the gather-more arm recovers ~20% of abstained correct answers. Useful as a non-probe label-free baseline and as a perturbation lens on the "prefill encodes intrinsic difficulty" reading of F-2.

**Key claim we tested:** A non-probe agentic clarification policy can recover abstained-but-correct answers, raising effective coverage without dropping accuracy.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — H-152 will run the text-CoT analogue on MATH-500 1.5B against F-8's 71.6%/50% baseline; H-153 will run the paraphrase-perturbation test on F-2's AUROC 0.7731.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE185, P11-FE186, P11-FE187, H-152, H-153.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **VLM confidence + LLM-driven sub-question generation for selective prediction** — at low VLM confidence on the primary question, prompt an LLM to ask related sub-questions about the image, accept VLM answers only above a sub-question confidence threshold, then re-decide commit/abstain on the primary question.
  *Replication cost*: text-only analogue is ~2h CPU on cached MATH-500 1.5B K=1 outputs (no new model runs required for the abstention layer; needs one fresh K=1 pass over self-generated clarifications, ≈ 1h H100).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — as a baseline arm for F-8 / H-12. It directly quantifies whether the probe's marginal value survives a non-probe agentic comparator.

- **Confidence-gated chained inference (sub-question must clear its own threshold to count as evidence)** — reusable pattern: don't trust auxiliary outputs to inform the primary commit unless they themselves pass a calibration bar.
  *Replication cost*: trivial post-hoc filter on cached outputs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — could sharpen H-19 (C_exact verification routing), where verifier outputs need a confidence gate before they get to vote.

### Approaches & framings

- **Reframes selective prediction as a 3-state policy (commit / abstain / gather more) instead of binary commit/abstain.** Intersects F-8 directly: F-8 evaluates only the binary policy. The 3-state framing implies F-8's coverage curve is a degenerate slice of a larger Pareto frontier.
- **Treats LLM/VLM as a queryable sub-system rather than as a fixed function from prompt to answer.** Intersects H-12 and H-19: both assume a single forward pass; ReCoVERR's framing is that the *inference loop* is the right unit of abstention analysis.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **VQAv2** — public, HF-accessible. Applicable? **no** — vision-language; we work text-only on math.
- **A-OKVQA** — public, HF-accessible. Applicable? **no** — same reason.

The methodology transfers; the datasets do not.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- BLIP2, InstructBLIP, LLaVA-1.5 used as the three VLMs — irrelevant to our stack but signals the method is model-agnostic at the VLM level.
- The clarification LLM is a separate model from the answering VLM — useful design pattern: judge ≠ answerer.
- Code: https://github.com/tejas1995/ReCoVERR — worth peeking at the threshold-tuning / sub-question generation prompts if we run the text analogue.

### Replicable intermediates

- Build a text-CoT analogue of ReCoVERR using cached 1.5B prefill activations + cached K=1 outputs from `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`: on the bottom-50% prefill-DoM problems (where F-8 abstains), run one extra K=1 generation conditioned on a self-asked rephrase ("Restate the problem in your own words, then solve."), compare answered-set accuracy to F-8's 71.6%. This is the smallest cross-check of refutation #1 above.
- For refutation #3: re-extract L19 prefill on 3 paraphrases of each bottom-quartile MATH-500 problem (cached extractor; ~1h H100); recompute DoM scores and SD across paraphrases.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2509.18116** (ALS) — already in graph (CITED ONLY). Conceptually adjacent: layer-wise steering as another inference-time intervention; ReCoVERR's prompt-side intervention is a complementary axis.
- **2504.05419** (Zhang self-verification) — already in graph (CITED ONLY). Closer to ReCoVERR than to F-8; both are evidence-gather-then-commit patterns. Worth linking explicitly.
- **2604.22271** (Kumaran internal-confidence-signals) — already in graph (TO TEST). The contrast is sharp: Kumaran says internal signals already detect/correct errors; ReCoVERR says external clarification is needed. A head-to-head on MATH-500 would adjudicate.

No off-graph papers cited that obviously belong; ReCoVERR's bibliography is VLM-heavy (selective prediction in VQA, abstention in vision tasks) and is unlikely to cross our perimeter filter.

## 2402.18048 — Characterizing Truthfulness in Large Language Model Generations with Local Intrinsic Dimension (Yin, Srinivasa, Chang, 2024)

**Relevance:** A direct competitor / collaborator to our DoM-based
correctness probe.  Yin et al. show that local kNN-MLE intrinsic
dimension at the last token of an LLM's generation predicts
truthfulness on free-form QA at AUROC 0.737–0.764, *beating*
Semantic Entropy and SAPLMA, on Llama-2-7B and -13B.  Two facts make
this a high-leverage paper for us: (i) it uses a *local* ID estimator
(MLE / GeoMLE with k=500) rather than the global TwoNN we tried in
EXP-021 (which scored 0.407) or the layerwise PH that gave F-10 its
null result, and (ii) its empirical regime (last-token activations on
chain-style generation) is the regime where our final-token DoM
underperforms our prefill DoM (F-3).  Together these suggest F-10 is a
result about *coordinate-free global topology* rather than about
"residual geometry is uninformative", and that final-token activations
carry a signal our linear probes are missing.

**Key claim we tested:** Local kNN intrinsic dimension at the last
token of LLM generation predicts correctness at AUROC ≈ 0.74–0.76 on
free-form QA — a regime where our equivalent (final-token L19 DoM)
scores 0.7186, and our TwoNN benchmark scored 0.407.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — H-154 / P11-FE188 will run LID-GeoMLE
(k=500) on cached H100 prefill activations and compare directly to
F-2 (0.7731) and EXP-021 TwoNN (0.407).  Expected outcome based on
Yin's Llama-2 numbers: AUROC in the 0.7–0.78 range on Qwen-2.5-1.5B.
If confirmed, F-10 must narrow to "PH at null" rather than "geometry
at null".

**Related experiments:** P11-FE188, P11-FE189, P11-FE190, P11-FE191,
P11-FE192; H-154, H-155, H-156; EXP-021 (TwoNN, abandoned); EXP-026 (PH
under null).

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **LID-MLE** — Levina & Bickel (2004) maximum-likelihood estimator of
  intrinsic dimension from kNN distances:
  `m̂(X^i) = ((1/(T-1)) · Σ_{j=1..T-1} log(Q_T(X^i)/Q_j(X^i)))^{-1}`
  where `Q_j` is the distance to the j-th nearest neighbour of `X^i`
  in a fixed pool of T candidate activations (T=500).
  *Replication cost*: 20 min CPU on cached `pathway11_h100/`
  per-token L19 NPZs (kNN over 500 problems × 7 stage markers).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — it directly tests F-10 and is the
  cheapest thing in the queue.
- **LID-GeoMLE** — Gomtsyan, Mokrov, Panov, Yanovich (2019) variant
  with a quadratic distance correction that handles boundary /
  anisotropic neighbourhoods.  Yin reports +0.01 AUROC over plain MLE.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU; same data, slightly more
  arithmetic.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — drop-in replacement once LID-MLE
  is wired up.
- **Layer-selection by cumulative LID argmax** — pick layer
  `l* = argmax_l Σ_i m̂(X_l^i)` over a held-out batch.
  *Replication cost*: 5 min CPU once LID-MLE exists.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a non-DoM justification for
  L19 (or moves the anchor).
- **Cross-dataset neighbour pool** — when probing dataset A, draw the
  500-NN pool from dataset B; Yin reports a small drop (~2 AUROC)
  showing the LID signal is mostly local-anisotropy, not
  dataset-specific neighbour geometry.
  *Replication cost*: 1 h CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct probe of F-1 universality
  (does LID transfer across MATH-500/HumanEval/etc.?).
- **Mixing experiment** — prepend a true-prefix prefix, let the model
  continue, then measure LID of the merged sequence.  Mechanistic
  test for whether high LID reflects distributional mixing.
  *Replication cost*: 2 h H100 (need new generations).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct mechanistic counterpart to
  F-7 (D-bucket = distributional mixing?).
- **kNN robustness sweep** — Yin tests k = 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000,
  1500; performance plateaus above ~200.
  *Replication cost*: trivial once LID-MLE exists.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes, as part of the basic ablation.

### Approaches & framings

- **Truthfulness-as-low-dimensional-manifold.**  Truthful continuations
  live on a low-dimensional human-language submanifold; untruthful
  continuations leave it.  Concretely intersects F-4 (asymmetric
  collapse) with a non-PR, non-DoM language: collapse manifests as
  reduced *neighbour-pool* dimension, not reduced participation
  ratio.
- **Signal-mixing hypothesis for elevated LID.**  When prompt-style
  and continuation-style activations co-exist in a neighbour pool,
  pairwise distances inflate and LID rises.  Direct mechanistic
  alternative for the F-7 D-bucket signature (currently described
  collectively but without a generative mechanism).
- **Local-vs-global ID separation.**  The paper's quiet but strong
  point: "PH/TwoNN at null" is a finding *about a global invariant*;
  conditioning on a fixed-k neighbour pool changes the answer.  This
  reframes F-10 from "geometry is null" to "scale-invariant geometry
  is null; scale-conditional geometry is informative."
- **Detection-vs-mechanism layer separation.**  The peak-LID layer
  (where the geometric signature is strongest) and the
  peak-detection layer (where you should probe to predict
  truthfulness) are not the same.  This is a framing that we have
  not internalised — our L19 anchor was chosen by detection
  performance, not by where the signal originates.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **TriviaQA** — closed-book QA; 2000 validation samples used by Yin.
  License/access: HF (`mandarjoshi/trivia_qa`), open. Applicable?
  no — short-form factual QA, not chain-of-thought; would not test
  F-2/F-7.
- **CoQA** — conversational QA; 2000 validation samples. HF,
  open. Applicable? no — short-form, conversational.
- **HotpotQA** — multi-hop QA; 2000 validation samples. HF, open.
  Applicable? marginal — multi-hop is closer to CoT but answers are
  still short-form.
- **TydiQA-GP** — multilingual reading comprehension; 2000 samples.
  HF, open. Applicable? no — reading-comprehension, not generation.
- *(We bring our own MATH-500 1024-tok cache.)*

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Repo: https://github.com/fanyin3639/LID-HallucinationDetection
  (graph stores it under `Truthfulness-LID`; check both).
- Models tested: Llama-2-7B and Llama-2-13B; some ablations on
  earlier Llama / OPT mentioned but not in main tables.
- Default k = 500; stable above k = 200.
- Activations are sampled at the *last token of the generated
  sequence* (post-EOS or end-of-generation), single forward pass per
  problem.
- Layer selection: per-model `argmax_l` over summed LID; for
  Llama-2-7B the "hunchback" peaks around layers 14–18 of 32, with
  detection peaking 1–2 layers later.
- Distance metric: L2 in residual-stream space (no whitening).
- Neighbour pool: drawn from the *same* dataset's training split
  (their default); cross-pool ablation in their Table 3.
- Calibration: AUROC against a ground-truth-correctness label
  (rouge-L vs gold answer thresholded at 0.3 in their setup).
- Compute: numbers reported on a single A100; the kNN step is the
  dominant cost.
- Sensitivity: GeoMLE adds ~+0.01 AUROC over MLE on average; the
  paper recommends GeoMLE as default.

### Replicable intermediates

- **LID-GeoMLE on cached H100 prefill activations** —
  `pathway11_h100/qwen15b/stage_markers/L19_prefill_final_token.npz`
  has 500-problem × 1536-dim Qwen-2.5-1.5B activations at L19,
  prefill final token.  Compute LID-MLE and LID-GeoMLE with k = 500
  (whole pool minus self).  Predict K=1 correctness.  Compare
  AUROC against F-2 (DoM 0.7731).
- **Same, at final token** — corresponding final-token NPZ; predict
  correctness.  Compare AUROC against final-token DoM (F-3,
  0.7186).
- **Layer sweep** — repeat LID-MLE at L15, L17, L19, L21, L23 on the
  same 500 problems.  Plot the hunchback; check for layer-detection
  lag.
- **TwoNN-vs-LID-MLE on the SAME data** — definitive resolution of
  whether TwoNN's 0.407 (EXP-021) was a method failure rather than
  a signal-absence finding.  Both estimators run on the same NPZ in
  one CPU pass.

### Cross-paper signals

- **Azaria & Mitchell 2023 (`2304.13734`, "The Internal State of an
  LLM Knows When It's Lying" / SAPLMA)** — cited as Yin's main
  supervised-classifier baseline.  `query.py paper 2304.13734` →
  not in graph.  Recommend admission: SAPLMA is the canonical
  supervised internal-state truthfulness probe and is the closest
  prior art to F-2's DoM-as-correctness-classifier framing.
- **Kuhn, Gal, Farquhar 2022 (`2302.09664`, Semantic Entropy)** —
  the SE baseline Yin compares against.  `query.py paper 2302.09664`
  → not in graph.  We already have `2406.15927` (SEPs) which builds
  on it; the original Kuhn paper deserves admission as the head of
  that lineage.
- **Yin et al. cite Levina & Bickel (2004)** for MLE-ID and Gomtsyan
  et al. (2019) for GeoMLE.  Neither is on arxiv with a
  triage-relevant ID; they belong in a footnote, not the graph.
- **2509.11569 (D2HScore)** — already in graph as `pending_triage`.
  Connection: D2HScore also extracts a per-layer dispersion-style
  score from residuals; comparing LID vs D2HScore as label-free
  scoring families would be informative.
- **2406.15927 (SEPs)** — already in graph as `pending_triage`.
  Connection: same regime (label-free correctness/truthfulness
  probe); LID is empirically dominant on Llama-2 free-form QA, so
  the SEPs–vs–LID head-to-head is a natural follow-up.
- **2604.18419 (Knowing When to Quit)** — already graphed,
  REPLICATED.  Connection: that paper's probe is
  question-conditional uncertainty; LID is generation-conditional
  geometric uncertainty; comparing the two on MATH-500 would
  triangulate F-8.

## 2403.05767 — Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours (van der Weij, Poesio & Schoots, 2024)

**Relevance:** Methodological reference for any DoM-steering experiment in
this project. Uses contrastive-activation-addition (CAA) at the last token of
the residual stream on Llama 2 7B Chat — the same extraction shape as our
prefill DoM at L19 for Qwen-2.5-1.5B. Three findings constrain how H-1 must
be designed: (a) layer-0 steering produces *opposite* effects, attributed to
copy suppression; (b) combining multiple steering vectors via mean/sum
*fails* and produces mode collapse; (c) simultaneous injection at distinct
layers works for ~2 of 5 behaviors, suggesting distinct concepts live at
distinct layers. Also documents a non-trivial alignment tax (10%
in-domain → 3% out-of-domain) that contradicts the steering literature's
"low tax" narrative.

**Key claim we tested:** Single-layer single-vector contrastive steering is
sufficient for distinct behaviors and capabilities, with negligible
alignment tax. (We translate to: prefill L19 DoM is a sufficient
correctness-signal direction, with redundancy across higher-PR features and
no general-purpose tax.)

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** The paper's findings *predict* (a) L19 DoM
correctness steering will mode-collapse before reaching meaningful accuracy
deltas, (b) multi-layer DoM mosaic will outperform single-layer L19, (c)
the cos(prefill, final)=0.046 in F-3 is generic. Three new hypotheses
(H-157, H-158, H-159) and four FutureExperiments (P11-FE193, FE71, FE72, FE73)
operationalize these tests against cached or near-cached data.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE193, P11-FE194, P11-FE195, P11-FE196 / H-1, H-6,
H-157, H-158, H-159 / F-2, F-3, F-9.

**Status:** TO TEST (HIGH — H-158 is CRITICAL precondition for H-1).

### Methodologies extracted

- **Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA), last-token of residual stream** —
  for each of N matching-prompt / non-matching-prompt pairs, take the
  last-token residual at a chosen layer and subtract; average the diff across
  N pairs.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached Stage 2 prefill NPZs (we already
  have prefill activations at L19 for 500 MATH-500 problems).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — H-1 already needs CAA-style steering
  vectors and this paper's last-token / Llama-2 setup is the closest direct
  reference for our Qwen pipeline.

- **Permuted-vector baseline** — generate a per-layer permutation of the
  steering vector that preserves mean and std but destroys directional
  content, used as null. §2.1.
  *Replication cost*: 5min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — should be the *first* H-1 control before
  reporting any DoM steering effect; cleaner than random-direction baselines
  because matched in marginal stats.

- **Multi-layer simultaneous injection (one vector per layer, single
  global coefficient)** — instead of summing into one vector, inject distinct
  vectors at distinct layers and sweep one global coefficient. §2.2 / Fig 7.
  *Replication cost*: 4h H100 (requires inference with intervention hooks).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — for testing whether a multi-layer DoM
  mosaic captures correctness signal that L19 alone misses (Refutation 4).

- **Mode-collapse / faulty-output discard rule** — drop hyperparameter
  combinations where >5% of outputs are off-grammar OR a single answer
  exceeds 95% frequency. §2.2.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (post-hoc filter).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — must apply to any H-1 result before
  reporting accuracy deltas.

- **Mean-centring (cited Jorgensen 2312.03813)** — add a "text" steering
  vector while subtracting the target-skill vector, anchoring inference
  near the natural-text manifold to reduce alignment tax.
  *Replication cost*: free if running CAA; just compute an extra contrast.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — H-1 should pre-register whether mean-
  centring is applied; results without it are likely worse.

- **Layer × coefficient grid search** — sweep layer in {0,5,10,15,20,25,29,31}
  and coefficient in a log-spaced grid, pick best. Table 1.
  *Replication cost*: 8h H100 for Qwen-1.5B's 28 layers.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes for H-1, no for production probing (we
  already know L19 is the operating point for prefill DoM).

### Approaches & framings

- **"Broad vs narrow skills are about equally steerable"** — the headline
  surprise of §3.1. Reframes the steering literature: steering does not
  require the target to be a "single concept" with a clean linear direction;
  even diffuse capabilities like "general coding" yield similar effect sizes
  to specific targets like "Python." Intersects F-2: our prefill L19 DoM may
  be steering "general correct-ness" rather than any specific reasoning
  competence — that's *fine* for a probe, but means H-1's intervention will
  generalize across math sub-skills (positive) but also across non-math text
  (alignment tax).

- **"Combined vectors fail; distributed vectors work"** — §4.2. Reframes
  multi-target steering as a layer-routing problem rather than a
  vector-combination problem. Intersects H-6 / F-9: if correctness has
  components that live at different layers, the right pipeline is
  multi-layer simultaneous probing, not single-layer projection.

- **"Alignment tax is real, not zero"** — §3.1 Fig 3b explicitly prices the
  tax at 10%-coding-loss → 3%-text-loss, contradicting prior steering
  literature (Rimsky, Turner, Zou, Li) which claimed minimal tax.
  Intersects H-1: any honest steering experiment must report tax separately,
  not just the in-domain effect.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **The Pile (5000 samples, 4096-tok truncation)** — open / HF. Applicable: no
  for the MATH-500 1024-tok regime, but applicable as the held-out
  text-perplexity slab for measuring alignment tax under H-1 steering.
- **CodeParrot Python subset (Tunstall et al. 2022)** — open / HF. Applicable:
  no — we don't steer for coding ability.
- **Perez et al. 2212.09251 behavioral binary-Q evals (5 datasets:
  anti-immigration, agreeableness, myopia, sycophancy, wealth-seeking)** —
  open / HF (`Anthropic/model-written-evals`). Applicable: not directly to
  correctness, but the *format* (binary A/B with `[` template forcing the
  next token) is a clean evaluation pattern for testing whether
  steered-Qwen still respects answer formatting on MATH-500
  (mode-collapse check).

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Llama 2 7B Chat, bfloat16, no sampling for generation.
- Steering vectors are *not* normalized (allows the same coefficient to work
  across layers). §2.1.
- Random shuffle seed = 13 (for reproducibility against this paper).
- Adaptive coefficient sweep: relative score < 0.05 → stop run; relative
  score < 0.15 → step size 5 instead of 1. Appendix A.2.
- 500 samples for activation generation, 200 validation, rest for test
  (multi-behavior section). §2.2.
- Inject one *behavior* per *layer* in simultaneous setup: myopia@L11,
  wealth-seeking@L12, sycophancy@L13, agreeableness@L14,
  anti-immigration@L15. Linear layer ordering, no overlap.
- Code: <https://github.com/TeunvdWeij/extending-activation-addition>.
- Sycophancy steering specifically *failed* on this dataset (vs Rimsky 2023
  where it worked) — authors attribute to dataset's narrow political-topology
  framing. Cautionary tale for evaluating any "behavior" via single dataset.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Layer-0 sign-flip test on Qwen-1.5B prefill DoM.** Use cached Stage 2
  prefill NPZ at L0 (if extracted) or extract from H100 pod once. Compute
  L0 DoM against same correct/incorrect split as F-2. AUROC < 0.5 (i.e.
  *flipped*) replicates the paper's L0 finding and would constrain the
  copy-suppression hypothesis (Refutation 1).
- **Generic-contrast cosine baseline at L19.** Use cached Stage 2 prefill
  NPZ for 500 MATH-500 problems. Build 20 arbitrary 250/250 splits at L19,
  compute mass-mean direction for each, compute pairwise cosines. If median
  ≤ 0.1, F-3's cos=0.046 is at the median of the null and not a meaningful
  geometric finding (Refutation 3).
- **Multi-layer DoM concatenation probe.** Use cached prefill NPZs at
  {L11, L13, L15, L17, L19, L21, L23} (re-extract if not cached). Train
  logistic regression on concatenated (problem × 7-layer) DoM projections
  with the same 5-fold OOF split as F-2. If AUROC ≥ 0.79, multi-layer
  exceeds single-layer L19 (Refutation 4 / contradicts H-6 claim that
  CoE-60 redundancy is total).

### Cross-paper signals

- **2306.03341** — already in graph (status: graphed, CONTRADICTED partial).
  Inference-Time Intervention; this paper's methodological cousin (mass-mean
  direction at last token).
- **2312.06681** — already in graph (status: pending_triage / rejected as
  duplicate-CAA at admission). Rimsky CAA — *the* canonical contrastive
  activation addition reference; this paper's direct methodological parent.
  Should be re-considered for full triage given how much of our H-1 design
  it constrains.
- **2308.10248** — already in graph (status: pending_triage / admission_only).
  Turner ActAdd — foundational; cited heavily here for non-normalized
  vectors and broad applicability.
- **2312.03813** — already in graph (status: pending_triage / rejected as
  duplicate-mean-centring). Jorgensen mean-centring — used here to anchor
  steering near the text manifold; relevant to H-1 as an alignment-tax
  mitigation that should be pre-registered.
- **2310.04625** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. McDougall et al.
  *Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding an Attention Head*. Cited
  here to explain the L0 sign-flip; if this mechanism explains why L19 DoM
  works (Refutation 1), it's a candidate alternative-mechanism paper for F-2.
- **2310.01405** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Zou et al.
  *Representation Engineering* (RepE). Foundational top-down framing for the
  whole steering literature; absence is a gap.
- **2212.09251** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Perez et al.
  *Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations*. The
  source dataset for the multi-behavior section, useful as a benchmark for
  testing answer-format integrity under DoM steering.

## 2403.18680 — Non-Linear Inference Time Intervention: Improving LLM Truthfulness (Hoscilowicz et al., 2024)

**Relevance:** Direct successor to ITI (2306.03341), same family as Truth Forest (2312.17484). Replaces LR probe with MLP probe and extends single-token probing/intervention to multi-token (τ=4 probing, ρ=6 intervention) windows. Reports +13.84 absolute MC1 on TruthfulQA over baseline ITI on LLaMA-2-7B (33.54 → 50.19), with non-trivial OOD generalization to ARC, MMLU, OpenBookQA. The methodology is directly portable to our F-2 / F-3 / F-8 / H-1 / H-13 stack and challenges three of our framings: (a) the LR probe at F-2 may underestimate signal in earlier layers, (b) the F-3 prefill-vs-final orthogonality may be a window-vs-window cleavage rather than a per-token rotation, and (c) H-1's residual-stream-level intervention may be a wrong-granularity null.

**Key claim we tested:** Non-linear MLP probing + multi-token averaging across the answer-token window finds substantially more concept-bearing heads than linear single-token probing; head-level intervention dominates residual-stream-level intervention.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** No experiments run yet. P11-FE197 (H-160), P11-FE198 (H-161), P11-FE199, P11-FE200 (H-162), P11-FE201 form the test plan. Most informative cheap experiment is P11-FE197 (H-160): MLP-probe-per-layer, ~30min CPU on cached data; settles whether F-2's 0.7731 is a probe-class ceiling. Most informative expensive experiment is P11-FE200 (H-162): head-level vs residual-stream steering, ~4h H100; settles H-1's granularity question.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE197, P11-FE198, P11-FE199, P11-FE200, P11-FE201, H-160, H-161, H-162, H-1, H-13.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **MLP probe (1 hidden layer)** — Replace logistic regression with single-hidden-layer MLP per (layer, head). They report deeper MLPs overfit on TruthfulQA's ~800 samples.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached pathway11 prefill activations (Qwen-2.5-1.5B has 28 layers × ~16 heads = 448 head-positions; trivially cheap).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct head-to-head with our LR probe; potential to lift F-2's 0.7731 if non-linearity carries signal.

- **Multi-token probing (τ-window average)** — Average activations across the last τ tokens (τ=4 optimum for LLaMA-2-7B + TruthfulQA) before training the probe.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU; pathway11 has per-token activations for many problems.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly tests Refutation 1; cheap.

- **Multi-token intervention (ρ-window bias)** — At inference, add the mean direction (computed across the last ρ tokens of training Q+A pairs) to attention head activations during the last ρ tokens of generation. ρ=6 optimum for LLaMA-2-7B.
  *Replication cost*: 4h H100 (requires online generation with interventions; same envelope as H-1).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — combine with H-1 head-selection arm.

- **Top-K attention head selection by probe accuracy** — Rank all (layer, head) pairs by MLP probe accuracy; intervene only on Top-K (K is a hyperparameter). NL-ITI sweeps K, picks the (α, K) that minimizes KL-vs-MC1 trade-off.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — fixes H-13.

- **KL-divergence-vs-task-metric Pareto curves** — Sanity-check intervention strength by tracking KL(intervened || original) on a neutral corpus (OpenWebText). Plot MC1 vs KL across (α, K) sweeps; an MC1 maximum near KL ≈ 0.5 is normal. KL is a "sanity check" only — generalization should be assessed on held-out benchmarks, not KL alone.
  *Replication cost*: trivial — we have a pile of unrelated MATH problems for the KL reference distribution.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — would discipline the H-1 sweep.

- **Cross-benchmark generalization protocol** — Train probe on dataset A (TruthfulQA), evaluate intervention on B (ARC, MMLU, OBQA) without re-tuning. Reports MC1 + CE + KL per benchmark.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU per held-out benchmark on cached activations + 1h H100 if re-extracting on B.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gold-standard test for F-5 (Refutation 4).

### Approaches & framings

- **"Truthful knowledge is distributed across answer tokens, not concentrated at the final token."** Direct contradiction of the implicit final-token-as-summary assumption baked into ITI. For us: a smooth-direction-across-answer-tokens framing reframes F-3's orthogonality as prefill-vs-answer-window (singleton vs subspace), not prefill-vs-final-token.

- **"Linear probes systematically underestimate non-linearly encoded concepts in early layers."** Direct push-back on F-2's "L19 is the layer" claim, which uses LR. This intersects our methodology, not our findings — but if a non-linear probe at L4 beats LR at L19, the finding's frame collapses.

- **"KL-divergence on a neutral corpus is a sanity check, not a primary metric."** Useful framing for H-1: sweep α-on-KL not α-on-task-loss to avoid overfitting the steering direction to the eval distribution.

- **Head-level rather than residual-stream-level steering granularity.** NL-ITI's biggest implicit framing shift: the residual stream is too coarse a target. Different heads at the same layer carry different concepts; steer the right ones, not all of them.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **TruthfulQA** — ~800 multiple-choice Q+A pairs, MC1/MC2 metric. License: Apache-2.0 / public. Applicable? **partial** — labeled at problem level, not token level; mismatched with MATH-500's reasoning-chain regime, but a viable orthogonal benchmark for OOD probe transfer (Refutation 4).
- **ARC (Challenge)** — 7,787 multiple-choice science questions. License: CC-BY-SA. HF-accessible. Applicable? **yes for OOD generalization tests** (Refutation 4).
- **MMLU** — 14k multiple-choice across 57 subjects. License: MIT. HF-accessible. Applicable? **yes for OOD generalization tests** (Refutation 4).
- **OpenBookQA** — 5,957 multiple-choice elementary-science questions. License: Apache-2.0. HF-accessible. Applicable? **yes for OOD generalization tests**.
- **OpenWebText** — used as KL reference distribution. License: open. Applicable? **yes** — a neutral corpus for the KL sanity check; we can substitute any held-out MATH-style baseline.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Model: LLaMA-2-7B (32 layers, 32 heads/layer = 1024 head-positions). Our work uses Qwen-2.5-1.5B (28 layers, 12 heads/layer = 336 head-positions) — comparable scale.
- MLP probe: 1 hidden layer was best; deeper overfit on ~800 samples. Hidden width not specified in paper but their GitHub (Samsung/NL-ITI) has the spec.
- (ρ, τ) joint optimum = (6, 4) for LLaMA-2-7B + TruthfulQA. Asymmetric (ρ > τ): more tokens used at intervention than at probe training.
- Intervention: `x_l ← x_l + α · σ_l^h · θ_l^h` only at Top-K heads, where σ is the per-head per-layer standard deviation across Q+A pairs.
- α swept over a range that produces KL ∈ [0, ~1.5] vs OpenWebText. MC1 maximum sits near KL ≈ 0.5; pushing α further degrades.
- Code: github.com/Samsung/NL-ITI (MIT license, full replication).
- Few-shot prompting was used for evaluation (consistent with their ITI baseline reproduction at MC1 = 36.35%).
- Probe training set is small (~800 TruthfulQA pairs) — be careful about probe variance.

### Replicable intermediates

- **MLP-probe vs LR-probe at L19**: train a 1-hidden-layer MLP on cached Qwen-2.5-1.5B prefill L19 activations from `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`. If MLP-AUROC > 0.7731 by ≥0.02 OOF, F-2's 0.7731 is a linear-probe artifact. (~30min CPU.)
- **Per-token DoM cosines on the last 8 answer tokens**: from cached per-token activations in pathway11, compute DoM at positions [-1, -2, ..., -8] and the 8×8 cosine matrix. Settles Refutation 1 directly. (~20min CPU.)
- **Per-(layer, head) MLP-probe heatmap on MATH-500**: 28×12 = 336 head-positions; train MLP probes on cached per-head activations (if cached at head granularity; otherwise use residual-stream as proxy). Identifies Top-K heads à la NL-ITI. (~1h CPU if per-head cached, else needs re-extraction.)
- **OOD transfer of prefill DoM**: take F-2's L19 LR probe, evaluate it on MMLU-stem and ARC-Challenge (we have a Qwen-2.5-1.5B extractor pipeline). AUROC drop directly tests F-5. (~2h CPU on cached activations + 30min H100 if re-extracting.)

### Cross-paper signals

- **2306.03341** — already in graph (status: pending_triage despite being seeded — needs re-promotion). NL-ITI's direct baseline; ITI is the canonical predecessor we already CONTRADICTED partially.
- **2312.17484** — Truth Forest (TrFr), Chen et al. 2024. **NOT in graph; recommend admission.** Cited by NL-ITI as the ~10% relative improvement comparator. Multi-dimensional orthogonal probes — directly relevant to F-7's "low-dim manifold" / P11-FE7's SVD-of-prefill question.
- **2402.03744** — INSIDE / EigenScore. Already in graph (CITED ONLY). NL-ITI's MLP probe is a more direct measurement of the same hidden-state truthfulness latent that EigenScore tries to derive from covariance.
- **2410.13640** — Chain-of-Embedding. Already in graph (PARTIALLY CONFIRMED). NL-ITI's "multi-token averaging in answer space" is qualitatively similar to CoE-style aggregation.
- **2406.15927** — Semantic Entropy Probes. Already in graph (CITED ONLY, motivates H-12). NL-ITI is its supervised mirror.
- **2310.02168** — "Editing personality for LLMs" (Mao et al.). NOT in graph; out of scope (personality not correctness), do not admit.
- **2303.08896** — SelfCheckGPT. NOT in graph; tangential (sample-consistency hallucination detection, not internal-state); do not admit unless H-12 expands.

## 2404.05971 — Does Transformer Interpretability Transfer to RNNs? (Paulo, Marshall, Belrose, 2024)

**Relevance:** Tests whether transformer interpretability methods (CAA, Tuned Lens,
ELK-quirky probing) transfer to RNN architectures (Mamba, RWKV). For our research
program this paper functions as (a) a cross-architecture sanity check on the
"prefill DoM" framing — if RNNs show parallel-not-orthogonal prefill/final
directions, F-3 is transformer-specific; (b) a literature ceiling for Mahalanobis-on-
concatenated-probes anomaly detection (Mamba 0.82 / BTLM 0.85) directly applicable to
F-7 / H-7 D-bucket detection; (c) evidence against H-12 (label-free probes), since
unsupervised CCS/CRC consistently underperform supervised probes on transfer settings;
(d) cross-architecture support for the "middle layers dominate" finding that
challenges F-2's specific L19 commitment.

**Key claim we tested:** Linear probes (DiffInMeans, LogR, LDA) reach AUROC ~0.76–0.78
on Mamba 2.8b for distribution-shift transfer (Alice-easy → Bob-hard); unsupervised
CCS/CRC underperform; Mahalanobis on concatenated layer-probes reaches 0.79–0.85 for
hard-vs-hard distribution-shift detection; Tuned Lens transfers from transformers to
RNNs with monotonic per-layer perplexity; CAA steering works on RNNs with smaller but
more stable effects than transformers.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** P11-FE208 (per-layer AUROC sweep refuting F-2's L19
specificity) and P11-FE210 (Mahalanobis D-bucket detector against the 0.82–0.85 ceiling)
are the highest-leverage immediate tests. P11-FE211 (Tuned Lens on Qwen-2.5-1.5B)
refutes F-9 if monotonicity holds. P11-FE209 (seven-method probe sweep) downgrades H-12
if CCS/CRC underperform on our data as they do on the paper's.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE208, P11-FE209, P11-FE210, P11-FE211, H-169, H-170, H-171, F-2,
F-3, F-7, F-9, H-7, H-12.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA)** — Diff-in-means on residual-stream
  activations at the answer-letter token, indexed by behavior label. Steering vector
  added at inference time with multiplier ∈ [-3, 3], no normalization across models.
  *Replication cost*: minutes CPU once activations are cached; need a chat-tuned model
  for behavior-style probing. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly extends H-1.
- **State steering (RNN-only)** — Diff-in-means on the RNN's compressed hidden state
  (Mamba SSM state or RWKV WKV state) added at the boundary token. *Replication cost*:
  needs Mamba/RWKV chat model; not directly applicable to our Qwen-2.5 transformer
  pipeline. *We'd plausibly run this*: no — out of architecture scope.
- **Tuned Lens** — Per-layer affine translator (A_ℓ, b_ℓ) trained to make
  LogitLens(A_ℓ h_ℓ + b_ℓ) match the final-layer distribution; trained on Pile
  validation. *Replication cost*: ~few hours H100 to train translators for Qwen-2.5-1.5B
  on MATH-500-style data; codebase at github.com/AlignmentResearch/tuned-lens.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly tests F-9 and gives per-layer information
  curves for free.
- **Seven probing methods (LDA, mass-mean, LogR, CCS, CRC, LogR on contrast pairs,
  diff-in-means on contrast pairs)** — All take residual-stream activations at one layer
  and output a scalar. CCS and CRC are unsupervised consistency-style probes.
  *Replication cost*: minutes CPU per probe per layer on cached NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — broadens the F-2 single-method ceiling test.
- **Mahalanobis anomaly detector on concatenated per-layer probe log-odds** — Fit a
  multivariate Gaussian on "easy" or "in-distribution" examples and use d²(x, P) as the
  detection score. *Replication cost*: ~1h CPU on cached P11 NPZs once per-layer probes
  exist. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct test of F-7 / H-7.
- **LoRA-quirky fine-tuning protocol** — Fine-tune base models to make systematic errors
  conditioned on a keyword. *Replication cost*: 2–4h H100 per quirky model, plus dataset
  prep. *We'd plausibly run this*: no — orthogonal to MATH-500 pipeline; useful only if
  we move into deception/ELK territory.

### Approaches & framings

- **Representation engineering vs mechanistic interpretability dichotomy.** §6 Conclusion
  explicitly aligns with rep-eng (probing, steering, lensing) and excludes mechanistic
  approaches as future work. Reinforces that our F-N findings live in rep-eng-land —
  H-13 (head-level attribution) is the only mechanistic hypothesis we have, and the gap
  is a known one in the literature, not a missed framing.
- **"Compressed state" framing for RNNs.** The state aggregates the entire history into
  a fixed-size vector — analogous to a transformer's "prefill" boundary representation,
  but causally upstream of every future token. Suggests reframing F-2 (prefill DoM)
  as "the transformer's only stateful summary," contrasted with the RNN's continuous
  state. Could change how H-5 (familiarity vs decomposability) is operationalized.
- **Iterative inference framing for probes (Jastrzębski et al. 2017).** Both pre-norm
  transformers and modern RNNs share the residual-block structure that makes probing /
  early-exiting interpretable. Implies F-2's L19 prefill probing is part of a broader
  pre-norm-residual phenomenon — useful for paper writeups.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **Anthropic CAA dataset (Rimsky 2023)** — 7 alignment behaviors, multiple-choice with
  answer-letter targets. License: open. Applicable? no — orthogonal to MATH-500
  reasoning. Useful only if we extend to alignment-style steering.
- **OpenHermes 2.5 chat dataset** — Used to fine-tune base models into chat models.
  License: open on HF. Applicable? no — Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Instruct already chat-tuned.
- **Pile validation set (Gao 2020)** — Used to train tuned lens. License: open.
  Applicable? yes — direct training set for Qwen-2.5-1.5B tuned lens.
- **Mallen & Belrose quirky datasets** (cap, hem, sciq, snt, nli, aut, add, sub, mul,
  mod, sqr) — 11 binary-classification tasks. License: open at
  github.com/EleutherAI/elk-generalization. Applicable? partial — the arithmetic ones
  (add, sub, mul, mod, sqr) are an easier sandbox than MATH-500 for D-bucket-style
  experiments and the "easy → hard generalization" framing.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Steering vectors **NOT normalized** across models — different model norms make
  same-norm steering give different effect sizes. (§3.1, footnote 3.) Important for any
  cross-architecture comparison of H-1 results.
- Multiplier range [-3, 3]; max steering effect taken across layers, not at fixed layer.
- For Mamba: tied embedding/unembedding causes the tuned lens to decode *input tokens*
  in the early layers (Fig. 7). If we tune-lens Qwen-2.5-1.5B (which does *not* tie),
  early-layer behavior should differ.
- Tuned Lens training code (lightly modified): github.com/AlignmentResearch/tuned-lens
- ELK-quirky probing code: github.com/EleutherAI/elk-generalization
- Probe is trained on residuals at the answer-position only, using "Earliest Informative
  Layer" — they don't use the last layer naively.
- CCS and CRC are unsupervised, the rest are supervised; CCS-trained-on-all-contexts
  collapses to AUROC ≈ 0.54 (chance).
- Behaviors with "weak steering" (sycophancy, refusal) are weak across *all*
  architectures — informs which steering targets are realistic.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Per-layer DoM AUROC sweep on Qwen-2.5-1.5B** — Train DiffInMeans probe at every
  layer 1–28 on cached P11 H100 prefill NPZs, plot AUROC curve. Tests F-2's L19
  specificity. Cached artifact: `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` NPZs. ~30min CPU.
- **Tuned Lens per-layer perplexity on Qwen-2.5-1.5B** — Train translators on Pile
  validation (or MATH-500 prompts), compute per-layer perplexity, check monotonicity.
  Tests F-9. Existing tuned-lens codebase + cached residuals. ~few hours H100.
- **Seven-method probe sweep** — Run LDA, mass-mean, LogR, CCS, CRC, LogR-on-contrast,
  DiffInMeans-on-contrast at L19 on cached P11 NPZs and compare AUROCs. Tests H-12
  (CCS/CRC underperformance) and gives us an L19 method-ceiling. ~1h CPU.
- **Mahalanobis anomaly detector for D-bucket** — Concatenate per-layer probe log-odds
  on cached P11 NPZs, fit Gaussian on ABC-bucket activations, compute Mahalanobis on
  D-bucket. Tests H-7 / F-7. ~1h CPU after per-layer probes are computed.

## 2404.12038 — Uncovering Safety Risks of Large Language Models through Concept Activation Vector (Xu, Huang, Chen, Wang, 2024)

**Relevance:** SCAV is the closest published methodological precedent to F-2 / H-1: a supervised linear probe (`Pm(e) = sigmoid(w·e + b)`, L2 reg, ~140 examples) on residual-stream embeddings, used both as a correctness/safety predictor and as a closed-form steering direction (`v = w/‖w‖`, `ε = [sigmoid⁻¹(P₀) − b − w·e] / ‖w‖`). It reports >95% probe TestAcc starting at layer 10–11 in aligned LLaMA-2/Vicuna/Mistral, sharply higher than our 0.7731 OOF AUROC at L19 — a gap that licenses two cheap experiments: a per-layer probe sweep (P11-FE212) and a closed-form-magnitude steering arm in E1 (P10-FE12). The paper also surfaces a multi-layer-correction mechanism (Fig 4b) that provides a concrete alternative reading of F-3's prefill ⊥ final orthogonality, namely active cross-layer cancellation rather than encoding-of-different-concepts.

**Key claim we tested:** Linear probes on aligned-LLM residual streams achieve near-perfect class separation from layer 10–11 onward, and the probe-normal direction (not the difference-of-means) is the canonical steering vector.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — direct contact with F-2 (probe-layer choice), F-3 (orthogonality interpretation), F-9 (single-layer redundancy), and H-1 (steering vector and magnitude formula). Three FutureExperiments queued (P11-FE212, P10-FE12, P11-FE213); one further patching test (P10-FE13) gated on H100 pod.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE212, P10-FE12, P11-FE213, P10-FE13, H-172, H-173, H-174; transitively P10-FE1.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Per-layer linear safety probe** — `Pm(e) = sigmoid(wᵀe + b)` trained with cross-entropy + L2 reg on 140 malicious + 140 safe instruction embeddings; reported per-layer test accuracy.
  *Replication cost*: 10 min CPU on cached prefill NPZs (per layer × 28 layers).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — we already do single-layer probes; this just sweeps every layer with the same machinery.

- **Closed-form embedding-level attack** — `ε = [sigmoid⁻¹(P₀) − b − wᵀe] / ‖w‖`, `v = w / ‖w‖`, with magnitude minimization subject to `Pm(e + ε·v) ≤ P₀`.
  *Replication cost*: 1 day H100 (needs full generation rerun with intervened activations).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct H-1/E1 method.

- **Multi-layer sequential perturbation (early → late)** — perturb only on layers with TestAcc > 90%, in increasing-layer order, single closed-form step per layer.
  *Replication cost*: 1–2 day H100 (variable depending on perturbation count).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — refutation arm for F-9.

- **t-SNE on probe-layer embeddings** — qualitative separability check before AUROC reporting.
  *Replication cost*: 5 min CPU per layer on cached prefill NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — fast sanity step before any AUROC claim.

- **Auto-selected perturbation hyperparameters** — binary search on `P₀` threshold (0.01% in the paper) until ASR-useful is maximized.
  *Replication cost*: free (logic only) once embedding-level attack is implemented.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — eliminates a manual α sweep in P10-FE1.

- **Probe-weight direction `w/‖w‖` as the canonical steering vector** (vs mass-mean / DoM).
  *Replication cost*: free (already extracting both).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — comparison arm in P10-FE1.

- **Prompt-level attack via AutoDAN genetic algorithm + dual loss `Pm(eˢ) + ‖eˢ − e‖`** — not applicable to our work; we don't do prompt optimization.

### Approaches & framings

- **Linear separability as a function of alignment training, not architecture.** SCAV shows aligned LLaMA gets >95% probe accuracy while unaligned Alpaca gets near-chance. Reframes our F-2 result: the prefill correctness direction may be a side-effect of Qwen-1.5B-Instruct's SFT/RLHF rather than fundamental computation. Cross-tests against base-model Qwen would settle this.

- **Embedding-level attack as inverse steering.** Behavior change framed as crossing a learned decision boundary by minimum-norm perturbation. Re-frames our H-1 (per-position DoM steering) — instead of "add α·v" the question becomes "find ε that crosses the probe's threshold" — a quantity, not just a direction.

- **Late-layer correction circuits.** SCAV demonstrates that residual-stream perturbations are not additive across layers; later layers actively reverse earlier-layer modifications. Directly bears on F-3 interpretation and on any P10/P11 patching experiment.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **AdvBench (50-instruction subset)** — public on HuggingFace, MIT-licensed. Applicable? no — instructions are harmful-behavior queries, not math.
- **HarmfulQA** — public on HF, MIT. Applicable? no — same reason.
- **StrongREJECT (50)** — public benchmark. Applicable? no.

(SCAV's training set is 140+140 GPT-4-generated safe/malicious pairs; not released as a standalone artifact.)

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Probe form: `Pm(e) = sigmoid(wᵀe + b)`, L2-regularized cross-entropy.
- Layer-inclusion threshold for attack: TestAcc > 90% (otherwise excluded from perturbation set).
- Perturbation threshold: `P₀ = 0.01%` on the probe output post-attack.
- Sequential perturbation order: early → late layer.
- Embeddings extracted at all L layers; aligned LLMs cross 95% TestAcc at layer 10–11.
- Training data minimum: ~5 instruction pairs already gives near-100% ASR-keyword (Figure 3); 140+140 is comfortably above the saturation point.
- Models tested: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, LLaMA-2-13B-Chat, LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B, Qwen-1.5-7B-Chat, Vicuna-v1.5-7B, WizardLM-2; black-box GPT-4 transfer.
- Code reference: https://github.com/SproutNan/AI-Safety_SCAV

### Replicable intermediates

- **Per-layer prefill probe AUROC sweep on Qwen-1.5B** — we have or can cheaply re-extract per-layer L0..L27 prefill activations from `pathway11_h100/`; train SCAV-style probes at each layer; compare to L19 = 0.7731. Script: adapt `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` probe code to loop over layers. Cost ~30 min CPU.
- **t-SNE on L19 prefill — correct vs incorrect** — direct visualization; if separability looks like SCAV's aligned-LLaMA t-SNE we have geometric corroboration of F-2; if it looks like unaligned-Alpaca we have a problem. Cost ~5 min CPU.
- **Cosine angle: probe weight `w` vs raw DoM at L19** — cheap (one cached NPZ + sklearn LR fit). If `cos(w, DoM) > 0.95`, the probe-weight-vs-DoM debate is moot for L19 and SCAV's closed-form formula is interchangeable with our DoM scaffolding; if low, probe-weight steering and DoM steering will diverge in P10-FE1.
- **Single-step closed-form steering magnitude prediction** — for any held-out problem we have prefill `e`, probe `(w, b)`, threshold `P₀`; compute ε via SCAV's formula and check whether the predicted magnitude lies in the same range our manual α-sweep explored.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2406.11717 — Arditi et al., "Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction"** — already in graph (`status: graphed` per `query.py paper`). Directly methodologically adjacent — SCAV is the supervised, multi-layer extension of Arditi's single-direction refusal result. Worth an `EXTENDED_BY` edge from 2406.11717 to 2404.12038.
- **2310.06824 — Marks & Tegmark, Geometry of Truth** — already in graph, CORROBORATED_BY F-4. Same probe-direction-vs-DoM tension; SCAV's preference for `w/‖w‖` over DoM is data on the same debate.

RepE uses PCA on malicious/safe difference vectors as the steering direction; SCAV explicitly outperforms it.
