## 2404.15255 — How to use and interpret activation patching (Heimersheim & Nanda, 2024)

**Relevance:** Methodology / best-practices tutorial for activation patching, the standard mechanistic-interpretability technique for upgrading correlational findings to causal ones. The paper does not directly contradict any F-N finding — it instead supplies the methodology that would be required to *causally validate* F-2, F-3, F-7, F-8, and F-9, all of which currently rest on correlational probes and AUROCs. The paper's headline distinction (denoising = sufficiency, noising = necessity, *and they are not symmetric*) directly motivates a noising sweep on L19 prefill (FE73) as the cheapest causal upgrade of our headline finding F-2. §3.2 backup-behaviour / Hydra-effect discussion supplies a clean refutation route for F-9's redundancy claim. §4.2 metric pitfalls (continuous-linear logit-diff > binary accuracy) suggests F-2's AUROC 0.7731 may be a lower bound on the true L19 signal strength.

**Key claim we tested:** "Activation patching is the gold standard for circuit-component identification; correlational probes are insufficient evidence of causal involvement; denoising and noising answer different questions (sufficiency vs necessity); discrete metrics (accuracy, AUROC) overrepresent threshold effects."

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** No direct test of the paper's methodological claims yet; rather, the paper exposes that *our project has not yet run the patching experiments that would distinguish causal from correlational interpretations of F-2, F-7, F-8, F-9.* P11-FE214 (noising L19 prefill) is the recommended first test and would close the largest evidentiary gap in the project. P11-FE216 (logit-diff probe re-target) is a 30-min CPU sanity check that should be run regardless. P11-FE217 (backup-pathway test for F-9) is a more targeted check.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE214, P11-FE215, P11-FE216, P11-FE217, H-1, H-13, H-175, H-176

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Denoising (clean → corrupt patching)** — copy clean activations into a corrupted run; tests sufficiency. *Replication cost*: one extraction pass per source/destination pair on cached MATH-500 prompts (~2h CPU if activations are cached, ~1 H100-hour if re-generating). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — converts F-2 from correlational to causal.

- **Noising (corrupt → clean patching)** — copy corrupted activations into a clean run; tests necessity. *Replication cost*: same as denoising. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — strictly stronger evidence than denoising for our use case (we want to know whether the L19 DoM is *necessary* for correct answering, not just sufficient).

- **Path patching** — patch only the path A → B, not the whole downstream subtree. Distinguishes mediation from amplification/calibration. *Replication cost*: 4–8h CPU on cached activations using transformer_lens hooks. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes, if denoising/noising sweep flags L19 as causal — path patching is the natural follow-up to ask "via which downstream component does L19 act?"

- **Causal Scrubbing (Chan et al. 2022)** — full circuit verification by noising every non-circuit connection. *Replication cost*: heavy — needs a complete hypothesised circuit to scrub against, and that circuit doesn't exist yet for our findings. *We'd plausibly run this*: not yet — pre-requisite is finding a candidate circuit via path patching first.

- **Attribution patching / AtP\*** (Nanda 2023) — first-order Taylor approximation to activation patching; runs in 2 forward passes regardless of granularity. *Replication cost*: minimal — a few hours of code, runs on cached activations. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — natural exploratory tool to identify which heads/layers are worth full patching, before paying the per-component cost.

- **Logit-difference metric** — measure model's logit(correct) − logit(incorrect); linear in residual stream, controls for "boost everything" components. *Replication cost*: trivial when answer-token positions are known (which they are for MATH-500). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — should be added alongside binary AUROC for every existing probe (F-2, F-8) as a sanity check.

- **KL-divergence over full output distribution** — alternative metric that captures both positive and negative components, used by Conmy et al. ACDC (2304.14997). *Replication cost*: trivial. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — natural complement to logit-difference.

- **Direct logit attribution / logit lens** — decompose the residual stream by component contribution to logit(answer). *Replication cost*: trivial on cached data. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a per-layer / per-head attribution map that complements F-2's L19-only result.

### Approaches & framings

- **Sufficiency vs necessity are not the same.** This is the paper's headline conceptual move. Our entire current evidence stack (probes, AUROC, cosine similarities) is correlational and does not even attempt either — let alone distinguish the two. Adopting this framing would require us to label every finding F-N as either "sufficient (denoising-confirmed)", "necessary (noising-confirmed)", or "correlational only (probe)". Currently *all* of F-1…F-10 are in the third bucket.

- **"A circuit is the *difference* the patch traces, not an absolute property of the model."** §2.6 — every patching result is conditional on (clean prompt, corrupt prompt) pair. Reframes our F-N findings as "MATH-500-difficulty differences traced by L19 DoM" rather than "the correctness signal lives at L19." This is a *softer* but more defensible framing.

- **Pareto frontier of circuit size vs. performance recovered.** Encourages reporting "we recover X% of correctness with Y% of components" rather than chasing 100%. Useful framing for any future minimal-circuit claim about the prefill signal.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **TransformerLens** (referenced throughout) is the canonical library for hook-based patching; all of ACDC, AtP*, and the Heimersheim/Nanda examples assume it. P11 H100 currently uses raw HuggingFace + custom hook code; switching to TransformerLens would unlock a large existing patching codebase but requires confirming Qwen-2.5-1.5B is supported (TransformerLens has spotty Qwen coverage as of mid-2024).
- **Mean-zero residual stream / mean-zero logits** (default in TransformerLens) — important when using raw-logit metrics; otherwise components that uniformly inflate logits look like real contributors.
- **ARENA chapter 1.3** — practical exercises for activation patching; useful onboarding before any project member runs the first patching sweep.
- **Logit difference > probability > accuracy** for exploratory patching; reverse for confirmatory patching.
- Code link: paper does not publish code; ACDC (Conmy et al. 2304.14997) and TransformerLens are the implementation references.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Denoising sweep on cached prefill activations**: we have prefill L19 activations cached for all 500 MATH-500 problems on Qwen-2.5-1.5B (`pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`). We can simulate denoising offline by replacing the L19 prefill activation of an *incorrectly-answered* problem with the L19 prefill activation of a *correctly-answered* problem and re-running *only the final-token decoding* through the model — this is a cheap H100-hour test of whether the L19 prefill activations are *sufficient* to flip an incorrect prediction to correct. Script needed: `pathway11_h100/patching_sweep.py`.
- **Logit-difference probe re-fit**: re-train F-2's L19 probe with target = logit(answer-token) − logit(top-incorrect-token) instead of binary correct/incorrect. Pure CPU, ~30min on cached activations. Tells us whether the AUROC-0.7731 binary signal is hiding a stronger continuous signal.
- **Direct logit attribution at L19**: project the prefill L19 residual stream onto the unembedding direction of correct/incorrect answer tokens and report per-problem contributions. Pure CPU, 1h. Validates whether L19 acts on the correctness logit *directly* or through later layers.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2304.14997 (ACDC, Conmy et al.)** — already in graph (status: graphed). Direct sister paper — automated circuit discovery using activation patching. Together with this paper forms the practitioner stack for H-13.
- **2211.00593 (IOI, Wang et al.)** — already in graph (status: graphed). Canonical example throughout this paper; foundational for any head-level analysis.
- **2202.05262 (ROME / Causal Tracing, Meng et al.)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. The original "find where a fact lives" experiment via Gaussian-noise patching; this paper is partly a reaction to ROME's sometimes-misinterpreted methodology. Relevant to F-2 (locating where correctness lives) by direct analogy.
- **2309.08600 (Sparse Autoencoders, Cunningham et al.)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. The §2.2 reference for "patching at SAE-feature granularity"; if H-13 ever moves to head/feature-level attribution, SAEs are the natural granularity above neurons.
- **2307.15771 (Hydra effect, McGrath et al.)** — NOT in graph; worth checking for admission. Direct relevance to F-9 redundancy refutation (Refutation 3) — the canonical reference for OR-gate / backup behaviour that would invalidate F-9's "redundant = same mechanism" inference.
- **2310.17191 (Feng & Steinhardt entity binding)** — NOT in graph; lower priority — entity-binding is somewhat orthogonal to MATH-500 reasoning.

## 2405.10928 — The Local Interaction Basis: Identifying Computationally-Relevant and Sparsely Interacting Features in Neural Networks (Bushnaq, Heimersheim, Goldowsky-Dill, Braun, Mendel, Hänni, Griffin, Stöhler, Wache, Hobbhahn — Apollo Research, 2024)

**Relevance:** Introduces a Jacobian-SVD-aligned, importance-rescaled rotation (Cˡ = Λˡ^(1/2) Vˡ (Dˡ^(1/2))⁺ Uˡ Hˡ) of residual-stream activations as an alternative to PCA for mechanistic interpretation. Key result: LIB succeeds on modular addition / CIFAR-10 but **fails on language models** (GPT2-small, TinyStories-1M) — the authors attribute this to superposition (LMs have more features than dimensions, violating LIB's non-overcomplete-basis assumption). The negative result is the relevant signal for us: it implies our F-2/F-3/F-9 single-direction / orthogonality / redundancy framings rest on linear-basis assumptions that may not hold for Qwen-2.5.

**Key claim we tested:** Linear-basis decompositions (PCA, single-direction probes, raw cosines) are computationally uninformative on LM residual streams; SAE-style overcomplete bases are needed.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** (HIGH priority — H-183, H-184, H-185). We have not yet run any SAE or Jacobian-importance analysis on the cached pathway11_h100 L19 residuals. The paper's diagnosis predicts our F-2 AUROC=0.7731 survives as a *predictive* number while the *mechanistic* claim of a "single L19 direction" gets reframed as a linear summary of a sparse population. Until H-183 runs, F-2/F-3 narrative-level claims should carry a "linear-basis interpretation" caveat.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE226, P11-FE227, P10-FE14, H-183, H-184, H-185.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Local Interaction Basis (LIB)** — two-step rotation Cˡ = Λˡ^(1/2) Vˡ (Dˡ^(1/2))⁺ Uˡ Hˡ: PCA-center, drop near-zero variance directions (threshold <10⁻¹⁵ via pseudoinverse), then rotate into right-singular vectors of the layer-to-layer Jacobian Gram matrix, scaled by Λ^(1/2).
  *Replication cost*: ~6h CPU (or 1h H100) per layer-pair on cached residuals using stochastic-sources approximation; full pipeline + Leiden modularity clustering ~1 day.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — narrow scope (only L18→L19, only on prefill activations) to test refutations 1 and 3 above.

- **Stochastic-sources approximation for transformer Jacobians** — replaces O(d⁴) full Jacobian with a randomized sketch tractable for transformer hidden-state widths.
  *Replication cost*: low (algorithm fully specified in paper appendix).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes if we ever pursue Jacobian-based attribution; otherwise no.

- **Jacobian Gram matrix Mⱼⱼ'^l = (1/|𝒟|) Σₓ Σᵢ J_ij^l(x) J_ij'^l(x)** — quantifies which input directions matter for the next layer's outputs in expectation over data.
  *Replication cost*: ~30min CPU on 500 sequences from cached residuals.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a simple "which L19 directions actually drive L20" report, directly testable against where prefill DoM lives.

- **Leiden modularity clustering on the interaction graph** (γ=1 default) — bins LIB features into computational modules.
  *Replication cost*: trivial CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: probably no unless we already built the LIB graph.

- **Edge-ablation interpretability proxy** (loss tolerance: 0.1 cross-entropy / 0.1pp accuracy) — measures fraction of pairwise feature interactions ablatable below tolerance; reported as 80–95% for LIB on LMs.
  *Replication cost*: O(d²) ablations per layer; expensive (1 H100-day for L19 alone).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: only if we want a direct head-to-head against the paper.

### Approaches & framings

- **Superposition as the explanation for "feature directions are not single directions."** Reframes our F-2 / F-3 narrative from "one direction predicts correctness" to "one *projection over a sparse code* predicts correctness." This is a non-trivial framing shift because it would change how we describe the result in any writeup — the AUROC stays, the mechanistic claim weakens.
- **Jacobian-SVD as the canonical importance metric.** Replaces variance-based (PCA) with computation-based (Λ from Mˡ). Useful framing for asking which subspaces of L19 actually matter for next-layer compute, distinct from which directions vary most.
- **Linear-basis MI as a preconditioning step for SAEs, not a substitute.** The paper's negative-result framing ("non-overcomplete assumption is wrong") is itself a strong narrative move worth importing into PERSPECTIVES.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **OpenWebText** — 50,000 sequences for PCA, 500 for Jacobian estimation. Standard, HF-accessible. Applicable? no — different domain (web text vs MATH-500); we'd use our own cached MATH-500 residuals instead.
- **TinyStories-1M, GPT2-small** — model-side, not dataset; mentioned for context of where LIB was tried.
- **Modular addition / CIFAR-10** — toy domains where LIB succeeds. Not applicable to our pipeline.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Cˡ = Λˡ^(1/2) Vˡ (Dˡ^(1/2))⁺ Uˡ Hˡ — the transform composes as PCA-center → PCA-rotate → drop-low-variance → Jacobian-SVD-rotate → importance-rescale.
- Pseudoinverse threshold < 10⁻¹⁵ for dropping near-zero directions; in practice this drops ~half of dimensions on residuals of width 768.
- Loss-tolerance for edge ablation: 0.1 nats cross-entropy increase (LM) / 0.1 pp accuracy (CIFAR-10) / 99.9% accuracy floor (modular addition).
- Leiden resolution γ=1 default (γ=0.5 reported as cherry-picked example, signals authors' own caveat).
- They explicitly report 80–95% of LIB interactions on LMs are ablatable with no interpretability gain — this is the diagnostic to copy if we want to assess any candidate basis.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Single-pair Jacobian Gram on cached L18→L19 residuals.** Use `pathway11_h100/...l19_prefill.npz` + the corresponding L18 prefill cache (regenerable via DATA_MANIFEST). Stochastic-sources sketch → V, Λ for L18→L19. Project the existing prefill_DoM unit vector into the V basis and report (a) which Λ-rank bin it falls in, (b) what fraction of |DoM|² lives above the median-Λ cutoff. This is a ~6h CPU sanity check that directly tests refutation 3.
- **PCA-rank of prefill_DoM in raw L19 residuals.** Already cheap given cached residuals: SVD of L19 prefill matrix, project DoM, report rank of |dot products|. This is a weaker version of the Jacobian test that costs ~10min CPU and answers "is DoM a high-variance direction or a low-variance computational one?"

### Cross-paper signals

- 2402.03744 (INSIDE / EigenScore) — already in graph (status: graphed/CITED ONLY). Both papers operate on covariance-style decompositions of hidden states; LIB extends with Jacobian rescaling.
- 2509.11569 (D²HScore) — already in graph (PARTIALLY CONFIRMED). Spectral-on-residual-stream framing overlaps; LIB would predict D²HScore lives partly on superposed features.
- 2509.15735 (EigenTrack) — already in graph (CITED ONLY). Spectral-trajectory framing; LIB's Λ-importance is an orthogonal claim about which spectral components matter computationally.
- *Cunningham et al. "Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features"* (2309.08600) — NOT in graph; the LIB paper itself recommends SAEs as the alternative when LIB fails. Recommend admission as the natural follow-up that solves what LIB couldn't.
- *Bricken et al. "Towards Monosemanticity"* (Anthropic, 2023, no arxiv canonical) — NOT in graph; same SAE-on-LM thread.

## 2405.12250 — Your Transformer is Secretly Linear (Razzhigaev, Mikhalchuk, Goncharova, Gerasimenko, Oseledets, Dimitrov, Kuznetsov; AIRI/Skoltech/SberAI/HSE/MSU, 2024)

**Relevance:** Direct mechanistic context for F-1 (dimensional breathing universality), F-2 (L19 prefill DoM AUROC = 0.7731), F-9 (CoE-60 redundancy with single-layer DoM), and F-10 (PH at Gaussian null). The paper claims transformer-decoder layer-to-layer embedding maps have generalized-Procrustes similarity ≈ 0.99 across GPT, LLaMA, OPT, BLOOM and Mistral, with consistently low block-output norms relative to residual-stream norm. Two implications collide with our finding stack: (i) if true, F-2's L19 peak should be a plateau across the linear middle layers — testable via per-layer AUROC sweep; (ii) F-1's breathing signal may be dominated by slow residual-stream drift rather than active per-layer reorganization — testable by residual-removal control. The paper's "feature triggering regime" (Figure 9 long-tailed L2 error distribution) is also a candidate mechanism for F-7's D-bucket fragility.

**Key claim we tested:** Decoder-only transformers have near-perfectly linear inter-layer embedding maps (Procrustes 0.99) and consistently low per-block output norms; therefore middle layers are largely interchangeable / prunable, and the actual non-linear "computation" lives in a sparse minority of triggering tokens.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — the paper triggers five concrete cheap experiments (P11-FE228, P11-FE229, P11-FE230, P11-FE231, P11-FE232). The Procrustes/linearity protocol is directly applicable to our cached P11 NPZs and the paper offers a clean mechanism for H-17 (RoPE-mechanical DoM rotation) and F-9 (CoE redundancy via near-affine inter-layer maps). Until the per-layer AUROC sweep and residual-removed breathing curve are run, we cannot say whether F-1 and F-2 are genuine non-linear features or measurement artifacts of the residual-stream slow drift the paper describes.

### Methodologies extracted

- Generalized Procrustes linearity score: `linearity_score(X,Y) = 1 − min_A ||X̃A − Ỹ||²` over all linear A on Frobenius-normalized embeddings; bounded [0,1], scale-invariant.
- Block output norm vs residual-stream norm tracking (Figure 3) as a diagnostic for whether observed inter-layer "linearity" is genuine or just residual-dominance.
- Per-token L2-error distribution after linear approximation (Figure 9) to identify rare non-linearity-spike tokens.
- Sequential-linearity-ranked depth pruning + linear-replacement + layerwise MSE distillation (depth-pruning recipe).
- Inter-layer cosine / MSE regularization at pretraining (loss terms `L_cos` and `L_MSE` with coefficient λ).

### Approaches & framings

- "Residual stream dominates; blocks barely contribute" — reframes deep transformers as a single near-linear track plus sparse non-linearity events.
- "Feature triggering regime" — rare specific tokens carry the model's actual non-linearity load; candidate mechanism for F-7 D-bucket fragility.
- Pretraining decreases linearity, fine-tuning increases linearity (Table 1) — directional prediction for H-10.
- Procrustes generalized to all linear maps (not just orthogonal) as a similarity score — methodologically clean, useful for cross-model alignment work in H-20.

### Datasets

- TinyStories, Tiny-textbooks, SuperGLUE (MultiRC, BoolQ, CB, COPA, RTE, WiC, ReCoRD, XStoryCloze), Anthropic-Helpful (RM), WikiText, ARC-easy. None directly applicable to MATH-500 / 1024-tok regime; ARC-easy marginally close.

### Implementation details

- Reference impl: https://github.com/AIRI-Institute/LLM-Microscope
- Models tested: GPT2 (small/large/XL), OPT-125M/1.3B/2.7B, LLaMA2-7B, BLOOM, Mistral 150M/650M (their own pretraining).
- Cosine regularization sweet spot: λ=0.5; MSE λ=2.0 destabilized training.
- Reward-model fine-tuning showed more seed-stable linearity-increase than NLI fine-tuning (Table 1).

### Replicable intermediates

- Per-layer linearity_score sweep on Qwen-2.5-1.5B P11 NPZs (~30 min CPU).
- Residual-removed breathing curve (~1 h CPU; folds into P11-FE16).
- D-bucket vs A-bucket linear-approximation residual comparison (~30 min CPU).
- Cross-layer DoM-orthogonality robustness check (~20 min CPU).
- RoPE-vs-fitted-A correspondence test (~1 h CPU).

### Cross-paper signals

- 2303.08112 (Tuned Lens) — already pending_triage; CORROBORATED_BY relationship (per-layer linear decoders work *because* of the paper's linearity claim).
- 2012.13255 (Aghajanyan) — already pending_triage (was rejected); cited foundationally; reconsider admission.

- 2401.15024 (SliceGPT) — NOT in graph; admit if we ever do pruning experiments.
- 2106.09685 (LoRA) — likely already in graph; foundational citation.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE228, P11-FE229, P11-FE230, P11-FE231, P11-FE232; H-186, H-187, H-188, H-189. Folds into P11-FE16 (MP correction).

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Generalized Procrustes linearity score** — `linearity_score(X,Y) = 1 − min_A ||X̃A − Ỹ||²` over all linear A (not just orthogonal), with `X̃ = X/||X||_F`. Bounded in [0,1], scale-invariant.
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU on cached P11 NPZs (lstsq per layer pair).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly probes whether F-2's L19-uniqueness is a non-linearity peak, and gives layer-pair scores we can correlate with bucket membership for F-7.

- **Block output norm tracking** — measure `||block_i(x)|| / ||residual_i||` per layer per token (paper's Figure 3).
  *Replication cost*: minutes on cached P11 NPZs (we already have residual streams, just need to subtract).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — required as the residual-removal control for refutation #2 and a free F-1 sanity check.

- **L2-error-by-token distribution after linear approximation** — fit best A per layer-pair, compute per-token L2 residual `||x_i A − y_i||`, look at the histogram tail (paper's Figure 9).
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — the test for refutation #3, and operationalizes the paper's "feature triggering regime" against our D-bucket.

- **Sequential-linearity-ranked depth pruning** — rank layers by linearity_score, drop top-K most-linear in order, measure perplexity / downstream metric.
  *Replication cost*: 1-2h CPU per pruning level on Qwen-2.5-1.5B with cached MATH-500 eval; mostly inference time.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes (with caveats) — gives a direct test of whether F-2's signal survives layer pruning, but at the cost of running fresh generation.

- **Linear-replacement + layerwise MSE distillation** — replace pruned layer with learned linear A, train on TinyStories with MSE on layerwise embeddings as auxiliary loss.
  *Replication cost*: H100 days; needs new training run.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — not aligned with the project's read-only-extraction methodology and the cost is high relative to information yield.

- **Cosine / MSE inter-layer regularization at pretraining** — `L_cos = λ(1 − cos(emb_i, emb_{i−1}))` as auxiliary loss during pretraining.
  *Replication cost*: H100 weeks (full pretraining run).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — out of scope, we don't pretrain.

- **Linear probing across all layers** — train a linear classifier on each layer's embedding vs. label and read off per-layer accuracy curve (paper Figure 5).
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — already partially what F-2's per-layer AUROC sweep does; paper formalizes the protocol and gives a comparison point.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Residual stream dominates; blocks barely contribute"** — reframes the standard "deep transformer = many layers of computation" picture into "deep transformer = single near-linear track with sparse high-non-linearity spikes." Intersects F-1 (we may be measuring the residual stream's slow drift, not breathing-as-computation), F-9 (explains why single-layer = trajectory-features), and F-10 (Gaussian null on PH falls out naturally).
- **"Feature triggering regime"** — the paper's hypothesis that *rare* token positions carry the model's actual non-linearity load. This is a near-perfect mechanistic candidate for F-7 (D-bucket = pathological-but-causally-load-bearing problems) and for F-2's prefill-token specialness (the prefill last token is one such trigger).
- **"Pretraining decreases linearity, fine-tuning increases linearity"** (Figure 2 + Table 1) — predicts that base→instruct conversion *flattens* dimensional breathing. Directly applicable to H-10.
- **"Procrustes generalized to all linear maps as a similarity score"** — a methodologically clean way to compare residual-stream geometries that is bounded, scale-invariant, and weaker than orthogonal-Procrustes; useful for cross-model alignment work in H-20.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **TinyStories** — small (~2GB), open, HF accessible. Applicable? no — toy stories, not math reasoning; only useful if we ever train a small model.
- **Tiny-textbooks** — small synthetic, HF. Applicable? no — same reason.
- **SuperGLUE** (MultiRC, BoolQ, CB, COPA, RTE, WiC, ReCoRD, XStoryCloze) — moderate, HF. Applicable? no — classification benchmarks, not reasoning; out of MATH-500 regime.
- **Anthropic-Helpful (HH-RLHF reward modeling)** — open, HF. Applicable? no — RLHF data.
- **WikiText** — open, HF. Applicable? no — perplexity benchmark only used for pruning eval.
- **ARC-easy** — open, HF. Applicable? marginal — closer to MATH-500 in being multiple-choice reasoning; could replicate paper's pruning eval cheaply but is below MATH-500 difficulty.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Code: https://github.com/AIRI-Institute/LLM-Microscope (paper's reference impl).
- Models tested: GPT2 (small/large/XL), OPT (125M/1.3B/2.7B), LLaMA2-7B, BLOOM, Mistral 150M/650M (their own pretraining).
- Linearity-score normalization: Frobenius `||·||_F` on centered embedding matrices `X, Y ∈ R^{n×d}`, then lstsq on the normalized pair.
- "Linearity profile" is layer-index (normalized to [0,1]) on x-axis vs linearity score on y-axis — middle layers are most linear in their plots.
- Block-output norm vs residual-stream norm ratio (Figure 3) is the diagnostic for whether observed inter-layer "linearity" is genuine layer linearity or just residual-stream slow-drift dominance — important confound to control for when comparing to F-1.
- Cosine regularization coefficient: λ=0.5 worked best for both 150M and 650M Mistral; λ=2.0 (MSE) destabilized.
- Reward-model fine-tuning showed the same linearity-increase trend more *stably* across seeds than NLI fine-tuning (Table 1).
- L2-error long tails: Figure 9 (OPT-1.3B) shows a small fraction of layers / tokens with much larger linear-approximation errors — the "spike" tokens that carry non-linearity.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Per-layer linearity_score on Qwen-2.5-1.5B P11 NPZs** — pathway11_h100 cached prefill + final-token residual streams across 28 layers, run lstsq per consecutive layer pair, expect linearity_score curve. Script: trivial NumPy `lstsq` over `pathway11_h100/data/*.npz`. (~20min)
- **Block-contribution norm ratio** — same NPZs, compute `||emb[L+1] − emb[L]||_F / ||emb[L]||_F` per layer; expect very small ratio per the paper, gives us a diagnostic for whether F-1 breathing is dominated by residual or block updates. (~minutes)
- **Per-layer prefill DoM AUROC sweep** — refits the L19 probe at every layer using the existing 5-fold OOF protocol from `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json`, plots per-layer AUROC. The plateau-vs-peak shape is the direct test of refutation #1. (~30min CPU)
- **Linearity-ranked layer pruning on Qwen-2.5-1.5B** — drop top-1, top-2, top-3 most-linear layers (no retraining), re-run K=1 MATH-500 eval; check whether the 48.6% accuracy and the L19 DoM signal survive. (~2h H100 if pod is up)
- **D-bucket vs A-bucket linear-approximation residual** — fit A per layer pair, score per-problem L2 residual at L18→L19 and L19→L20, compare 36-problem D-bucket distribution to 207-problem A-bucket using Mann-Whitney U. Refutation #3 test. (~30min CPU)

## 2405.15302 — Understanding the Language Model to Solve the Symbolic Multi-Step Reasoning Problem from the Perspective of Buffer Mechanism (Wang, Wang, Zhang, Zhou, Jin, Hu, Sun, Li, Zhang, Xu, 2024)

**Relevance:** Proposes a mechanistic *buffer mechanism* in transformers, where
each token's residual stream stores multiple intermediate results in
near-orthogonal subspaces defined by the value-output projection matrices `W_vo^(l)`,
and information is retrieved by `W_qk^(l)` ≈ `W_vo^(l-1)` ("same-token matching").
Distinguishes Vertical Thinking Strategy (VTS, single-pass multi-step) from
Horizontal Thinking Strategy (HTS = CoT, buffer reuse via emitted tokens). Two
probes (Matching Score, Kernel Score) are computable on real LLMs from weights
alone — directly applicable to Qwen-2.5-1.5B and our F-2 / F-3 / F-9 numerical
anchors. Paper provides a structural, label-free alternative to our AUROC sweep
for picking L19, and a mechanistic re-reading of F-3's cos = 0.046 prefill/final
orthogonality.

**Key claim we tested:** Multi-step reasoning in transformers proceeds by
storing distinct intermediate results in distinct W_vo "buffers" that are
addressable via Ker^(l) ≈ I; CoT works by reusing buffers across emitted tokens
rather than allocating new ones.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** The buffer mechanism makes specific structural
predictions about Qwen-2.5-1.5B head weights (KS peaks at the F-2 layer; W_vo's
are pairwise near-orthogonal; prefill_DoM and final_DoM align with different
W_vo subspaces) that we can falsify with cached weights and existing NPZs. If
confirmed, F-3's interpretation flips from "two independent probes" to "two
buffer reads of one circuit" and gives F-2 a label-free anchor. If refuted on
Qwen-1.5B, the buffer framing does not lift past 3-layer toy models.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE233, P11-FE234, P11-FE235, P11-FE236, P11-FE237,
H-190, H-191, H-192, H-193; cross-references P11-FE3 (causal patching).

**Status:** TO TEST (HIGH priority for P11-FE233, P11-FE234; MEDIUM for the rest).

### Methodologies extracted

- **Matching Score (MS)** — `MS(h^(l)) = E_X[Trace(σ(h^(l)(X)))]/n`. Layer-level
  measure of "same-token matching" — how strongly each token's query attends to
  itself after multi-step buffer extraction. Computable from a single forward pass
  on cached prompts.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached Qwen-1.5B Stage 2 prompts.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — provides a label-free layer-selection
  criterion for F-2 / H-13.

- **Kernel Score (KS)** — `KS(Ker^(l)) = Trace(σ(Ker^(l)))/d_m` where
  `Ker^(l) = W_vo^(l−1) W_qk^(l) W_vo^(0),T`. Diagnoses layers structurally, from
  weights only — *no activations needed*.
  *Replication cost*: 5min CPU per layer per model (weights only).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — cheapest layer-selection diagnostic on offer.
  Could give F-2 a structural rationale for L19 (or refute it).

- **Multi-head MS / KS extension (App G)** — recipe for computing MS/KS on
  multi-head Transformers (GPT-2, Phi-3, Llama, Qwen). Includes per-head extraction
  and aggregation.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on Qwen-1.5B (28 layers × 12 heads).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — direct map onto our model.

- **Buffer cosine diagnostic** — pairwise `cos(W_vo^(l), W_vo^(l'))` and
  `cos(W_vo^(l), I)` to test buffer orthogonality.
  *Replication cost*: <10min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — gives F-3 a mechanistic falsifier.

- **RMBA (Random Matrix-Based Algorithm)** — replace `W_qk^(l) → W_qk^(l) + α^(l) Z^(l−1)`
  and `W_vo^(l) → W_vo^(l) + β^(l) Z^(l)` with `Z^(l) ~ N(0, 1/d_m)` fixed and
  `{α^(l), β^(l)}` learnable. 132 total trainable parameters for 12-layer GPT-2.
  Improves multi-step reasoning data-efficiency by >65% on PrOntoQA, LogicAsker,
  PararulePlus and lifts Clutrr/RuleTaker/StepGame/LogicInference final accuracy.
  *Replication cost*: 1 day H100 to RMBA-finetune Qwen-1.5B + re-evaluate MATH-500.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **maybe** — interesting as a parameter-efficient
  intervention to test against H-1 steering and H-19 verification, but not yet
  obviously a *correctness-prediction* method.

- **Same-token matching ablation** — set `Ker^(l) = I` artificially and check
  whether OOD generalisation is preserved (the paper's setting: tokenOOD ∉ training).
  *Replication cost*: 4h H100 (model surgery + re-evaluation).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — OOD test set construction would need a fresh
  symbolic dataset we don't have.

- **Causal intervention to identify reasoning circuits (App H)** — they cite Feng
  & Steinhardt (2310.17191), Meng et al. (ROME, 2022), Vig et al. (2020). Standard
  patching machinery applied to the symbolic dataset.
  *Replication cost*: covered by P11-FE3 (already in queue).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **already planned** — see P11-FE3.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Buffer" as the noun for residual-stream subspace.** Reframes the residual
  stream as a structured composition of orthogonal subspaces, each addressable by
  a different `W_vo` matrix. Intersects F-3 directly: prefill / final-token
  orthogonality stops being "two unrelated probes" and becomes "two complementary
  buffers in one reasoning circuit".
- **VTS vs HTS as a buffer-allocation distinction.** VTS = allocate fresh buffer
  per step (expensive in parameters); HTS (= CoT) = reuse buffers via emitted
  tokens. Cleanly explains why CoT helps reasoning more than depth does. Intersects
  H-19 (verification-pass = HTS step) and H-22 (Abstract-CoT compresses
  buffer-allocation cost).
- **Same-token matching as the core of multi-step transfer.** Argues that the
  *only* nontrivial requirement on weights is `Ker^(l) ≈ I`. This is a *structural*
  property of trained weights, not of activations — gives F-2 a label-free layer
  test.
- **Induction heads as "1-step reasoning"; multi-step ≠ stacking 1-step.** They
  show RMBA improves *multi-step*, but IMBA (the analogous identity-matrix trick
  from Boix-Adsera 2023) improves only single-step. Cautions us against
  generalising single-step probe results to multi-step regimes.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **Symbolic 2-step reasoning (paper-internal)** — synthetic, `m=5`, `G={0,1,4}`,
  vocabulary 201, sequence length 13. License: not separately released; experiment
  pipeline in paper Appendix B. **Applicable? no** — not generative-math; pure
  symbolic chains.
- **Clutrr (Sinha et al., 2019, 1908.06177)** — kinship reasoning, 34.3 → 42.8%
  with RMBA. Public, MIT-style license. **Applicable? no** — text-based kinship,
  not math.
- **RuleTaker (Clark et al., 2020, 2002.05867)** — natural-language rule
  application, 67.0 → 83.5% RMBA. Public. **Applicable? no** — categorical answers.
- **StepGame (Shi et al., 2022)** — robust multi-hop spatial reasoning. Public.
  **Applicable? no** — spatial domain.
- **LogicInference (Ontanon et al., 2022, 2203.15099)** — 68.1 → 78.3% RMBA.
  Public. **Applicable? no** — propositional logic.
- **LogicAsker (Wan et al., 2024, 2401.00757)** — 99.7 → 100% (epoch reduction
  test). Public. **Applicable? no** — capability evaluation.
- **PararulePlus (Bao et al., 2022, 2207.14000)** — multi-step deductive
  reasoning. Public. **Applicable? no** — natural-language deduction.
- **PrOntoQA (Saparov & He, 2022, 2210.01240)** — formal logical inference. Public.
  **Applicable? no** — propositional, not math.

(The whole reasoning-benchmark suite is symbolic / propositional. None map to
MATH-500's open-ended numerical-symbolic answer space.)

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **3-layer single-head Transformer for the symbolic task** — `d=201`, `d_m=400`,
  `d_q=d_k=d_v=64`, batch 100, AdamW, lr 2e-5 → 1e-4 (warmup 400 epochs) → 1e-5
  (decay 3600 epochs). 200,000 sequences. AMD EPYC 7742 server, 256GB RAM.
- **GPT-2 12-layer for real datasets** — 5 epochs, lr 1e-5, RMBA hyperparameters
  initialised at 0.05.
- **RMBA per-head extension (§6)** — `W_qk^(l,h) → W_qk^(l,h) + α^(l,h) Z^(l−1,h)`,
  `W_vo^(l,h) → W_vo^(l,h) + β^(l,h) Z^(l,h)`. Each head gets its own Z fixed at
  init. Trainable parameter count per layer = 2 × n_heads (so 132 = 12 layers ×
  11 heads × something — paper's exact accounting is in App E; 132 is reported in
  the abstract).
- **Sign condition** — they observe `α^(l) · β^(l) ≥ 0` enhances reasoning;
  `< 0` does not. Useful constraint for reproductions.
- **Buffer cosine validation (App D)** — they explicitly compute pairwise cosines
  between `W_vo^(0), W_vo^(1), W_vo^(2)` and `I` for the 3-layer trained model.
  This is the cleanest empirical anchor for the buffer-orthogonality claim.
- Code: not visibly linked in the body; standard practice is supplementary GitHub
  but unverified here.

### Replicable intermediates

- **KS per layer for Qwen-1.5B from cached weights** —
  `pathway11_h100/checkpoints/Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Instruct/` should already contain
  the head matrices. Compute `Ker^(l) = W_vo^(l−1) W_qk^(l) W_vo^(0),T` and
  `Trace(σ(Ker^(l)))/d_m` for `l=1..28`. ~30min CPU. Direct test of whether L19
  is structurally "the right layer" or whether the paper points to a better one.
  Cached artifact: model weights only (no NPZ needed).
- **Pairwise W_vo cosine for Qwen-1.5B** — `cos(W_vo^(l), W_vo^(l'))` for all
  layer pairs and `cos(W_vo^(l), I_d_m)`. <10min CPU. If F-3's prefill (L19) and
  final (also L19) sit in orthogonal `W_vo` heads of the same layer, that
  reproduces the paper's prediction; if not, F-3 is interpretation-incompatible.
- **MS at L19 on cached MATH-500 prompts** — using cached prefill activations from
  P11 Stage 2, compute the matching matrix `h^(l)(X)` and its trace-softmax. ~1h CPU
  on existing NPZ cache. Yields a label-free L19 quality metric.
- **VTS-vs-HTS partition of MATH-500 K=1 generations by length** — split the 500
  generations into <100-token (≈VTS-only), 100-500 (mixed), >500-token (≈HTS).
  Re-compute prefill DoM AUROC and CoE-60 vs single-layer DoM redundancy
  separately per partition. Tests F-9 against the paper's VTS/HTS prediction. ~2h
  CPU on cached Stage 2.

## 2405.15471 — Emergence of a High-Dimensional Abstraction Phase in Language Transformers (Cheng et al., ICLR 2025)

**Relevance:** Direct depth-axis analog of F-1's time-axis dimensional breathing claim. Across 5 pretrained transformer LMs (OPT-6.7B, Llama3-8B, Pythia-6.9B, OLMo-7B, Mistral-7B) and 3 corpora, the paper demonstrates a robust mid-network ID-peak that (a) coincides with abstract syntactic/semantic processing and downstream-task transfer onset, (b) vanishes on shuffled corpora and untrained models (Cheng's null), (c) shows cross-model neighborhood-equivalence at peak-peak layer intersections via Information-Imbalance Δ, and (d) onset-depth correlates with model surprisal (Spearman ρ = 0.65). The methodological toolkit (GRIDE estimator, Δ measure, shuffled-corpus null, Conneau probing battery) is directly applicable to our hidden-state pipeline. The paper's framing also generates testable refutations of F-2 (L19 DoM may be an abstract-syntax probe) and F-10 (ID is non-null where PH was null), and provides a precedent for the per-problem ID predictor of correctness in H-195.

**Key claim we tested:** "Across pretrained transformer LMs, mid-network layers show a peak in intrinsic dimension that marks the first locus of abstract linguistic processing, and onset-depth of this peak correlates with model quality."

**Our result:** **CITED ONLY (TO TEST under P11-FE238, P11-FE239, P11-FE240, P11-FE241, P11-FE242; H-194, H-195, H-196, H-197).** Existing graph edge `(F-1)-[CORROBORATED_BY]->(2405.15471)` captures the depth-vs-time axis distinction at a coarse level; the planned experiments will test whether the L19 DoM intersects Cheng's ID-peak structure on Qwen-2.5-1.5B and whether GRIDE on our cached NPZs gives a label-free correctness predictor competitive with our supervised DoM.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE238, P11-FE239, P11-FE240, P11-FE241, P11-FE242; H-194, H-195, H-196, H-197; cross-references EXP-026 (PH-at-null) and EXP-032 (Qwen-1.5B PR breathing).

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **GRIDE intrinsic dimension** (Denti et al., 2022) — scale-aware extension of TwoNN.
- **Information-Imbalance Δ** (Glielmo et al., 2022) — asymmetric rank-based neighborhood-information measure.
- **Last-token-per-sequence representation** as canonical observable (matches our prefill convention).
- **Shuffled-corpus null** preserving unigram frequencies, destroying syntax/semantics.
- **Pythia training-checkpoint trajectory analysis** for ID emergence over training.
- **Conneau (2018) probing battery** (Bigram Shift, Coordination Inversion, Odd Man Out, Sentence Length, Word Content).
- **Cross-model Δ matrix** of layer-by-layer information containment.

### Approaches & framings

- **Three-region depth split** (pre-peak surface / peak abstract / post-peak refinement).
- **ID-as-quality-proxy** via surprisal correlation across (model, corpus) pairs.
- **Cross-model alignment is layer-localized** — Platonic-style convergence is conditioned on the high-ID phase, not uniform across depth.

### Datasets used

- Bookcorpus, Pile (10k-doc subsample), Wikitext-103 — 50k 20-token sequences each.
- Conneau (2018) probing tasks via SentEval.
- IMDb sentiment (Maas 2011), Toxic Comment (Adams 2017) for downstream transfer.

### Implementation details

- 5 LMs: OPT-6.7B, Llama3-8B, Pythia-6.9B, OLMo-7B, Mistral-7B; all 32 layers, hidden_dim 4096 (Qwen-2.5-1.5B is *outside* this size range at 28 layers, hidden_dim 1536 — generalization to our base model not directly validated).
- 50k 20-token sequences/corpus; partitioned 5×10k for variance.
- 128-token replication on Pile/Pythia/OPT confirms 20-token results.
- Scale analysis on k for GRIDE (Appendix C); robustness verified.
- HuggingFace `hidden_states` = residual stream after each block (matches our P11 convention).
- Code: https://github.com/chengemily1/id-llm-abstraction.

### Replicable intermediates

- GRIDE on cached Qwen-1.5B prefill NPZs at every layer (P11-FE238).
- Per-problem GRIDE-ID as label-free correctness predictor (H-195).
- Δ between L19 and L0/L_final (P11-FE242).
- Shuffled-prefill null on MATH-500 (P11-FE241).

### Cross-paper signals

- 2509.26560 (already TO TEST, H-16) — same finite-sample-bias question for ID estimators.
- 2410.13640 (already PARTIALLY CONFIRMED) — CoE trajectory features overlap with Cheng's three-region split.
- 2506.06609 (already CITED ONLY) — Cheng's cross-model Δ is a stronger framing for cross-scale stitching.
- 2405.07987 (already TO TEST, H-20) — Cheng provides depth-localization evidence for Platonic-Representation alignment.
- 2312.01648 (Balestriero "Characterizing LLM Geometry") — NOT in graph; recommend admission if H-12 escalates.
- 2304.01373 (Pythia suite, Biderman) — NOT in graph; reference for any H-8 training-checkpoint follow-up.

### Methodologies extracted

- **GRIDE intrinsic dimension estimator (Denti et al., 2022).** Extends TwoNN by exposing scale (k) as a tunable parameter, allowing scale-plateau analysis. Replication cost: ~1h CPU on cached residual-stream NPZs per model, library exists. We'd plausibly run this: yes — corroborates / refutes F-10 framing and gives a per-problem scalar geometric feature complementary to PR.
- **Information Imbalance Δ (Glielmo et al., 2022).** Asymmetric rank-based measure of which neighborhood-information set contains another; robust to dim mismatch. Replication cost: ~30min CPU per layer-pair on cached NPZs. We'd plausibly run this: yes — Δ between Qwen 1.5B L19 and Qwen 7B L_k provides an alternative to the cosine-similarity framing in F-3 and the cross-scale stitching framing in 2506.06609.
- **Last-token representation per sequence as the canonical observable.** Cheng justifies this by causal-attention argument (last token is the only one with full sequence info, and the only one decoded). Aligns with our prefill-DoM choice. Replication cost: zero (already what we do). We'd plausibly run this: already do.
- **Shuffled-corpus null control.** Re-token the corpus, preserve unigram frequencies, destroy syntax/semantics; ID peak vanishes. Replication cost: 1h CPU + re-extract activations. We'd plausibly run this: yes — direct null analog of EXP-041 (random-token PR control), but for ID/breathing on math problems.
- **Training-checkpoint trajectory analysis.** Pythia public checkpoints used to show ID peak emergence over training. Replication cost: ~6h H100 to extract activations at 4–6 checkpoints + 1h CPU. We'd plausibly run this: yes if H-8 (DoM stability) is escalated.
- **Conneau (2018) probing battery on hidden states.** Bigram Shift (syntax), Coordination Inversion (event order), Odd Man Out (semantic), Sentence Length (surface), Word Content (surface). Trains lightweight MLP probes per layer. Replication cost: 4h CPU on cached activations. We'd plausibly run this: yes — directly tests Refutation 2 (is L19 DoM a syntax-abstraction probe?).
- **Cross-model Δ matrix.** N×N matrix of Δ(model_i_layer_a → model_j_layer_b) across architectures. Replication cost: 4h CPU on extracted activations from ≥3 models. We'd plausibly run this: yes for the H-20 (cross-model kernel alignment) experiment.
- **Surprisal vs ID correlation test.** Per (model, corpus) pair, regress surprisal on max-ID and on relative ID-peak onset. Replication cost: trivial once IDs are computed. We'd plausibly run this: yes — direct adapter for H-9.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Central high-dimensionality phase as the locus of linguistic abstraction."** Reframes intermediate layers from "incremental refinement" to "phase transition with three regions." Intersects F-9 (single-layer DoM works) and F-3 (prefill ⊥ final): the phase-transition view predicts both, since L19 sits in the peak and the post-peak region is functionally a different operator.
- **"ID as proxy for model quality."** Cheng's surprisal-vs-ID-onset correlation reframes ID from a descriptive geometry to a predictor of next-token-prediction performance. This is a testable claim in the topo-confidence frame: does *per-problem* ID at the peak layer predict *per-problem* correctness? If yes, ID-at-peak is a label-free correctness predictor that competes with our supervised L19 DoM.
- **"Cross-model representational alignment is conditioned on the high-ID phase."** Cheng's Δ matrices show alignment localized at peak-peak intersections, not at first-layer or last-layer alignments. Reframes the Platonic-Representation hypothesis (2405.07987, currently TO TEST under H-20) from "all models converge" to "all models converge *at the abstraction phase*."

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **Bookcorpus** — ~10k 20-token sequences sampled, HF accessible. Applicable? no — not math, not CoT.
- **The Pile (10k-document HF subsample)** — HF accessible. Contains code/math fragments. Applicable? partial — could be used as the unshuffled-language null for breathing-on-non-math tests (P11-FE1 already addresses BBH; this offers a different control).
- **Wikitext-103** — HF accessible. Applicable? no — generic text.
- **Conneau et al. 2018 probing tasks** (Bigram Shift, Coordination Inversion, Odd Man Out, Sentence Length, Word Content) — HF accessible via SentEval. Applicable? yes — Refutation 2 turns directly on these probes.
- **Toxic Comment Classification (Adams et al. 2017)** — public Kaggle dataset. Applicable? no.
- **IMDb sentiment (Maas et al. 2011)** — HF accessible. Applicable? no.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- All 5 LMs are 6.5B–8B parameters, 32 hidden layers, hidden_dim 4096 — Qwen-2.5-1.5B differs at 28 layers and 1536 hidden_dim; the scaling claim ("ID peak generalizes across model size") is supported in Appendix D for Pythia variants but not validated below 6.5B.
- 50k 20-token sequences per corpus, partitioned into 5 × 10k for variance estimation.
- Replicated with 128-token sequences for Pythia/OPT on Pile — confirms 20-token results not artifacts of context length.
- Sampling does not constrain the last token to be sentence-final.
- ID is computed *per partition* and averaged ± 2 SD.
- Scale-analysis: estimate ID as a function of k (neighborhood size), pick k at plateau (visual inspection in Appendix C).
- Code and a README to reproduce: https://github.com/chengemily1/id-llm-abstraction. License/checks not noted in main text.
- HuggingFace transformers `hidden_states` is the residual stream after each block (attn + MLP). Same convention as our P11 H100 extracts.
- They explicitly evaluated CKA, neighborhood-overlap, and RSA — only CKA gave coherent results comparable to Δ. RSA and neighborhood-overlap failed. This is a useful data point for our future cross-model alignment work (H-20).

### Replicable intermediates

- **GRIDE on Qwen-2.5-1.5B prefill activations across layers 0–28** using the cached `pathway11_h100/prefill/*.npz` 500-problem activations. 1h CPU. Tests whether L19 sits in or near the Cheng ID-peak window on math inputs.

- **Information-Imbalance Δ between L19 prefill activations and L0 (input-embedding) and L_final** on cached Qwen-2.5-1.5B activations. ~30min CPU. Tests whether the F-2 "prefill DoM" layer matches Cheng's "high Δ to first, low Δ to first-peak structure" signature.
- **Shuffled-corpus null on math:** randomize token order within MATH-500 prefills, re-extract L19 activations on H100 (~30min), compute PR and DoM-AUROC. If both collapse, Cheng's null framework cleanly extends F-1/F-2.

## 2405.17767 — Linguistic Collapse: Neural Collapse in (Large) Language Models (Wu & Papyan, NeurIPS 2024)

**Relevance:** Trains 230 GPT-Neo CLMs (3.4M–205M params) on TinyStories,
measures all four neural-collapse (NC) properties — within-class variability
collapse (NC1 / CDNV), generalized hyperspherical uniformity (GNC2),
classifier–class-mean alignment (NC3 / UNC3), and NCC classifier agreement
(NC4) — and reports their development with scale and weight regularization.
Their permutation test on 21 fixed-architecture seeds shows NC1, NC2
equiangularity, GNC2, NC3, and NC4 *all* correlate with generalization
*independent of scale* (p < 0.05). Directly relevant to F-1 (universal
collapse), F-4 (asymmetric collapse), F-3 (prefill⊥final orthogonality), and
F-10 (PH at Gaussian null) — provides published, canonical-implementation
metrics that may rebrand each as a special case of generic NC phenomena.
Their `neural-collapse` PyPI package is a drop-in measurement tool for our
cached pathway11_h100 NPZs.

**Key claim we tested:** Neural-collapse properties (NC1, GNC2, NC3, NC4)
develop with model scale in causal LMs and correlate with generalization
*independent of capacity* (permutation-test R² up to 0.49, p ≤ 0.0001).

**Our result:** **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED** for the *direction* of the
scale-correlated collapse (matches F-1 direction). The deeper claims — that
F-4, F-3, F-10 are independent reasoning-specific findings — are **not yet
tested** against their canonical NC metrics; H-198, H-199, H-200 are
explicitly designed to perform that test. After those run, this entry is
upgraded to **REPLICATED + EXTENDED** or downgraded to **CONTRADICTED** for
F-4/F-3 framing, depending on outcome.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE243, P11-FE244, P11-FE245, P11-FE246;
H-198, H-199, H-200, H-201

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **CDNV (class-distance normalized variance) with k=2 power augmentation** —
  ratio of within-class variance to mean-distance² between class-mean pairs,
  with extra `‖μ_c - μ_c'‖²` divisor to downweight well-separated pairs in
  imbalanced settings (eqn 4).
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU on cached pathway11_h100 NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct test of refutation #1 on F-4.

- **Hyperspherical uniformity via logarithmic inverse distance kernel** —
  -log‖a-b‖₂⁻¹ kernel on pairwise class-mean distances; quantifies GNC2 when
  C > d+1 prevents simplex ETF (eqn 7).
  *Replication cost*: ~1h CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct probe of whether residual streams
  have hidden hyperspherical structure invisible to raw PH (refutation #4).

- **Coefficient-of-variation (CoV) of pairwise interference** — eqn 6, ratio
  of std to mean for pairwise cosine similarities; their "equiangularity"
  measure.
  *Replication cost*: trivial on cached NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a direct number for "how
  ETF-like is our hidden state" without needing exact ETF.

- **NCC classifier agreement metric** — proportion of test samples where
  argmax linear classifier matches argmin distance-to-class-mean classifier
  (eqn 10).
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU once class means are computed.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a baseline for whether
  prefill DoM is "just an NCC classifier."

- **Permutation test (10⁴ trials) on fixed architecture, varied seeds** —
  §3.8: train ≥20 instances of the same architecture with different shuffling
  seeds, compute correlations between geometry metrics and validation loss,
  permute pairings to get null distribution.
  *Replication cost*: H100-week (would need ≥20 Qwen-1.5B trains).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — too expensive at our scale; but the
  *design pattern* is reusable for any future small-model verification.

- **Augmented `neural-collapse` PyPI/GitHub package** — generic NC quantities
  (Wu's footnote 3, https://github.com/rhubarbwu/neural-collapse). Drop-in
  measurement tool for CDNV / interference / equinormness on any tensor of
  embeddings + class labels.
  *Replication cost*: 2h to wire into our cached NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — fastest path to running all four
  NC metrics on pathway11_h100 data with consistent definitions.

### Approaches & framings

- **C ≫ d+1 framing.** When classes vastly outnumber embedding dimensions
  (their setting: C=29,233, d ≤ 1024; our Qwen-2.5-1.5B: C=151,936, d=1536),
  the simplex ETF is unreachable but *generalized* hyperspherical uniformity
  GNC2 is. This gives us a principled lens for analyzing per-token activations
  in the residual stream that is consistent with our breathing/PH framings.

- **Self-duality (NC3) vs Uniform-duality (UNC3) dichotomy.** §5.2 — within
  fixed scale, NC3 develops; across scales, it doesn't. Suggests that
  self-duality is a *fine-grained generalization indicator* while uniform
  duality is a *capacity proxy*. Sharp lens for our F-3 prefill⊥final-token
  finding: "orthogonality" might be self-duality at one resolution and
  uniform-duality at another.

- **Generalization-without-scale via permutation tests.** Their §3.8 method
  (fix everything but seed, run permutation test) is a usable design pattern
  for separating *intrinsic* geometric signal from *capacity-correlated*
  geometric signal — a recurring confounder in our pathway 5–11 work.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **TinyStories** (Eldan & Li 2023; arxiv 2305.07759) — 1500-word vocabulary,
  ~2GB synthetic text, license unclear (apparently public on HF). Applicable?
  **no** — domain (toy children's stories) and scale (200M params max) are
  too far from MATH-500 / Qwen-2.5-1.5B regime. The methodology transfers; the
  data does not.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- 30 architectures × widths {64, 128, 256, 512, 768, 1024} × depths {1, 2, 4,
  8, 12} × epochs {1, 3, 10} × weight-decay β ∈ {0.0005, 0.1}; total ~230 CLMs
  trained.
- GPT Neo backbone (Black et al. 2021), tokenizer subset of 50K, only 29,233
  tokens actually appear in TinyStories.
- Their permutation test: 21 instances of `(d=768, L=2, β=0.0005, 1 epoch)`
  with different seeds; 10⁴ permutations.
- Code: https://github.com/rhubarbwu/linguistic-collapse (paper code) and
  https://github.com/rhubarbwu/neural-collapse (generic NC measurement
  package) — the latter is the import-and-go tool.
- Aggressive weight decay β=0.1 produces stronger NC than β=0.0005 (§5.3) —
  worth checking which regime Qwen-2.5-1.5B was trained under before
  comparing.

### Replicable intermediates

- Run `neural-collapse` package (their footnote-3 GitHub) on
  `pathway11_h100/.../prefill_activations.npz` and `final_activations.npz`,
  partitioned by correctness label (F-2 / F-4 setup). Outputs CDNV,
  interference, equinormness, classifier agreement.
- Compute hyperspherical uniformity (eqn 7) on the same data, two
  partitions: per-correctness-class and per-token-class. Compares whether
  geometric structure is correctness-organized or token-organized.
- Compute cos similarity between final-token L19 DoM and rows of W_unembed
  for the top-K most-frequent answer tokens — single-line cosine on
  cached weights + the existing DoM JSON. Tests refutation #2 directly.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2305.07759** — TinyStories (Eldan & Li 2024). NOT in graph; do **not**
  recommend admission — out of scope (training-data study, no hidden-state
  analysis relevant to MATH-500 / 1024-tok regime).
- **2310.05351** — Jiang et al., "Generalized neural collapse for a large
