## 2502.03628 — The Hidden Life of Tokens: Reducing Hallucination of Large Vision-Language Models via Visual Information Steering (Li et al., ICML 2025)

**Relevance:** Domain-adjacent (VLM hallucination, not LM math reasoning),
but methodologically central. Two of VISTA's core empirical claims —
(a) a single per-image, end-of-prefill steering vector applied
uniformly at every layer × every timestep reduces hallucination by ~40%,
(b) multi-layer logit-lens ensembling (w=5) monotonically beats single-
layer (w=1) — directly stress-test our F-3 "orthogonal directions"
framing, our F-9 "CoE-60 redundant with single-layer L19" claim, and
our H-1 "per-position DoM bank required" hypothesis. The paper is
training-free, code-available, and the techniques transfer to
text-only LMs with minimal modification.

**Key claim we tested:** A constant end-of-prefill steering direction
applied at every layer/timestep, plus a w-layer logit-lens ensemble
near the final layer, both improve generation quality without
correctness labels.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — three falsifiable replications queued as
P11-FE382 (constant-VSV on math), P11-FE383 (SLA window probe), P11-FE384
(L27 prefill DoM). Total cost ~1 h CPU + ~30 min H100. Outcomes will
update F-3, F-9, F-2, and H-1.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE382, P11-FE383, P11-FE384, H-306, H-307,
F-2, F-3, F-9, H-1, H-17.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- VSV (Visual Steering Vector) — per-image contrastive direction
  extracted from end-of-prefill residual, injected at every layer and
  timestep with norm rescaling.
- SLA (Self-Logits Augmentation) — w-layer logit-lens ensemble
  (default w=5, γ=0.3) blended with final-layer logits.
- Token-ranking via logit lens — 2-D heatmap (layer × timestep) of an
  arbitrary target token's softmax rank.
- Hidden-state norm rescaling after additive intervention — defensive
  practice for steering experiments.

### Approaches & framings

- "Hidden Genuine Information" — model perceives more than it
  expresses; maps onto our B-bucket framing.
- Per-image (per-input) steering vs amortized concept steering —
  reinforces F-7's "collective, not per-problem" axis.
- Activation-space vs logit-space contrastive decoding — confirms our
  activation-space DoM choice generalizes across decoding strategies.

### Datasets

- MSCOCO 2014 val (500-image subset, MIT, public) — not applicable.
- CHAIR / POPE / MMHal-Bench / MME — all VLM-specific, not applicable.

### Implementation guidance

- VSV strength λ ≈ 0.17 (narrow viable band [0.10, 0.18]); SLA γ = 0.3
  best across four architectures; SLA window w = 5 layers prior to
  final.
- Norm rescaling after injection is critical for stability.
- Latency overhead: VSV+SLA ≈ 1.27× greedy; cheaper than VCD (2.04×) and
  PAI (0.49× throughput).
- Code: https://github.com/LzVv123456/VISTA.

### Replicable intermediates

- L27 prefill DoM AUROC vs F-2's L19 baseline (15 min CPU).
- SLA-style w=4 logit-lens probe at L24–L27 vs single-layer L28
  baseline (1 h CPU).
- Constant-direction cosine comparison: VSV-equivalent v at L19 vs
  supervised L19 DoM (5 min CPU; no model run).

### Cross-paper signals

- 2306.03341 (ITI) — already in graph (CONTRADICTED).
- 2410.15778 (VTI) — recommend admission; predecessor LVLM steering.
- 2407.21771 (PAI) — recommend admission; strongest VLM baseline.
- 2309.03883 (DoLa) — recommend admission; canonical layer-contrastive
  logit-space intervention, F-9-relevant.
- 2210.15097 (Contrastive Decoding) — recommend admission; foundational
  for the lineage.

### Methodologies extracted

- **VSV (Visual Steering Vector)** — per-image contrastive activation
  direction, extracted as `v_steer^l = F(X_p)^l − F(X_n)^l` for paired
  prompts that differ only in presence/absence of the steered modality.
  Injected as `h_l += λ·v_steer^l` at every layer and every timestep,
  followed by hidden-state norm rescaling `h ← h · ‖h_orig‖₂ / ‖h+λv‖₂`.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min H100 with cached prefill NPZs (the only new
  thing is the contrast prompt).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct refutation handle for F-3 and
  H-1.

- **SLA (Self-Logits Augmentation)** — logit lens at the *w* layers
  prior to the final layer, averaged into `o_aug = (1/w) Σ H(h^l_t)`,
  ensembled with final-layer logits as `õ = (1−γ)·o_L + γ·o_aug`.
  Hyperparams: w=5, γ=0.3 best; γ in [0.2, 0.3] is the sweet spot.
  *Replication cost*: 1 h CPU on cached Stage 2 final-token activations
  (need to apply the LM head to L24–L27, then ensemble).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct refutation handle for F-9.

- **Token-ranking via logit lens** — rank of an arbitrary target token
  `x` in `softmax(H(h^l_t))`, aggregated into a 2-D heatmap (layer ×
  timestep). Used to expose the three OBS phenomena.
  *Replication cost*: trivial on cached activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — useful as a sanity probe for
  whether MATH-500 *answer tokens* show "early excitation" or "gradual
  loss" patterns analogous to OBS-1/2.

- **Hidden-state norm rescaling after additive intervention** —
  `h̃ ← (h + λv) · ‖h‖₂ / ‖h + λv‖₂` to prevent drift. Worth borrowing
  for any future H-1 / FE3 patching experiment.
  *Replication cost*: 5-line code change.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — defensive practice for any future
  steering experiment.

- **GPT-4o oracle for token-class labelling** — three-way classification
  (decoded-genuine / hidden-genuine / hallucinated) of generated text
  vs visual ground truth.
  *Replication cost*: not applicable; we have correctness labels for
  free on MATH-500.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — math reasoning has unambiguous
  correctness, no oracle needed.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Hidden Genuine Information" frame** — tokens visible to the model
  internally but not surfaced. Maps cleanly onto our **B-bucket** (K=1
  wrong, K=8 right — the right answer is in the distribution but not
  picked at K=1). VISTA's framing is sharper and could reframe F-7's
  bucket discussion: B-bucket = "hidden correct token, not decoded";
  D-bucket = "decoded with hidden inconsistency."
- **Per-image (per-input) steering vs amortized concept steering** —
  VSV explicitly contrasts itself with Zou-style RepE (one direction per
  concept, amortized over many pairs) and Li-style ITI (mean-mass
  direction). Per-image fits our per-problem framing more naturally.
  Reinforces F-7's "collective signature, not per-problem".
- **Activation-space vs logit-space contrastive decoding** — paper
  argues activation-space generalizes across decoding strategies (greedy
  / beam / nucleus) whereas logit-space (DoLa, VCD) doesn't. We already
  operate in activation space; this is a confirming framing.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MSCOCO 2014 validation (500-image subset)** — Lin et al. 2014, MIT
  license, HF-accessible. Applicable? **no** — image captioning
  hallucination, not relevant to MATH-500.
- **CHAIR (CHAIR-S, CHAIR-I)** — Rohrbach et al. 2018, public.
  Applicable? **no** — caption-vs-ground-truth object overlap metric.
- **POPE** — three-split (random / popular / adversarial) yes/no VQA on
  COCO. Applicable? **no** — VLM-specific binary VQA.
- **MMHal-Bench** — 96 image-question pairs across 8 categories
  (ATTR/ADV/COMP/COUNT/SPAT/ENV/HOL/OTHER), GPT-4-evaluated. Applicable?
  **no**.
- **MME** — 14 perception/reasoning sub-tests for LVLMs. Applicable?
  **no**.

(All five benchmarks are vision-language. None applicable to our 1024-
tok MATH-500 hidden-state pipeline.)

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **VSV strength λ**: 0.17 for LLaVA-1.5 + InstructBLIP, 0.10 for
  MiniGPT-4, 0.12 for Shikra. Tuned on a 100-image MSCOCO holdout. F1
  degrades sharply outside [0.10, 0.18] (Fig. 6) — narrow viable band.
- **SLA mixing γ**: 0.3 best across all four architectures; γ > 0.4
  degrades quality.
- **SLA window w**: 5 layers (i.e., last 5 of 32 for LLaVA) is best.
  Inverse relationship between w and optimal γ — wider window wants
  more conservative mix.
- **Normalization**: hidden-state norm rescaling after injection (Eq. 6
  of the paper). Without it, repeated injection blows up activation
  scale.
- **POPE adjustment**: λ reduced to 0.01 because short Yes/No responses
  don't exhibit gradual loss — strength must be tuned per response
  length regime.
- **Latency**: VSV+SLA = 36.32 ms/token vs greedy 28.54 ms/token (1.27×
  slower). VCD = 2.04× slower; PAI = 0.49× throughput vs greedy.
- **Code**: https://github.com/LzVv123456/VISTA — released, MIT-style
  permissive.

### Replicable intermediates

- **L27 prefill DoM AUROC sanity check** (Refutation 3): compute prefill
  L27 DoM AUROC on cached `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`
  activations, compare to F-2's L19 = 0.7731. Cost: ~15 min CPU. Script:
  reuse the L19 DoM extractor with `layer=27`.
- **SLA logit lens window probe** (Refutation 2): apply Qwen LM head to
  cached Stage 2 final-token residuals at L24–L27, ensemble with L28 at
  γ ∈ {0.1, 0.2, 0.3}, train linear correctness probe on the rank of
  the gold answer's first token, compare AUROC to 0.7186 (final-token
  L19 baseline) and 0.7731 (prefill L19). Cost: ~1 h CPU. Cached NPZs
  sufficient.
- **VSV-equivalent constant-direction extraction** (Refutation 1 + 4):
  compute `v = h_L19[last_prefill, X_p] − h_L19[last_prefill, X_n]`
  where `X_p = system+question+CoT-marker` and `X_n = system+question`
  for each of the 500 MATH-500 problems. Compare cosine to supervised
  L19 prefill DoM (F-2's direction). Cost: 5 min CPU on cached
  activations. *No model run required for the cosine comparison.*
- **"Early excitation" check on math answer tokens**: pick 50 MATH-500
  problems with single-token gold answers, compute logit-lens rank of
  the gold token at every layer × every CoT timestep, look for
  penultimate-layer peak. Cost: ~30 min CPU on cached residuals. Tests
  whether OBS-2 generalizes from VLM caption tokens to math answer
  tokens.

## 2502.04043 — Probe-Free Low-Rank Activation Intervention / FLORAIN (Jiang, Nguyen, So, Nguyen, NAACL 2025)

**Relevance:** Core METHOD_DIFFERS reference for our DoM-based steering work. FLORAIN replaces ITI's linear additive intervention with an ellipsoid manifold + Mahalanobis projection + input-dependent nonlinear low-rank map, intervening at *all attention heads in a single layer*. The construction's "overall direction" `μ̂⁺ − μ̂⁻` is exactly the global DoM, making FLORAIN the canonical second-order generalisation of our F-2 / H-1 framing.

**Key claim we tested:** Input-dependent low-rank steering with second-order region modeling outperforms first-order fixed-vector steering for activation intervention.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** We have the cached activations and infrastructure (P11 H100 results). H-308 (Mahalanobis-AUROC vs DoM-AUROC) is a 30-minute CPU sanity check and gates the more expensive H-309 (FLORAIN-on-MATH-500). FLORAIN was evaluated only on TruthfulQA, never on math reasoning; we cannot directly REPLICATE/CONTRADICT without running the experiments.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE385, P11-FE386, P11-FE387, P11-FE388, H-308, H-309, H-310.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **FLORAIN intervention map** — `f(a) = (I + L(a) R^T) a + s`, with `L_i(a) = tanh(W_i ∘ a + b_i)`, R constant, s bias. Sample-wise (input-dependent) nonlinear low-rank.
  *Replication cost*: ~1 day H100 to train + ~30 min eval. We have the activations cached.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — cleanest test of input-dependent vs fixed-vector steering for H-1.

- **Ellipsoid manifold + Mahalanobis projection** — `M_q = {x : (x − μ̂_q)^T Σ̂^{-1} (x − μ̂_q) ≤ ρ_q}`, distance `c_q(a, a') = (a − a')^T Σ̂^{-1} (a − a')`. Theorem 4.1 collapses Mahalanobis-projection objective to the closed-form `(√c_q(f(a_i), μ̂_q) − √ρ_q)_+^2`.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU on cached NPZs (no FLORAIN training needed; just classification AUROC).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — first-order vs second-order test for F-2.

- **Extrapolation scheme for μ̂_q** — `μ̂_q = μ̂⁺_q + λ(α·(μ̂⁺_q − μ̂⁻_q)/‖·‖ + (1−α)·(μ̂⁺ − μ̂⁻)/‖·‖)`. Pulls per-question mean *away* from undesirable mass, blending local and global directions.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (CPU).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — only if we adapt to MATH-500's "no-per-question repetition" data structure (each problem unique, so `G(q)` has cardinality 1).

- **Linear shrinkage covariance** — `Σ̂^{-1} = (β·S + (1−β)·diag(S))^{-1}`, Ledoit-Wolf-style. Used to make the ill-conditioned empirical S invertible at small sample sizes.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (already in `sklearn.covariance.LedoitWolf`).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — exactly the regulariser we need for any second-order test on small per-bucket sample counts (D-bucket has only ~36 problems).

- **Preconditioned scaled gradient descent** — `W_{t+1} = W_t − η ∇_W F · (R_t^T R_t + εI)^{-1}` and analogous for R, b, s. Adaptive scaling, condition-number-free convergence rate (cites Tong et al. 2021).
  *Replication cost*: standard SGD-with-conditioning.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes if and only if we run FLORAIN itself.

- **Single-layer, all-heads intervention** — chooses one layer ℓ and intervenes on its full `D = d × H` activation. Contrasts with ITI's spread across multiple layers. The exact ℓ per model is in Appendix A (which I did not load).
  *Replication cost*: free — just a layer choice.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct check for our L19-special claim.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Probe-free" intervention** — bypass the detect-then-rectify two-stage pipeline; intervene unconditionally. Intersects H-12: probe-free ≠ label-free, narrows H-12's scope to specifically the *classifier* component being replaceable.
- **"Region modeling"** — desirable answers occupy a manifold, intervention = projection. Recasts our F-2 (DoM as a *direction*) into F-2′ (DoM as a *boundary normal* of a manifold). Compatible reframe; could regenerate our DoM via the special case `α=0`, k=0, ϕ linear.
- **"Single-layer concentration"** — consolidating intervention into one layer parallelises and reduces cumulative drift. Resonates with F-9 (single-layer L19 ≈ multi-layer CoE-60); orthogonal mechanism (computational vs informational).
- **"Sample-wise mapping"** — `L(a)` depends on the input. Reframes activation steering away from "find the universal direction" toward "learn the input-conditional projection". Strong METHOD_DIFFERS for H-1.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **TruthfulQA** — 817 questions × 38 categories, 5,918 QA pairs after processing, 2-fold CV split (326 / 82 / 407). HF, public. Applicable? **no** — different task (truthfulness QA, not math reasoning); the *method* however is dataset-agnostic and could be applied to our MATH-500 cache.
- **Toxic Comments Classification (Jigsaw)** — public, used in Appendix C only. Applicable? **no** — different task.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Code: https://github.com/nguyenngocbaocmt02/EFI (read-and-borrow target).
- Compute: 4× NVIDIA RTX A5000, i9-14900K, 128GB RAM. Modest hardware → re-implementation is tractable on our setup.
- Activation: ϕ = tanh (chosen for boundedness in (−1, 1) — auto-resolves the bilinear scale ambiguity).
- 2-fold CV throughout (matches Li 2024b protocol).
- Per-question samples are very small (`< 10` samples per `G(q)` according to footnote 2) → ill-conditioned Σ̂ → linear shrinkage is load-bearing, not optional.
- Hyperparameters: λ (extrapolation magnitude), α (local vs global mix), β (shrinkage strength), k (low-rank dimension), ℓ (target layer). Per-model values are in Appendix A (not loaded — flag for promote-time follow-up if we run this).
- The exact target layer ℓ for each model is **not** stated in the body — probably tuned per model.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Mahalanobis vs DoM AUROC at L19 prefill (Qwen-2.5-1.5B, MATH-500).** From cached `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/*` NPZs: build μ̂⁺, μ̂⁻, fit Ledoit-Wolf Σ̂ (single global covariance, MATH-500 has unique problems → no per-`q` averaging), compute Mahalanobis distance to μ̂⁺ and to μ̂⁻; report ΔAUROC vs the F-2 anchor (0.7731). ~30 min CPU.
- **Single-Gaussian likelihood test for F-10.** On the same NPZs, compute log-likelihood of held-out correct activations under N(μ̂⁺, Σ̂) vs under a Gaussian mixture / KDE; the gap quantifies how non-Gaussian the desirable region is. ~1 h CPU.
- **Layer sweep for FLORAIN target.** Compute Mahalanobis-projection AUROC at L4 / L9 / L14 / L19 / L24 on existing extracted layers (P11 has these). If peak is at L19, this corroborates F-2's layer specificity; if peak is elsewhere, F-2's "L19 special" framing is qualified. ~1 h CPU.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2306.03341** (Inference-Time Intervention / Li et al. 2024b) — already in graph (status pending_triage; PAPER_INDEX status: CONTRADICTED, partial). Direct baseline FLORAIN beats; canonical ITI predecessor.
- **2410.13640** (Chain-of-Embedding / Wang) — already in graph. Tangentially related (also probes hidden state for correctness signal); FLORAIN is intervention-side, CoE is monitoring-side.

Cited as the conceptual seed for "intervention via direction in activation space" — direct ancestor of both ITI and FLORAIN, and an important reference for our F-2 framing of "DoM as latent-knowledge direction".

## 2502.05242 — Beyond External Monitors: Enhancing Transparency of Large Language Models for Easier Monitoring (Chen et al., 2025)

**Relevance:** Inverts the standard probe-engineering paradigm relevant to the F-2 / F-8 line. Where this program treats the prefill L19 DoM as a discovery about the base model, TELLME shows that lightweight LoRA-based contrastive disentanglement at one layer can raise even a trivial mean-cosine monitor on Llama-3.1-8B from 68.3% to 83.2% binary-safety accuracy without degrading general capability — implying that "AUROC ceilings on residual-stream probes" are at least partly a base-model artefact rather than an architectural property. Their five disentanglement metrics (Coding Rate, eRank, `l_2`, Angle, Hausdorff) and optimal-transport-based generalization-bound theory provide a quantitative vocabulary that this program currently lacks for F-7 (D-bucket distinctiveness). Most importantly: TELLME's evidence that the orthogonality of disentanglement axes is *malleable* under a contrastive objective applies directly to F-3's cos(prefill_DoM, final_DoM) = 0.046 finding — that orthogonality may be the absence of a training signal, not the presence of an architectural constraint.

**Key claim we tested:** Residual-stream representations at a chosen layer are sufficiently malleable that contrastive disentanglement can substantially raise *any* monitor's accuracy on that layer without harming general capability. Predicted consequence in our terms: applying TELLME to Qwen2.5-1.5B with correct/incorrect MATH-500 prefills as pairs would raise prefill DoM AUROC from 0.7731 to ≥ 0.85.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — we have not yet run TELLME on our pipeline. Two cheap precursor experiments (Self-Sim baseline and 5-metric disentanglement audit on cached NPZs) are queued (P11-FE390, P11-FE391) and will calibrate the expected lift before committing 1d H100 to FE73.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE389 (TELLME on 1.5B correctness), P11-FE390 (Self-Sim baseline), P11-FE391 (5-metric audit), P10-FE21 (TELLME for F-3 orthogonality test), H-311, H-312.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **TELLME contrastive disentanglement loss (`L_d`)** — InfoNCE over residual-stream representations: `z_i = h^l_t / ||h^l_t||`, with positive pairs from same behavior and negative pairs across behaviors, temperature `σ` (Eq. 3).
  *Replication cost*: 1d H100 for LoRA on Qwen2.5-1.5B + dataset construction. Code public: https://github.com/AI45Lab/TELLME
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — the pivotal experiment that disambiguates whether F-2's 0.7731 is a model-property or a probe-only ceiling.

- **Retention loss (`L_r`)** — `l_2`-norm constraint on representations of held-out general-capability data + KL penalty on output distributions for the disentangled-behavior data (Eq. 4). Coefficient `λ` balances against `L_d` (Eq. 5).
  *Replication cost*: trivial once `L_d` is set up.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — without `L_r` the LoRA destroys MMLU; we'd need this to not nuke the 1.5B's MATH-500 baseline.

- **Self-Sim baseline (mean-of-class cosine probe)** — for each behavior class, compute mean of representations; classify a new point by argmax cosine to means.
  *Replication cost*: 20 min CPU on cached `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a label-free correctness AUROC floor on cached data without any new training; checks whether the F-2 supervised DoM is wringing signal that any trivial probe finds.

- **Latent Guard (cross-attention disentangler)** — separate module attends across the residual stream to extract behavior label (Liu et al., cited as ref [48]).
  *Replication cost*: implementation work, ~3d engineering.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — orthogonal direction, not in our roadmap.

- **Five disentanglement metrics on residual streams** — Coding Rate (rate distortion of subspace, intra-class compression), eRank (effective rank, dimensionality of the inter-class span), `l_2` distance between class means, average angle between class means, Hausdorff distance between class point clouds.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU on cached prefill activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — these directly characterize how much disentanglement headroom the base 1.5B has on correct/incorrect MATH-500 prefills.

- **80%-depth target-layer heuristic** — TELLME selects the LoRA target layer at 80% of model depth (e.g., layer 22 for a 28-layer Qwen). Note: this is *deeper* than F-2's L19 (≈68% of 28). Layer-wise ablation in Appendix B.7 reports near-flat MMLU degradation across 10%-90% range (std < 1%).
  *Replication cost*: minimal — a hyperparameter choice.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — the 80% vs L19 (68%) gap is the kind of non-trivial layer-locus question we already track in F-2 (e.g., is L19 special, or is the optimum drifting deeper?).

### Approaches & framings

- **"Make the model monitor-friendly, not the monitor smarter."** Inverts the standard probe-engineering paradigm: instead of choosing between supervised DoM (F-2) and label-free SEP (H-12), modify the model so trivial monitors work. Intersects every supervised-probe finding (F-2, F-7, F-8) by suggesting the probe ceiling is partly a model-architecture artefact.

- **Optimal-transport / Wasserstein generalization-bound theory.** Theorem 1 (proven in their ref [14]) bounds the zero-one expected loss by a sum over `Lip(g, j) · τ · Var_n_j(φ#p_j) + R̂_τ,n`. Reduces to: smaller intra-class `k`-variance + better margin → tighter bound. Connects to our F-1 breathing-as-population-geometry framing — `k`-variance ≈ within-bucket dispersion ≈ bucket-bound prefill DoM ratio.

- **Disentanglement-as-transparency.** Equates "the model is interpretable" with "behaviors are separable in the residual stream", measured by 5 metrics. Intersects F-7 (D-bucket distinctive geometric signature) by giving us a 5-metric vocabulary for *how distinctive* a bucket is.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MATH (Hendrycks et al., ref [27])** — same family as our MATH-500 split, 7 mathematical branches. HF-accessible. Applicable? yes — TELLME tests use the *full* MATH dataset; we already work with the 500-problem subset and could re-use any TELLME math-disentanglement pairs verbatim.

- **MMLU** — 57 domain knowledge tasks. HF. Applicable? partially — used as their Knowledge scenario and as a general-capability evaluator. Not in our active pipeline but already gettable.

- **BeaverTails** — 5 safety-risk categories + 1 safe category, ~330k QA. HF, Apache-2.0. Applicable? no — orthogonal to our correctness pipeline.

- **UltraChat (Retain Set)** — large general-capability conversational data. HF. Applicable? yes — would be the natural retain-set when we run TELLME on 1.5B to preserve MATH baseline.

- **SaladBench / XSTest** — safety-evaluation harness. Applicable? no — safety domain.

- **GSM8K / AGIEval** — general-capability evaluators. HF. Applicable? partially — useful as no-regression checks if we run TELLME on 1.5B.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- LoRA on a single decoder layer at 80% × `num_layers` (so for Qwen2.5-1.5B with 28 layers → L22; F-2 currently uses L19, ~68%).
- Edit applied to **last token of input** only (i.e., the prefill end-position) — directly aligns with our "prefill" definition.
- `σ` (InfoNCE temperature) and `λ` (loss balance) are the two key hyperparameters; specific values in Appendix B.2 (which we'd need to read for replication).
- KL penalty in `L_r` uses the *original* model's output distribution as reference — standard preference-tuning trick.
- Code: https://github.com/AI45Lab/TELLME (CC-BY-4.0 paper; code license unspecified in abstract, must check).
- Reported batch sizes for "B kinds of behaviors" not in main text — Appendix B.2.
- Layer-wise stability: std-dev of MMLU < 1% across 10%-90% target-layer choices (Appendix B.7, Table 11).

### Replicable intermediates

Predicts ≤ 0.7731 (the supervised DoM number). Compare gap. Cost: 20 min CPU. Script: easy mod of `prefill_gated_compute/eval_dom.py`.

- **Five-metric disentanglement audit on cached prefill activations** — Coding Rate, eRank, `l_2`, angle, Hausdorff between correct vs incorrect prefill clouds. Predicts: large `l_2` gap if the base 1.5B has low TELLME headroom; small gap if it has high headroom. Cost: 30 min CPU. Wholly cached, no new extraction.

- **Cross-layer Self-Sim sweep** — repeat Self-Sim probe across all 28 layers using cached `temporal_and_verifier_results.json` activations (if those NPZs are still on disk). Compare to F-9's CoE-60 trajectory. Cost: 1h CPU.

## 2502.05911 — GRAIT: Gradient-Driven Refusal-Aware Instruction Tuning for Effective Hallucination Mitigation (Zhu, Jiang, Wu et al., 2025)

**Relevance:** GRAIT is the gradient-space analogue of our DoM probing pipeline: it learns a "refusal direction" `g_idk = E[∇L over D_idk]` in LoRA parameter space and uses gradient inner products `⟨∇L(x), g_idk⟩` to (a) select training samples (Refusal Influence) and (b) re-weight the SFT loss (Stable Influence). The structural parallel to our F-2 (prefill L19 DoM) and F-3 (prefill/final DoM orthogonality) is exact — only the space (parameter-grad vs residual-activation) differs. GRAIT's Assumption 2 (orthogonality of class gradient means) is the gradient-space twin of F-3's `cos(prefill_DoM, final_DoM) = 0.046`. The Truthful Helpfulness Score (THS) is a cleaner single-number summary of selective-prediction quality than the risk-coverage curves we currently use for F-8.

**Key claim we tested:** "A learned gradient direction `g_idk` over an `idk` (incorrect→refuse) training set ranks samples by their contribution to refusal learning, and softmax-weighting by `⟨∇L, g_idk − g_ik⟩` mitigates over-refusal." — restated in our terms: "the correctness signal lives in a low-rank gradient direction whose mean is approximately orthogonal to the answer-class gradient mean."

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — GRAIT validates orthogonality on TriviaQA / MMLU (factual recall) only. Whether the same property holds on MATH-500 (multi-step reasoning) is open. P11-FE392, FE74, FE76 are the cheap sanity checks; H-313, H-314, H-315 are the deeper questions.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE392, P11-FE393, P11-FE394, P11-FE395, H-313, H-314, H-315; closest siblings F-2, F-3, F-8, F-9.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Refusal Influence (`I_ref`)** — inner product of a training sample's per-sample gradient with the mean gradient of the `idk` set: `I_ref(x) = ⟨∇L(x;θ), E_{x_o ~ D_idk}[∇L(x_o^idk, y_o^idk; θ)]⟩`. Used to rank `idk` samples by their contribution to refusal learning.
  *Replication cost*: 4h H100 (one LoRA-tune pass on Qwen-1.5B + per-sample gradient extraction over 500 MATH problems).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct analogue of DoM, would test whether gradient-direction beats activation-direction as a correctness oracle.

- **Stable Influence (`I_sta`)** — inner product of sample gradient with the *difference* of class means: `I_sta(x) = ⟨∇L(x;θ), E[∇L over D_idk] − E[∇L over D_ik]⟩`. Larger `I_sta` ⇒ less over-refusal contribution.
  *Replication cost*: same pass as `I_ref` (free additional projection).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly measures the orthogonality-of-class-gradients (F-3 analogue).

- **Adaptive softmax-weighted SFT loss** — assigns each `idk` training sample a weight `ω(x) = e^{I_sta(x)/τ} / Z` with temperature `τ=0.05`, then minimizes `Σ ω(x)·L_idk + Σ L_ik`. Constraint: `Σω = 1`.
  *Replication cost*: cheap once `I_sta` is computed; modifies SFT loop only.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes if we ever run a refusal-tuning experiment.

- **LESS-style low-dim gradient features** — LoRA (r=64, α=16) + Johnson–Lindenstrauss random projection of per-sample gradient vectors to make pairwise inner products tractable. Cites Xia et al. 2402.04333.
  *Replication cost*: existing LESS code is OSS.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — required for any future "gradient-as-DoM" experiment.

- **Truthful Helpfulness Score (THS)** — single-number metric defined as the cross-product ratio of `OS_2 × OS_1 / OU × OS_1` in the (P_c, P_w) coordinate plane, where S_1 is the baseline (no-refusal) operating point and S_2 is the refused model's. Encodes "did we move below the baseline frontier" in one signed scalar.
  *Replication cost*: 5 minutes once you have P_c, P_w, P_r per model.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — strictly better summary of selective-prediction quality than the AUROC-at-coverage-0.5 we currently use for F-8. Consider adding to validate_claims.py.

- **Correctness gating with N=10 sampling for OEQA** — GRAIT computes `C(x)` by sampling `N=10` answers and measuring agreement; `T_C=0.5` is the threshold. For MCQA they use ground-truth-token probability.
  *Replication cost*: 1h H100 for 500-problem MATH set at K=10.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes (we already have K=8 from EXP-033 — close enough).

### Approaches & framings

- **Hallucination = "answering when you should refuse"** vs our framing **correctness = "predict K=1 success from prefill geometry"**. GRAIT recasts the same correctness-prediction problem as a *training-time* loss-weighting problem rather than a *test-time* abstention problem. This shifts the burden from "find a good probe" (our F-2/F-8) to "shape the loss landscape so the model abstains correctly without an external probe."
- **Gradient inner product as influence proxy.** Pruthi et al.'s TracIn first-order Taylor expansion of the loss is the underlying machinery. This re-frames "what does this training sample teach the model?" as "what gradient direction does it pull θ in?" — the same logic that motivates DoM, lifted from activation space to parameter space. Useful for H-13 (head-level circuit attribution).
- **Two-axis trade-off in (P_c, P_w) space**, summarized by THS triangle area. Cleaner than risk-coverage curves for headline numbers; we should consider adopting it for F-8.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MMLU** — 14k train / 1.5k val MCQA factual recall. HF, public. Applicable? **no** — not reasoning, not 1024-tok, no CoT.
- **ARC-c** — 1.2k MCQA science Q's. HF, public. Applicable? **no** — same reason.
- **TriviaQA** — 87k train / 11k dev OEQA. HF, public. Applicable? **no** — short-form factual recall, not multi-step reasoning.
- **NQ (Natural Questions)** — 3.6k dev OEQA. HF, public. Applicable? **no** — factual-recall, OOD test only.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- LoRA: `r=64, α=16, dropout=0.1, lr=2e-4`.
- Training: 3 epochs, `max_seq_len=2048`, XTuner framework (https://github.com/InternLM/xtuner), evaluation via OpenCompass (https://github.com/open-compass/opencompass).
- Hyperparameters: `T_C = 0.5` (correctness threshold), `τ = 0.05` (weight-softmax temperature).
- Sample budget: 5,000 MMLU train, 10,000 TriviaQA train, **1:4 ratio of ik to idk** samples in `D_rait`.
- Hardware: 8× A100-80GB.
- Init models: LLaMA2-7B-Chat, LLaMA3-8B-Instruct.
- Code release: https://github.com/opendatalab/GRAIT (promised in paper).
- Gotcha: the gradient-mean direction `g_idk` is computed *once* on the initial model and *not* updated during training (their "static" treatment, acknowledged limitation). A dynamic version would re-estimate per-epoch.
- Few-shot evaluation: MCQA 5-shot, OEQA 3-shot for the correctness step; 0-shot greedy for the actual eval.

### Replicable intermediates

- **`I_ref`-analogue on MATH-500**: For each of the 500 MATH problems, take cached prefill L19 activation as a stand-in for `∇L`. Compute the mean activation vector for the K=0/8 (idk) set and for the K≥7/8 (ik) set. Score each problem by `⟨a_x, mean_idk⟩`. Compare to prefill DoM probe AUROC (0.7731). Cached artifact: `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json` activations + `pathway11_h100/exp_K8/results.json` for K-counts. Should run in ~30 min CPU.
- **THS recomputation for F-8**: We already have `P_c`, `P_w`, `P_r` for the prefill-DoM-gated 1.5B at coverage 0.5 (71.6% accuracy, plus refusal rate). Compute THS via Eq. 12 of GRAIT and add to `FINDINGS.md` F-8 as a secondary metric. ~5 min CPU.
- **Cross-set Pearson check on MATH-500**: GRAIT's Pearson 0.886 between `I_ref` on `D_ik` vs `D_idk` (Figure 5) — replicate using prefill L19 DoM-projection as the influence proxy. If we get a similarly high correlation (>0.7), corroborates F-9. Cached: pathway11 prefill activations.

## 2502.06115 — Task-driven Layerwise Additive Activation Intervention (Nguyen, Nguyen, Nguyen, Nguyen, 2025)

**Relevance:** Optimization-based replacement for the heuristic mean-difference (DoM) steering vector that H-1 plans to use. The paper's central claim is that a single Δ vector at one layer, optimized via NLL or KL task-loss with lasso + group-lasso regularization, beats every heuristic intervention baseline (Function Vectors, ICV, ITI) and even PEFT baselines (LoRA, IA³, Soft Prompt) in the N=10 small-data regime on rule-understanding and opinion-distribution tasks. The single-layer principle is justified mechanistically: scattering Δ across layers is degraded by accumulated representation shift in later layers — which independently corroborates F-9 (CoE-60 redundant with single-layer L19 DoM).

**Key claim we tested:** A single-layer optimized Δ outperforms heuristic activation-extraction interventions in the small-N regime; the optimal intervention layer is shallow (ℓ=4 on Llama3-8B with 32 layers), not late.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — the paper's optimization framework is directly applicable to H-1, F-2, F-3. P11-FE396 / FE74 / FE75 will test (a) whether optimized L19 Δ beats heuristic L19 DoM on MATH-500, (b) whether the generation-objective optimal layer matches our probe-objective L19 or is shallower, and (c) whether the optimized Δ overlaps with both prefill and final DoMs (which would refute F-3's "two distinct circuits" reading of cos = 0.046). The paper's single-layer-vs-scattered argument *corroborates* F-9 with a mechanistic explanation (representation drift) we should annotate.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE396 (heuristic-vs-optimized Δ on MATH-500), P11-FE397 (layer scan), P11-FE398 (Δ-vs-DoM cosine), H-316, H-317, and modification to H-1.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Layerwise additive activation intervention with lasso + group-lasso (Eq. 2)** — single vector Δ ∈ ℝ^D added to last-token activations at one layer ℓ, optimized to minimize task-loss with `γ‖Δ‖₁ + λ Σ_h ‖Δ_h‖₂` regularization (group = attention head). *Replication cost*: ~2h H100 once code is wired into our pipeline (loss is autograd; N=10 trivial). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct candidate replacement for H-1's heuristic DoM.
- **Additive task-vector composition (Δ_τ + Δ_τ')** — sum of independently-optimized task vectors used as a no-extra-training intervention for the composed task. *Replication cost*: trivial once Δ vectors exist (~minutes). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly applicable to combining "be correct" Δ with "use scratchpad" Δ if H-1 splits MATH-500 task into subtasks.
- **NLL task loss for next-token prediction tasks; KL task loss for distribution-matching tasks** — two concrete loss families for the same intervention framework. *Replication cost*: trivial. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — NLL is the natural choice for MATH-500 final-answer steering.
- **Group-lasso-by-attention-head sparsity** — penalizes whole-head usage rather than individual coordinates, motivated by Hernandez et al. and Li et al. attention-head sparsity findings. *Replication cost*: trivial (one extra loss term). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — also gives an interpretable head-importance map for free that we could compare against H-13 (head-level attribution).
- **N=10 demonstration small-data protocol** — paper deliberately operates in low-data regime to show the optimization is sample-efficient; 10 input/output pairs per task. *Replication cost*: trivial. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — matches our typical "we have 500 MATH-500 problems but want to validate from few".

### Approaches & framings

- **Single-layer intervention principle ("avoid representation shift")** — paper's central reframe: rather than scatter Δ across layers (Function Vectors, ITI), focus on one layer because later-layer activations are downstream of earlier-layer interventions, which contaminates effects. Intersects F-9 (single-layer DoM ≈ CoE-60) — gives the F-9 redundancy a *mechanistic explanation*.
- **Task vectors as algebraic objects** — interventions form a (linear) algebra under additive composition. Intersects H-1 (steering vector design) — suggests H-1 should be designed as a vector-space-of-task-fixes rather than a single fix.
- **Optimization vs heuristic ICL signal extraction** — reframe of the entire steering literature: heuristics (mean-difference, FV) are unconditionally improvable by gradient-based optimization with regularization. Intersects every steering hypothesis we have (H-1, H-12).

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **Antonym / Synonym / Eng-Fr / Eng-Ger** — small word-level rule tasks from Todd et al. 2310.15213, used here. License: open. Applicable? **no** — these are word-level pairs, not multi-token reasoning; not the 1024-tok MATH-500 regime.
- **OpinionQA (Santurkar et al. 2303.17548)** — distribution-matching benchmark over demographic subgroups. License: open (HF). Applicable? **no** — opinion alignment, not correctness prediction.
- The paper introduces no new dataset; all benchmarks are inherited.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Llama3-8B: L=32, H=32, d=128, D=d×H=4096. They intervene at layer ℓ=4 (early). For Qwen-2.5-1.5B (L=28, H=12, d=128, D=1536), the analogous shallow layer would be ℓ ≈ 4 (depth 0.14).
- Regularization: λ = γ = 0.01 (group lasso = lasso parameter, both small).
- Optimizer details unspecified; assume Adam with default lr from PEFT defaults.
- Hardware: 4× NVIDIA A5000 (sufficient for 8B; for our 1.5B/7B Qwen runs we have H100 oversupply).
- Code: https://github.com/HieuNT91/LayerwiseIntervention.git (PyTorch, public).
- N=10 train pairs per task; metric = Exact Match + GPT-4-as-judge ("GPT-Eval").
- Layer scan in Figure 1 is for *unregularized* losses; with regularization the layer-sensitivity may differ — caveat for any replication.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Eq. 2 at L19 last-token, Qwen-2.5-1.5B, N=10 MATH-500 pairs (5 correct + 5 incorrect)**: NLL loss on the gold final answer token; λ=γ=0.01; optimize Δ ∈ ℝ^1536; measure cos(Δ, prefill_DoM_L19) and cos(Δ, final_DoM_L19). Cached artifacts: `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json` already has prefill and final DoM directions and per-problem L19 prefill activations. Need: per-problem L19 *last-token* activations from MATH-500 generations (may need re-extract; check P11 H100 cache for last-token L19).

## 2502.06233 — Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs (Taubenfeld et al., 2025)

**Relevance:** Introduces Confidence-Informed Self-Consistency (CISC), a confidence-weighted majority-vote variant of self-consistency that achieves 40-46% cost reduction on average across nine LLMs and four reasoning datasets including MATH. Compares four confidence extraction methods (Sequence Probability, Verbal Binary, Verbal 0-100, P(True)) and shows P(True) wins despite being the *least calibrated* of the four. Introduces Within-Question Discrimination (WQD) as the right metric for selective-prediction-style problems and shows it perfectly predicts CISC ranking, while ECE-t and Brier-t do not. Directly bears on F-2 (correctness probe AUROC), F-8 (selective prediction), F-9 (CoE-60 redundancy), H-12 (label-free abstention), and H-19 (verification routing).

**Key claim we tested:** P(True) verbal probe — a single-token forward pass after the answer — provides a stronger within-question correctness signal than calibrated verbal confidences and than sequence probability, sufficient to reduce K=30 self-consistency cost by 40-46%.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — proposed P11-FE399/73/74/75 will run P(True) and CISC on the cached MATH-500 K=8 set and compare directly against F-2 prefill DoM (AUROC 0.7731), F-8 selective prediction (71.6% at coverage 0.5), F-9 CoE-60, and H-19 verification routing.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE399 (P(True) WQD vs prefill DoM), P11-FE400 (WQD-based selective prediction), P11-FE401 (CISC vs F-8 vs H-19 at matched compute), P11-FE402 (confidence-gap-stratified WQD curve), H-318, H-319, H-320.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **P(True) verbal-probability probe** — append "Now I will rate my confidence on a scale of 1-10. Proposed confidence:" or binary 0/1 prompt after generated answer, take the model's probability mass on the "1" / high-confidence token. Single forward pass, ~20 added tokens, prefix-cacheable.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached K=8 generations (we already have logits from generation, but P(True) requires *new* forward passes with the confidence prompt suffix; needs small GPU, ~30 min on Qwen-2.5-1.5B for 500×8 paths).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct head-to-head with prefill DoM AUROC, low cost, high information value for refuting/confirming F-2.

- **Verbal Binary / Verbal 0-100 confidence prompts** — instruct model to output binary 0/1 or scaled 0-100 confidence after generation. Use the *generated token* (not log-prob) as the score.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min H100 for the same 500×8 paths.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — same job as P(True), gives us the calibration vs WQD ablation that motivates H-12 reframing.

- **Within-Question Discrimination (WQD) metric** — for each question with both correct and incorrect samples, count pairs (correct, incorrect) where confidence(correct) > confidence(incorrect); normalize by total pairs. Pure ranking metric, no scale dependence.
  *Replication cost*: 20 min CPU — pure post-hoc on existing scored arrays.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — drop-in replacement for AUROC throughout Pathway 11. Sharper for the K=8 regime than AUROC-on-K=1.

- **Confidence-weighted majority vote (CISC aggregation)** — softmax-normalize confidences with temperature T (tuned on 10% held-out, dataset-agnostic), weighted vote over K samples.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU — trivially scriptable on any K-sample correctness array with per-sample confidence.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a concrete inference-time scaling baseline to put alongside F-8's selective prediction and H-19's verification routing.

- **Two-step prompting with KV-cache reuse** — generate (q, r, a) under one prompt; concatenate confidence prompt e (~20 tokens) and continue; do *not* reprocess the prefix. Reduces P(True) overhead to ~5% of base inference cost.
  *Replication cost*: minor — implementation detail using HF `past_key_values` or vLLM prefix cache.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes if we run any P(True) experiments — keeps the budget honest.

- **Per-method temperature scaling for confidence normalization** — softmax with T tuned on 10% held-out aggregated across all four datasets. Different methods need wildly different T (P(True) needs low T because confidences cluster tightly).
  *Replication cost*: included in CISC implementation.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — baked into CISC.

- **Confidence-gap stratified WQD curve (Figure 4)** — plot WQD as a function of percentile-binned confidence-gap to show monotonic discrimination at fine resolution.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — strong sanity-check artifact for any signal we promote (e.g. prefill DoM gap percentiles vs within-question discrimination).

### Approaches & framings

- **Within-question vs between-question evaluation distinction.** Recasts a long-standing confusion in calibration literature: the question "is this confidence well-calibrated globally?" answers a different question than "can this confidence distinguish correct from incorrect for *this* problem?" Our F-2 and F-8 implicitly use between-question framings (AUROC across all problems at K=1, global score-threshold for abstention). Adopting WQD reframes Pathway 11 evaluation around the operationally-meaningful axis.

- **Confidence as a path ranker, not a path filter.** CISC's bet is that confidence *weighting* (soft) beats confidence *thresholding* (hard). Our F-8 abstention is hard thresholding. The CISC framing suggests a smoother selective-prediction protocol where path weights reduce variance even at full coverage.

- **Self-assessment as decoder-side capability.** The paper's strong claim is that LLMs *can* judge their own outputs (contributing to the Huang et al. 2023 vs Kadavath 2022 debate). This pushes against H-12's implicit assumption that supervised probes are necessary — verbal P(True) needs no labels at all.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MATH** (Hendrycks 2021) — 5K test set, full. License: MIT, public. **Applicable: yes** — superset of our MATH-500 evaluation. CISC results on MATH directly comparable to F-2/F-8 numbers.
- **GSM8K** (Cobbe 2021) — 1320 validation. License: MIT, public. **Applicable: yes** — easier comparator than MATH-500; H-2 (breathing on short CoT) lives here.
- **MMLU-Pro** (Wang 2024) — 5K random sample. License: MIT, public. **Applicable: marginal** — wide-domain knowledge, not aligned with our reasoning focus, but useful for domain-transfer of prefill DoM.
- **Big-Bench-Hard** (Suzgun 2022) — 5,761 examples across 20 tasks. License: Apache 2.0. **Applicable: marginal** — useful only if we want to test whether DoM signal generalizes off-MATH.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Code released at `https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/cisc` — direct CISC implementation we can clone and run on Qwen-2.5 outputs.
- Two-step prompting uses HuggingFace `past_key_values` for KV-cache reuse — avoid reprocessing the (q, r, a) prefix when computing P(True). Critical for honest cost accounting.
- Temperature T tuned per (model, confidence-method) pair on 10% held-out aggregated across all four datasets — single hyperparameter, dataset-agnostic, simple to re-tune for Qwen.
- Bootstrap protocol: sample 30 paths per question once, then bootstrap n=500 sets of size b ∈ [1, 30] per budget. Reduces variance in cost-reduction estimates. Worth adopting for Pathway 11 K-sweep figures.
- P(True) prompt: `"Is the proposed answer correct? (Yes/No):"` style; take P(token="Yes") (or "1" depending on prompt variant).
- Verbal 0-100 prompt: `"Now I will rate my confidence on a scale of 1-10."` — note the 1-10 in prompt despite Verbal 0-100 method name; numeric range varies by config.
- Optimal P(True) temperature is *low* (Supplementary Fig 8) because P(True) values cluster tightly — confirms the within-question normalization step is doing real work.

### Replicable intermediates

- **P(True) on K=8 cached MATH-500 generations.** Run the confidence-prompt forward pass for each of the 500×8 paths in `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`. Compute (a) WQD across all 500 questions, (b) AUROC for K=1 correctness vs F-2's 0.7731, (c) cost-reduction curve vs vanilla SC at K=2…30. ~30 min H100 + 20 min CPU.
- **WQD score for prefill L19 DoM.** Pure post-hoc — for each question, rank K=8 path-level prefill DoM scores, count pairwise correctness inversions. No new generation needed.
- **WQD-based selective-prediction curve for F-8.** Re-do F-8 using within-question DoM-gap thresholds instead of global score thresholds. ~20 min CPU on cached arrays.
- **CoE-60 vs P(True) WQD head-to-head.** On the same 500×8 paths, score with CoE-60 (existing pipeline) and P(True) (new), compute WQD for each. ~1h CPU + 30 min H100.

### Cross-paper signals

- 2203.11171 — already in graph (status: graphed, REPLICATED + EXTENDED). Self-Consistency (Wang 2022) — CISC's direct baseline; both papers' results are now joinable.
- 2410.13640 — already in graph (status: graphed, PARTIALLY CONFIRMED). Chain-of-Embedding — closest analog to "Sequence Probability" baseline that CISC's P(True) beats by 15-20 percentage points.
- 2402.03744 — already in graph (status: graphed, CITED ONLY). INSIDE — multi-sample covariance approach that CISC implicitly compares against via SP baseline.
- 2406.15927 — already in graph (status: graphed, CITED ONLY). Semantic Entropy Probes — H-12's basis; CISC Table 3 is direct evidence that calibration-trained SEPs may underperform P(True) on WQD.
- 2207.05221 — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Kadavath et al. 2022, "Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know" — original P(True) paper, cited 4× in CISC, foundational reference for the entire P(True)-vs-calibrated-verbal debate. Should be admitted.
- 2305.14975 — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Tian et al. 2023, "Just Ask for Calibration" — the verbal-confidence calibration baseline CISC outperforms; relevant for grounding the calibration↔discrimination distinction.
- 2304.13734 — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Azaria & Mitchell 2023, "The internal state of an LLM knows when it's lying" — internal-state probes similar to our DoM, cited in CISC as alternative to P(True).

## 2502.06703 — Can 1B LLM Surpass 405B LLM? Rethinking Compute-Optimal Test-Time Scaling (Liu et al., 2025)

**Relevance:** Same regime as our Pathway 11: MATH-500 + Qwen2.5-1.5B / 7B
+ test-time compute scaling. Provides the canonical 2025 reference for
PRM-guided BoN, beam search, and DVTS, and the strongest available
open-weight PRM (Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B). Directly bears on F-2 (correctness
prediction), F-8 (selective prediction), F-9 (trajectory features), F-7
(behavioral hardness), and H-19 (verification routing). The paper's
reward-aware compute-optimal framing is essentially H-19 with a richer
verifier slot.

**Key claim we tested:** Compute-optimal TTS (with the right PRM and method)
allows much smaller policy models to match or exceed much larger models —
e.g. Qwen2.5-1.5B to ~85.6% MATH-500, Qwen2.5-7B-Inst + Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B
to 91.0%. PRM choice dominates the design space; OOD between PRM and policy
is the failure mode.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** No replication run yet. Cheapest cross-check
is H-321 / P11-FE403 — score our cached P11 K=1 generations with
Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B and compare AUROC to F-2's 0.7731.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE403, P11-FE404, P11-FE405, P11-FE406, H-321, H-322;
indirectly H-19, H-1, H-5, F-2, F-8, F-9.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Best-of-N (BoN) with PRM scoring**. Generate N independent samples,
  score each by PRM (PRM-Min, PRM-Last, or PRM-Avg), select via Majority
  Vote, PRM-Max, or PRM-Vote (vote-weighted by PRM score).
  *Replication cost*: ~30 min H100 to score the cached P11 K=8 generations
  with Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B, run all 9 voting variants.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — already have K=8 cached, only need PRM
  forward pass; lets us read out a directly-comparable PRM AUROC against
  F-2's 0.7731.

- **Beam search guided by PRM (beam width N, beam size M=4)**. At each
  step, PRM scores M expansions per beam, top-N retained.
  *Replication cost*: ~4 h H100 — needs new generation, not just scoring.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — feeds H-19's C_exact framing but
  requires a fresh generation pipeline integrated with PRM.

- **Diverse Verifier Tree Search (DVTS)**. Partition the search tree into
  N/M independent subtrees of width M, run beam search within each subtree
  to maintain diversity. Outperforms beam search on easy/medium with large
  N.
  *Replication cost*: ~4 h H100 + tree-management code (Beeching et al.
  released a version).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — incremental over beam search; defer
  unless beam search gives signal.

- **Reward-aware compute-optimal TTS objective**:
  Target(θ, N, x, ℛ) — algorithm and N chosen jointly per (policy, PRM,
  difficulty) triple rather than per-policy alone.
  *Replication cost*: combinatorial — needs the full grid; the paper
  effectively *defines* this method.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no full grid, but yes a constrained version
  where the policy is fixed to Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B and the algorithm is chosen
  per-difficulty.

- **Pass@1-quantile difficulty binning** (easy 50–100%, medium 10–50%, hard
  0–10%). Replaces MATH's hand-labeled difficulty levels because Pass@1
  varies dramatically by policy model.
  *Replication cost*: trivial — already have K=1 correctness on 500 problems.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes, immediately — directly testable signal
  for whether prefill DoM percentile correlates with behavioral hardness
  (H-5).

- **PRM voting ablation (PRM-{Min,Last,Avg}-{Max,Vote,Majority}, 9 variants)**.
  *Replication cost*: bundled with BoN-with-PRM step.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes, as part of the BoN bake-off.

- **PRM length-bias measurement**: average tokens per scored response,
  reveals length confound between PRMs.
  *Replication cost*: ~5 min, post-hoc analysis on cached generations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly relevant to F-2 length-residual
  control story.

### Approaches & framings

- **Reward-aware compute optimality**: explicit acknowledgment that the
  optimal (algorithm, N) pair depends on the verifier as much as on the
  policy. Maps cleanly onto our H-19 framing but generalizes the verifier
  slot from "internal probe" to "any reward-source-aware verifier".

- **PRM-as-OOD-detector framing**: the paper attributes weak-PRM failure
  modes to OOD between PRM training distribution and policy generation
  distribution, paralleling our F-2 controls (length residualization) and
  F-7 (D-bucket as OOD geometry).

- **Per-policy difficulty binning**: rejects MATH's static labels in favor
  of behavior-defined bins. Naturally aligns with our A/B/C/D-bucket
  framing on Qwen2.5-1.5B (F-7) and would let us test H-5 directly.

- **TTS vs long-CoT-distillation pivot**: explicitly compares search-based
  TTS to RL/SFT-based long-CoT methods (rStar-Math, Eurus-2, SimpleRL,
  Satori, R1-Distill). On MATH-500 7B, TTS ≈ R1-Distill; on AIME24 R1-Distill
  dominates. Useful framing for the project's "verifier-routing vs reasoning
  training" axis.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MATH-500** — 500 problems from MATH test set (Lightman et al. 2024,
  same subset as our P11 cache). License: MIT. Accessibility: HF.
  Applicable? yes — this *is* our benchmark.

- **AIME24** — ~30 American Invitational Mathematics Examination problems
  (AI-MO 2024). License: open. Accessibility: HF.
  Applicable? yes — natural harder companion benchmark for any TTS extension
  experiment; we have not run it yet.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Beam width = 4 for both beam search and DVTS.
- Temperature = 0.0 for CoT, 0.7 for sampled methods (BoN, beam, DVTS).
- N (compute budget) ranges to ≥256, with N=512 used for the 1B-beats-405B
  headline.
- All policy models use the *Instruct* version (no base models).
- Voting taxonomy: PRM-Min/Last/Avg × Majority/Max/Vote = 9 variants.
- Llama-3.2-1B's outputs sometimes lack `\boxed{}`; they extract answers
  with Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct as a parser — gotcha for any 1B replication.
- Skywork-PRM-1.5B is built on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct — same family as
  our P11 base model, so no architecture-mismatch confound when scoring.
- Code: not visibly linked in the main text, but Beeching et al. 2024 (the
  DVTS reference) released search-and-learn at huggingface/search-and-learn;
  Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B is on HuggingFace at Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B.

### Replicable intermediates

- **PRM AUROC on cached P11 K=1 generations**. Smallest cross-check: load
  Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B, score the 500 cached Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-7B K=1
  trajectories from `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`, compute AUROC
  on K=1-correctness, compare to F-2's 0.7731 / 0.876 (R1).

- **PRM AUROC on cached P11 K=8 generations**. Same idea but on the K=8
  data; lets us back-compute selection-via-PRM accuracy and compare against
  selection-via-DoM (F-8 selective prediction).

- **Difficulty-bin alignment**. Bin our 500 MATH-500 K=1 problems by
  paper-style Pass@1 bins (easy/medium/hard); test whether prefill L19 DoM
  percentile predicts bin membership (cheap H-5 sanity check).

- **PRM length-bias on cached generations**. Compute correlation between
  Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B per-trajectory mean score and trajectory token length;
  feeds F-2's length-residual story.

- **No replicable check** is possible for the 1B-beats-405B headline
  itself — that requires running BoN with N=512 on Llama-3.2-1B, which is
  fresh compute we have not committed.

## 2502.06884 — Learning Conformal Abstention Policies for Adaptive Risk Management in LLMs/VLMs (Tayebati et al., 2025)

**Relevance:** Proposes CAP (Conformalized Abstention Policy), a REINFORCE-trained policy that learns two conformal thresholds (q̂_predict, q̂_abstain) over softmax-derived nonconformity scores, partitioning each query into single-prediction / set-prediction / abstention regimes. Method is signal-agnostic — it operates on any score function — so it slots cleanly above prefill-DoM, CoE, or any other correctness-predictor we hold. Directly relevant to F-8 (selective prediction) and as an ablation for F-2's softmax-vs-DoM AUROC comparison.

**Key claim we tested:** Learnable thresholds substantially outperform fixed conformal thresholds (LAC, APS) on AUARC, AUROC, ECE, and accuracy at fixed 90% coverage, using only softmax-derived scores.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** Paper's improvements (AUARC up to +21pp, ECE 70-85% reduction, AUROC up to +22pp on hallucination detection) are reported on multi-choice QA benchmarks (MMLU, CosmosQA, HellaSwag, HaluDial, HaluSum) and VLM benchmarks (MMBench, OODCV-VQA, ScienceQA, SEEDBench, AI2D). They do not transfer trivially to free-form MATH-500. P10-FE22 will run CAP on cached Qwen-2.5-1.5B prefill-DoM scores under MATH-500 1024-tok labels; outcome determines whether F-8's 71.6% at coverage 0.5 understates achievable selective-prediction performance.

**Related experiments:** P10-FE2 (static conformal abstention, TRIGGERED), P10-FE22 (CAP on prefill DoM, READY), P10-FE23 (softmax-AUROC sanity check, READY), P11-FE407 (CAP routing vs verification routing, READY blocked by P11-FE19), H-323, H-324.

### Methodologies
- CAP: REINFORCE policy network outputting Gaussian (α, β) actions over two conformal thresholds.
- Three-regime decision rule with sigmoid-mapped action probabilities (single / set / abstain).
- Cost function `C(α, β) = (1 − acc) + λ₁·avgSet + λ₂·abstention − λ₃·coverage − λ₄·div`.
- Softmax nonconformity `s(X, Y) = 1 − p_Y(X)`.
- LAC and APS conformal baselines.

### Approaches
- Abstention-as-RL-policy reframing.
- Three-regime decision replacing binary predict/abstain.
- Coverage as soft-constraint via reward shaping (loses formal distribution-free guarantee).

### Datasets
- LLM: MMLU, CosmosQA, HellaSwag, HaluDial, HaluSum.
- VLM: MMBench, OODCV-VQA, ScienceQA, SEEDBench, AI2D.
- All multi-choice. Only MMLU is plausibly applicable to text reasoning; none are MATH-500 substitutes.

### Implementation
- Code at `github.com/sinatayebati/vlm-uncertainty`.
- Models tested: LLaVA-v1.6 (7B/13B/34B), MoE-LLaVA-Phi2 (2.7B), Yi-VL-6B, Monkey-Chat-7B, InternLM-XComposer2-VL-7B, CogAgent-VQA-7B, MobileVLM-v2-7B, mPLUG-Owl2-7B, Qwen-VL-Chat-7B, Qwen-7B/14B, Yi-34B, Llama-2-7B/13B.
- Coverage target 1 − α = 0.90 across all reported experiments.
- λ₃ = 1.0 for coverage; other λ values not tabulated in main text.

### Replicable
- CAP REINFORCE policy on cached prefill-DoM scores: ~4h CPU.
- Static LAC/APS baselines on same scores: ~30min CPU.
- Softmax-AUROC sanity check: ~30min CPU if logits cached.

### Cross-paper signals
- 2402.10978 (Mohri & Hashimoto, *Conformal Factuality*) — graphed; CAP's static-threshold predecessor; METHOD_DIFFERS edge.
- 2406.15927 (Farquhar SEPs) — graphed; label-free comparator; CAP indirectly contradicts H-12.
- 2405.01563 (LLM hallucination via conformal abstention) — NOT in graph; recommend admission to round out conformal-abstention cluster.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **CAP — Conformalized Abstention Policy with REINFORCE** — policy network πθ outputs Gaussian (μ_α, σ_α, μ_β, σ_β); samples α, β as actions; computes two conformal thresholds q̂_predict and q̂_abstain on calibration scores; runs decision rule on test set; uses scalar cost as negative reward.
  *Replication cost*: ~4h CPU on cached softmax / DoM scores, no GPU needed.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — folds directly into P10-FE2 as the "learnable" arm and gives a new selective-prediction baseline for F-8.

- **Three-regime stochastic decision rule (single / set / abstain)** — sigmoid-mapped action probabilities `p_single = σ(−c·(s − q̂_predict))`, `p_abstain = σ(c·(s − q̂_abstain))`, `p_set = 1 − p_single − p_abstain`; sample one action per query.
  *Replication cost*: trivial wrapper over existing scoring functions.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — set-prediction regime has no clear analogue for free-form MATH-500 (no fixed answer set), but reformulates naturally for K-shot answer-distribution sampling.

- **Cost function `C(α, β) = (1 − acc) + λ₁·avgSet + λ₂·abstention − λ₃·coverage − λ₄·div`** — multi-objective scalarisation with entropy-balance term `div` to prevent collapse to single regime.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (5 lines).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — reusable as the reward design for any RL-based threshold tuner we build.

- **Softmax nonconformity score `s(X, Y) = 1 − p_Y(X)`** — vanilla 0-margin baseline; not novel, but used here as the *only* signal source.
  *Replication cost*: free on cached MATH-500 generations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — needed as the F-2 / F-8 softmax-AUROC sanity check.

- **LAC and APS conformal baselines** — Least Ambiguous Classifier (set = {Y' : 1 − p(Y') ≤ q̂}) and Adaptive Prediction Set (cumulative softmax mass).
  *Replication cost*: free (off-the-shelf in `mapie` or 20 lines).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — standard comparators we're missing.

### Approaches & framings

- **Abstention-as-RL-policy framing** — recasts the static "calibrated threshold + abstain-if-above" pipeline as a Markov decision process with thresholds-as-actions. Intersects F-8 directly: F-8's 50% coverage is a fixed operating point on a *deterministic* policy; this paper says the relevant object is the *policy*, not the operating point.

- **Three-regime decision (single / set / abstain) replacing binary (predict / abstain)** — adds a middle regime that admits epistemic ambiguity without paying the abstention cost. For MATH-500 this would manifest as "report top-K candidate answers" — a plausible but currently absent output mode in the project.

- **Distribution-free coverage as a *constraint* rather than a *guarantee*** — paper softens the conformal coverage guarantee to a soft target enforced via reward shaping (λ₃·coverage). This is a meaningful theoretical retreat (no longer distribution-free) that the paper does not loudly acknowledge — relevant if anyone wants to *cite* CAP as "conformal" in our docs.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MMLU** — multi-task multi-choice, ~14k Qs across 57 tasks, MIT licence, HF (`cais/mmlu`). Applicable? maybe — usable for cross-domain DoM/CoE generalisation tests but currently unused in P11. Free-form MATH-500 mismatch is the primary blocker.
- **CosmosQA** — 35k commonsense MC, HF (`cosmos_qa`). Applicable? no — far from MATH-500 domain.
- **HellaSwag** — 70k sentence-completion MC, HF (`hellaswag`). Applicable? no — irrelevant to math reasoning.
- **HaluDial / HaluSum (HaluEval)** — hallucination-labelled dialogue/summary pairs, HF (`pminervini/HaluEval`). Applicable? no — generation-style hallucination, not math correctness.
- **MMBench / OODCV-VQA / ScienceQA / SEEDBench / AI2D** — VLM benchmarks. Applicable? no — project is text-only LLM reasoning.

Net: only MMLU is even a candidate; use case is "does prefill DoM transfer to broader QA" rather than "does CAP help on MATH-500".

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Code: `https://github.com/sinatayebati/vlm-uncertainty` — reference REINFORCE implementation with policy network architecture and cost-function defaults.
- Policy network: small MLP mapping current calibration-score vector → (μ_α, σ_α, μ_β, σ_β); Gaussian action distribution.
- Action sampling: clip α, β to (0, 1); enforce α < β so q̂_predict < q̂_abstain.
- Sigmoid scaling constant `c` in stochastic action probabilities controls policy smoothness — paper does not tabulate sweep but it's a knob.
- Reward computed on a *separate test split* from calibration; without that split CAP overfits the calibration set.
- Coverage target enforced via λ₃ = 1.0 in paper's experiments; other λs are not tabulated in main text — likely tuned per dataset.
- 90% coverage is the headline target across all reported experiments — must be stated whenever citing CAP numbers, since LAC/APS use the same target.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Softmax-AUROC sanity check on Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500** — extract `1 − p_correct(answer)` from cached P11 H100 generation logits (if logits are cached; check `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`). Compute AUROC under the 1024-tok correctness labels. If softmax-AUROC matches L19 DoM 0.7731, F-2's residual-stream story is severely undercut. ~30 min CPU.
- **Static-conformal threshold sweep on prefill DoM** — implement LAC/APS-style fixed-threshold abstention on cached prefill-DoM scores from `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json`. Compare against F-8's 50% coverage operating point. Establishes the static-threshold ceiling before P10-FE2b adds learnable thresholds. ~20 min CPU.
- **3-regime decision rule on prefill DoM (deterministic)** — apply CAP's two-threshold partition (q̂_predict < q̂_abstain) to prefill-DoM scores with grid-searched α/β rather than RL-trained ones. If grid-search matches RL-trained CAP within 1% AUARC, the RL machinery is overkill; if not, RL is doing real work. ~1 h CPU.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2402.10978 (Mohri & Hashimoto, *Conformal Factuality*)** — already in graph (status: graphed). Direct precursor; CAP cites it as the static-threshold baseline that motivates RL. Edge type: METHOD_DIFFERS from 2502.06884.
- **2406.15927 (Farquhar et al., Semantic Entropy Probes / SEPs)** — already in graph (status: graphed). Cited as the label-free comparator for hallucination detection. Adds weight to the contradiction with H-12.
- **2405.01563 (LLM hallucination via conformal abstention)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Direct precursor to CAP for LLM-specific conformal abstention; would round out the conformal-abstention cluster.

## 2502.11096 — Mixture of Tunable Experts: Behavior Modification of DeepSeek-R1 at Inference Time (Dahlke, Klagges, Zecha, Merkel, Rohr, Klemm — TNG Technology Consulting, 2025)

**Relevance:** Methodologically adjacent. The paper's fTRI (functional
Token Resonance Imaging) — class-averaged differential activation
analysis to identify a sparse subset of computational units associated
with a behavior — is the discrete-routing analogue of our DoM (F-2).
fTRI's empirical success (52% refusal flip with 10 of 14,848 experts,
no MT-Bench loss) raises the open question whether correctness in our
dense Qwen-2.5 models is similarly sparse-and-basis-aligned at L19, in
which case F-2's continuous DoM is a lossy projection. The paper is on
a different model family (DeepSeek-R1 MoE, 671B) and a different
behavior (refusal, reasoning language), so transfer is hypothetical, not
direct. Three FEs (P11-FE408, P11-FE409, P11-FE410) and three Hs (H-325,
H-326, H-327) are proposed to translate fTRI from MoE-routing to dense
MLP-neuron level on cached pathway11 activations.

**Key claim we tested:** Behavior in large MoE models is partially
encoded in a small number of basis-aligned computational units (experts)
identifiable via class-averaged differential activation. Translation to
our setting: correctness in dense models is partially encoded in a
small number of basis-aligned MLP neurons at L19, identifiable via the
same class-differencing method.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** Architecture mismatch (MoE vs dense) means
the headline claim does not transfer literally; the methodological
translation is testable on existing cached activations and is the
subject of P11-FE408 and H-325.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE408, P11-FE409, P11-FE410, P10-FE24, H-325,
H-326, H-327.

**Status:** TO TEST.

### Methodologies extracted

- **fTRI (functional Token Resonance Imaging) — class-averaged
  differential activation.** For each behavior class, average
  prompt-aggregated expert-activation maps; subtract the average over
  all other classes; identify top-K experts by resonance. Equivalent to
  a one-vs-rest mean-difference filter on a binarized activation
  signal.
  *Replication cost*: 2–4h CPU on cached `pathway11_h100/prefill`
  MLP-intermediate activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — it is the cheapest direct test of
  Refutation 1.

- **Routing override (suppress / stimulate).** At inference, force
  selected experts' router weights to 0 (suppress) or to max-of-row
  (stimulate) and renormalize the remaining top-k. Dense analogue is
  zeroing or boosting individual MLP-neuron post-activations at L19.
  *Replication cost*: 1d H100 to re-run MATH-500 K=1 on Qwen-1.5B
  with one-line forward-pass hook.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — it is the test for Refutation 4 /
  H-1.

- **t-SNE on activation maps as cluster-discovery probe.** Pure
  visualization; we already have UMAP+PCA on prefill in
  `pathway11_h100`. Low novelty.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (1h CPU).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — we already have equivalent.

- **Parameterized prompt template (Cartesian product) for behavior
  elicitation.** "What happened {time}{place}?" → 756 prompts; cheap
  way to construct controlled behavior datasets without LLM-generated
  ambiguity.
  *Replication cost*: 1h to author template + run inference.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: not for current findings, but worth
  remembering for any future refusal / abstention experiment under
  H-12.

- **Random-expert ablation control.** Always include random-K
  ablation as the null distribution.
  *Replication cost*: same as the targeted ablation.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — must be paired with FE74's targeted
  neuron ablation.

- **MT-Bench impact assay.** 80 multi-turn questions, 7 categories.
  Cheap regression check that an intervention has not broken general
  capability.
  *Replication cost*: 1–2h H100.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — must accompany any steering / DoM
  intervention to prevent hidden capability damage (cf. F-6 inversion
  artefact lessons).

### Approaches & framings

- **"Behavior is partially encoded in a small number of basis-aligned
  units"** — sparse-localization framing as an alternative to
  continuous-subspace framing. Directly intersects F-2/F-3/F-9 (which
  are continuous-subspace claims) and H-1/H-12 (which are
  continuous-direction interventions).
- **System 1 / System 2 framing for behavior classes (REFUSED /
  ALIGNED / REASONED).** Maps onto our A/B/C/D buckets with the
  observation that A-bucket may be System 1 (no CoT inflation needed)
  and D-bucket may be System 2 with broken collective signature. Worth
  noting for F-7 narrative but not load-bearing.
- **"Specialization emerges naturally from large expert count without
  training-time pressure"** — relevant to F-1's universality claim
  (sparse basis-aligned structure may be a generic property of
  high-dimensional models, not architecture-specific).

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **756-prompt "What happened {time}{place}?" Cartesian template** —
  custom, presumably released. License unclear. Not directly
  applicable to MATH-500.
- **CCP Sensitive Prompts (Promptfoo, HF dataset)** — 1,360 prompts;
  HF-public. Applicable: no — refusal-flavored, off our axis (math
  reasoning correctness).
- **600-prompt math + reasoning-language template** — custom. Not
  applicable to our pipeline.
- **MT-Bench (LMSYS, 80 multi-turn)** — public, well-known.
  Applicable: yes — should be added as a sanity-check regression
  benchmark for any FE that modifies inference (FE74 in particular).

### Implementation details worth capturing

- DeepSeek-R1: 14,848 routed experts across 58 MoE layers, 256
  experts/layer, top-k=8, plus 1 shared expert/layer.
- Suppression: set targeted expert's gate weight to 0 in top-k softmax
  output, *renormalize remaining top-k*. Crucially — they do *not*
  re-route to alternates; the gate vector is normalized post-zero. The
  dense analogue is zeroing post-GELU MLP neurons at L19, not
  zeroing-and-replacing.
- Stimulation: insert target expert into top-k irrespective of its
  gate; evict the lowest-weighted current top-k member; set target's
  weight to row-max; renormalize. The "evict lowest" detail matters —
  if naively appended, the top-(k+1) softmax dilutes everyone.
- Inference stack: 8× H100 NVL, modified vLLM. Authors note vLLM
  modifications are intended to be released.
- Top-10 distinctive experts for refusal (their Appendix A): layers
  span 14–53 (i.e., not concentrated near input or output). For our
  L19 hypothesis, this suggests checking *all* layers, not only L19.
- Stimulation produces smaller effects than suppression (10% vs 40%);
  asymmetry note — "refusal is easier to break than to enforce". This
  is the opposite asymmetry from F-4 ("correct trajectories collapse
  harder than incorrect"). Worth a paragraph in HYPOTHESES.
- MT-Bench scores actually *improved* with refusal experts suppressed
  (8.97 vs 8.72 average). Sample size n=80; not significant, but a
  hint that refusal circuitry imposes a measurable cost.

### Replicable intermediates

- **fTRI-on-MLP-neurons sanity check** — apply class-averaged
  differential activation to L19 MLP intermediate activations on
  `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` cached NPZs (have prefill
  activations + correct/incorrect labels for all 500 MATH-500 problems
  on Qwen-1.5B). Compute one-vs-rest mean differences for both
  {correct, incorrect} and {A, B, C, D buckets}. Score AUROC of
  `sum(top-K neurons)` for K ∈ {1, 5, 10, 50}; compare to 0.7731.
  No GPU required; CPU only.
- **Top-K Jaccard between prefill and final-token differential
  neuron sets** — same activations + the cached final-token
  activations from `scratch/pathway10_temporal_and_verifier_results.json`.
  CPU only.
- **Per-bucket distinctive-neuron count** — on the same cached
  activations, with bucket labels from `pathway11_h100`. Plot
  histograms of differential-activation z-scores per bucket; count
  neurons above z=5. CPU only.

### Cross-paper signals

- 2501.12948 — already in graph (status: graphed,
  admission_only). DeepSeek-R1 base model. Connection: this paper's
  target.
- 2401.06066 — NOT in graph; recommend admission. DeepSeekMoE
  architecture paper, foundation for the experts/shared-experts

- 2406.04093 — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Gao et al.,
  *Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders*. Direct

  models. Strong candidate for our SAE pathway (P10-FE5
  triggered by 2604.19974 already plans an SAE; this paper
  precedes that work).
- 2401.04088 — NOT in graph; lower-priority admission. Mixtral.
