## 2509.13450 — SteeringSafety: A Systematic Safety Evaluation Framework of Representation Steering in LLMs (Siu, Crispino, Park, Henry, Wang, Liu, Song, Wang, 2025)

**Relevance:** Direct methodological precedent and benchmark for any P11 steering
experiment. The paper systematizes five training-free steering methods (DIM, ACE,
CAA, PCA, LAT) into a direction generation × selection × application decomposition,
runs them across three models (Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B; plus
Qwen-2.5-1.5B/3B for scaling) on 17 datasets across seven safety perspectives, and
quantifies effectiveness (in-domain) vs. entanglement (out-of-domain side effects).
Core findings: DIM is consistent; all methods entangle substantially (social
behaviors degrade up to 76%, hallucination steering shifts political views,
jailbreaking compromises commonsense morality); KL<0.1 Alpaca filter is required to
keep directions steering-eligible; conditional steering (CAST) Pareto-dominates
global steering. Directly bears on F-2 (DIM is structurally our DoM construction),
F-3 (their direction-application axis is the right vocabulary for our orthogonality
finding), and H-1 (our planned per-position DoM steering must adopt their KL filter
and entanglement panel to be defensible).

**Key claim we tested:** Representation steering methods produce reliable
in-distribution effectiveness only when filtered by KL<0.1 on Alpaca, and even then
they entangle substantially across out-of-distribution safety axes.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** Three concrete experiments are proposed: P11-FE552
(layer-AUROC sweep), P11-FE553 (KL-on-Alpaca check for our L19 prefill DoM), and
P11-FE554 (smallest-possible H-1 ablation prototype). Until those run, we cannot
say whether F-2's direction is steering-eligible or whether H-1 is methodologically
viable.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE552, P11-FE553, P11-FE554, P11-FE555, P11-FE556,
H-441, H-442, H-443, H-1.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **DiffInMeans (DIM) direction generation** — mean(activations | positive class) −
  mean(activations | negative class), one direction per layer.
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU on cached prefill activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — already operationally identical to our DoM extraction.
- **Affine Concept Editing (ACE)** — DIM + DirectionalAblation + an affine offset to
  the residual stream (Marshall et al. 2024). One additional bias term per layer.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached prefill activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — minimal cost, would test whether the affine
  addition improves selective-prediction beyond F-2's pure direction.
- **DirectionalAblation** — project residual stream onto direction's complement
  (`x_new = x - (x·d/d·d) d`), applied at every token.
  *Replication cost*: 30min on H100 with K=1 generation, MATH-500.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — this is the canonical "remove the direction"
  intervention and the right primitive for any H-1 protocol.
- **CAA-style ActAdd at POST_INSTRUCTION tokens** — add direction × scale to
  residual stream only at tokens after the user instruction.
  *Replication cost*: 30min on H100.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — competing protocol vs. ALL-tokens DIM ablation.
- **PCA-direction (top eigenvector of correctness-class activation covariance)**
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — sanity-checks whether DoM and PC1 are aligned.
- **LAT (Linear Artificial Tomography)** — RepE-format prompts, direction extraction
  via per-prompt activations, applied cumulatively across a sequence of layers.
  *Replication cost*: 2h H100 (needs RepE-format prompt rewrite).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: marginal — only if cumulative-layer steering is on the
  roadmap.
- **Conditional steering (CAST)** — apply intervention only when input activation
  similarity to a "trigger direction" exceeds learned threshold. Wraps any of the
  above.
  *Replication cost*: 1–2h CPU + 1h H100 for evaluation.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — ROI is high because it Pareto-dominates global
  steering in their results, and gives H-1 a defensible knob for entanglement.
- **KL-divergence check on Alpaca for direction-validity filtering** — drop any
  candidate (layer, direction, scale) tuple whose final-token KL on Alpaca prompts
  exceeds 0.1.
  *Replication cost*: 30min H100 across our existing direction candidates.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — cheap and gates whether F-2's direction is even
  *eligible* as a steering vector by current-best-practice criteria.
- **Effectiveness / Entanglement aggregate metrics** (Eq. 1 + 2 in §2.1) — normalized
  improvement on target perspective (effectiveness), L2-aggregated deviation across
  out-of-distribution perspectives (entanglement).
  *Replication cost*: trivial once we have multi-task evals.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — adopt as the success metric for any future H-1
  variant.
- **Grid search over 25–80th percentile of layers, step 2** — restrict candidate
  layers to mid-network.
  *Replication cost*: trivial; we already have all-layer activations cached.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — a sweep would directly test whether L19 is the
  AUROC-peak or just a single sample.

### Approaches & framings

- **Direction generation × selection × application as orthogonal axes.** The paper
  decomposes steering into three independent choices. Our project currently
  treats DoM as a monolith ("a direction at L19 used the way DoM was extracted"),
  which conflates extraction and application. Adopting this decomposition would
  let us write F-2/F-3/H-1 in terms that compose with the literature.
- **Effectiveness ⊥ Entanglement, both required for any steering claim.**
  Their Eq. 1 + Eq. 2 framing means that *every* future selective-prediction or
  steering claim in our project should report not only the in-domain metric (e.g.,
  MATH-500 K=1 accuracy or AUROC) but also a vector of out-of-domain deviations.
  This intersects all of F-2, F-8, H-1, H-19.
- **Conditional vs. global intervention as a Pareto axis.** Their conditional
  steering result is the strongest practical takeaway. If we want any of our
  steering hypotheses (H-1, H-19) to be competitive with current literature, the
  default protocol should be conditional, not global.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **SaladBench (Li et al. 2024b)** — harmful QA, GPT-4o-filtered, with Alpaca
  negative pairs. License: research-only. HF-accessible. Applicable? no — not a
  reasoning task; orthogonal to MATH-500.
- **BBQ (Parrish et al. 2022)** — implicit-bias MCQ. HF. Applicable? no — bias
  framing, but useful as a SteeringSafety-style entanglement panel for any future
  H-1 run on Qwen.
- **ToxiGen (Hartvigsen et al. 2022)** — explicit-bias binary classification. HF.
  Applicable? no.
- **FaithEval intrinsic-hallucination subsets** (counterfactual, inconsistent,
  unanswerable). HF. Applicable? **yes** — closest analogue to our 1024-tok
  correctness regime; would let us test whether L19 prefill DoM transfers to
  intrinsic-hallucination prediction.
- **PreciseWikiQA (HalluLens, Bang et al. 2025)** — extrinsic hallucination.
  Generated with LLaMA-3.1-70B-Instruct. HF/research. Applicable? marginal — out
  of our model size range without re-extraction.
- **DarkBench (Kran et al. 2025)** — social behaviors (sycophancy, brand bias,
  anthropomorphism, user retention). HF. Applicable? no, but useful entanglement
  panel.
- **GPQA (Rein et al. 2023)** — expert MCQ. HF. Applicable? **yes** — a small,
  hard reasoning benchmark we could run as an H-1 entanglement check.
- **ARC-C (Clark et al. 2018)** — simple-reasoning MCQ. HF. Applicable? **yes** —
  cheap entanglement panel for any future H-1 run.
- **TruthfulQA (Lin et al. 2022)** — binary truth-vs-plausible-false. HF.
  Applicable? **yes** — already in many of our cited papers; cheap entanglement
  signal.
- **DecodingTrust commonsense morality** (Wang et al. 2024a). HF. Applicable? no.
- **TwinViews-13k (Fulay et al. 2024)** — political views agreement. HF.
  Applicable? no.
- **Alpaca (Taori et al. 2023)** — neutral instruction prompts used for the KL
  filter. HF. Applicable? **yes** — direct dependency for the KL<0.1 filter.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Code: <https://github.com/wang-research-lab/SteeringSafety>.
- Layer-search range: 25–80th percentile, step 2. For 28-layer Qwen-2.5-1.5B that
  maps to layers 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21 — note L19 is *inside* the range but
  not centered.
- Direction extraction uses **input** to the transformer block (pre-LN, pre-attn).
  Confirm whether our cached activations are pre- or post-LN and reconcile before
  any cross-comparison.
- KL divergence threshold: 0.1 on the *last-token probabilities* over Alpaca
  prompts. Average across prompts; reject (layer, direction, scale) above 0.1.
- Application positions: ALL (every token), POST_INSTRUCTION (tokens after user
  prompt), or cumulative across a sequence of layers. Method-dependent.
- Models all use IT/Instruct variants; our P11 work is on Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Instruct
  + Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, so format compatibility is good.
- Conditional steering implementation follows CAST (Lee et al. 2024); they use
  similarity-threshold gating computed from a held-out trigger set.

### Replicable intermediates

## 2509.22067 — The Rogue Scalpel: Activation Steering Compromises LLM Safety (Korznikov, Galichin, Dontsov, Rogov, Oseledets, Tutubalina, 2026)

**Relevance:** Direct evidence on the side-effects, calibration, and null-baselines for any activation-steering experiment, which is the entire family of H-1 / H-17. The paper's finding that 817/1000 SAE features and most random unit vectors at MMLU-safe coefficients perturb model behavior in a wide-spread, prompt-specific way is a strong null hypothesis against our F-2 framing of prefill-L19 DoM as a "privileged correctness direction." The App. E result that the top-30 most-harmful SAE features have cos=0.027 ± 0.021 with the Arditi refusal direction — i.e., the labeled-interpretable direction is not what's doing the work — directly parallels and pressures our F-3 cos=0.046 observation between prefill and final-token DoM.

**Key claim we tested:** Activation steering at MMLU-safe coefficients (c≤0.75 for Llama3.1-8B; c≤0.5 for Qwen-style) produces broad, direction-agnostic behavioral perturbations that are statistically indistinguishable from random steering across SAE-derived "interpretable" features. Specific to our pipeline: random unit vectors at L19 should also predict / perturb MATH-500 correctness comparably to the prefill_DoM, if the DoM is operating as a generic high-leverage perturbation rather than a privileged direction.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** No replication run yet. Four FutureExperiments (P11-FE557, P11-FE558, P11-FE559, P11-FE560) cover the random-vector null for AUROC, cosine geometry, steering accuracy, and per-layer dependence respectively. The lightest cross-checks (P11-FE557 — 20 min CPU; P11-FE558 — 5 min CPU) can be run today against cached P11 NPZs.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE557, P11-FE558, P11-FE559, P11-FE560; H-444, H-445, H-446, H-447; bears on H-1, H-17, F-2, F-3, F-10.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Adaptive-norm steering coefficient** — `α = c · μ^(l)` where μ^(l) is the average activation norm at layer *l* across the dataset. Normalizes intervention strength across models/layers.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU (compute μ^(l) on cached prefill activations).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a principled α for any future H-1 / DoM-steering experiment.

- **Random-vector null baseline for steering** — sample N unit vectors uniformly from S^(d-1), measure effect distribution, treat per-vector mean as null.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU per 100 vectors on cached AUROC pipeline; 1h H100 per 10 vectors on generation pipeline.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly tests whether prefill-DoM is a privileged direction (refutation 2 above).

- **Universal-attack via averaged jailbreak vectors** — sample 1000 random vectors, keep the 20 that jailbreak a single prompt, mean-and-renormalize to get a transferable attack vector.
  *Replication cost*: 1 H100 day for the sampling pass.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — irrelevant to math-correctness; we don't care about jailbreak transfer.

- **LLM-as-judge with precision-bounded eval** — Qwen3-8B in reasoning mode classifies each generation as SAFE/UNSAFE; human-validate on a sample to bound precision (94%). Incoherent outputs default to SAFE.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU per 100 generations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — math correctness has a ground-truth answer; LLM-as-judge is overkill.

- **MMLU sweet-spot calibration** — sweep c, find largest c such that MMLU drops <1%, use that for downstream steering experiments.
  *Replication cost*: 4h H100 (MMLU is 14k questions).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — *partial*: substitute MATH-500 for MMLU since our regime is reasoning, not general capability. Pre-condition for any honest H-1 experiment.

- **Special-token steering exclusion** — exclude `<bos>`, `<start_of_turn>`, etc. from steering (cite Lin & Bloom 2023). Improves coherence.
  *Replication cost*: free (a one-line mask).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — should be folded into any H-1 implementation.

- **Layer-trichotomy steering depth sweep** — apply at ⌊L/3⌋, ⌊L/2⌋, ⌊2L/3⌋ as canonical comparison points (cite Wu et al. 2025 / AxBench).
  *Replication cost*: 3× single-layer cost.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — refutation 4 above; useful for testing H-17 RoPE-mechanical claim.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Precise control over internals does not guarantee precise control over behavior"** — the paper's central reframing. Direct challenge to the linear-representation-hypothesis-as-design-tool. Intersects F-2/F-3: if our DoM is "interpretable" only in the sense that benign SAE features are interpretable (i.e., the labels are post-hoc), then DoM-as-correctness-encoding is over-claiming.
- **Steering as generic perturbation rather than concept injection** — the framing that 817/1000 SAE features all jailbreak suggests perturbations of a particular *magnitude* matter more than perturbations of a particular *direction*. Bears on F-2's framing of L19 DoM as a privileged direction.
- **Disclaimer-then-compliance / fictional-framing failure modes** — the model produces a safety preamble then violates it, or wraps harmful content in fiction. Not directly applicable to MATH-500 (no safety preamble), but a useful caution: under steering, our 1.5B may produce fluent CoT that still arrives at wrong answers — coherence is not correctness.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **JailbreakBench** — 100 harmful prompts × 10 categories. License: open. Applicable? **no** — math-correctness is the target, not safety/refusal.
- **MMLU** — capability benchmark used for sweet-spot calibration. Applicable? **partial** — we'd substitute MATH-500 for the calibration role; MMLU itself isn't our regime.
- **Goodfire SAE for Llama3.1-8B layer 19** — open-source SAE from Goodfire. Accessibility: HF / open. Applicable? **no** — our pipeline is Qwen-2.5-1.5B, mismatched architecture/scale; we'd need a Qwen SAE (Galichin et al. 2503.18878 trains one but not at our scale).

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Greedy decoding throughout (matches our P11 K=1 convention).
- α = c · μ^(l) with c ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0}.
- Steering applied to *both* prompt and generation tokens (cite Durmus et al. 2024).
- Special tokens excluded from steering (cite Lin & Bloom 2023).
- LLM-as-judge: Qwen3-8B in reasoning mode, precision 94% on harmful class.
- Sweet-spot c values: Llama3.1-8B → 0.75; Qwen2.5-7B → 0.5; Falcon3-7B → 0.5.
- Universal attack: 100–500 random trials suffice to find 20 single-prompt jailbreakers.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Random-vector AUROC null distribution.** Load the cached `pathway11_h100/prefill_l19_activations.npz` (per-problem prefill L19 vectors) + correctness labels. For each of 1000 random unit vectors v, compute the projection score and OOF AUROC. Report the 50th / 95th / 99th percentile. Compares directly to F-2's 0.7731. **20 min CPU**, fully cached.
- **Cosine null between DoM and random.** Compute cos(prefill_DoM, v_i) for 1000 random unit vectors; report mean, std, and percentile of the F-3 cos=0.046 observation. **5 min CPU**, fully cached.
- **DoM ↔ refusal-direction proxy alignment.** We don't have Arditi's Llama refusal direction for Qwen-2.5-1.5B, but we can substitute: train a binary "refuse vs comply" probe on Qwen-2.5-1.5B prefill activations using JailbreakBench prompts (paper-released, open) + benign Alpaca prompts. Compute cos(prefill_DoM_correctness, refusal_direction_qwen). If near-zero (matching paper's 0.027), correctness and refusal live in different subspaces — separates the questions. **2h CPU + 1h H100** (the H100 is for one prefill pass over 200 prompts).

### Cross-paper signals

## 2509.24988 — Generalized Correctness Models: Learning Calibrated and Model-Agnostic Correctness Predictors from Historical Patterns (Xiao, Patil, Lee, Stengel-Eskin, Bansal, 2025)

**Relevance:** A frontal challenge to the implicit "self-knowledge" framing of our prefill L19 DoM (F-2). The paper establishes via RQ1 that an LLM has no privileged access to its own correctness — Qwen2.5-7B predicting Llama3.1-8B is as good as Llama predicting itself. RQ2A then trains a Generalized Correctness Model (Qwen3-8B finetuned on 8 model histories) that beats both Specific Correctness Models trained on each target and the self-emitted P(True) of much larger models (Llama-3-70B). The result challenges our framing in two ways: (a) the predictive content of L19 prefill may be a generic question-answer-readability axis rather than an internal-self signal; (b) our F-8 selective-prediction story is operating-point-bound and underexplored against history-aware baselines.

**Key claim we tested:** Their RQ1 says self-knowledge does not exist for purposes of correctness prediction; their downstream story says GCMs beat single-model probes on selective prediction.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — we have not run the text-only-CM-vs-DoM comparison. The paper's headline numbers (Acc 0.820 / ECE 0.023 / AUROC 0.890 on Llama3.1-8B MMLU; AURC 0.069 vs Llama-3-70B P(True) 0.108) are on MMLU/TriviaQA short-form, not our 1024-tok MATH-500 reasoning. Whether RQ1's no-self-knowledge result transfers to long-CoT reasoning is the empirical question.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE561, P11-FE562, P11-FE563, P11-FE564, P11-FE565; H-448, H-449, H-450, H-451

**Status:** TO TEST (HIGH priority — refutation pressure on F-2 / F-8 / H-12)

### Methodologies extracted

- **Specific Correctness Model (SCM)** — LoRA rank 32, batch size 16, 1 epoch, ~10k examples, Qwen3-8B base, finetune as a P(True) classifier on a single target model's history. *Replication cost*: 1–2h H100 per target model. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct competitor to F-2's L19 DoM as an MATH-500 correctness predictor.
- **Generalized Correctness Model (GCM)** — same recipe but train on the concatenation of correctness datasets from 8 different LLMs. *Replication cost*: 4–8h H100 once if we collect MATH-500 K=1 histories for ≥4 models. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — refutation experiment for "self-knowledge" framing of F-2.
- **Answerless / Answer-only / Full ablation framework** — three CMs trained on `P(c|q)`, `P(c|q, r̂)`, `P(c|q, r̂, r)` to attribute predictive contribution to query, answer, and full response. *Replication cost*: 3× the SCM cost. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — clean attribution test for whether MATH-500 prefill DoM is doing more than reading the question.
- **P(True) extraction prompt** — verbatim "Please respond just 'yes' or 'no' in lowercase if [Model Name] will respond correctly to Model Prompt:" with logit of token "yes" as confidence. *Replication cost*: zero training; ~1h CPU/GPU eval per (target × dataset). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — easy zero-training baseline we don't currently have for MATH-500.
- **k=5 semantic-ICL retrieval via Chroma vector DB** — embed the train split of `(q, r, r̂, c)` tuples, retrieve top-5 by similarity at eval time, inject as context, elicit verbalized confidence. *Replication cost*: 30min CPU once history is collected. *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — high inference cost per query but cleanly compares to F-2 without finetuning.
- **Spline calibration as posthoc layer** — Lucena 2018 spline calibration applied on top of the CM logits using as little as 5% of target dataset. *Replication cost*: minutes CPU. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly applicable to the existing prefill-DoM scores to drop ECE without retraining.
- **Specialized batch-size selection for ECE ≤ 0.03** — appendix C of the paper claims an "optimal batch size" yields well-calibrated CMs out of the box with vanilla cross-entropy. *Replication cost*: minimal once SCM pipeline exists. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes if SCM/GCM gets stood up.

### Approaches & framings

- **Self-knowledge ≠ correctness prediction.** The paper reframes correctness prediction as *historical pattern recognition*, not introspection. This is a frontal challenge to the implicit framing in P10 and F-2 that "the residual stream knows things about itself" — if the paper is right, the L19 prefill direction is a generic question-answer-readability axis, not a self-aware confidence axis. Intersects F-2 / F-3 / H-5.
- **CM as a probe of *what training data is sufficient for correctness prediction*.** By systematically ablating conditioning variables, the paper turns the CM from a black-box scoring system into a controlled lens on which features carry correctness information. Useful template for ablating MATH-500 prefill features beyond "DoM works".
- **Forecasting analogy with explicit history.** Frames calibration as a Brier-style forecasting problem and identifies "history" as the missing component vs human forecasters. Suggests our F-8 selective-prediction story is incomplete without an explicit history-of-predictions module.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MMLU** — 57 subject MCQ benchmark. ~14k questions, public HF. Applicable? **partial** — not our reasoning regime (1024-tok labels, MATH-500), but a clean cross-task generalization target.
- **TriviaQA** — short-form QA, ~95k questions, public HF. Applicable? **no** — too far from MATH-500 reasoning.
- **18 correctness datasets built by the authors** — MMLU + TriviaQA × 8 models each + 2 OOD. License: presumably released with code at https://github.com/The-Inscrutable-X/CalibratedModelAgnosticCorrectness. Applicable? **yes** — drop-in training material for a cross-task GCM experiment if we want to see whether their MMLU-trained GCM transfers to MATH-500 directly.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- LoRA rank 32, batch size 16, 1 epoch, ~10k examples → calibrated CM out of the box.
- Average MMLU response length: 198 tokens. Their prompts are dramatically shorter than our 1024-tok regime.
- ECE evaluated with both standard and RMSCE (Hendrycks 2019 adaptive binning) — RMSCE is the more robust metric we should adopt.
- Spline calibration (Lucena 2018) outperforms the alternatives in their appendix H.
- Code repo: https://github.com/The-Inscrutable-X/CalibratedModelAgnosticCorrectness — pull this for the SCM/GCM training scripts and the prompt templates.
- Compute footprint: GCM eval at 0.125s/example, 7.3 minutes for 3511 MMLU samples on Qwen3-8B; ICL adds 20× to that (2.6s/example).
- They use a Qwen3-8B reasoning model as base; reasoning models with `<think>` blocks are out-of-distribution — the GCM trained on non-reasoning histories still beats Qwen3-32B reasoning model's P(True), which is interesting for our 1.5B/7B non-reasoning baseline analysis.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Cheap text-only baseline**: take `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json`, extract per-problem (question, K=1 response, K=1 correctness), prompt Qwen3-8B with the paper's verbatim P(True) template, compute AUROC. **Cost: 1h H100 once Qwen3-8B is loaded.** This is the *zero-training* GCM-equivalent number to compare against F-2's 0.7731. If P(True) on Qwen3-8B reading 1.5B's responses ≥ 0.7, we have an immediate refutation pressure on F-2.
- **Cross-model self-vs-cross test on cached MATH-500**: prompt Qwen-2.5-1.5B and Qwen-2.5-7B each to predict the other's correctness on MATH-500 with the P(True) template; compare to self-prediction. Replicates the paper's RQ1 in our setting in <2h H100.
- **Spline-calibrate the existing prefill-DoM scores**: take the OOF prefill-DoM probe outputs from `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json`, fit Lucena 2018 spline calibration on a 5% holdout, recompute ECE/RMSCE on the rest. Cost: 5min CPU. Direct replicable check on whether DoM ECE drops without changing AUROC.

## 2510.01105 — Geometric Properties of Neural Multivariate Regression (Andriopoulos, Dong, Adhikari, Ross, 2025)

**Relevance:** Provides a manifold-geometric framework (intrinsic dimension
ID_H of features vs ID_Y of targets) that *predicts the opposite direction*
of our F-4 asymmetric-collapse finding when imported to LLM next-token
prediction (Sard-theorem-based unavoidable-error argument). Also supplies
TwoNN, an across-family alternative to participation-ratio that complements
H-16's within-family Marchenko-Pastur correction, and NRC1, a per-trajectory
PCA-residual collapse metric that gives us a clean diagnostic for the F-4
direction question. No language/transformer experiments in the paper itself
— the methodologies (TwoNN, NRC1, layer-wise ID profile) are what transfer.

**Key claim we tested:** "Collapsed models exhibit ID_H < ID_Y, leading to
over-compression and poor generalization." Imported to our setting: more-
collapsed (lower-ID) final-token residuals should produce *worse* outputs,
not better — the opposite of F-4.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** Both F-4 inversion test (H-458 / FE-72) and per-
layer ID profile test (H-459 / FE-73) are READY on cached NPZs and pending.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE574 (TwoNN breathing reproduction), P11-FE575
(NRC1 vs F-4 direction), P11-FE576 (per-layer ID profile vs F-9), H-458, H-459,
H-460.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **TwoNN (Two-Nearest-Neighbor) intrinsic dimension estimator.** For each
  point, take r₁, r₂ to first and second NN; ratio μ = r₂/r₁ follows Pareto
  CDF F(μ) = 1 − μ^(−d) under local uniformity; estimate d by linear
  regression of log-transformed pairs through the origin. Stable for ID < ~20
  with modest n; scale-aware via subsampling.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached pathway11_h100 NPZs — small
  Python call, no extra dependencies.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — cleanest cross-check on participation-ratio
  breathing using a non-eigenvalue-based estimator; complements H-16
  (Marchenko-Pastur) along the orthogonal "estimator family" axis.

- **NRC1 metric (Neural Regression Collapse residual).** With normalized
  feature vectors h̃_i and the d×n matrix H_PCA of top-n principal components
  (n = target dim), NRC1 = (1/M) Σ_i ‖h̃_i − proj(h̃_i | H_PCA)‖². Small NRC1
  ⇒ features collapse to an n-dim subspace.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached MATH-500 L19 NPZs (need to pick what
  plays the role of "n = target dim" — vocab embedding rank? answer-token
  basis?).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — provides a per-trajectory collapse measure
  to test the F-4 NRC1-vs-correctness direction (Refutation 1).

- **Layer-wise ID profile as a model-state diagnostic** (their Figure 5).
  Track ID across all hidden layers; monotonic decay = healthy/non-collapsed,
  non-monotonic = collapsed. Their use is qualitative; we'd use it as a
  feature vector.
  *Replication cost*: 2h CPU — already have per-layer L0–L27 activations
  cached for the MATH-500 pathway11 sweep.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly tests F-9 redundancy (Refutation 4).

- **Weight-decay-as-ID-knob protocol.** Sweep λ_WD ∈ {0, 1e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4,
  5e-4, 7e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3} during training; track NRC1 + ID_H evolution;
  identifies regime boundary.
  *Replication cost*: requires retraining — H100 days for any meaningful LLM
  scale; not feasible at the 1.5B+ scale we operate.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — far outside our compute envelope; flag as
  literature-only.

- **Sard-theorem framing for over-compression bound.** Theorem 1: smooth map
  from m-manifold to n-manifold with m < n cannot be surjective. Imports
  cleanly to LLM next-token prediction if one frames the unembedding linear
  layer as a regression onto vocab logits.
  *Replication cost*: derivation only.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: this is a framing tool, not an experiment —
  worth citing in PROJECT_RECORD §1f if Refutation 1 fires.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Two regimes" framing — over-compressed (ID_H < ID_Y) vs under-compressed
  (ID_H > ID_Y).** Reframes feature dimensionality as a *bidirectional*
  knob rather than a "more-is-better" or "compression-is-better" axis. For
  our LLM work, this re-frames asymmetric collapse (F-4) into a question
  about which side of an effective regression-collapse threshold the
  per-trajectory L19 representation sits on. Sharper than the current
  PR-amplitude-as-confidence story.

- **Content-vs-regularization causal axis.** The paper *operationalizes*
  the regularization-driven account of dimensional structure (weight decay
  → ID_H → collapse). Our F-5 (content-dependent) implicitly rejects this;
  the paper provides a concrete experimental knob to challenge that rejection.

- **Manifold-topological lower bound on regression error.** Sard-based
  unavoidable-error argument is a different shape of theoretical claim
  than the AUROC/PR-based empirical claims dominating our findings, and
  its import is to predict *unsolvable* over-compressed regimes — relevant
  for D-bucket interpretation under F-7.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MuJoCo D4RL locomotion** (Swimmer 8/2, Reacher 11/2, Hopper 11/3,
  Halfcheetah 17/6, Ant 111/8 — input-dim/target-dim). 20K samples each.
  HF/public. Applicable? **no** — continuous-control regression, no
  language signal.
- **MNIST-regression (synthetic)** — 50K, grayscale 28×28 → 25-dim target,
  target ID ≈ 8.02. Public. Applicable? **no** — synthetic regression task,
  off-domain for MATH-500.
- **CIFAR-10-regression (synthetic)** — 50K, RGB 32×32×3 → 10-dim target,
  target ID ≈ 9.51. Public. Applicable? **no** — same.

(No language/sequence data in the paper; their method-set, not their data,
is what transfers.)

### Implementation details worth capturing

- MLP grid: depth ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, width ∈ {64, 128, 256, 512, 1024}, ReLU.
- Optimizer: Adam, lr 1e-3 to 5e-3.
- Weight-decay sweep (the load-bearing one): λ_WD ∈ {0, 1e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4,
  5e-4, 7e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, …}.
- TwoNN linear regression is fitted *through the origin* on log-transformed
  (log μ, −log(1 − F_emp(μ))) pairs — easy to mis-implement.
- NRC1 uses *normalized* h̃_i (unit norm) — without normalization, scale
  contaminates the residual.
- Layer-wise ID is computed at every hidden layer with the same TwoNN
  protocol (their Figure 5 panel).

### Replicable intermediates

  MATH-500, cached pathway11_h100 NPZs). Compare per-token TwoNN curve to
  the existing PR breathing curve in
  `scratch/pathway10_temporal_and_verifier_results.json`. Smallest cross-check

- **NRC1 per problem on final-token L19 residuals**, with target subspace =

  Compare NRC1(correct) vs NRC1(incorrect) — direct test of Refutation 1.
- **Per-layer TwoNN-ID profile (28 entries) per problem** from cached L0–L27
  activations. Logistic-regress on correctness, OOF 5-fold; compare AUROC
  against L19-DoM = 0.7731 baseline (F-9 redundancy test).
- **NRC1 vs PR scatterplot** on the same residuals, to assess whether NRC1
  and PR are measuring the same axis or two separate axes (informs whether
  Refutation 1 and the existing F-4 are even commensurable).

## 2510.01591 — CLUE: Non-parametric Verification from Experience via Hidden-State Clustering (Liang et al., Tencent AI Lab, 2025)

**Relevance:** Direct same-pipeline competitor. CLUE uses an L×D activation-delta matrix `Δh = h(end-of-</think>) − h(start-of-<think>)` and classifies new traces by layer-averaged Euclidean distance to success/failure centroids built from labeled experience (10k+10k balanced). This is the same hidden-state-as-correctness-predictor problem we worked on (F-2 / F-8) but with three methodological shifts: (a) all-layers instead of single-layer L19, (b) sequence-position delta instead of prefill state, (c) supervised-but-training-free instead of logistic-regression DoM probe. Tested on Nemotron-1.5B / Polaris-4B / DeepSeek-7B / Qwen3-4B / DeepSeek-R1-Qwen3-8B — Nemotron-1.5B AIME24 is the closest scale match to our 1.5B Qwen MATH-500 setup.

**Key claim we tested:** Hidden states encode correctness as a geometrically separable signature — and this signal is *stronger when read across all layers as a delta* than when read at any single position/layer. They also claim signal monotonically strengthens with layer depth, peaking in final layers (Figure 4).

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** P11-FE577 (CLUE replication on our cached 1.5B MATH-500 activations) and P11-FE578 (layer-AUROC monotonicity test) directly evaluate the two strongest CLUE claims against our F-2 (AUROC 0.7731 single-layer L19) baseline. Both are 30-min CPU jobs on already-cached NPZs. Until run, the F-9 (CoE-60 redundant) and F-2 ("L19 peak") specifiers are at risk.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE577, P11-FE578, P11-FE579, P11-FE580, H-461, H-462, H-463, H-464.

**Status:** TO TEST.

### Methodologies extracted

- **Activation-delta representation** — `Δh = h(end-of-</think>) − h(start-of-<think>)` ∈ ℝ^(L×D), full L×D matrix kept.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU (we already have prefill + final-token cached; would need to re-mark `<think>`/`</think>` boundaries — Qwen-2.5-Instruct doesn't emit those tokens by default, so adapt to "last-prompt-tok" → "last-generated-tok").
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — cleanest way to test our own F-2 / F-9 claims via Refutations 2 and 3.

- **Layer-averaged Euclidean distance to centroids** — `d(A,B) = (1/L) Σ_ℓ ||A_ℓ − B_ℓ||₂`, classify by nearest of `V_succ`, `V_fail`. No training, no optimization.
  *Replication cost*: 5 min CPU (numpy means + distances on cached NPZ).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — a 5-line script that's strictly more powerful than single-direction DoM if F-9 turns out to be wrong.

- **Layer-wise centroid-distance curve `d^(ℓ)`** — measure how separable correct vs. incorrect become as a function of depth.
  *Replication cost*: 10 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct refutation test for F-2's "L19 peak" specifier (Refutation 1).

- **Cross-model verification** — use centroids from model A's experience to verify model B's solutions. Specifically RL-trained-model-as-verifier on SFT-model outputs.
  *Replication cost*: 1 day H100 (re-extract activations from a second model on same problems).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — interesting but expensive; only after intra-model replication.

- **PCA visualization of class-separability per layer** — Figure 1, Figure 4, projects deltas to 2D and shows clusters by color.
  *Replication cost*: 1 hour CPU (already have activations; just plot).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — visual sanity check for layer-wise separability story.

- **TPR/TNR breakdown** — report binary classification accuracy split by class to expose optimistic-bias of LLM judges (GPT-4o TNR drops to 34% on Polaris-4B AIME25).
  *Replication cost*: free — already breaks out cleanly from our existing AUROC arrays.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — useful framing for narrative docs comparing F-2 to LLM-judge baselines.

- **Train-on-AIME, test-on-GPQA OOD eval** — explicitly frame the math experience set as the training distribution and report OOD generalization.
  *Replication cost*: needs new GPQA generation traces (~$50 + few hours H100).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — desirable but not free; pairs with H-2 (breathing on short CoT).

### Approaches & framings

- **"Activation delta as the unit of analysis"** — they argue what matters is the *transformation* induced by reasoning, not the absolute state. This is a useful reframing for our P11 narrative which currently leans on the *prefill* state alone (F-2). The delta frame would unify F-2 (prefill) and the orthogonal final-state signal (F-3) under one representation.
- **"RL → separable geometry, SFT → entangled"** — a training-paradigm scoping condition on hidden-state probing methods. Our F-2/F-8 results were obtained on Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Instruct, which has DPO post-training; this paper raises the question of whether F-2 transfers to non-DPO SFT-only checkpoints.
- **"Supervised but training-free"** — aspirational efficiency: deterministic mean over labeled trajectories beats any gradient-trained probe. Argues against our reliance on logistic-regression DoM probes when a 5-line numpy script is competitive.
- **"Layer-averaged distance, not best-layer distance"** — methodological move that intentionally avoids per-layer peak-picking (no need for L19-vs-L23 sweeps if you just average all layers). Removes a hyperparameter.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **AIME 1983–2023** — 30+ problems/year × 40 years ≈ ~1200 problems. Public via Kaggle (Veeraboina 2023). Used as experience set. Applicable? yes — direct admission candidate to H-1 / H-5 testing on hard math problems beyond MATH-500.
- **AIME 2024 / 2025** — 30 problems each. Public. Applicable? yes — natural OOD test for F-2 if we want to extend beyond MATH-500.
- **GPQA** — 448 problems, graduate-level multi-domain. Public/HF. Applicable? yes — single best out-of-math benchmark for F-2 / F-8 generalization.
- **MATH (level 3-5)** — Hendrycks et al. 2021. Already public. Applicable? yes — we already use MATH-500 (a 500-problem subset).
- **WebInstruct-verified** — Ma et al. 2025, 5k train + 1k test, multi-domain (physics/law/finance/humanities). Hf-public (General-Reasoner). Applicable? yes — best non-math OOD probe.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **Models**: Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B (RL), Polaris-4B (RL), DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B (distillation/SFT), Qwen3-4B (SFT), DeepSeek-7B (SFT). Use HF "recommended inference setting" (temperature, system prompt).
- **Generation lengths**: 16k / 32k / 64k tokens — three settings ablated; conclusions stable across. (Our P11 1024-tok labels are well under this.)
- **Experience set construction**: for each problem in AIME+MATH, sample 32 unique solutions; rule-based verifier labels them; 10,000 correct + 10,000 incorrect randomly drawn for balanced centroids.
- **Test-time setup**: 64 candidate solutions per test problem.
- **Reasoning-block delimiters**: `<think>` and `</think>` literal tokens — only present in reasoning models that emit them. Adapting to Qwen-2.5-Instruct (which doesn't) requires picking analogous boundary tokens (e.g., end of prompt, end of generation, or a `\n\n`-terminated CoT).
- **Hidden-state extraction**: at the final token of `<think>` and final token of `</think>` — i.e., one token before and one token after the reasoning span.
- **No code released** in v1 of the paper (Tencent technical report; check arxiv v2 for code link).

### Replicable intermediates

- **Quick layer-AUROC sweep** — script: `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` already has per-layer activations for L0-L27 on 1.5B, MATH-500, prefill + final positions. Compute DoM AUROC at every layer; produce monotonicity plot. Tests Refutation 1.
- **Quick CLUE replication** — using the same NPZ, define `Δh = prefill_h − final_h` (closest analog to their `Δh` since we have no `<think>` markers), run 5-fold OOF nearest-centroid classifier, compute accuracy + AUROC. Tests Refutation 2.
- **Centroid-distance vs. layer plot** — element-wise centroid means already exist in the DoM-fitting code; just emit `d^(ℓ)` array. Tests Refutation 1 from a different angle.
- **Visualization (Figure 1 analog)** — 2D PCA scatter of correct vs. incorrect deltas at L0, L13, L19, L27 — visual sanity check for "deeper = more separable."

All four are 1-hour CPU jobs on the existing `prefill_gated_compute/results.json` cache.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2501.12948** — DeepSeek-R1 — already in graph (status: graphed). Used as base reasoner family for DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B / DeepSeek-7B. CLUE's RL-vs-SFT framing implicates R1's RL recipe.
- **2203.11171** — Self-Consistency (Wang 2022) — already in graph (REPLICATED + EXTENDED). CLUE's `majority@64` baseline.
- **2410.13640** — Chain-of-Embedding (Wang ICLR 2025) — already in graph (PARTIALLY CONFIRMED). CLUE's "trajectory" framing is the same lineage.

## 2510.02956 — Confidence and Dispersity as Signals: Unsupervised Model Evaluation and Ranking (Deng, Tu, Radwan, Alsheikh, Gould, Zheng, 2025)

**Relevance:** Vision-domain unsupervised accuracy estimation paper that nonetheless contributes the strongest available family of label-free correctness metrics — NuclearNorm, IM, COT, SoftmaxCorr — operating purely on softmax prediction matrices. The metrics transfer cleanly to LLM K=N sampling: a single problem's K=8 answer distribution is exactly the n_t × k prediction matrix the paper studies, with n_t=K and k=|answer space|. Directly competitive with our F-2 / F-8 supervised DoM story and a concrete instantiation of H-12's "label-free probes" abstraction.

**Key claim we tested:** *(In the paper's setting)* The nuclear norm of the prediction matrix jointly captures confidence and dispersity, achieves R²≈0.984 averaged across CIFAR-10, CUB-200, ImageNet-C, ImageNet-3D for unsupervised set-level accuracy estimation, and consistently beats confidence-only metrics under distribution shift.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — the paper's metrics are not yet evaluated on MATH-500 K=8 sampling. Three FE blocks (P11-FE581/75/76) and three hypotheses (H-465/79/80) propose direct head-to-head against F-2's L19 DoM AUROC 0.7731, against F-8's selective-prediction curve, and against F-7's D-bucket signature. All three experiments are CPU-only on cached P11 K=8 results once per-token softmax logits are confirmed cached.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE581, P11-FE582, P11-FE583; H-465, H-466, H-467; F-2, F-7, F-8, F-9, H-12.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **NuclearNorm of prediction matrix** — sum of singular values of the n_t × k softmax matrix, normalized by √(min(n_t, k) · n_t). Captures confidence (row peakedness) + dispersity (rank/spread across columns).
  *Replication cost*: 5 min CPU per pathway on cached softmax outputs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — direct unsupervised baseline against F-2 / F-8.

- **IM (Information Maximization)** — H(mean(p_i)) − mean(H(p_i)). Marginal entropy minus average per-sample entropy. Closed-form, no training.
  *Replication cost*: 5 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — bundled with NuclearNorm experiment.

- **COT (Confidence Optimal Transport)** — Wasserstein-∞ distance from the empirical pushforward distribution of predictions to the uniform distribution.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU (POT library, n_t × k OT problem).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes, low priority** — bundled with NuclearNorm; POT install needed.

- **SoftmaxCorr** — cosine similarity between class correlation matrix C = P_m^T P_m / n_t and a reference diagonal R = diag(d), where d is a prior class distribution from a zero-shot CLIP model.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU + needs prior class distribution from a separate model.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **maybe** — requires defining a "prior answer distribution" for MATH-500 (uniform-over-numerical-answers? CLIP-style is meaningless for math). Likely skip.

- **MaNo** — piecewise normalization of logits then L_p norm of the resulting Q matrix; aimed at alleviating overconfidence.
  *Replication cost*: 20 min CPU on cached logits (need per-token logits, not just sampled answers).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **no** — needs logits we don't cache; marginal vs NuclearNorm.

- **ATC, DoC, AvgEnergy, ConfScore, Entropy, ClassEntropy, CTD** — all standard baselines documented in Sec. III. Mostly already implicit in our work (Entropy ≈ semantic entropy proxy, ConfScore ≈ max-softmax baseline).
  *Replication cost*: trivial.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** as the baseline panel for the NuclearNorm experiment.

### Approaches & framings

- **Confidence ↔ Dispersity duality.** A model can be wrong by being underconfident OR by being overconfident on a small subset of answers. The paper's framing — sample-level certainty + set-level diversity — is a useful reframe of our F-7 D-bucket story: D-bucket may be the *high-confidence-low-dispersity* regime (overconfident on a single wrong reasoning pathway).
- **Set-level vs per-sample evaluation.** The paper operates at the *set* level (does this whole test set look hard for this model?). Our F-2 / F-8 operate at the *per-sample* level. Mapping their NuclearNorm onto K=N samples *of a single problem* converts their set-level metric into our per-sample metric — a transferable framing move.
- **"Output-only suffices" lens.** The paper's strongest claim is that you can rank models without probes, training, or hidden states — pure softmax suffices. Treats hidden-state probes as overengineered for the unsupervised-eval task. Useful counter-frame for the program: how much of F-2's signal lives at the output and how much *only* in the residual stream?

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **ImageNet-C / ImageNet-3D / ImageNet-V2-A/B/C / ImageNet-Sketch / ImageNet-R / ObjectNet** — image classification under distribution shift. Public, HF-accessible. Applicable? **no** — wrong modality.
- **CIFAR-10 / CIFAR-10.1** — Public. Applicable? **no** — image, not relevant to MATH-500.
- **CUB-200** — fine-grained bird classification. Public. Applicable? **no**.
- **WILDS** — real-world shift benchmarks (Camelyon17, iWildCam, FMoW, etc.). Public. Applicable? **no** — image/satellite/medical, not LLM correctness.

None applicable. The methods transfer; the benchmarks do not.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **Prediction matrix definition** is just `P_m = softmax(logits)` stacked over the test set — no model surgery, works on any classifier.
- **NuclearNorm normalization**: `||P_m||_* / sqrt(min(n_t, k) · n_t)` so the score lies in a comparable range across n_t (test-set size) and k (class count).
- **Backbone zoo**: ResNet-20, RepVGG-A0, VGG-11, ResNet-50/101, PMG, ViT-Base, DenseNet-121, ConvNeXt-Base, CLIP-ViT-B/32, CLIP-ConvNeXt-Base — all from `timm`.
- **Prob axis scaling** — both accuracy and the estimated quantity are mapped from [0,1] to (−∞, +∞) via probit before regression (per Taori et al. 2020). When porting their NuclearNorm-vs-accuracy correlation to LLM K=N, we should apply the same probit scaling to keep R² comparable to their numbers.
- **Conference-version code** likely lives at the original ICML'23 paper's repo (Deng et al. 2023, ref [15]); extended-version code release not yet announced in PDF.
- **No training, no probe, no held-out validation needed for any of the proposed metrics** — these are all closed-form summaries of the prediction matrix.

### Replicable intermediates

- **`pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json`** — has per-problem K=8 sampling results for 500 MATH-500 problems × 1.5B and × 7B. If per-sample softmax over the answer-token vocabulary is cached, NuclearNorm/IM/ClassEntropy can be computed in ~5 min CPU per model. If only argmax answers are cached, the K=8 → one-hot matrix per problem is a degenerate (rank ≤ K=8, k=|answer space|) prediction matrix on which NuclearNorm/IM still computes — gives a quick first cut.
- **`pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`** — verify whether per-token logits or just argmax answers are cached. If answer-token logits exist, this is a 30-min CPU job; if not, regenerate from the same prefill cache (a few hours on H100).
- **`scratch/pathway10_temporal_and_verifier_results.json`** — has the full F-8 selective-prediction K=2.5 trajectory; rerun the same coverage curve replacing supervised DoM with NuclearNorm of K=8. If the curve overlays, F-8's selective-prediction story is supervised-equivalent to a label-free aggregate.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2506.24106** — already in graph (status: pending_triage; brief_kind=seed_paragraph). Same author (Deng), described as "Representation Dispersion Predictive Power" — almost certainly closely related (perhaps a parallel/companion paper). Worth promoting alongside this one.
- **2402.03744 (INSIDE/EigenScore)** — already in graph (CITED ONLY). EigenScore is a singular-value-based confidence summary on the *internal embedding covariance*; this paper does the analogous singular-value summary on the *output softmax matrix*. Direct conceptual sibling worth a CITES edge.
- **2406.15927 (Semantic Entropy Probes)** — already in graph (CITED ONLY). Both are label-free correctness signals; a head-to-head on MATH-500 K=8 would resolve which family wins for LLMs.
- **2509.11569 (D²HScore)** — already in graph (PARTIALLY CONFIRMED). Hidden-state dispersity score. Close conceptual neighbor — paper's output-side dispersity vs D²HScore's hidden-state dispersity is a clean A/B for "where does the dispersity signal live?"
- **2410.13640 (Chain-of-Embedding)** — already in graph. CoE is hidden-state trajectory; this paper is its output-side analogue.
- **arXiv NeurIPS 2024 — MaNo (Xie et al., ref [17])** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Newest output-side method, directly cited as competitive with NuclearNorm.
- **arXiv ICLR 2024 — AvgEnergy / Energy-Based Model Evaluation (Peng et al., ref [16])** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Energy-based output-side score; direct competitor to NuclearNorm.
- **arXiv NeurIPS 2023 — COT (Lu et al., ref [18])** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. OT-based output dispersity score.
- **arXiv TMLR 2024 — SoftmaxCorr (Tu et al., ref [19])** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Same-team predecessor, same kind of output statistic.

## 2510.04309 — Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller (Nguyen, Pham, Vu, Zhang, Nguyen, ICLR 2026)

**Relevance:** Recasts existing activation-steering methods (ActAdd, DirAblate, Mean-AcT) as proportional (P) controllers and proposes adding integral (I) and derivative (D) feedback terms across *layers* to remove steady-state error and damp overshoot. Tested on safety-style tasks (toxicity, jailbreaking, image style) on Gemma2 / Llama3 / Qwen2.5 (3B–14B). Code at github.com/dungnvnus/pid-steering. Directly relevant to H-1 (steering); orthogonal to F-2 / F-8 (probing). The prior admission note ("addresses the rotation problem") is partially miscalibrated: the integral is across layers, not across token positions.

**Key claim we tested:** "Layer-wise integral feedback removes steady-state error in activation steering and yields stronger control than P-only methods like Mean-AcT on safety tasks."

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** No experiments run yet. Three falsifiable cross-checks queued: (a) PID feature direction as a probe (does NOT improve AUROC over 0.7731 if F-9 holds — H-469), (b) PID-AcT closed-loop steering on MATH-500 (the strongest steering baseline H-1 can test against — H-468), (c) cos similarity between PID-derived prefill and final-token directions (does NOT bridge the F-3 orthogonality if our reading is right — H-470). The paper's own scope is safety tasks; transfer to math-correctness steering is unverified.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE584, P11-FE585, P11-FE586, P10-FE32, H-468, H-469, H-470.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **PID feedback controller per layer** (Eqn. 18) — `u(k) = K_p r(k) + K_i Σ_{j<k} r(j) + K_d (r(k)-r(k-1))`. Drop-in replacement for diff-in-means steering vector. *Replication cost*: ~1h CPU on cached prefill activations to produce PID feature direction across L0–L27 of Qwen-1.5B. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — to test refutations 2 and 4.

- **PID-AcT** — PID applied within Mean-AcT's sequential framework (best variant in their toxicity table). *Replication cost*: 4h H100 — needs closed-loop generation with intervention at each layer. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — H-1 has been blocked on H100 pod time; PID-AcT is the strongest steering baseline now.

- **Mean local Jacobian estimation** — `Ā(k)` is the per-layer Jacobian averaged across the contrastive pair. Required for their ISS proof. *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on a 32-prompt sample. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — if we want to falsify ISS structure on math data (refutation 5).

- **Steady-state error scalar projection** `<e(0), e(k)>` (their Fig. 3 metric) — measures how much of the initial error direction survives after `k` layers under different controllers. *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached residuals. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct measurement of layer-wise drift, complements F-3 / H-17 analysis.

- **Stability-first one-gain-at-a-time analytical strategy** (paper's Sec. 6 limitation) — sweep `K_p`, then `K_i`, then `K_d` rather than joint optimization. *Replication cost*: trivial methodology note. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — for any PID-style sweep.

- **Hyperparameter ranges** — best `K_p ∈ [0.01, 0.05]`, `K_i ∈ [0.05, 0.10]`, `K_d ∈ [0.01, 0.05]` for jailbreaking; similar for toxicity (paper Fig. 6). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — initial sweep range for FEs below.

- **0-shot LLM-as-judge with QVQ-72B-Preview** — toxicity evaluation via large MLLM. *Replication cost*: not applicable to our task. *We'd plausibly run this*: no — we measure correctness against ground truth on MATH-500.

### Approaches & framings

- **Activation steering as state-feedback control** — recasts ActAdd / DirAblate / Mean-AcT as proportional controllers and identifies their steady-state error as the missing piece. Intersects our framing of L19 DoM as a "feature direction" (P-controller analogue): suggests we should distinguish the *direction* (P) from the *magnitude / persistence* (I) of any steering proposal under H-1.

- **Layer index k as a discrete time variable** — they treat `f^{(k)}(·)` as a dynamical system advancing in `k`. This is the same trick CoE used (P9). F-9 says it's redundant for correctness; the paper says it's load-bearing for steering. The asymmetry is interesting: layer-wise dynamics may matter for *changing* outputs but not for *predicting* them.

- **Disturbance decomposition** `w(k) = w∥(k) + w⊥(k)` (their Sec. 4.2.1) — splits error into the "matched" component PID can cancel and an "unmatched" component it cannot. Useful framing for understanding *why* DoM steering at H-1 might cap out: if the unmatched disturbance is large on MATH-500, even ideal control leaves residual error.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **RealToxicityPrompts** — 1000 prompts, public HF, license CC. Applicable? **no** — toxicity, not math/correctness.
- **ADVBENCH (jailbreaking)** — 520 harmful prompts, public, MIT. Applicable? **no** — refusal task.
- **ALPACA (harmless subset, 512 samples)** — public, CC. Applicable? **no** — used as paired contrast for refusal.
- **TINYBENCHMARKS** — TinyArc, TinyMMLU, TinyTruthfulQA, TinyHellaSwag, TinyWinoGrande, TinyGSM8K-strict (~100 samples each). Public HF, MIT. Applicable? **partially** — TinyGSM8K-strict could be a sanity check for math-side PID-AcT, but our canonical benchmark is MATH-500 (1024-tok labels), not GSM8K.
- **MMLU 5-shot** — Hendrycks et al. 2021, public HF, MIT. Applicable? **no** — utility metric for the safety-tuned model.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Code: https://github.com/dungnvnus/pid-steering
- Models tested: Gemma2-{2B,9B,27B}-IT, Llama3-8B-Instruct, Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-{3B,14B}-Instruct (3B–14B range), plus FLUX-Schnell + SDXL-Lightning for diffusion.
- Hyperparameter sweep ranges: `K_p ∈ {0.0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15}`, `K_i ∈ {0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15}`, `K_d ∈ {0.0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15}` (paper Fig. 6 ablation).
- Best regime for jailbreak (Llamaguard3 ASR proxy): high `K_i` (0.10–0.15) + small `K_d` (0.01–0.05) + small `K_p` (0.01–0.05).
- Steering function `ρ_steer` is unchanged from underlying method (ActAdd / DirAblate / Mean-AcT); only the *vector* fed into it changes from `r(k)` to `u(k)`.
- Sequential vs non-sequential mapping (Eqns. 4–6 vs 1–3) determines whether each layer's intervention is composed with prior interventions; PID-AcT is the sequential variant and consistently wins in their tables.
- Steady-state error metric: scalar projection `<e(0), e(k)>` plotted across "extraction points" (essentially layer indices on randomly-init Llama3 baseline + pretrained Qwen2.5-3B) — Fig. 3.
- Theoretical guarantees rest on `sup_k ||Ā(k)|| ≤ M < ∞` and `sup_k ||M_p(k)|| ≤ q < 1` where `M_p(k) = Ā(k)(I − K_p)`; ISS stability requires `q + Mh < 1` where `h = ||K_i||`.

### Replicable intermediates

- **PID-feature-direction probe at L19** — using cached `pathway11_h100/.../residuals_*.npz` (1024-tok labels, Qwen-1.5B), compute `u(L=19)` per Eqn. 18 over the train fold, fit logistic OOF, compare AUROC against 0.7731 baseline. Script analogue: `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/`.
- **Layer-wise scalar error trajectory `<e(0), e(k)>`** — on cached per-layer activations (L0–L27, prefill position) for the correct-vs-incorrect split, plot the paper's Fig. 3 analogue. If MATH-500 shows a non-decaying P trajectory (their pretrained Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct does, see Fig. 3b), the steady-state-error claim transfers; if it decays naturally, PID's I-term has nothing to fix.
- **Mean local Jacobian spectrum** at L18→L19→L20 — small CPU job, ~30min. Refutation 5.
- **`cos(u_PID(prefill), u_PID(final))` at L19** — directly tests refutation 1. Cached prefill + final-token activations exist for Qwen-1.5B (the source of the 0.046 number).

### Cross-paper signals

- **2306.03341** — Inference-Time Intervention (Li et al.). Already in graph (status: graphed, **CONTRADICTED**). Paper cites this as ITI baseline; their PID generally beats ITI in jailbreak tables — consistent with our CONTRADICTED status (ITI assumes static direction).

## 2510.06477 — Attention Sinks and Compression Valleys in LLMs are Two Sides of the Same Coin (Queipo-de-Llano, Arroyo, Barbero, Dong, Bronstein, LeCun, Shwartz-Ziv, ICLR 2026)

**Relevance:** Provides a unified mechanistic theory (Mix-Compress-Refine) for the mid-layer compression phenomenon that we have been calling "breathing" (F-1) and that anchors our "PH at Gaussian null" finding (F-10). The paper proves σ₁² ≥ M + αR (Theorem 1) and shows the entropy upper bound is empirically tight in compressed mid-layers, predicting that Phase 2 representations are effectively rank-1 (BOS direction) plus small perturbation. This gives a competing mechanistic story for nearly every geometric finding in our project: F-1 (breathing), F-2 (L19 DoM), F-3 (prefill/final orthogonality), F-4 (asymmetric collapse), F-10 (PH null) all gain or lose interpretation under their theory. Most importantly, their Phase 3 prediction (norm equalization, sharp positional/identity heads, generation tasks improve through full depth) is in tension with our F-2 result that L19 (67.8% depth, mid-Phase-2) is the *best* correctness predictor for a generative task — making this paper one of our highest-leverage refutation candidates.

**Key claim we tested:** Mid-layer compression valleys (low matrix-based entropy, high anisotropy ≥0.9) emerge synchronously with attention sinks at the layer where the BOS token develops massive activations (10³–10⁴× rest-of-tokens norm), and the resulting representation is rank-1 + small perturbation. Generation-correctness signals should improve monotonically with depth (Phase 3 dominant), while embedding/classification probes peak at 25–75% depth.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** Six FE blocks (P11-FE587 through P11-FE592) lay out the replication and refutation experiments. Pre-registered predictions: (a) per-layer entropy curve on Qwen-2.5-1.5B should show a Phase-2 valley overlapping the F-1 breathing curve; (b) σ₁ deflation should partially or fully remove correct-vs-incorrect breathing divergence (H-472); (c) per-layer DoM AUROC sweep will refute their generation-task prediction if the L19 peak holds across L0–L27; (d) MLP-on-BOS ablation will tell us whether F-2 is mechanically downstream of the massive activation (H-471).

**Related experiments:** P11-FE587 (entropy curve), P11-FE588 (rank-1 deflation), P11-FE589 (per-layer DoM), P11-FE590 (Phase-3 equalization check), P11-FE591 (phase-stratified PH), P11-FE592 (BOS-MLP ablation), H-471, H-472. Cross-references P11-FE15 (length-band PR), P11-FE16 (MP correction).

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Matrix-based singular-value entropy** H(X) = -Σ p_j log p_j with p_j = σ_j² / ‖X‖_F². One-line on cached NPZs.
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU on cached Pathway 11 NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives us a per-layer compression curve to compare to F-1 breathing curve directly.
- **Anisotropy** p_1 = σ_1² / ‖X‖_F². Trivially derivable from above.
  *Replication cost*: 5min CPU on cached NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct sanity check of "Phase 2 means p_1 ≈ 1".
- **BOS L2 norm per layer** ‖x_BOS^(ℓ)‖. Requires the BOS-position activation to be cached (or re-extracted with a single H100 hour).
  *Replication cost*: cached if extracted, else ~1h H100 to re-run last 4 layers + L0–L5.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — this is the headline causal variable in their theory.
- **Sink-rate** (per-layer) = (1/H) Σ_h I[mean attn to BOS ≥ 0.3]. Requires attention weights.
  *Replication cost*: medium — requires re-extracting attention from MATH-500 prompts; ~2-3h H100 for Qwen 1.5B + 7B.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes for follow-up; not for first pass.
- **Mixing-score** = average row entropy of attention matrix. Same data as sink-rate.
  *Replication cost*: free given attention-weight extraction.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes (paired with sink-rate).
- **MLP-on-BOS ablation** (zero MLP contribution to BOS at the emergence layer). Causal test.
  *Replication cost*: ~30min H100 forward pass with hook on Qwen 1.5B over 500 problems.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — single most powerful causal experiment in the paper.
- **Per-layer LogitLens / linear probe** for QA accuracy.
  *Replication cost*: 1-2h CPU per dataset.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — most directly comparable to DoM AUROC sweep.
- **Rank-1 (σ₁) deflation** of representation matrix to test whether downstream metrics survive the BOS direction.
  *Replication cost*: 10min CPU on cached NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — central ablation for refutation R2.
- **α-alignment metric** α = (1/R) Σ_{i≠0} ‖x_i‖² cos² θ_i (alignment of non-BOS rows with BOS direction).
  *Replication cost*: free given NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — useful diagnostic for whether mid-layer rank-1 structure is *just* BOS or also content.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Massive activation as the universal compression mechanism"** — recasts compression-valley phenomena (Skean 2025) and attention sinks (Xiao 2024) as one effect with one cause. For us, this is a *competing mechanistic story* for what we have been calling "breathing" in F-1: instead of trajectory-driven dimensional dynamics, it could be BOS-norm scheduling.
- **Three-phase Mix-Compress-Refine demarcation** — gives us a principled segmentation of the 28 Qwen layers into three regions and matched task expectations per region. Useful as a layer-selection scaffold for any future probe sweep, and as the framework against which our L19-peak result is anomalous.
- **"Phase-aware early-exit"** — practical implication: classification-style probes (DoM, ABC-44) belong at end of Phase 2; generation belongs at full depth. Reframes our selective-prediction story (F-8) as a *Phase-2 readout*.
- **Decoupling of "input-dependent sink strength" from "fixed-position phase boundary"** — Figure 5 shows mixing score in Phase 1 is constant across high-sink/low-sink prompts while Phase 2 varies. Predicts F-7's D-bucket signature should be a Phase-2 modulation, not a Phase-1 one.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **GSM8K** (7.5K train) — math reasoning, 8.5K total, MIT-license, HF accessible. Applicable: yes — direct overlap with MATH-500 regime (math chain-of-thought).
- **WikiText-2** — language modeling, ~2M tokens, BSD, HF accessible. Applicable: marginal — we're not measuring perplexity.
- **MTEB (32 tasks subset)** — embedding benchmark suite, public, HF. Applicable: no for first pass — we don't run embedding tasks.
- **ARC Easy / ARC Challenge / HellaSwag / WinoGrande** — multiple-choice QA, public, lm-eval-harness compatible. Applicable: yes if we want to replicate their LogitLens-vs-linear-probe divergence figure (Figure 8) on our model.
- **FineWeb-Edu (20K prompts subset)** — pre-training-style mixed text, HF accessible, ODC-By. Applicable: no — orthogonal to our reasoning task.
- **RedPajama (100 examples)** — used for the Figure 3 entropy-bound tightness check. Applicable: yes — small enough to throw at our model for the same Figure 3 plot.
- **SST-2** — sentence sentiment, GLUE, public. Applicable: no.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Sink-rate threshold τ = 0.3 (heads attending ≥30% of mass to BOS).
- Compression-bound tightness check needs only ~100 RedPajama examples (Figure 3 sample size).
- BOS norm spike factor: 10³–10⁴× over rest-of-tokens norm.
- Pythia 410M emergence at L5 (out of 24); Llama-3-8B at L1; Qwen2-7B at multiple layers (cumulative).
- MLP-zeroing ablation: x_BOS^(ℓ+1) ← x_BOS^(ℓ) + Attn^(ℓ)(x_BOS), removing only MLP^(ℓ)(x_BOS). Single-line hook.
- Some models develop massive activations in *multiple* stages (Pythia 410M, Qwen2 7B); ablating one only partially decompresses.
- Pearson correlations: r(ΔBOS_norm, Δentropy) = -0.9 ± 0.18; r(BOS_norm, sink_rate) = 0.58 ± 0.25.
- Linear probes per layer: trained on frozen backbone hidden states with standard logistic regression — same recipe as our DoM (drop-in compatible).
- Code not explicitly linked in the paper body (need to check appendix / their group's GitHub).

### Replicable intermediates

- **per-layer matrix-based entropy curve on cached MATH-500 prefill NPZs** (1.5B + 7B) — produces the Phase-2 valley directly. ~20min CPU. Compares against F-1 breathing curve at the same layers.
- **per-layer anisotropy p_1 curve on the same NPZs** — establishes whether Qwen-2.5-1.5B exhibits the 0.9-anisotropy plateau their theory needs.
- **per-layer DoM AUROC sweep** across L0–L27 on cached NPZs — already the natural extension of F-2; tests R1 directly.
- **σ₁ deflation followed by F-1 breathing recompute** — ~10min CPU; tests R2.
- **L27 final-token σ₁-dominance for correct vs incorrect** — already on disk; tests R3.
- **PH on per-phase NPZ subsets** — uses existing PH script with three layer-range slices; tests R4.
- **α (alignment) curve per layer on cached NPZs** — supports interpretation of all the above.

(BOS-position L0 activations may not be in current Pathway 11 caches — verify in DATA_MANIFEST before scheduling.)

### Cross-paper signals

## 2510.10494 — Tracing the Traces: Latent Temporal Signals for Efficient and Accurate Reasoning (Vilas, Yousefi, Nushi, Horvitz, Balachandran, 2025)

**Relevance:** Direct competitor in latent-space correctness prediction. Introduces a training-free family of trajectory signals (Net Change, Cumulative Change, Aligned Change) computed by averaging hidden states into k=500-token segments and measuring drift / step-update geometry, layer-averaged across all transformer layers. They test on three 14B reasoning models (R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, Phi-4-Reasoning-Plus, Qwen3-14B) on three domains (GPQA, AIME 2025, TSP) and report mean AUROC 0.71–0.74, beating Wang 2024 cross-layer (LayerMag 0.58, LayerAng 0.67) and output-distribution baselines (Entropy 0.67, Perplexity 0.49). They also demonstrate inference-time scaling (70% token reduction, +2.6% accuracy via early answer selection). The temporal aggregation axis is **orthogonal** to our prefill-vs-final endpoint framing — and we have not tested it.

**Key claim we tested:** Layer-averaged trajectory signals over coarse-grained reasoning segments outperform both cross-layer signals (Wang 2024 / CoE-style) and output-distribution confidence at predicting final-answer correctness.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — H-473 / H-474 / H-475 set up the replication on Qwen-2.5-1.5B 1024-tok cache. Outcome will determine REPLICATED vs CONTRADICTED vs PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. Critical comparator is whether any single LT signal beats prefill L19 DoM AUROC 0.7731 on our cache.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE593 (LT replication), P11-FE594 (Spearman path-length test), P11-FE595 (drift-projection axis test), P11-FE596 (D-bucket blindness test), H-473, H-474, H-475. Indirectly relevant: P11-FE5 (R1-Distill-1.5B comparison), H-6 (CoE-vs-DoM contest).

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Segment-averaged trajectory states** — divide the reasoning trace into k=500-token segments; compute segment-level state h̃_l^(n) = mean of token activations within segment n at layer l.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on existing 1024-tok cache (need to re-extract because cached pipeline is per-token, not per-segment).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — it's a direct extension of our pipeline and the most threatening competitor to single-layer DoM.

- **Net Change** = (1/L) Σ_l ‖u_l‖_2 / N where u_l = h̃_l^(N) − h̃_l^(1). Layer-averaged norm of overall drift, normalized by segment count.
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU once segments are computed.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes.

- **Cumulative Change** = (1/L) Σ_l Σ_{n=2..N} ‖v_l^(n)‖_2 where v_l^(n) = h̃_l^(n) − h̃_l^(n−1). Sum of step-update norms across the whole trace.
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes.

- **Aligned Change** = (1/L) Σ_l (1/(N−1)) Σ_n ⟨v_l^(n), u_l⟩ / (‖v_l^(n)‖ ‖u_l‖). Layer-averaged cosine of step-updates with overall drift.
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — this is the most novel signal we don't currently compute.

- **Combined LT score** — weighted sum of Net + Cumulative + Aligned, weights chosen on a calibration set so signals more correlated with accuracy contribute more.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes.

- **Step-wise early-exit evaluation** — at each k=500 token checkpoint, recompute LT signals on the partial trace and measure ROC-AUC vs. final correctness. Yields an AUROC-vs-tokens curve.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly applicable to F-8 selective prediction.

- **Random forest on LT signals at 2k tokens for early path selection** — sample 5 traces in parallel; at 2k tokens, compute LT signals on each partial trace; classifier picks one to continue, others terminate.
  *Replication cost*: 4h H100 (need to generate 5 samples per problem).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes if we want to extend F-8 from selective abstention to selective compute allocation.

- **Threshold calibration via cross-validation** — choose τ such that fraction of accepted-but-wrong traces is bounded; on calibration set, simulate full decision rule and pick τ that maximizes accuracy then evaluate on held-out.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes.

- **Cross-layer baselines** (LayerMag = mean magnitude of layer-to-layer changes; LayerAng = mean angle of layer-to-layer changes, from Wang 2024).
  *Replication cost*: already implemented for our CoE-60 pipeline; trivial.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a clean apples-to-apples comparison with our F-9 setup.

### Approaches & framings

- **Temporal axis as the primary correctness signal**, separate from cross-layer geometry. This decouples the "depth" axis (Wang 2024 / CoE / our F-9) from the "time" axis (segments along the generation). Our pipeline currently treats prefill (single position) and final-token (single position) as endpoints; Vilas et al. coarse-grain the in-between into segment-averaged states. Intersection: F-2 (prefill) and F-4 (final-token collapse) are both endpoint phenomena; the trajectory between them has not been probed at our 1024-tok scale.
- **Drift-vs-update decomposition** — separating overall direction (drift) from step-by-step motion (update) is a different geometric primitive than per-position DoM probing. Intersection: H-6 should be re-examined under this decomposition; CoE-60 is a per-layer summary at fixed token, which doesn't capture the drift-update split.
- **Reasoning trace as a coarse-grained random-walk-vs-directed-walk** — the negative correlation of Cumulative Change with accuracy (more wandering → less correct) reframes correctness as a path-geometry property. Intersection: F-4's asymmetric collapse may be a special case of this directed-walk hypothesis evaluated at the endpoint.
- **Training-free, model-agnostic recipe** — they explicitly pitch LT as needing no probe training, no annotations, no model-specific calibration beyond τ-tuning. This is in tension with our supervised DoM (which needs labeled correct/incorrect to compute). Could the unsupervised drift direction substitute for our supervised mass-mean?

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **GPQA Diamond** — 198 graduate-level multiple-choice in biology, chemistry, physics. License: research-permitted, HF-hosted (`Idavidrein/gpqa`). Applicable? **yes** — non-MATH-500 reasoning eval; would test whether F-2's prefill signal is math-specific or generalizes. Not currently in our pipeline.
- **AIME 2025** — 30 problems, USAMO-style. License: HF (`lchen001/AIME2025`). Applicable? **yes** — short, hard math; useful complement to MATH-500 if we want a harder-tier eval. 30 problems is too small for stable AUROC alone (their error bars ±0.09 reflect this).
- **TSP NP-Hard (n=180)** — path-optimization, 6–13 nodes. License: HF (`GeoMeterData/nphard_tsp1`). Applicable? **possibly** — non-natural-language reasoning. Would test whether prefill DoM is a reasoning-domain-general signal or math/text-specific. Lower priority than GPQA.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Segment size k=500 tokens, fixed. They tried alternative segmentations (delimiter-based) in Appendix F.
- All hidden states averaged at segment level *before* computing drift / update; this denoises token-level fluctuation.
- Net Change is normalized by N (segment count) to control for trace length; Cumulative Change is *not* normalized — by design, longer traces accumulate more.
- They average across **all** L transformer layers; no layer selection. (Ours uses L19 specifically.)
- Cumulative Change reported "sign-reversed" in their AUROC plots because the raw signal is negatively correlated with correctness — they invert for plotting comparability.
- Output-distribution baselines (Logit Margin / Entropy / Perplexity) were elicited via prompt `[…{trace_end} Final Answer:]` — interesting trick if we ever need a clean output-confidence comparison on our pipeline.
- Random forest classifier at 2k tokens uses LT signals as features; classifier is "lightweight" but no architecture details in main text.
- Models tested are all 14B-class reasoning-tuned (R1-D, Phi4R+, Qwen3-14B). Generalization to base (non-reasoning-tuned) models like our Qwen-2.5-1.5B is **not** demonstrated in this paper.
- No code link given in the abstract or main text we read; check appendix for repo URL.

### Replicable intermediates

- **LT-Net / LT-Cumulative / LT-Aligned on Qwen-2.5-1.5B 1024-tok cache** — the cached residuals at 1024 tokens are per-token, not per-segment, but the per-token tensors can be averaged into k=500 segments offline. Script: extend `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` to read cached NPZs, segment, compute the three signals, output ROC-AUC vs MATH-500 ground truth. ~20min CPU once segments are formed.
- **LayerMag / LayerAng cross-layer baseline (Wang 2024)** — already partially implemented in CoE-60 pipeline; pull the formulas and produce direct AUROCs on our cache. ~10min CPU.
- **Combined LT score on our cache** — once the three signals exist, weighted sum is trivial.
- **Sign of Cumulative Change correlation** — quick Spearman r between cumulative path and per-problem correctness on our cache; matches/doesn't-match Vilas's −0.38. ~5min CPU.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2410.13640** (Wang 2024 / Chain-of-Embedding) — already in graph (status: pending_triage at admission, was seed). Vilas et al. **explicitly frame their cross-layer baseline as Wang 2024**. This makes the Vilas paper a temporal extension that supersedes the cross-layer view CoE established. Strengthens our F-9 result that single-position cross-layer is weak.
- **2501.12948** (DeepSeek-R1) — already in graph. Vilas et al. use R1-Distill-Qwen-14B as one of their three models; relevant for any P11-FE5 R1-Distill comparison.
- **2406.15927** (Semantic Entropy Probes) — already in graph. Vilas et al.'s output-distribution baseline (Entropy / Perplexity) is the same family; they show entropy-style baselines are weaker than LT — confirms the H-12 framing.
- **2306.03341** (ITI) — already in graph. Not directly cited in Vilas main text; their LT signals are observational, not interventional, so no direct conflict.
