## 2603.00437 — Self-Correction Inside the Model: Leveraging Layer Attention to Mitigate Hallucinations in Large Vision–Language Models (April Fu, 2026)

**Relevance:** Vision-language hallucination paper, but the core method (ICLA — diagonal cross-layer attention with parameter-shared latent-bottleneck CLA module trained on a small positive-sample set) is directly transferable to our residual-stream pipeline. The most striking finding is methodological: on Qwen2.5-VL-7B (28 layers), cross-layer attention concentrates at **layers 19–21 and 24–25** with explicit unattended bands at 22–23 and 26–28. Two independent methods (their layer-attention map; our prefill L19 DoM probe) land on the same depth band of the Qwen2.5 family, despite operating on entirely different tasks (vision-grounded VQA vs math reasoning).

**Key claim we tested:** That structured cross-layer attention with diagonal token masking and parameter sharing improves correctness in advanced LVLMs by routing information from specific intermediate layers (19-21, 24-25 on Qwen2.5-VL-7B) to deeper layers, enabling self-correction without external signal.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — H-550 and H-551 quantify the cross-check. P11-FE702 is the cheap heatmap test (30min CPU) and P11-FE703 is the expensive trained-CLA test (3h H100). Until run, we tag this as **TO TEST**, not REPLICATED, because the published numbers are vision-language and don't directly apply.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE702, P11-FE703, H-550, H-551, F-2, F-3, F-10, H-13.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Diagonal Cross-Layer Attention (CLA) module** — at layer l, query = h^l, keys/values = stacked h^{k0}…h^l; attention is masked to keep only the same-token-position attention weights (diagonal of the token-dim attention matrix); output is RMSNorm'd and added with scaling factor α to h^l. Parameter-shared across all layers.
  *Replication cost*: ~3h on 2× RTX 4090 to train, per the paper. We have 1× H100 access. Implementation is ~60 lines on top of HF transformers (forward-hook on each LlamaDecoderLayer, latent bottleneck Wq/Wk/Wv with d'=d/r). About **half a day of engineering, then a 2h training run**.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives us direct mechanism-test for Refutations #1, #2, #4 above.
- **Layer-attention pattern visualization** — for each layer l (as query), record average attention weight over preceding layers k0..l-1 and plot as a 2D heatmap to identify which layer-pair retrievals dominate.
  *Replication cost*: 2h CPU on cached prefill_gated_compute hidden states (we already have h^k for k=0…27 on Qwen-2.5-1.5B for 500 problems).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct, runs on existing NPZs, no training needed if we approximate the attention weights via cosine similarity of cached h^l vs cached h^k.
- **Diagonal-only attention mask along token dimension** — a specific masking trick: each position only attends to its own position across layers. Worth borrowing for any future cross-layer probe.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (mask construction).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes, in any cross-layer probe we build.
- **Latent-space bottleneck (r=128 reduction ratio) for parameter sharing** — the d→d/r→attention→d/r→d projection lets a *single* CLA module be shared across all 28 layers, dropping params to 105K total for Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (architectural choice).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes if we implement CLA, otherwise no.
- **Lightweight fine-tuning on positive-sample subset only** — paper trains 3 epochs on 17K positive samples from POVID (= subset of LLaVA-Instruct-150K), all other params frozen. Demonstrates that minimal training data + frozen backbone + tiny module suffices.
  *Replication cost*: ~3h on 1× H100 if data is curated; comparable for a math-domain analog.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes for any future LoRA-style intervention experiments on Qwen-2.5-1.5B.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Pattern-specific mitigations stop generalizing as backbones improve."** Paper documents that DoLA, VCD, DAMO, DeCo all *hurt* Qwen2.5-VL-7B (DoLA: MME 1689→1403). This is the same scaling-renders-old-tools-obsolete framing relevant to our Pathway 6.5 deconfounding work — methods that worked at one scale fail at the next. Cautions us against assuming P11 H100 1024-tok numbers will hold for Qwen-2.5-32B.
- **"Cross-layer routing as the unit of analysis"** — instead of asking "which layer carries the signal" (per F-2), ask "which layer-pair carries the signal." This is a genuine framing shift adjacent to but distinct from CoE (which is a concatenation of per-layer features).
- **"Self-correction without an external corrector"** — frames hallucination mitigation as an internal residual-stream operation rather than as decoding-time logit contrast. Aligns with our preference for residual-stream mechanism over surface-level decoding tricks.
- **Interleaved attended/unattended layer pattern** as a discovery tool — paper observes alternating bands and uses this as a diagnostic. We can run the same diagnostic on Qwen-2.5-1.5B/7B math runs cheaply.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **POPE** (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation) — vision-language hallucination benchmark on MSCOCO + A-OKVQA, three settings (adversarial/popular/random); HF accessible. Applicable? **no** — vision-language only, our regime is math reasoning.
- **MME** — multimodal perception benchmark; vision-language. Applicable? **no**.
- **MMMU** — multimodal reasoning benchmark; vision-language. Applicable? **no**.
- **LLaVA-Bench** — GPT-4o-judged dialog benchmark on vision inputs. Applicable? **no**.
- **POVID training set** — 17K positive samples from LLaVA-Instruct-150K. Applicable? **no** for direct use; *yes* as a recipe (use 17K positive math-instruct samples to train a math-domain CLA).

No applicable benchmarks for our pipeline. The methodology (CLA + layer-attention map) is what transfers, not the data.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Default hyperparameters: **k0=16** (don't refine layers <16), **r=128** (reduction ratio), **α=0.02** (residual scaling factor), **3 epochs**, **lr=2e-5**.
- Trained on **2× RTX 4090** in **~3 hours**.
- Parameter footprint: **0.2M** for LLaVA-1.5-7B (32-layer), **0.1M** for Qwen2.5-VL-7B (28-layer). Halving from 32→28 layers + parameter sharing explains the drop.
- Inference overhead: **0.37%** (LLaVA-1.5-7B) and **0.07%** (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) compute increase.
- **Greedy decoding** (T=0) used throughout for all baselines — fair-comparison standard.
- **RMSNorm** applied to CLA output before adding to residual stream. (Not LayerNorm.)
- Weights `W_q, W_K, W_V` are reduced from `d → d' = d/r` ; `W_out` projects `d' → d`. Single shared instance across all layers.
- Diagonal-mask construction: instead of an `(L,L,T,T)` attention tensor, take the per-token diagonal (`L,L,T`) — major memory savings.
- No code link visible in extracted body; this is a recent independent-researcher submission so a public repo may not yet exist.
- Negative result reported: ICLA-Last-Layer-Only and ICLA-Random-Aggregation **do not** outperform vanilla — the structured layer-wise attention is what matters.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Layer-pair similarity heatmap on Qwen-2.5-1.5B from cached H100 NPZs**: load `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json` and corresponding hidden-state NPZs (per DATA_MANIFEST.md), compute `cos(h^l_t, h^k_t)` for all l,k ∈ [0,27] at the prefill final-token position, average over correct vs incorrect MATH-500 problems, plot as 28×28 heatmap. Look for the L19–L21 / L24–L25 attended bands and the L22–L23 / L26–L28 unattended bands. **Cost: 30min CPU.** This is a *cheap* replication that needs no training.
- **Layer-pair signal diff on D-bucket**: same heatmap restricted to F-7's 36 D-bucket problems vs 207 A-bucket problems; check whether the canonical interleaving pattern is broken on D-bucket.
- **DoLA-style contrast on Qwen-2.5-1.5B** as a sanity baseline: paper shows DoLA hurts Qwen2.5-VL-7B; we should check whether DoLA also hurts Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Math at 1024 tok, which would be a useful negative control validating the "modern Qwen breaks old tricks" framing.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2309.03883 (DoLA)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Highly cited baseline (paper shows it *hurts* Qwen2.5-VL-7B). It would also be the natural baseline against any future cross-layer correctness experiment we run on Qwen-2.5-1.5B.
- **2410.11779 (DeCo: Dynamic Correction Decoding)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Layer-information fusion baseline that ICLA outperforms; closely related conceptually to ICLA and to our F-9 CoE results.
- **2410.13640 (Chain-of-Embedding)** — already in graph (status: graphed). ICLA's layer-pair attention pattern is the natural next-level abstraction beyond CoE's per-layer trajectory.

## 2603.01025 — One-Token Verification for Reasoning Correctness Estimation (Zhuang et al., 2026)

**Relevance:** OTV is the closest published mechanistic alternative to our F-2 prefill DoM probe and F-8 selective prediction. It trains a LoRA-gated verifier with a special `[ToT]` token that probes the cached KV states of the prefix, and reports a 3-layer MLP regression head over the final-layer hidden state. Their "probe" baseline (last-layer + MLP, no LoRA) is structurally equivalent to our F-2 head — and they show it is the *floor*, not the ceiling: LoRA r=16 across multiple layers beats it by >3 points MAJ@128 on AIME. Their Table 4 also reports that mean/min aggregation over the last 100 tokens dominates prefill-only scoring, directly opposing F-2's "prefill > final-token" headline. Same problem class (math reasoning correctness estimation), overlapping model family (Qwen3, MetaMath-LLaMA, Mistral), comparable scale (4B–32B vs. our 1.5B–7B).

**Key claim we tested:** Multi-layer LoRA-gated probe of the KV cache extracts non-redundant correctness signal beyond what a single-layer linear DoM head can extract. Late-trajectory aggregation (last 100 tokens) dominates prefill aggregation.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — three replicable intermediates queued (P11-FE704 aggregation sweep, P11-FE705 OTV-on-1.5B replication, P11-FE706 perturbation sensitivity). The aggregation sweep is the cheapest direct test of F-2 and is unblocked.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE704, P11-FE705, P11-FE706, H-552, H-553, H-554.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **LoRA-gated verification pathway** — a binary gate `m_t ∈ {0,1}` toggles a LoRA update `W + m_t · R·S` per linear layer, so the base reasoner is bit-identical when `m_t=0`. Only the special `[ToT]` token has `m_t=1`. *Replication cost*: 1 day H100 to fine-tune on Qwen-1.5B with 1k MetaMathQA samples. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — single-step path to a "supervised verifier ceiling" against which F-2's 0.7731 can be benchmarked.

- **`[ToT]` (token of truth) + KV-cache probing** — special token inserted at any position; probes the cached `K^(l), V^(l)` of the prefix via LoRA-augmented attention, regression head on final-layer hidden state. *Replication cost*: 4h CPU prototype on cached activations (no training, just attention-pooling). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — cleanly replaces our final-token-only DoM head.

- **Linear-ramp pseudo-confidence labels** — `c_t = 0.5 + (y−0.5)·t/T` interpolates from "uncertain at start" to "outcome at end". MSE loss on per-token confidence. *Replication cost*: 30min CPU label generation on cached MATH-500 traces. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — alternative to our binary correctness label that may help with mid-trace probes (cheap to test).

- **Triangular probe mask for parallel single-pass training** — insert `[ToT]_{1:T+1}` simultaneously at all positions; a triangular mask `M_{i,j} = 0 if i<j else -∞` enforces that probe `t+1` only attends to prefix `1:t`. Equivalent to T+1 independent single-token verifications in one forward pass. *Replication cost*: 2h CPU implementation against the existing extractor. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — would let us sweep "prefill vs every-token" cheaply.

- **Trace-level aggregation = min/mean over last 100 tokens** — Table 4 ablates {all, last 10%, last 1600, last 400, last 100} × {max, mean, min} × {0%, 25%, 50%, 75% filter}. Best is mean/min over last 100 tokens with 50%–75% trace filtering. *Replication cost*: 1h CPU re-aggregation on existing per-token DoM scores. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — applicable as-is to our current DoM trajectory data, no new model.

- **Semantics-preserving vs logic-breaking perturbation test** (Appendix E, Table 6) — same problem, modify trace via {shortening, lengthening, formatting changes, removing newlines} (semantics-preserving) vs. {changing numbers, altering logic, adding extra steps, corrupting final step} (logic-breaking). Verifier should be invariant to the former, drop on the latter. *Replication cost*: 4h CPU on cached MATH-500 traces with hand-written perturbations. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct robustness test for our DoM probe; a refutation pathway for F-2.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Internal vs external" verification taxonomy** — paper splits verifiers into model-native internal (logit/calibration/probe heads) vs. external (separate reward models). OTV occupies a middle position: model-native architecture + LoRA + supervised on outcome. Maps cleanly onto our F-2 (probe = internal) vs. F-8 (selective prediction = downstream use). Frames our project as living entirely on the internal axis.

- **"Pseudo-confidence labels from outcome supervision"** — instead of process labels (which require expensive step-level annotation), derive token-level confidence targets from the final binary outcome via a deterministic ramp. This is cheaper than rStar-Math/Math-Shepherd but supervised — sits between H-12 (label-free) and process-reward models. Suggests we may be over-investing in F-2's prefill-only frame; the trace-distributed signal might be richer.

- **"Reasoner = verifier" via LoRA gating** — same model parameters, gate flips behavior. Argues against our implicit "verification needs a separate model" assumption (relevant to H-19 routing experiments).

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MetaMathQA** — 395k problems, MIT license, HF (`meta-math/MetaMathQA-40K`). Used for OTV training. Applicable? **yes** — our 1.5B is also Qwen-family and we have no current training set for verifier-style heads.
- **GSM8K** — 8.5k problems, MIT license, HF (`openai/gsm8k`). Used for eval on LLaMA/Mistral backbones. Applicable? **yes** — already in our data lineage; OTV reports 88.46→91.27 Pass@k headroom on Mistral-7B.
- **DAPO17K** — 17k advanced math problems (DAPO project). Permissive, HF available. Applicable? **partial** — only matters if we move beyond MATH-500.
- **AIME24, AIME25** — 30 problems each, public competition. Applicable? **yes (small)** — useful as long-horizon stress test for asymmetric collapse (F-4) and breathing (F-1) at 8000+ tokens.
- **MATH-500** — *not used* by OTV but should be — would let us directly cross-check OTV vs. F-2's 0.7731 on the same 500 problems.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Base reasoners frozen; only LoRA modules + 3-layer MLP regression head are trained.
- LoRA applied to Q, K, V projections at "selected layers" (paper does not enumerate which — Appendix A confirms layer set is a design knob; default reproduced from LlamaFactory configs).
- Default LoRA rank `r=16`; Figure 3 sweeps `r ∈ {2, 4, 8, 16, 32}`. Diminishing returns past r=16.
- 3 epochs, lr `1e-4`, batch 128, LlamaFactory training stack.
- Per training instance: 8 reasoning traces sampled from the frozen base.
- Inference: 256 traces per question at temperature 1.0; subsets of {4,8,16,32,64,128} drawn for downstream voting.
- Aggregation windows differ across baselines: OTV uses last 100 tokens; DeepConf uses last 2048. Apples-to-apples requires matching the window.
- Code repo: not stated in the body. Authors are at SUSTech / CityU HK / Zhejiang — likely upcoming on Zhuang's GitHub.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Re-aggregate existing per-token DoM scores using OTV's window+filter sweep.** Take Stage 4a per-token L19 DoM scores on MATH-500 (1.5B and 7B), compute mean/min/max over {all, last 1600, last 400, last 100} × {0%, 25%, 50%, 75% filter}. Compare AUROC to F-2's 0.7731 prefill anchor. Cached artifact: `pathway11_h100/per_token_activations/*.npz`. ~1h CPU.
- **Probe-baseline replication.** OTV's "probe" baseline is structurally identical to our F-2 head; replicate at LoRA r=0 to get an apples-to-apples floor on Qwen-1.5B. ~4h CPU on cached MetaMathQA features.
- **Linear-ramp re-labeling on existing traces.** Recompute F-8's selective-prediction at 50% coverage with `c_t = 0.5 + (y−0.5)·t/T` instead of binary correctness; check if smoother labels lift the 71.6% number. ~30min CPU.
- **Sensitivity perturbation table on cached 500 traces.** Apply Table 6's 4 semantics-preserving + 5 logic-breaking edits to MATH-500 traces, re-extract L19 DoM scores, check whether DoM is invariant to the former and drops on the latter. ~4h CPU.

### Cross-paper signals

- 2504.05419 — already in graph (status: pending_triage). Same supervision setup (probe at chunk boundaries on AIME), confirms OTV's design space.
- 2410.13640 — already in graph (CoE, pending_triage). OTV's "probe" baseline ≈ closest comparable single-layer probe; CoE-60 is the trajectory-feature analogue.

- 2509.11569 — already in graph (D²HScore, pending_triage). Closely related dispersion-based confidence.
- 2508.15260 (DeepConf, Fu et al. 2025) — NOT in graph; recommend admission. OTV's primary internal-baseline competitor; documents the "log-likelihood aggregation" approach we should benchmark our DoM against directly.

## 2603.03163 — Conditioned Activation Transport for T2I Safety Steering (Chrabąszcz, Szymczyk, Dubiński, Trzciński, Boenisch, Dziedzic, 2026)

**Relevance:** T2I safety paper but its central methodological argument transfers
directly to LLM hidden-state work: linear activation steering (ActAdd, Linear-ACT)
fails on activation manifolds with variance mismatch, non-convex shape, or multi-modal
structure, and apparent "safety" from linear methods is often a side-effect of
pushing activations off-manifold rather than precise concept removal. The proposed
remedy — non-linear MLP residual transport with geometry-aware (Mahalanobis-OOD)
conditioning, and a regularized-shrinkage precision matrix usable in the d ≫ N
regime — is directly applicable to F-2 (linear DoM probe), F-3 (cos=0.046
orthogonality), F-7 / H-7 (D-bucket detection), F-8 (selective prediction), and
H-1 (DoM steering).

**Key claim we tested:** That activation manifolds for high-level concepts often have
covariance/rotation/multimodal structure that a single mean-difference vector cannot
capture, so any ActAdd-style intervention either underperforms or destroys utility
via off-manifold corruption.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** The paper demonstrates this on T2I architectures
(Z-Image, Infinity) and 4 synthetic 2D manifolds. We have not yet checked whether
our L19 prefill correctness manifold exhibits variance-mismatch or XOR-style
geometry; FE76 / H-558 is the cheap diagnostic that gates the rest. If it does,
F-2's 0.7731 is a linear-projection lower bound and H-1's design needs revision.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE707, P11-FE708, P11-FE709, P11-FE710, P11-FE711;
H-555, H-556, H-557, H-558.

### Methodologies extracted from this paper
- Residual MLP transport `T(z)=z+MLP(z)` with zero-init final projection (identity
  at init).
- Dual-objective loss `‖z_s−T(z_u)‖² + λ‖z_s−T(z_s)‖²` with explicit identity-
  preservation regularization.
- Kubokawa-Srivastava shrinkage estimator for precision matrix in d ≫ N regime
  (their Eq. 4).
- Mahalanobis-OOD conditioning (Eq. 6): ellipsoidal decision boundary at quantile
  threshold η_q.
- GDA classifier (Eq. 5): closed-form linear discriminant with class-specific Σ̂⁻¹.
- Synthetic-manifold validation suite (4 distributions: Gaussian / variance-mismatch
  / moon / XOR) — diagnostic taxonomy for manifold complexity.

### Approaches & framings
- "Linear-method 'safety' is often image corruption, not concept removal" → for our
  setting, a steering vector that hurts MATH accuracy by destroying fluency is not
  steering correctness.
- Layer-wise gating (gate at the steered layer) vs CAST-style early-layer gating —
  applies to our prefill-vs-final-token gate placement.

### Datasets
- SafeSteerDataset (2300 contrastive T2I pairs, 23 subcategories, HuggingFace) —
  not applicable to MATH/CoT pipeline.

### Implementation details
- Steering applied only to second half of model layers (early-layer steering
  destroys generation).
- Mean-pool over N tokens before computing gate; broadcast steering δ to all N.
- α swept over {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}; η_q default 0.95.
- Code: https://github.com/NASK-AISafety/conditional-activation-transport.

### Replicable intermediates
All four cross-checks listed in brief Section "Replicable intermediates" run on
existing P11 NPZs without GPU.

### Cross-paper signals
- Cites 2306.03341 (ITI, in graph), 2410.13640-adjacent CoE family, and Lee et al.
  CAST (ICLR 2025, not in graph — recommend admission).
- DSAS (2512.03661) not in graph — recommend admission.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **MLP residual transport map** — `T(z)=z+MLP(z)`; single hidden layer, RMSNorm + GELU,
  zero-init final projection so untrained map is identity.
  *Replication cost*: ~30 min CPU per layer/category on cached prefill NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct H-1 supplement and F-2 ceiling test.

- **Regularized dual-objective loss** —
  `L = ‖z_s − T(z_u)‖² + λ‖z_s − T(z_s)‖²`. The second term penalizes the map for moving
  already-safe inputs, so the MLP learns its own conditioning.
  *Replication cost*: trivial (loss change only).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — λ provides a clean knob for fluency-vs-correctness
  trade-off in any LLM steering experiment.

- **Regularized shrinkage precision matrix (Kubokawa-Srivastava 2008, Eq. 4)** —
  `Σ̂⁻¹ = d·[(N−1)Σ_emp + tr(Σ_emp)·I]⁻¹`; produces stable Σ⁻¹ when d ≫ N.
  *Replication cost*: <1 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — immediate enabler for any Mahalanobis-style scorer at
  d=1536 / N≈500 (we are in d > N regime).

- **Mahalanobis-OOD conditioning (Eq. 6)** — squared Mahalanobis distance to unsafe
  centroid + quantile threshold η_q (default 0.95) — ellipsoidal decision boundary
  conforming to class covariance.
  *Replication cost*: <1 min CPU on cached features.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct alternative gate for selective prediction
  (F-8) and D-bucket detector (H-7).

- **Gaussian-Discriminant-Analysis classifier (Eq. 5)** — closed-form linear discriminant
  with class-specific shrinkage Σ̂⁻¹: `w_k = Σ̂⁻¹μ_k`, `b_k = ln π_k − ½μ_k^T Σ̂⁻¹ μ_k`.
  *Replication cost*: <1 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — non-trivial generalization of logistic probe; may
  raise F-2 AUROC if class covariances differ.

- **Affine transport baseline `T_aff(z)=Wz+b` (zero-init)** — explicitly between ActAdd
  (translation only) and full MLP (non-linear); learns rotations.
  *Replication cost*: ~10 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — disentangles which capability gain comes from rotation
  vs full non-linearity.

- **Synthetic-manifold validation suite** — 4 toy 2D distributions (isotropic Gaussian /
  variance-mismatch / moon / XOR) for stress-testing transport methods.
  *Replication cost*: ~1 hour CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — diagnostic mapping our L19 prefill (correct vs
  incorrect) onto one of these manifold classes via low-dim projection.

- **Layer-wise (vs early-layer) conditioning** — gate fires only when *the current layer's*
  representation is close to the unsafe manifold, not based on the input embedding.
  *Replication cost*: implementation only, no data needed.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — natural fit for the per-layer breathing curve we
  already have from P11 stage markers.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Safety in T2I models is geometrically complex and cannot be resolved by traversing a
  single linear direction."** Direct conceptual challenge to F-2's single-direction reading;
  reframes "DoM" as an artifact of the probe family rather than a fundamental feature.
- **"Apparent safety from linear steering is a side-effect of image corruption — pushing
  activations off-manifold rather than steering them along it."** For our setting:
  a steering vector that lowers MATH accuracy by destroying fluency is not steering
  correctness. Caution applies to interpreting any negative H-1 result.
- **"Conditioning before vs at the layer that produces the concept."** Implies that *where*
  along the network you gate is a non-trivial design choice — for our pipeline, this maps
  to whether the prefill-vs-final-token gate fires on prompt activations (early) or after
  the model has dynamically constructed correctness signal (deeper).
- **"Variance and rotation, not just centroid, encode the concept boundary."** Reframes the
  cos=0.046 result of F-3 as plausibly compatible with non-orthogonal underlying circuits.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **SafeSteerDataset** — 2300 contrastive safe/unsafe T2I prompt pairs across 23
  subcategories; HuggingFace (NASK-PIB/SafeSteerDataset). Applicable? **no** — T2I-only,
  doesn't touch our MATH/CoT/correctness pipeline.
- **MS-COCO val (CLIP score)** — text-image alignment metric. Applicable? **no**.
- **ShieldGemma-2-4b-it** — safety judge model. Applicable? **no** for correctness, but
  *worth noting* as a paradigm: an external judge model produces an automated quality
  signal. The "Limitations" section flags reliance on this judge.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- MLP transport: single hidden layer, RMSNorm + GELU activation, **final projection
  zero-initialized** so untrained map = identity (prevents pre-training degradation).
- Regularization weight λ in dual-objective loss (Eq. 3) — explicit knob trading off
  steering aggressiveness vs identity-preservation on already-safe inputs.
- Steering applied only to **second half of model layers** — early-layer steering produced
  "completely degraded images." Consistent with our P11 result that L19 (mid-late, not
  early) carries the correctness signal.
- Pre-steering reduction: **mean-pool over N tokens** before computing gate/transport,
  then broadcast steering δ to all N tokens (Eq. 1 / Algorithm 1). Worth noting we currently
  use the prefill-final-token activation, not a mean-pool.
- Steering strength α swept over {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}.
- Mahalanobis quantile threshold η_q = 0.95 default.
- Cosine-similarity filter S(z_u, z_s) > 0.7 to retain semantically aligned safe/unsafe
  pairs in dataset construction (Section 3.2) — useful pattern for any contrastive-pair
  curation we do later.
- Code: https://github.com/NASK-AISafety/conditional-activation-transport.

### Replicable intermediates

The smallest cross-checks runnable *now* against cached P11 NPZs, no GPU:

- **Mahalanobis-OOD AUROC vs F-2's 0.7731** — apply Eq. 4 (shrinkage Σ̂⁻¹) +
  Eq. 6 (squared Mahalanobis to incorrect-class centroid) to
  `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/.../prefill_l19.npz`. Compare 5-fold OOF AUROC.
  ~30 min CPU.
- **GDA classifier AUROC vs logistic AUROC** at L19 prefill, same cached features,
  Eq. 5. ~30 min CPU.
- **Manifold-class diagnosis** — project prefill activations onto top-2 PCs within each
  correctness class; visually classify which of CAT's 4 synthetic regimes
  (Gaussian / variance-mismatch / moon / XOR) most resembles the data. ~1 hour CPU.
- **Affine transport AUROC ceiling** — fit `T_aff(z)=Wz+b` with the dual loss (Eq. 3) on
  cached prefill, evaluate post-transport class separability. ~30 min CPU.
- **Per-layer Mahalanobis stack** — repeat Eq. 6 across all P11 stage markers (28 layers),
  combine via class-conditional log-likelihood sum, OOF AUROC. ~2 hours CPU; gates the F-9
  redundancy refutation.

## 2603.12372 — ReBalance: Efficient Reasoning with Balanced Thinking (Li et al., 2026)

**Relevance:** Training-free framework that defines a steerable "overthinking
vs underthinking" behavioural axis from confidence statistics, derives a
single steering direction from hidden-state prototypes at step-boundary
tokens, and modulates injection strength via a confidence-keyed tanh control
function. Reports +3.4 Pass@1 / −23.1% tokens on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B
/ MATH-500 (representative of nine benchmarks, 0.5B–32B). Methodologically
adjacent to H-1 (per-position DoM steering) but with a label-free direction
derivation; data-adjacent because they evaluate on the exact MATH-500 our
1.5B 48.6%-Pass@1 anchor uses. Directly informs F-2 / F-3 / F-7 / F-8 / F-9
through the experiments above.

**Key claim we tested:** A confidence-variance-defined hidden-state prototype
direction yields *both* accuracy lifts and length reductions on MATH-style
reasoning, without any correctness labels — suggesting an alternative,
unsupervised route to the steering signal we've been deriving from labelled
correctness DoM.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — replication blocked on FE74 prototype extraction
(30 min CPU on cached L19 NPZs), then FE76 end-to-end run on H100 (4h).
Outcome will assign one of REPLICATED / PARTIALLY CONFIRMED / CONTRADICTED.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE712, P11-FE713, P11-FE714, P11-FE715, P11-FE716;
H-559, H-560, H-561.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Step-wise confidence (geometric mean of max token probs per step)** —
  `c_s = exp((1/|T_s|) Σ ln p^max_t)`. *Replication cost*: trivial,
  ~1 line over cached log-probs. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a
  scalar to align against L19 DoM.

- **Confidence variance over sliding window `|W|=2`** — short-term fluctuation
  of step-wise confidence. *Replication cost*: trivial, post-processing of
  cached confidences. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — feeds FE73 below.

- **Quantile-thresholded over-/under-thinking labels** — `O = {s : c_s ≤ τ_c^L
  ∧ Var(c_s) ≥ τ_v^H}`, `U = {s : c_s ≥ τ_c^H ∧ Var(c_s) ≤ τ_v^L}`.
  *Replication cost*: trivial. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives label-free
  bucket assignment to compare against our A/B/C/D buckets.

- **Hidden-state prototype averaging at step-boundary token** —
  `μ^O = mean(h_{t_s^(1)} : s ∈ O)`, same for U; first-token-of-step extraction
  from a deep, auto-selected layer. *Replication cost*: 30min H100 if we
  re-extract; <10min CPU on cached Stage 2 NPZs once we tag step-boundary
  tokens. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes.

- **Linear-probing-driven layer auto-selection** — pick the deep layer with
  highest R² for predicting confidence-mode label from the hidden state.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached NPZs, all 28 layers × O/U labels.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — same idea as our DoM AUROC sweep but with
  a different target label.

- **Sign-modulated tanh dynamic strength function** —
  `g(c, v) = sign(c − τ_c^H) · B(c, v) · tanh(|c − τ_c^H|)`.
  *Replication cost*: ~10 lines. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — drop-in for
  H-1 steering at inference.

- **Variance-aware amplitude `B(c_s, v_s)`** — piecewise function over
  (moderate, overthinking, underthinking) regions with boundaries `B_m, B_o,
  B_u ∈ [0, 0.2]`. *Replication cost*: trivial. *We'd plausibly run this*:
  optional — only after the simpler tanh modulation is shown to give traction.

- **First-token-of-step injection (Eq 8)** — apply steering at the residual
  stream before final projection at step boundary only, not every token.
  *Replication cost*: 30min H100 to integrate into our generation harness.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — much cheaper than per-token steering and
  could rescue the per-position DoM steering plan in H-1.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Overthinking vs underthinking" as a continuous behavioural axis distinct
  from correctness** — frames the steerable property as a generation-dynamics
  mode (variance of confidence), not as a correctness label. Intersects H-1
  (steering target need not be the correctness DoM) and H-5 (problem
  familiarity vs decomposability — their "underthinking" is plausibly the
  unfamiliar-but-decomposable case our prefill direction conflates).

- **Steering at step-boundaries rather than every token** — a sparse-injection
  approach. Intersects F-3 (DoM rotation) — sparse injection at a privileged
  token-class might side-step the rotation problem H-1 has been wrestling with.

- **Confidence variance as a "reasoning-dynamics" signal** — reframes what
  we'd been treating as just a noise quantity. Intersects F-9 by giving a
  different operational definition of "trajectory feature" than the CoE
  parameterisation that was killed.

- **Training-free framework via offline prototype + online modulation** —
  matches the stance behind H-1 (all our experiments are inference-time, no
  fine-tuning) and provides a concrete control surface.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MATH-500** — 500 problems, public (HF). Applicable? yes — *the* canonical
  benchmark in our headline numbers; direct comparison possible.
- **AIME24** — 30 problems, public. Applicable? yes — an "out-of-MATH-500"
  hard sanity check we don't currently use, low cost.
- **AIME25** — 30 problems, public. Applicable? yes — same as above.
- **GSM8K** — 1,319 problems, public. Applicable? yes — ties to H-2 (short-CoT
  breathing).
- **AMC23** — 40 problems, public. Applicable? yes — small, cheap, hard.
- **OlympiadBench** — 675 problems, public. Applicable? yes — for H-9
  difficulty-prediction work.
- **GPQA Diamond** — 198 problems, gated (HF). Applicable? marginal — science
  domain, only relevant if H-3 (code generalisation) is generalised to
  science.
- **StrategyQA** — 2,780 problems, public. Applicable? no — commonsense, not
  reasoning-trace heavy.
- **LiveCodeBench v1** — 400 problems, public. Applicable? yes — directly
  feeds H-3 (breathing on code generation).

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Models tested: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-{1.5B, 7B}, Qwen3-14B, QwQ-32B,
  OpenPangu-Embedded-7B-V1.1. Note that DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and
  Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Instruct (our model) share the base — non-trivial transfer
  expectation but distillation-specific behaviour likely differs.
- Steering injection layer: auto-selected via per-layer linear-probing R²;
  authors report mid-late layers (Appendix A.5 figure). Our headline layer is
  L19 of 28, which is roughly the same regime — supports cross-paper
  applicability.
- Calibration set: 500 random MATH problems (one-pass, offline).
- Window size for variance: `|W| = 2` (default; sensitivity in Table 11).
- Quantile thresholds: `q_L, q_H ∈ (0, 1)` empirical, model-specific.
- Mode boundary `B_u ∈ [0, 0.2]` (Table 11).
- No fine-tuning; no RL; no extra inference cost beyond +1 vector add per
  step boundary.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Step-wise confidence + variance on cached MATH-500 Stage 2 traces** —

None of the above need fresh generation; everything sits on the existing

## 2603.14923 — Directional Routing in Transformers (Taylor, 2026)

**Relevance:** Single-author preprint introducing K=4 unit-norm direction vectors per attention head plus a 4-layer mean-pooled MLP router that produces sigmoid suppression weights, at 3.9% parameter cost on a 433M model. The paper's central interpretive claim — "routing is a decoder of pre-existing knowledge, not a feature" (CKA 0.95-0.99 with baseline at every layer despite 31-56% PPL drop) — is a direct stress-test of our F-2 framing of the L19 prefill DoM as a distinct correctness feature. Three other findings carry refutational weight: (i) within-head learned-direction angles average 75.9° (not 90°), placing our F-3 cos=0.046 inside a natural superposition tolerance, (ii) routing's strong perplexity gain fails to transfer to multiple-choice accuracy, predicting that F-8's selective-prediction may plateau on unfamiliar distributions, and (iii) the most critical layer is the *lowest-variance* one (L9, +42.6 PPL when knocked out, variance 127× below L0), inverting our implicit search direction for F-7. The architectural mechanism itself — sequence-pooled directional suppression — is also a P10-style steering analog we have not yet built.

**Key claim we tested:** "Directional intervention at attention output dominates raw head outputs in determining which token wins, and the directional structure is interpretable as a decoder of pre-existing knowledge rather than a new feature axis."

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** The decoder-vs-feature claim is directly testable on cached Qwen-2.5-1.5B P11 activations (P10-FE36 / H-562). The orthogonality-vs-superposition claim is testable from the same cache (P10-FE37 / H-563). The variance-anti-correlation claim is testable across 28 Qwen layers from cached residuals (P11-FE718 / H-564). All three tests are sub-day CPU + at most 4h H100. Vocabulary-projection of our DoM (P11-FE717) is the cheapest sanity check (30min CPU) and may immediately show whether our supervised DoM lands in the same content-token / syntactic-pruning subspaces that emerge unsupervised in their routed model.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE717, P11-FE718, P10-FE36, P10-FE37, H-562, H-563, H-564. Also tightens controls for H-1 (per-position vs sequence-pooled steering) and H-13 (head-level circuit attribution may be empty if coordination dominates).

**Status:** TO TEST.

### Methodologies extracted

- **Vocabulary projection of attention-output directions** — embed direction `d_{h,k} ∈ R^{d_h}` in full d_model (zero-pad outside the head's slice), project through `W_out`, then dot with `W_LM^T` to get vocab-sized logits; top-10 tokens label the direction. Causally validated: overriding routing weight for the 25 article-encoding directions shifts P(article-as-next-token) by −6.2% on n=50 held-out sequences.
  *Replication cost*: ~1h CPU on Qwen-2.5-1.5B (we have model + W_LM cached).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — we would project our L19 prefill DoM through Qwen's W_LM to see what tokens it encodes. Cheap, and gives a content/syntactic label for the direction we've been using as a black-box AUROC vector.

- **Cross-domain routing-weight variance as specialization metric** — for each (head, direction), measure variance of `r_{h,k}` across math/code/prose/factual inputs; high variance = domain-adaptive, low = fixed pruning.
  *Replication cost*: not directly applicable (we don't have a learned routing module). But the analog — variance of L19 DoM-projection across MATH-500 problem domains — is ~30 min CPU on cached activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes**, as a check on H-5 (prefill encodes problem familiarity vs decomposability).

- **Within-head pairwise direction-angle measurement** — among K=4 learned directions per head, compute pairwise angles; compare to angles of K random vectors in d_h dimensions. Detects superposition.
  *Replication cost*: requires per-head DoM extraction (we currently have per-layer pooled). ~3h CPU + cache reorganization.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — directly tests F-3's orthogonality framing.

- **Marginal logit attribution by direct subtraction** — for each component class (token embed, raw heads, routing delta, MLPs), set component to zero, recompute, take ΔLogit. Non-additive due to LayerNorm but interpretable as relative magnitude.
  *Replication cost*: cheap on a single example, ~10min CPU. Already what we do for F-2 OOF eval if reframed.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — apply to MATH-500 final-token logit decomposition to see where the +/− answer-token contribution lives.

- **Routing-OFF / routing-NEUTRAL inference-time intervention** — set `w=0` (suppress everything) or `w=0.5` (uniform half-suppression) at inference; observe perplexity / circuit collapse. Distinct from training-from-scratch ablation.
  *Replication cost*: trivial once a steering hook is in place — standard P10 v2 steering program territory.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — the analog for us is "DoM-suppress at L19 during generation" (essentially H-1's negative control).

- **Cross-domain routing-weight swap** — replace router weights for code-domain inputs with prose-domain weights at a chosen layer; measure ΔPPL. Tests whether layer-level routing is domain-fungible.
  *Replication cost*: not directly applicable; analog would be "use 7B's prefill DoM for 1.5B inference" which we partially do already.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **no** — we have no routing module to swap; the analog is already implicit in P11 H100 cross-model experiment.

- **PCA + nearest-centroid domain classification of routing vectors** — at a chosen layer, run PCA on routing weights across input domains; check if 4-domain separation is clean.
  *Replication cost*: ~30min CPU on cached L19 activations projected through DoM.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes**, as a cheap check on H-5.

### Approaches & framings

- **Routing as denoising / decoding rather than feature creation.** Discussion §8: "Routing is a better decoder of the same underlying knowledge, not a source of new knowledge." Reframes directional intervention as removing cross-domain interference rather than computing new features. **Intersects F-1/F-2/F-8**: our DoM may be a decoder of pre-existing geometric structure rather than a distinct correctness feature. This is actually a stronger framing for the H-12 (label-free semantic-entropy probe) program — if signal is decoder-side, label-free probes that read the same underlying structure should match supervised AUROC.

- **Two-regime architecture: domain-adaptive early layers + syntactic-pruning late layers, emerging without architectural pressure.** Without auxiliary loss, the model self-organizes into specialist layers. **Intersects F-1/F-7**: our pathway-level analysis has not asked whether breathing has *layer-specialized* roles (early-vs-late). Suggests testing whether early-layer breathing is content-adaptive while late-layer breathing is task-invariant.

- **Within-head superposition tolerance ≠ true orthogonality** (75.9° vs 89.4° random). Reframes "are these directions independent" as a question about statistical separation under the model's effective rank. **Intersects F-3**: our cos=0.046 is decision-grade only relative to a baseline angle distribution we have not measured.

- **Coordinator vs components: when explicit coordination exists, head-level attribution is empty.** **Intersects H-13**: our planned head-level circuit decomposition assumes the standard transformer has implicit (residual-stream) coordination that head-level KO can still uncover; this paper suggests it may not.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **FineWeb (Penedo et al. 2024)** — ~2.5B tokens for training. HF, public, ungated. Applicable? **no** — we're not pretraining; only relevant if we re-run their architecture from scratch, which is out of scope.
- **TinyStories** — 26M ablation training. HF, public. Applicable? **no** — ditto.
- **HellaSwag, ARC-Easy/Challenge, PIQA, WinoGrande, BoolQ, LAMBADA** — n=500 each MC eval. All HF, public. Applicable? **partial** — we don't currently evaluate on any of these; could add ARC-Challenge as an out-of-domain selective-prediction benchmark to test refutation #3.
- **Hand-written domain perplexity passages (1264 tokens: 570 code, 252 math, 253 prose, 189 factual)** — not released. Applicable? **no** — proprietary, too small to reproduce reliably.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- 433M param model: 12 layers, 12 heads, d_model=1536, d_head=128, K=4 directions per head → **576 total directions**, 73,728 direction params.
- Router: 4-layer MLP shared across all heads in a layer, takes mean-pooled sequence representation, produces `r ∈ [0,1]^{H×K}`. Sigmoid temperature **T=5.0** to push toward binary decisions. **One** routing decision per sequence (mean-pool bottleneck).
- 12 router MLPs total = 16.1M params (3.7%); +74K direction = 16.2M params total (3.9% overhead, 0.02% FLOPs).
- Training: AdamW + cosine LR, **20K steps**, **2.5B tokens**, GPT-2 tokenizer. **No auxiliary routing loss, no load-balancing, no special init.** Single seed (no variance reported — flagged as a paper limitation).
- Wall-clock penalty: 3,651 → 3,210 tok/s at seq_len=1024 (13.7% slower) due to mean-pool requiring full-sequence forward pass before routing weights are known.
- 6K-step convergence speedup: routed model hits baseline final PPL 1.3× faster, then continues improving — possible inductive-bias gain.
- Pythia-410M cited as directional reference at 120× more training data — we are not in their efficiency-claim regime.
- No code release announced in the paper text we read; single-author preprint.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Vocabulary-project our cached L19 prefill DoM through Qwen-2.5-1.5B's W_LM head.** Output: top-10 tokens that the DoM encodes. Cost: ~30min CPU. Tests whether our DoM aligns to content-token / punctuation / article axes (paper's 88.2/2.4/4.3 split).
  *Cached artifact*: `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json` has the DoM vector or it can be recomputed from cached residuals. Need `model.lm_head.weight` from HF Qwen-2.5-1.5B.
- **Compute paired routing-OFF analog: run inference with L19 DoM projected out of the residual stream during generation, log ΔPPL on MATH-500 prefill.** Cost: ~2h CPU on cached activations + brief H100 for fresh forward passes. Tests refutation #4.
  *Cached artifact*: cached L19 residual streams from P11 + Qwen weights for the rest-of-model forward pass.
- **Compute CKA between Qwen L19 activations on correct vs incorrect MATH-500 problems.** Cost: ~30min CPU on `pathway11_h100` cached residuals. If CKA ≥ 0.95, our DoM is operating in a near-identical representational subspace — supports decoder framing.
- **Per-layer ablation analog: probe AUROC at every Qwen layer 0-27 using L19 DoM-style logistic probe.** Cost: ~1h CPU. We have this from F-2 era already; need to surface min-variance layer to test refutation #5.

### Cross-paper signals

## 2603.18280 — Detection Is Cheap, Routing Is Learned: Why Refusal-Based Alignment Evaluation Fails (Anonymous, 2026)

**Relevance:** Methodologically central even though the substantive domain (Chinese-origin LLM political censorship) is far from MATH-500 correctness. The paper formalises three pieces of probe hygiene we have been informal about: (i) random-split probe accuracy is non-diagnostic — null controls and shuffled-label baselines can reach 100% — and only held-out *category* generalization is informative; (ii) ridge-residualization against a capability basis is the right way to separate concept from confound; (iii) single-direction CAA-style ablation `h' = h − α·(h·v̂)·v̂` works *within-model* but fails to transfer across model families. Each of these directly stresses F-2 (prefill L19 DoM AUROC 0.7731) and F-8 (selective prediction at 71.6%). The paper's "detect → route → generate" three-stage framework also gives a non-trivial reframing of F-3's prefill/final orthogonality.

**Key claim we tested:** In our terms, "probe AUROC under random-split CV is not enough — leave-one-category-out and capability-residualization are the diagnostic tests." We have not yet run either on F-2.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** F-2 has not been subjected to LOCO-subject CV (P11-FE719), ridge-residualization (P11-FE720), concept-cone expansion (P11-FE721), null-baseline comparison (P11-FE722), or cross-model transfer (P11-FE723). Until those run, F-2's STRONG label is provisional under this paper's diagnostic standard.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE719, P11-FE720, P11-FE721, P11-FE722, P11-FE723, H-565, H-566, H-567

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **CAA-style rank-one projection ablation** — `h' = h − α·(h·v̂)·v̂` applied across a band of layers with sweep α ∈ {2,5,8,12,20}.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min H100 on cached Qwen-2.5-1.5B (just need forward pass with hooks).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — it's the causal complement to F-2 we've been deferring (P11-FE3-style activation patching).

- **Ridge residualization against capability axes** — Tikhonov-regularised projection that removes capability-aligned components (math, coding, reasoning, writing, safety) from the candidate direction *before* probing/ablating, λᵣ=0.01.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached prefill activations + need to define a capability basis (problem length, latex density, subject one-hot, math-token logit norm).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly addresses Refutation #4. Cheapest step toward "is F-2 actually correctness or capability/topic?"

- **Leave-one-category-out cross-validation (LOCO-CV)** as probe diagnostic — train on 5 of 6 categories, test on held-out; demand >>50% accuracy on held-out as the only meaningful generalization test.
  *Replication cost*: 20 min CPU on cached prefill NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — leave-one-subject-out across MATH-500's 7 subjects is the obvious analogue. Highest-leverage cheap refutation test in this brief.

- **Null/permutation probe controls** (food-vs-tech, shuffled labels) to establish the noise floor of the probe pipeline.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — shuffle-label baseline is one we should have already run for F-2.

- **Multi-judge LLM scoring** (Gemini 2.5 Flash + 3 AI judges + 1 human, 1–5 scale, 8-category taxonomy) for behavioral evaluation.
  *Replication cost*: minimal API.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — our outcome variable is correctness (binary, MATH-500 has gold answers), not narrative compliance.

- **Cross-model direction transfer test** — extract direction from model A, ablate in model B, measure behavioral change.
  *Replication cost*: 2h H100 on Qwen-2.5-1.5B → Qwen-2.5-7B pair.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly tests whether F-2's DoM is universal or model-specific (paper says model-specific, would constrain H-11 distillation).

### Approaches & framings

- **Three-stage descriptive framework: detect → route → generate.** Reframes our prefill/final orthogonality (F-3) as a detection/generation decoupling with an unobserved routing layer between them. Suggests a missing third probe target ("which layer/circuit *routes* detection to behavior?") that we haven't searched for.

- **"Probe accuracy is necessary but not sufficient" as a normative principle.** Reframes every AUROC we've reported as a *candidate* signal that needs (a) null-control floor, (b) held-out category test, (c) capability-residualization before being treated as evidence of a correctness mechanism.

- **Mechanism shift / behavioral substitution** — refusal can collapse while narrative steering compensates. Analogue for us: if we steer against the "incorrect" pole on MATH-500 and accuracy stays flat, the model may have substituted a different failure mode (e.g., refused to answer, hedged, returned trivially-wrong format) rather than become more correct. Argues for richer outcome metrics than binary correctness in any future H-1 trial.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **CCP-sensitive prompt corpus (24+24 control v1; 32+32 v3 with Western parallels)** — proprietary to authors, small, political-content domain. Applicable? no — outcome variable is narrative compliance, not correctness.
- **HarmBench (60 stratified behaviors, used for safety-direction extraction)** — public, HF. Applicable? no for direct use; relevant only if we ever run H-12 (semantic-entropy probes) on safety-tinged subsets.
- **MATH-500 7-subject decomposition** — *our* existing dataset, already cached. Applicable? yes — natural substrate for the LOCO-CV analogue (leave-one-subject-out).

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Ridge probe hyperparameter: λ=1.0 (fixed, not swept). For our DoM probes that's a defensible default rather than the sklearn default.
- Effective ablation depth band: 40–65% of model depth (their finding across 5 model families). For Qwen-2.5-1.5B (28 layers), this maps to layers ~11–18 — brackets our L19 DoM, modestly above mid-depth.
- α sweep range: {2, 5, 8, 12, 20} with effective range α=5–8. Useful prior for any DoM-steering trial under H-1.
- Capability basis for ridge residualization: math, coding, reasoning, writing, safety. Direct template for our analogue (math-formula recall, latex density, problem length, subject one-hot).
- Sample-set size: 48 prompts (24+24) sufficient for direction extraction. Suggests our 1024-tok DoM extracted from 500 problems is generously over-specified; we could compute LOCO-CV on tiny per-subject splits without sample-size concerns.
- Code/data availability: paper mentions GitHub repo (not URL-extracted from PDF); worth `pip` checking before any replication.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Leave-one-subject-out CV on F-2.** MATH-500 has 7 subjects (Prealgebra, Algebra, Number Theory, Counting & Probability, Geometry, Intermediate Algebra, Precalculus). Train DoM on 6 subjects' prefill activations from `pathway11_h100/.../prefill_*.npz`, evaluate AUROC on the held-out subject. Repeat 7 times, report mean and worst-case. **This is the single highest-leverage cheap test in the brief — ~20 min CPU on already-cached data.** Script: extend `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/run.py` with subject-stratified split or write `scripts/loco_subject_cv.py`.
- **Shuffle-label null control.** Same prefill NPZ, randomly permute correctness labels, retrain DoM, report AUROC. Should land at ~0.5; if higher, we have leakage. ~10 min CPU.
- **Length/latex-density null baseline for F-8 selective prediction.** Logistic regression on `len(problem_text)`, `latex_token_count`, `digit_count` only (no hidden states), compute selective-prediction curve, compare to F-8's 71.6% at coverage 0.5. ~15 min CPU.
- **Ridge-residualised DoM AUROC.** Project capability basis (length, latex density, subject one-hot, math-token logit norm) out of L19 prefill activations, recompute DoM AUROC. If it stays ≥0.74, F-2 survives the capability-control test; if it drops below 0.65, F-2 is mostly capability/topic. ~1 h CPU.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2406.11717 (Arditi, Refusal Single Direction)** — already in graph, status `graphed`. Paper directly cites as the canonical single-direction precedent. No new admission needed.
- **2310.06824 (Marks & Tegmark, Geometry of Truth)** — already in graph, status `graphed`. Likely cited as another single-direction probing precedent.
- **2310.01405 (Zou et al., Representation Engineering / RepE)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Foundational ablation/steering methodology paper this work builds on; should be a peer of 2406.11717 in our PAPER_INDEX.
- **Wollschlager et al. 2025 "The Geometry of Refusal: Concept Cones and Representational Independence" (ICML 2025)** — arxiv ID not yet resolved by us; recommend admission. Directly attacks the single-direction ansatz F-2/F-3 rest on; concept-cone framing is a candidate refutation generator for our work.
- **Zhao et al. NeurIPS 2025 "LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately"** — arxiv ID not yet resolved; recommend admission. "Two separable concepts in residual stream" parallels prefill-vs-final orthogonality (F-3), giving a non-correctness analogue of the same mechanism.
- **1909.03368 (Hewitt & Liang, Probe Control Tasks)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission as **CRITICAL** methodological reference. Original source of the "non-diagnosticity of probe accuracy" critique that drives our Refutation #1 and motivates LOCO-CV.

## 2603.24787 — ReLope: KL-Regularized LoRA Probes for Multimodal LLM Routing (Zeng, Wang, Chen, Lin, 2026)

**Relevance:** Direct probe-architecture upgrade over our F-2 / F-8 single-layer linear DoM. Multimodal-specific application (their problem: visual inputs weaken correctness separability) translates structurally to our text-only correctness-prediction setup. Three reusable methodological primitives: (a) attention-aggregation across preceding tokens/layers, (b) LoRA-adapter probe (rank 128, α=256) on a single layer, (c) KL-regularized variational bottleneck for distribution-shift robustness. Their text-only baseline number (95.36 AUC on ScienceQA) is an apples-to-oranges-easy benchmark, but the *gap* between baseline-MLP and full-ReLope (+4.35 avg AUC absolute) is the relevant signal for porting to MATH-500.

**Key claim we tested:** "Hidden-state probe quality is bottlenecked by single-token single-layer linear extraction; attention aggregation + LoRA + KL bottleneck lifts AUROC and stabilizes it under perturbation."

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** Triggers H-568 (linear-probe ceiling test, HIGH), H-569 (prefill/final orthogonality is aliasing, HIGH), H-570 (KL-regularized lift to F-8 ceiling, MEDIUM). H-568 and H-569 are CPU-only on cached NPZs and should run before any new H100 pod is brought up.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE724, P11-FE725, P11-FE726, H-568, H-569, H-570.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Attention Probe (token-level hidden-state aggregation)** — learnable query vector `q` produces softmax weights `βᵢ` over preceding-layer hidden states; weighted sum becomes probe input.
  *Replication cost:* 30min CPU on cached L18–L20 NPZs (MATH-500 × 500 × 3 layers × 1.5B activations).
  *We'd plausibly run this:* **yes** — directly tests F-3's "orthogonal directions" claim and is the cheapest possible probe-architecture upgrade. No retraining needed.

- **ReLope (KL-regularized LoRA probe with variational bottleneck)** — LoRA rank 128, α=256, inserted into a single transformer layer; output mapped to Gaussian posterior `N(μ, σ²)`; trained with BCE + β·KL(N(μ,σ²) ‖ N(0,I)), β∈[0.5, 1.0] optimal.
  *Replication cost:* 4h H100 to train per layer + per model (no full-model retraining; LoRA only).
  *We'd plausibly run this:* **yes** — direct probe-family upgrade for F-2/F-8, and the KL term is the right architectural answer to the perturbation-robustness story.

- **5-layer MLP probe head** — used as the classifier on top of aggregated/LoRA features.
  *Replication cost:* trivial, 10min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* **yes** — minimum-effort upgrade from logistic to nonlinear probe; settles whether F-2's 0.7731 ceiling is linear-probe-bound.

- **Cross-dataset OOD probe evaluation (train on N−1, test on held-out)** — they report ReLope's strongest cross-dataset transfer at 76.66 (MMMU), 83.68 (AOKVQA), etc.
  *Replication cost:* 1h CPU once probes are trained.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* **partially** — we have only one MATH-500 split, but we could split by problem difficulty (level 1–5) and run a leave-one-difficulty-out variant of F-2 / F-8, which would also tighten F-7 (D-bucket).

- **Variational bottleneck for distribution-shift robustness** — gauges ΔAUC under controlled perturbations.
  *Replication cost:* depends — for text we don't have an obvious analogue of image noise, but paraphrase / prompt-format jitter is the equivalent.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* **yes, downstream** — useful as the next-after-ReLope-port experiment if H-12 is parked.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Signal is distributed across positions and layers, not localized"** — directly opposes the single-position L19 DoM framing of F-2/F-3. Forces us to revisit whether prefill/final orthogonality is real or aliasing.
- **"Variational bottleneck = robust correctness representation"** — a principled architectural answer to the implicit assumption in F-8 that linear probing is sufficient. Frames probe design as a regularization problem, not a representation-extraction one.
- **"Routing as the downstream task, probe quality as the upstream bottleneck"** — their problem statement (multimodal probes degrade) is structurally identical to ours (Qwen-1.5B prefill DoM saturates at 0.7731). The F-8 selective-prediction setup is a one-model special case of their cascade-routing setup.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MMMU** — ~12K multi-discipline academic VQA. License: research, HF available. Applicable? **no** — multimodal-only.
- **A-OKVQA** — 25K+ visual QA with world knowledge. HF available. Applicable? **no** — multimodal-only.
- **ScienceQA** — 21K+ middle-school science. HF available. Applicable? **partial** — text-only subset *is* used by their abstract's 95.36 number; could be a cross-domain probe-transfer test.
- **ChartQA, MathVision** — multimodal; not applicable to text-only MATH-500 pipeline.

None of these are direct MATH-500 substitutes. The methodology transfers; the data does not.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **Probe layer placement:** L24 of 32 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B / Phi-4-MM (≈ layer 0.75 of depth); L40 of 48 for Gemma3-12B (≈ 0.83). Our F-2 uses L19 of 28 (Qwen-2.5-1.5B) ≈ 0.68 — we are slightly shallower than their optimum. Worth checking L21–L23 in cached NPZs.
- **LoRA rank ablation:** 32, 64, 128, 256 — plateau at 128.
- **KL coefficient β ablation:** 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 — optimal 0.5–1.0.
- **Optimizer:** AdamW, lr 1e-4, A100 80GB.
- **Probe head:** 5-layer MLP (architecture details not given in fetched excerpt).
- **GitHub code released** per abstract — not yet located; recommend a follow-up fetch before serious replication.
- **Robustness eval:** image noise / JPEG / Gaussian blur (multimodal-only, not directly portable).

### Replicable intermediates

- **Drop-in MLP probe on cached prefill L19 activations** — `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` already contains the prefill-position L19 mean-pooled activations and labels for 500 MATH-500 problems on Qwen-2.5-1.5B and 7B. Fitting a 5-layer MLP (5-fold OOF) is one Python script (sklearn or torch) and gives the cheapest possible probe-of-probes refutation of F-2's linear ceiling. Cost: 30min CPU.
- **Attention-probe over L18–L20 prefill** — assuming Stage-2 NPZs include all layers (verify against `DATA_MANIFEST.md`). Cost: 1h CPU.
- **No replicable intermediate against ReLope's main claim itself** — their headline is multimodal-routing AUC; we have no MLLM and no multimodal benchmark. Pure methodology transfer only.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2402.03744** — INSIDE / EigenScore — already in graph (status: **graphed**, CITED ONLY). Adjacent baseline-probe family that ReLope's framing implicitly competes with.
- **2410.13640** — Chain-of-Embedding — already in graph (status: **graphed**, PARTIALLY CONFIRMED). CoE is a layer-trajectory probe; ReLope's attention-aggregation across layers is methodologically related but adds *learned* aggregation rather than fixed concatenation.
- **2406.15927** — Semantic Entropy Probes — already in graph (status: **graphed**, CITED ONLY). The natural label-free competitor for the H-12 head-to-head proposed in Refutation 3.
- **RouteLLM, FrugalGPT, MoT** — not in graph; off-axis (routing-specific, no probe-design content directly relevant). **Do not recommend admission** unless the routing axis becomes a project goal.
- **Author github (per abstract)** — recommend fetching the code repo URL after the abstract page is re-fetched; useful for verifying probe-head architecture and KL-regularization implementation.

## 2603.25052 — Closing the Confidence-Faithfulness Gap in Large Language Models (Miao & Ungar, 2026)

**Relevance:** Direct geometric counterpart of our F-2/F-3/F-8 cluster. Across three
7B base+instruct families (Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5, Mistral) and four datasets (MATH, MMLU,
TriviaQA, TruthfulQA), they find that gold-calibration (linear probe of empirical
accuracy from a "pure correctness" prompt) and verbalized confidence (probe from a "pure
confidence" prompt) are encoded in nearly orthogonal directions (cos < 0.04), and that
joint solve-and-rate prompts invert the relationship from +0.26 to −0.63 ("Reasoning
Contamination Effect"). They use this to build a two-stage adaptive steering pipeline
that drops MATH ECE 4–7× over unsteered verbalized confidence and over SteerConf
prompt-based baseline.

**Key claim we tested:** A single linear direction in the residual stream tracks
empirical accuracy and is recoverable via a linear probe from prompt-completion
activations.

**Our result:** **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED.** Our F-2 reports prefill L19 DoM AUROC 0.7731
on Qwen-2.5-1.5B — directly analogous to their gold-calibration probe at r=0.80 on
Qwen-2.5-7B at L21. Their cos < 0.04 between pure-correctness and pure-confidence
directions is numerically twin to our cos = 0.046 between prefill and final-token DoM
(F-3) — but the two cuts are conceptually different (theirs: task-elicited; ours:
position-elicited). H-571 tests whether they are the same phenomenon under different
labels. Their joint-prompt contamination effect (−0.63) raises the possibility that our
joint-prompt-trained DoM is itself contaminated; H-573 / FE-77 directly tests this by
re-extracting under pure-correctness prompts.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE727, P11-FE728, P11-FE729, P11-FE730, P11-FE731; H-571, H-572,
H-573, H-574.

**Status:** PARTIALLY CONFIRMED (F-2 mechanism corroborated at 7B); TO TEST (whether
F-3 is a position-elicited or task-elicited orthogonality, and whether their two-stage
pipeline transfers to 1.5B).

### Methodologies extracted

- **Gold calibration linear probing** — ridge regression on residual-stream activations
  from a "pure correctness" prompt (no confidence wording) against empirical accuracy
  computed as fraction-correct over 50 samples per question.
  *Replication cost:* ~2h CPU on cached prefill NPZs + 6h H100 if we need to re-extract
  under a no-confidence prompt template.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes — directly tests F-2 prompt-template robustness.
- **Pure-confidence prompt + linear probe** — extract activations under a confidence-only
  prompt (no answer), probe verbalized confidence.
  *Replication cost:* 4h H100 to re-run on Qwen-2.5-1.5B + 1h CPU for probe.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes — establishes the verbalized-confidence direction we
  could compare to prefill DoM.
- **Joint-prompt orthogonality contrast (cos = −0.63)** — extract contrastive
  confidence direction (mean H − mean L over K=11 framings, within-question) and
  contrastive accuracy direction; measure cosine.
  *Replication cost:* 6h H100 (need K=11 framings × MATH-500) + 1h CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes — directly probes whether prefill DoM is contaminated.
- **Within-question CAA contrast (Eq. 1)** — per-question contrast across K confidence
  framings, then average across Q. Controls for question-level confounds (difficulty,
  topic, format) that a global mass-mean ignores.
  *Replication cost:* 1h CPU once K=11-framing activations cached.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes — better controlled than our DoM (mean-correct − mean-incorrect).
- **PCHIP-inverted α* transfer function** — sweep α ∈ [−2, +2] at 0.1 steps on
  validation; PCHIP-invert α → mean-verbal-confidence to obtain α*(c*) per question.
  *Replication cost:* 30min CPU once α-sweep generations exist.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* maybe — only relevant if we adopt their two-stage
  calibration framing.
- **Two-stage adaptive steering pipeline** — Stage 1 probe target c*; Stage 2
  question-specific α* steering to match.
  *Replication cost:* 8h H100 end-to-end on Qwen-2.5-1.5B at MATH-500 (need K=11
  framings + α-sweep + adaptive generations).
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes — high ROI for converting F-8 to a calibration story.
- **Isotonic regression calibration of probe outputs** — held-out validation split.
  *Replication cost:* 5min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this:* yes — trivial add-on to F-8.

### Approaches & framings

- **"Readout failure, not knowledge deficit" framing.** Recasts miscalibration as a
  generation-side problem: the signal is in the residual stream, the model just fails
  to surface it. Aligns with our F-2 ("model knows from prefill") but adds a normative
  conclusion (correct the readout, not the model).
- **Reasoning Contamination Effect.** Joint solve-and-rate prompts force the
  effort-encoding direction to be re-interpreted as confidence, inverting the
  confidence/accuracy alignment from +0.26 to −0.63. New conceptual handle for our F-3
  orthogonality story — possibly the *mechanism* behind it.
- **Within-question contrast vector design.** Computing CAA contrasts within a single
  question (across K framings) before averaging across questions removes question-level
  confounds. Cleaner alternative to our mean-correct − mean-incorrect DoM.
- **Prompt-completion vs answer-completion extraction equivalence.** They report both
  yield similar steering vectors and use prompt-completion for practicality. We use
  prefill-completion as the headline; this paper provides supporting evidence that
  prompt-position activations are sufficient for confidence-relevant probing.
- **Probe-as-target reframing.** Rather than thresholding the probe for abstention
  (F-8), use it as the regression target the model should *match*. Reframes selective
  prediction as adaptive calibration.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MATH (Hendrycks 2021b)** — overlaps directly with our MATH-500 subset. HF.
  Applicable: yes.
- **MMLU** — broad knowledge QA, multiple-choice. HF. Applicable: only as
  cross-domain transfer test for any prefill-DoM steering vector.
- **TriviaQA (Joshi 2017)** — open-ended factual QA. HF. Applicable: only for
  cross-domain transfer.
- **TruthfulQA (Lin 2022b)** — truthfulness eval. HF. Applicable: only for
  cross-domain transfer; not load-bearing for our reasoning-correctness story.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- **Activation extraction site:** residual stream after MLP sublayer; both
  prompt-completion and answer-completion positions yield similar vectors. They use
  prompt-completion throughout. Matches our prefill protocol.
- **Steering-layer choices found by validation sweep:** Qwen2.5-7B → L21,
  Llama-3.1-8B → L24, Mistral-7B → L27. All sit at fractional-depth ~0.75–0.96 of model.
  Our L19 in 28-layer Qwen-2.5-1.5B is at fractional-depth 0.68 — slightly earlier than
  their best layers but in the same regime.
- **Steering injection at answer-token outperforms last-prompt-only or both-jointly.**
  Slight effect, but consistent.
- **K=11 confidence framings, τ_hi = 0.75, τ_lo = 0.25 thresholds** for high/low-confidence
  partition (within-question).
- **All generations T = 1.0** — matches the temperature used during activation
  collection.
- **Steering vectors are unit-normalized then rescaled by mean activation norm at the
  layer** (Eq. 3). Gives α a model/layer-independent interpretation.
- **Validation split selects steering layer + strength** before any test eval.
- **Code/repo:** none linked in the abstract; would need to email authors or
  reverse-engineer from §2.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Already cached:** cos(prefill_DoM, final_DoM) = 0.046 in
  `scratch/pathway10_temporal_and_verifier_results.json` — directly comparable to their
  cos < 0.04 between pure-correctness vs pure-verbal-confidence probe directions.
- **Already cached, no re-extract:** apply isotonic regression to existing prefill L19
  DoM scores on MATH-500 (Pathway 11), compute ECE / Brier / MAE against per-question
  K=8 empirical accuracy. ~30 min CPU. Tests refutation (4) above.
- **Cheap re-extract:** fit a new probe on cached Pathway 11 prefill activations using
  ridge with broad ℓ2 sweep (their protocol) instead of mass-mean DoM, compare AUROC.
  ~1h CPU.
- **Requires new generation:** their K=11-framing activation collection, their pure-
  correctness vs pure-confidence vs joint comparison — all need fresh prompts +
  re-extraction on 1.5B, ~6h H100 each.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2604.22271 (Kumaran et al.)** — already in graph (status: graphed). The paper builds
  on Kumaran's "verbalized confidence cached at answer-adjacent positions" finding;
  their orthogonality finding is the geometric counterpart of Kumaran's PANL signal.
- **2306.03341 (Li et al., ITI)** — already in graph (status: graphed,
  CONTRADICTED). The paper is a cleaner instantiation of ITI-style steering with a
  better-controlled within-question contrast and a probe-driven adaptive α; supports
  our existing F-3-vs-ITI contradiction.
