## 2604.01170 — Online Reasoning Calibration: Test-Time Training Enables Generalizable Conformal LLM Reasoning (Zhou, Wang, Wu, Zhu, Shi, Wang, Wilson, Jaakkola, Bates, 2026)

**Relevance:** ORCA is the strongest single competitor to our static-DoM selective-prediction
framework (F-2, F-8). It frames calibration as an *online* objective optimized at every reasoning step
via TTT (test-time training) inner-loop fast-weight updates and an outer-loop meta-trained
initialization, with finite-sample risk control via Learn-then-Test (LTT). On MATH-500 (our shared
benchmark) it achieves 67.0% step savings at error rate 2.1% with δ=0.1, vs. 24.8% for the static
linear-probe baseline. The static baseline is conceptually identical to our prefill L19 DoM probe
(modulo layer choice — they use mean-pooled last-layer; we use L19), so its dominance by TTT is a
direct challenge to F-2's "single static direction at AUROC 0.7731 is sufficient" framing and F-8's
"71.6% accuracy at 50% coverage" headline. The paper also offers a methodological upgrade we
should adopt regardless of TTT outcomes: LTT calibration gives finite-sample risk guarantees on
selective-prediction rules that F-8 currently lacks.

**Key claim we tested:** A *static* linear probe on hidden states leaves 18–25% relative
selective-prediction efficiency on the table compared to a TTT probe whose weights are
gradient-updated per reasoning step against a Brier loss. On MATH-500 OOD specifically, the gap
widens to 2.6–2.7× under δ=0.1.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** We have not yet run a TTT update on top of our prefill L19 DoM, nor
have we applied LTT calibration to our selective-prediction pipeline. P11-FE732 (TTT update on
cached residuals, ~30min CPU) and P11-FE733 (LTT calibration, ~20min CPU) are READY.
Outcome of these will determine whether ORCA REPLICATES (TTT lifts AUROC, LTT improves
selective-prediction risk control), is CONTRADICTED at our scale (no lift on Qwen-1.5B → ORCA is
≥32B-only), or is PARTIALLY CONFIRMED (LTT works but TTT doesn't transfer).

**Related experiments:** P11-FE732, P11-FE733, P11-FE734, P11-FE735 (this brief);
H-575, H-576, H-577.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **No-QK TTT probe** — single linear probe `f(φ_t; W_t) = σ(W·φ_t + b)`, fast weights updated per step
  via online gradient descent on Brier loss against C_t.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached Stage-2 NPZs. *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — direct test
  of F-9 and Refutation 4.
- **QK TTT probe** — adds learned `θ_K, θ_Q ∈ R^{d_h × d_φ}` projections (d_h=128) so the update
  direction (K) and scoring direction (Q) attend to different aspects of the hidden state.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU. *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — natural ablation; tests whether
  "direction-of-update ≠ direction-of-scoring" is an effective inductive bias for our regime.
- **Bilevel TTT outer-loop training** — truncated BPTT through the inner-loop unroll, Adam outer
  lr=1e-3, gradient clipping 1.0, inner η=0.01.
  *Replication cost*: 4h CPU on our 5K-equivalent training corpus. *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — the
  paper's headline result depends on this; we cannot test refutations 1–3 properly without it.
- **LTT calibration of stopping rules** — sweep threshold grid Λ, compute binomial p-value
  `p_j = P(Binom(n, δ) ≤ n·R̂_n(λ_j))`, apply fixed-sequence testing for FWER, pick most aggressive
  rejected threshold.
  *Replication cost*: 20min CPU. *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — gives us finite-sample risk control on
  F-8's selective-prediction claim, currently absent.
- **Consistent-mode label C_t = I{ans(y_t) = ans(y_T)}** — self-consistency-style label that bypasses
  ground truth.
  *Replication cost*: needs intermediate-answer extraction at each step (we currently only checkpoint
  final answers); ~2h CPU + intermediate-answer parser. *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — closest
  label-free probe we've seen to date.
- **Score smoothing (rolling window of 10 steps).** *Replication cost*: trivial. *We'd plausibly run this*:
  **yes** — cheap baseline noise-reduction we should test.
- **Mean-pooled last-layer hidden state as φ_t.** *Replication cost*: zero — already cached at L19; switch
  to L_last is a one-line change. *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — sanity check whether layer choice
  matters.

### Approaches & framings

- **Calibration-as-online-objective.** Rather than treating calibration as a post-hoc fit on a held-out set,
  ORCA frames it as an objective the model adapts toward at every reasoning step. Intersects F-2 / F-8
  by suggesting our "single direction, fit once, deployed forever" framing is the *limiting* case of a richer
  online procedure.
- **Bilevel separation of "learn to calibrate" vs. "learn to learn to calibrate."** Conceptually decouples
  per-instance adaptation (inner) from cross-distribution generalization (outer). Maps onto our F-2/F-7
  tension: F-2 is the per-instance signal, F-7 is the collective-bucket signal — ORCA gives a principled
  way to fit both.
- **Conformalize the *deployed procedure*, not the *raw scorer*.** Their LTT calibration controls risk over
  the full pipeline including the online updates and the stopping rule, with finite-sample guarantees.
  Our F-8 currently has *no* finite-sample risk guarantee — this is a methodological upgrade we could
  adopt verbatim.
- **Distribution shift at two levels: sample-level (within-CoT step variation) and dataset-level
  (deployment vs. training prompt distribution).** Useful framing for our 256-tok / 1024-tok confound:
  the truncation-confound was effectively an undeclared dataset-level distribution shift.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MATH-500** (Hendrycks et al., 2021) — 500 problems, public, HF-accessible. Applicable? **yes** — our
  primary OOD benchmark; direct head-to-head possible.
- **GPQA-Diamond** (Rein et al., 2024) — 198 problems, public, HF-accessible. Applicable? **yes** —
  natural extension of our MATH-500 pipeline; we have not yet evaluated F-2/F-8 on GPQA.
- **AIME 2024 / 2025 / 2026** — 30 problems each, public. Applicable? **yes, with caveats** — small N
  (≤30) limits statistical power for our AUROC-style claims; better as a stress test than a primary eval.
- **s1K** (Muennighoff et al., 2025) — 1000 math problems, public, HF (`s1K`). Applicable? **yes** —
  candidate component of a 5K-style training corpus if we replicate ORCA on Qwen 1.5B.
- **OpenR1** (HuggingFace, 2025) — public. Applicable? **yes** — same.
- **DeepMath** (He et al., 2025; arxiv 2504.11456) — 103K math problems, public. Applicable? **yes** —
  same; not yet in our research-graph.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Outer Adam lr = 1e-3, gradient clipping 1.0, inner η = 0.01.
- Score trajectories smoothed with rolling window of 10 steps.
- Epoch selection: 20 for no-QK, 10 for QK variants (overfitting at higher epochs).
- Hidden state: mean-pooled *last-layer* (d_φ = 5,120 for Qwen2.5-32B / QwQ-32B; 8,192 for Llama-3.3-70B).
- Reasoning trajectories generated by DeepSeek-R1-671B; correctness labels from Qwen-3-32B as
  teacher; GPT-4.1 for evaluation.
- Train/calibration/test split: 3,000 / 1,000 / 1,000 (5K corpus from s1K + OpenR1 + DeepMath).
- Risk levels swept: δ ∈ {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20}; failure probability ε = 0.05.
- Code: https://github.com/wzekai99/ORCA (public).

### Replicable intermediates

- **No-QK TTT update on cached L19 prefill DoM, MATH-500.** Use
  `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json` and the cached L19 residuals. Initialize W_0 from
  our fitted prefill DoM, run η=0.01 online updates, measure 5-fold OOF AUROC at the final step. Tests
  Refutations 1, 2, 4. Cost: ~30min CPU.
- **LTT calibration on our existing prefill DoM scores.** Wrap `validate_claims.py`'s prefill-DoM eval
  with the binomial-p-value + fixed-sequence testing recipe. Tests Refutation 3. Cost: ~20min CPU.
- **`cos(W_0, W_T)` measurement** along the TTT trajectory on a 50-problem MATH-500 subsample.
  Single artifact: a NPZ of step-wise weights from a no-QK unroll. Tests F-3's "orthogonality is
  structural" claim. Cost: included in 30min above.
- **Layer-swap sanity check.** Re-run our static DoM at the *final* layer (L27 on Qwen-1.5B) instead of
  L19 to confirm whether ORCA's layer choice (last layer) matters for our regime. Cost: 10min on
  cached residuals — we should already have L_last activations from Stage 2.

### Cross-paper signals

## 2604.05655 — LLM Reasoning as Trajectories: Step-Specific Representation Geometry and Correctness Signals (Sun et al., 2026)

**Relevance:** Closest sibling paper to Pathway 11. They model CoT generation as a trajectory through hidden-state space and recover correctness signals (ROC-AUC 0.87 on Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K) from late-step trajectory features that directly contradict our F-9 redundancy claim along a step-wise axis we hadn't tested. They also empirically confirm length-balance is a non-issue for their trajectory predictor (0.852 → 0.847 under length-balanced resampling), giving us a clean control protocol for H-15. They steer Llama-3.1-8B with an in-sample termination vector that gives +1.80% on MATH-500 transferred from GSM8K — direct partial confirmation of H-1 with a calibrated effect-size reference.

**Key claim we tested:** "Late-step trajectory features predict final-answer correctness pre-emission with ROC-AUC 0.87 (vs 0.81 for final-marker alone, vs 0.63 for early-step features)."

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — direct cross-architecture replication is queued via P11-FE736 (step probes), P11-FE737 (trajectory features vs L19 prefill DoM), P11-FE738 (DoM rotation), P11-FE739 (D-bucket), P11-FE740 (length balance), P11-FE741 (steering vector pre-flight), P11-FE742 (logit-lens baseline). On MATH-500 their predictor transfers from GSM8K at AUC 0.73 — strikingly close to our prefill 0.7731 — but in-distribution training with their late-step trajectory features could plausibly reach 0.85+ on Qwen-1.5B if F-9 is wrong on the step-wise axis.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE736, P11-FE737, P11-FE738, P11-FE739, P11-FE740, P11-FE741, P11-FE742, H-578, H-579, H-580, H-581, H-582, F-1, F-2, F-3, F-7, F-9, F-10, H-1, H-13, H-15, H-17.

**Status:** TO TEST (HIGH priority — multiple direct refutation tests against F-2/F-3/F-7/F-9 are queued; partial confirmation of H-1 already in their data; H-15 length-balance protocol can be adopted directly).

### Methodologies extracted

- **Step-marker activation extraction** — Extract h(ℓ)_t at the token immediately preceding each "Step k:" marker and the termination marker (e.g., "####"). Captures state at decision boundaries.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU on cached Pathway 11 generations (need to re-locate boundary tokens; activations already cached).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives us a step-indexed view of L19 activations on MATH-500, naturally extending Pathway 11.

- **Step-identity linear probe** — Binary one-vs-all LR classifier per step, layer-wise. Trains step-k vs all-other-step activations. Used to certify step-specific subspace separability.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — sanity-checks whether Qwen-1.5B exhibits the same step-organized geometry. Connects to F-3 / H-17.

- **Cross-model transfer of step probes** — Train step probe on Model A, evaluate on Model B activations. Measures whether step-specific organization is shared across post-training regimes.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU once both models' step-marker activations are cached.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes for Qwen-1.5B vs Qwen-7B comparison — we already have both extractions.

- **Trajectory distance features (Euclidean + cosine, between consecutive steps)** — d(h(L)_step_k, h(L)_step_(k+1)) at the final layer, paired by correctness label. Compares early-step vs late-step distance differences as correctness signal.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct probe of whether "late-step divergence" generalizes to Qwen-1.5B MATH-500.

- **Concatenated trajectory features for correctness probe** — Concatenate (h_termination_marker) ⊕ (h_step_(N−1) − h_step_N), apply PCA dim=128, train ℓ2-LR. Their headline 0.87 AUC method.
  *Replication cost*: 2h CPU on cached Pathway 11 NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — tests F-9 directly (refutation #2).

- **Logit-lens correctness baseline** — At step boundaries: entropy, answer-marker token rank, top-1 probability. Their reported best AUC = 0.765 on GSM8K.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — gives a low-cost baseline for our 0.7731 prefill AUROC.

- **In-sample steering vector construction** — s(ℓ) = E_k[h(ℓ)_term − h(ℓ)_step_k] computed within each prompt, averaged over training prompts. Used as termination steering direction.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached activations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly relevant to H-1 and provides a cleaner construction than cross-example DoM.

- **Trajectory-based steering with ideal-trajectory PCA** — From correct-only training trajectories, compute PCA-projected step-wise mean μ_j and dispersion σ_j. At inference, project current activation, compute local deviation δ_j and cumulative D_j; if either exceeds optimized step-specific threshold, apply low-rank steering update toward μ_j.
  *Replication cost*: H100 day (requires inference-time hooks).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes for the Qwen-1.5B reproduction — high-value but pod-blocked.

- **Length-balanced resampling for predictor evaluation** — Resample examples to balance step count between correct and incorrect classes; verify predictor AUC barely drops. Used as their length-confound control.
  *Replication cost*: 20 min CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly addresses H-15 framing.

- **Format-robustness probe** — Train on fixed-form ("Step X:") activations, evaluate on freeform ("\n\n"-separated paragraphs, numbered lists, etc.). Tests whether step probes capture reasoning vs surface formatting.
  *Replication cost*: 4h CPU + small extraction run.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — relevant for prefill-DoM generalization across prompt formats.

### Approaches & framings

- **"CoT generation as a trajectory through representation space."** Frames per-token decoding as sequential geometric motion rather than separate per-step computations. Intersects directly with H-17 (RoPE rotation framing) and our breathing/PR temporal curve framing — they treat the trajectory as a *PCA-projected step-indexed path*, while we treat it as a *layer-wise PR curve at fixed token position*. The two views are orthogonal and complementary.

- **"Ideal trajectory" as a per-step distribution rather than a fixed direction.** Reframes DoM/steering from "single learned direction" to "step-indexed mean with dispersion bands." Intersects H-1 (now a per-step DoM hypothesis), H-17 (now a smoothly-rotating reference path), and our F-3 orthogonality framing (now possibly two endpoints of the same path).

- **"Late-step divergence" as the locus of correctness signal.** Reframes correctness prediction from "any-state probe" to "trajectory-late-region probe." Intersects F-2 / F-8 / F-9: forces us to ask whether the prefill-L19 signal is the late-divergence signal extracted at an unusual token (the question prefill might already encode the eventual late-step divergence direction).

- **"Training reshapes depth-of-convergence, not new representations."** Sun et al. argue Base / Instruct / R1-Distill share linear subspace structure; distillation just moves termination structure earlier in layer depth. This is a strong corroborator for F-1 (dimensional breathing universal across architectures) and prediction for H-10 (breathing changes after fine-tuning) — the prediction would be: fine-tuning shifts where breathing peaks but not the breathing structure itself.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **GSM8K** — 7,473 train / 1,319 test. License: MIT. HF accessible. Applicable? **yes** — cleanest step-marker dataset; our Pathway 11 covers MATH-500 but a GSM8K extension would test cross-dataset transfer for our prefill DoM.
- **MATH-500** — 500 questions. License: MIT (Hendrycks). HF accessible. Applicable? **yes** — our canonical 1024-tok benchmark; their probe transfers here at AUC 0.73 (vs our 0.7731).
- **MMLU validation** — 1,531 questions. License: MIT. HF accessible. Applicable? **partial** — knowledge-intensive, less step-structured; their probe transfers at AUC 0.64. Only relevant if H-22 (abstract reasoning) is pursued.
- **Freeform-prompted GSM8K** — Same questions, minimal CoT prompt without "Step X:" formatting. Constructed by them. Applicable? **yes** — tests format-robustness of any probe we replicate.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Extract activations at the token *immediately preceding* the Step marker (i.e., last token of step-k content), not the Step marker itself. Boundary detection uses tokenizer string match.
- Linear probe: ℓ2-regularized logistic regression on PCA dim=128 features. Reported on a held-out test split.
- Three random seeds for AUC stability — they report single-seed curves but seed-averaged best-layer values in Table 3 (0.852 ± 0.039).
- Steering applied at MID = middle 5 layers OR LAST = final 5 layers, with strength α ∈ [−0.05, 0.8] swept; |α| > 0.8 induces mode collapse.
- Gated intervention fires when the predictor flags (top fraction tunable; they use ≈12.3% flag rate for 35% improvement gain).
- Code: https://github.com/slhleosun/reasoning-trajectory.
- Models: Llama-3.1-8B Base / Instruct / R1-Distill (Llama-3.1-8B distilled by Deepseek). Single architecture family — explicitly noted as a limitation. Cross-architecture replication is open.
- Step-count distribution after R1-Distill (their Appendix H, not pasted here) confirms the "faster convergence" observation refers to layer-depth, not output token count.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Cumulative-deviation D_j on D-bucket members** (against Refutation #5): Use Pathway 11 cached Stage 2 K=1 + K=8 NPZs to identify the D-bucket members on MATH-500, locate Step boundaries in their generations, project to step-wise PCA, compute D_j vs A/B/C buckets. Script: extend `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/` analysis.
- **Step1→2 vs final-step trajectory distance on Qwen-1.5B** (Section 4.1 replication): Per cached MATH-500 generation, locate each Step boundary, extract h(L19), compute Euclidean + cosine distances between consecutive steps, group by K=1 correctness, report Δ(I−C) per transition. Cached: Stage 2 per-token activations.
- **Final-marker-only probe on Qwen-1.5B** (compare to their 0.81): Extract h(L19) at the answer-emission boundary (PANL — see H-18), train OOF logistic, report AUROC. Compare to our prefill 0.7731. Cached: Stage 2 NPZs already have late-token activations.
- **In-sample steering vector** (their s(ℓ) construction) — compute on cached activations; ready for an H-1 ablation if pod time becomes available.
- **Length-balanced resampling control** (H-15) — directly run on cached prefill probe predictions to confirm 0.7731 holds under length-balance.

## 2604.11962 — The Linear Centroids Hypothesis: How Deep Network Features Represent Data (Walker, Humayun, Balestriero, Baraniuk, 2026)

**Relevance:** Highly relevant. Walker et al. argue that the Linear Representation Hypothesis (LRH) — the foundation of every probe-on-latent-activations technique we use, including F-2's L19 prefill DoM — identifies "spurious features" because latent activations form linear directions even when the feature is not utilized in computation. They propose the Linear Centroids Hypothesis (LCH): replace latent activations with **centroids** (Jacobian-row-sums describing the local expert at each input region), and feature discovery becomes mechanistic by construction. They demonstrate the LRH→LCH improvement on (a) sparse-autoencoder feature dictionaries (DINOv2/v3), (b) mass-mean truth probes on Llama-3.1-8B — which is *the exact probe family used in F-2* — and (c) GPT2-Large circuit discovery via a centroid-perturbation attribution metric (Eq 2).

**Key claim we tested:** Mass-mean probes constructed on centroids generalize across truth datasets while mass-mean probes on latent activations capture "plausibility under the model's logit distribution" rather than truthfulness (their Llama-3.1-8B Fig 7).

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — The LCH→LRH gap on Llama-3.1-8B mass-mean probes directly threatens the interpretation of F-2's 0.7731 AUROC as "correctness prediction." Our F-2 probe is constructed identically (mass-mean on latent activations). The refutation test is concrete and cheap (P11-FE743): extract centroids at L19 on Qwen-1.5B, retrain the OOF probe, compare AUROC. If centroids win, F-2 is partially a plausibility signal and the selective-prediction pipeline (F-8) should be rebuilt; if latent wins, F-2 is robust to the substrate swap.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE743 (centroid-DoM probe — HIGH ROI), P11-FE744 (centroid-orthogonality test for F-3), P10-FE38 (centroid-PH refutation for F-10), P11-FE745 (centroid attribution for H-13), H-583 / H-584 / H-585 / H-586.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Centroid extraction via Jacobian row-sum (Prop 2.2)** — μ_x^(ℓ1→ℓ2) = J_x(f^(ℓ1→ℓ2))^T · 1. For any differentiable sub-component, computable as a single backward pass with output_grad = 1.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached residuals if we re-run forward + backward for L19 MLP across 500 problems × prefill + final token positions. ~2h H100 to extend across L0–L27.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — central refutation tool for F-2/F-3/F-10.

- **Centroid mass-mean probe (centroid version of Marks & Tegmark)** — replace latent activations with centroids in the probe construction.
  *Replication cost*: trivial once centroids are extracted (5min CPU, sklearn LR with 5-fold OOF).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — direct head-to-head with F-2.

- **Centroid-based neuron attribution (Eq 2)** — s_N^(i,ℓ) = mean_x ‖μ_x^f − μ_x^f(i,ℓ)‖_2 / ‖μ_x^f‖_2 where f^(i,ℓ) is f with neuron i of layer ℓ ablated.
  *Replication cost*: 1h H100 per layer of interest (1024 forward+backward pairs to ablate each MLP neuron at L19 on n problems). For Qwen-1.5B L19 MLP (~8960 neurons), 1h H100 / problem-batch.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — supersedes ablation-only approaches for H-13 head-level attribution.

- **Local centroid as saliency map** — average centroid over a neighborhood B_ε(x), analogous to SmoothGrad. For text/transformer it's the local centroid of the embedding-to-output Jacobian averaged over a small Gaussian ball in the embedding.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU for visualization on 10 illustrative problems.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **no** for now — saliency is not a load-bearing question for our project; would only run if writing up a paper.

- **TopK SAE on centroids** — train a TopK sparse autoencoder on the centroid stream rather than the latent stream.
  *Replication cost*: 1 day H100 to train an SAE on Qwen-1.5B L19 centroids over a sizable corpus.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **no** — out of scope for our correctness-prediction focus, but flagged as a future option for label-free probing (H-12 extension).

- **Effective-dimension along input interpolation between class anchors** — interpolate between two centroids and measure effective rank of the centroid neighborhood. Their MNIST result shows greater dim drop between more semantically distinct classes.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached residuals (after centroid extraction).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **maybe** — could be a sharper instrument for F-1 (dimensional breathing) since the breathing curve is currently measured on residuals.

### Approaches & framings

- **LRH vs LCH distinction** — features as latent-activation directions ("extracted features, possibly spurious") vs as centroid directions ("extracted *and* utilized"). Reframes our entire DoM analysis from "what direction do correct-vs-incorrect prefills span in residual space" to "what direction do their *local experts* span." Directly intersects F-2/F-3/F-7/F-9.
- **Mechanistic-by-construction interpretability** — centroids tie features to the network's computation via the Jacobian, not post hoc. Reframes "the prefill DoM is an indirect signal of correctness" to "the prefill local-expert direction *is* the correctness-extraction operation, by construction" — if it survives the substrate swap.
- **Local-expert / power-diagram framing of the network** — Voronoi-like tiling of input space, each tile has a centroid that is the *summary of its expert*. Provides a geometric vocabulary for "what does the model compute on this input" that is sharper than "what is its hidden state." Useful narrative scaffolding for the project's eventual writeup.
- **Hierarchical centroid analysis** — centroids of sub-components (input → ℓ vs input → final layer) yield coarser/finer features. Suggests a layerwise breathing analysis on centroids that could refine F-1 (currently only on residual streams).
- **Spurious-feature critique of LRH** — directly bears on H-12 (semantic entropy / label-free probing) and on the broader question of whether any of our F-N findings might survive on centroids but evaporate on activations (or vice versa).

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **DTD (Describable Textures Dataset)** — vision, NA — not applicable.
- **ImageNet, Imagenette, FashionMNIST, MNIST** — vision, NA.
- **`likely` + Marks & Tegmark truth datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, neg_*, etc.)** — text, ~1k–10k labeled statements, public via Marks's GitHub. Applicable? **yes** — directly the dataset on which they replicate the LRH→LCH improvement on Llama-3.1-8B; we could replicate on Qwen-1.5B as an independent validation before doing the centroid-DoM test on MATH-500.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Code: https://github.com/ThomasWalker1/LinearCentroidsHypothesis — has Jacobian-vector-product centroid extraction and probe code; check if Llama-3.1-8B mass-mean probe code is reusable for Qwen-2.5.
- Centroid via JVP: in PyTorch, `torch.autograd.grad(outputs=f_out, inputs=h, grad_outputs=torch.ones_like(f_out))[0]` gives J^T · 1 in one backward pass. Critical for cost: do not materialize the full Jacobian.
- Compute overhead: 10–15% over latent extraction for SAE/probe pipelines (Table 1). Llama-3.1-8B probe pipeline scaled ~5× (2329s vs 470s) because their centroid is full-model input-to-layer, not single-layer; for our L19-only experiment we should use the *layer-local* Jacobian (cheap).
- Local centroid (saliency): SmoothGrad-style averaging over Gaussian neighborhood, σ chosen as a fraction of the input norm. ε normalization important for stable attribution percentile (Fig 15).
- Their toy network setup uses ReLU + GELU softening (Balestriero & Baraniuk 2018c) — GELU centroids are stable approximations of ReLU centroids; relevant for transformer MLPs which use GELU/SwiGLU.
- For circuit discovery (Eq 2) they sample 256 points in B_ε(x) with ε = 0.25 × ‖μ‖. Robustness checks in Fig 15 show low variance; finite-sample percentile is stable.

### Replicable intermediates

- **Layer-19 MLP centroid extraction over the cached MATH-500 prefill positions**: re-run forward + 1 backward pass per (problem, position) to get J_L19_MLP^T · 1. Need access to the model graph, not just cached residuals — re-uses the P11 H100 extraction harness. Estimated cost: 30min H100 on Qwen-1.5B for 500 prefill positions.
- **Centroid-DoM probe**: once centroids are extracted, train OOF 5-fold mass-mean probe; compare AUROC to F-2's 0.7731.
- **Cross-task transfer test on Marks & Tegmark `cities` / `sp_en_trans`**: if Qwen-1.5B is run-able on these datasets, replicate Walker Fig 7 *before* attempting the harder MATH-500 replication. Establishes that the LCH→LRH gap is real on our model architecture.
- **PH on centroid clouds (refutation of F-10)**: same EXP-029 pipeline (Gudhi VietorisRipsPersistence) but on n=500 centroid vectors per layer instead of residuals. Need centroids first; PH itself is 30min CPU.

No fully self-contained sanity check is possible without re-extracting centroids — but the re-extraction can be done on Qwen-1.5B alone (no 7B needed), so the cost is bounded.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2405.07987 (Platonic Representation Hypothesis)** — already in graph (status: graphed). Walker §3.4 + Appendix E argues centroids *more faithfully* validate PRH than latent activations; direct relevance to H-20.
- **2407.02678 (Cosentino & Shekkizhar — Reasoning in LLMs: A Geometric Perspective)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Cited for the linear-region-density / reasoning connection — directly relevant to F-1 (dimensional breathing) and F-10 (PH null).
- **2501.16496 (Sharkey et al. — Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability)** — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Frames LRH limitations Walker leverages; useful overview for our writeup.
- **Smith et al. 2025 (negative results for SAEs on downstream tasks, "Medium" — likely no arxiv id)** — flagged but no arxiv id given; skip.
- **Marks & Tegmark 2024 ("Geometry of Truth") — likely arxiv 2310.06824** — NOT confirmed in graph; recommend admission as the canonical mass-mean probe reference (also the source of our F-2 probe construction).

## 2604.14084 — TIP: Token Importance in On-Policy Distillation (Xu, Sang, Zhou, He, Wang, Geramifard, 2026)

**Relevance:** Direct intersection with F-2 / F-7 / F-8. TIP introduces a
two-axis token taxonomy (student entropy × teacher–student divergence) and
shows that the low-entropy + high-divergence quadrant (Q3, "overconfident
wrong") carries dense corrective signal — a per-token analog of our D-bucket
finding (F-7). Their 50%-retention entropy frontier mirrors our 50%-coverage
selective-prediction frontier (F-8). They use Qwen2.5 + MATH-500, so their
signals are directly replicable on our cached 1.5B P11 traces.

**Key claim we tested:** A label-free per-token statistic (student entropy,
optionally combined with teacher–student KL) carries enough correctness signal
to match supervised probes — *except* on the overconfident-wrong (D-bucket / Q3)
region, where entropy alone fails.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — three FEs (P11-FE746/75/76) read directly off
cached MATH-500 1.5B data. Pre-registered: if mean per-token entropy AUROC
> 0.7731, F-2 leadership narrows; if Q3-density discriminates D-bucket, F-7's
"collective only" claim is overturned.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE746, P11-FE747, P11-FE748, H-587, H-588; constrains
H-12 (SEP replacement scope), refines H-19 (verification routing granularity).

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **Per-token entropy of student logits** — standard softmax entropy at each
  generation position; aggregate across the trace.
  *Replication cost*: 30min CPU if logits cached; 4h H100 if we need to
  recompute. We currently cache hidden states (NPZ), not logits, so this
  may require a small re-extract.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct comparator to F-2 prefill DoM AUROC.

- **Token-level teacher–student KL divergence** — KL between teacher (7B) and
  student (1.5B) softmax distributions at aligned token positions during
  on-policy student rollouts.
  *Replication cost*: H100 day — needs teacher forced-decode on student
  rollouts (token-position alignment is non-trivial because rollouts are
  student-driven).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes for a subset (e.g. 50 problems) — gives the
  second axis to test the Q3 quadrant hypothesis directly.

- **Two-axis quadrant binning (entropy ≷ median × divergence ≷ median)** —
  partition tokens into four quadrants; the Q3 quadrant (low entropy, high
  divergence) is the corrective signal locus.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU once both per-token signals are computed.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly tests "D-bucket = high-Q3-density"
  hypothesis (refutation #1, #3 above).

- **Type-aware token sampling for training** — selective backprop on Q3
  tokens only.
  *Replication cost*: H100 + custom training loop.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — we're not doing distillation; this is
  training-side, our regime is inference-side analysis.

### Approaches & framings

- **Two-axis decomposition (entropy × divergence)** — reframes "informative
  token" from a 1D uncertainty score to a 2D quadrant taxonomy. Maps onto
  our four-bucket A/B/C/D *problem* taxonomy at the token level: D-bucket
  ≈ Q3 (low entropy + wrong = high divergence). Reusable framing for
  per-token diagnosis of overconfident failure.
- **"Entropy is useful but structurally incomplete"** — formal acknowledgment
  that single-axis uncertainty fails to flag the overconfident-wrong region.
  Directly constrains the SEP/SEH family of label-free correctness probes
  (H-12).

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MATH-500** — 500 problems, public (HF). Applicable: yes — same benchmark.
- **AIME 2024 / AIME 2025** — 30 + 30 problems, public. Applicable: yes —
  natural harder-tier extension if we want to test prefill DoM transfer
  (links to H-2 short-CoT and existing extension hypotheses).
- **DeepPlanning** — long-horizon agentic planning benchmark. Applicable: no —
  different task family, off-topic for short-CoT regime.

  per-token entropy / KL computation utilities reusable for our analysis

- Models tested: Qwen3, Llama, Qwen2.5. The Qwen2.5-7B → Qwen2.5-1.5B pair is

## 2604.15350 — The Spectral Geometry of Thought (Liu, 2026)

**Relevance:** Same arena as F-2 / F-9 / H-12 (single-layer single-feature correctness prediction) but uses spectral α (power-law exponent of SVD singular values of T×d hidden activation matrix) instead of DoM directional probing. Across 11 models / 5 architecture families (Qwen, Pythia, Phi, Llama, DeepSeek-R1) / 21 reasoning + factual tasks, paper claims (1) reasoning produces lower α (more distributed activations) in 9/11 models; (2) instruction tuning *reverses* this signature (Qwen-3B base ∆α=−0.318 vs. Qwen-3B-Instruct ∆α=+0.121); (3) generation-shift taxonomy keyed to RMSNorm vs. LayerNorm; (4) spectral scaling law α_reasoning ∝ −0.074 ln N, R²=0.46; (5) cross-layer cascade with τ=19.8 layers; (6) reasoning-step spectral punctuation at "\\n\\n" / "Step:" / "therefore"; (7) AUC=1.000 single-layer α-based correctness prediction on Qwen-7B (L23 of 28), mean AUC=0.893 across 6 models. Direct competitor to L19 DoM with the additional advantage of being label-free.

**Key claim we tested:** Spectral α at a single late layer is a near-perfect single-scalar single-feature predictor of reasoning correctness — AUC=1.000 in-distribution on Qwen-7B and AUC=0.600 OOD on a 40-problem novel-category test set.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** The in-distribution AUC=1.000 result is dramatically stronger than F-2's 0.7731 (Qwen-1.5B prefill DoM, 1024-tok MATH-500). Three caveats temper the claim before testing: (a) paper used 200 problems per model from a 13-task synthetic reasoning benchmark, not MATH-500 with 1024-tok labels; (b) OOD AUC=0.600 (Qwen-7B) and 0.437 (Qwen-3B) on a tiny 40-problem test set indicates the in-distribution result may be benchmark-specific; (c) α is computed on T×d matrices where T = full sequence length, leaving an unaddressed length-confound risk analogous to our 256-tok bug. P11-FE749 / FE81 / FE82 / FE83 directly test α-vs-DoM head-to-head, the F-10 Gaussian-null framing, the length confound, and breathing replication on cached pathway11 data. Decision deferred to FE80 outcome.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE749, P11-FE750, P11-FE751, P11-FE752, H-589, H-590, H-591.

**Status:** TO TEST.

### Methodologies extracted

- **Spectral α via SVD on H^(ℓ) ∈ R^(T×d)** — power-law exponent fit by OLS on log-log singular values: α = −Σ(lnk−⟨lnk⟩)(lnσ_k−⟨lnσ⟩) / Σ(lnk−⟨lnk⟩)². Mean R²>0.85 across models/layers (Appendix B.4).
  *Replication cost*: ~5min CPU per (model, problem) on cached residuals, ~30min CPU for full pathway11 sweep.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct head-to-head against L19 prefill DoM is the highest-leverage refutation in this brief.

- **Token-level sliding-window α (w=10 tokens)** — α(t,ℓ) recomputed at every generation step over the last 10 tokens. Gradient ∇_t α(t,ℓ) = α(t+1,ℓ)−α(t,ℓ) reveals step-boundary spikes.
  *Replication cost*: ~1h CPU on cached pathway11 Stage-4a per-token NPZs.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — adds a parallel temporal signal to F-1's PR breathing curve.

- **Prompt-response decomposition ∆α_P→R = α_response − α_prompt** — three-category generation taxonomy (expansion / equilibrium / compression) keyed to RMSNorm vs. LayerNorm.
  *Replication cost*: ~15min CPU on cached prompt+response NPZs (1.5B prompt-vs-response is in pathway11 Stage-2).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — complements F-3 orthogonality measurement with a magnitude scalar.

- **Cross-layer α-gradient correlation ρ(d) ≈ 0.998·exp(−d/19.8)** — Pearson correlation of per-token α gradients between layer pairs at distance d.
  *Replication cost*: ~1h CPU on cached per-token activations across all 28 layers.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — interesting for understanding cascade structure but mostly orthogonal to current correctness-prediction findings.

- **Phase-bucket logistic regression** — Early (first 25% of layers) / Mid (25–50%) / Late (50–75%) / Response (last 25%, generation phase). Train per-phase classifier on aggregated α features, report best phase + best single layer.
  *Replication cost*: ~30min CPU on cached residuals.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct refutation test for F-2 (P11-FE749).

- **Permutation test (1000 permutations) for AUC>0.5 significance** — controls for tiny-sample AUC inflation.
  *Replication cost*: ~5min CPU per AUC.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — should be added to F-2's 0.7731 reporting alongside 5-fold CV stderr.

- **Randomized SVD streaming (Halko 2011)** — for d≫T cases; useful if we extend to 7B (d=4096) or larger.
  *Replication cost*: in `numpy` / `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds` already available.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes if memory becomes a constraint.

### Approaches & framings

- **Spectral α as a macroscopic geometric signature** — single-scalar summary of the entire activation manifold's variance-allocation shape. Reframes F-2/F-9's directional probing as one of multiple complementary lenses (probing tells us *what* is encoded; α tells us *how* it is structured).

- **"Reasoning = lower α = more distributed representations"** — frames effective reasoning as activation of higher-dimensional subspaces. *Reverses* the intrinsic-dimension-collapse narrative behind F-4 (correct trajectories collapse harder at the final token): paper says low α (= distributed = high effective rank) is the correctness signal, not high collapse. Forces a re-statement of when in the trajectory the distributed-vs-collapsed contrast applies.

- **Generation-shift taxonomy keyed to normalization architecture** — RMSNorm+SwiGLU → spectral expansion; LayerNorm → spectral compression. Predicts that the choice of normalization layer determines dynamic representational behavior, not just static training stability. Bears on H-10 (breathing pattern after fine-tuning).

- **Spectral cascade with characteristic length τ≈19.8 layers** — claims information propagates with exponentially decaying inter-layer synchronization; reasoning *decouples* distant layer pairs (∆ρ = −0.19 for L0–L35). Predicts that 28-layer Qwen models have ~1.4 cascades, and that reasoning specifically increases cross-cascade independence. Bears on F-3 orthogonality (a special case of cross-layer decoupling).

- **Punctuated spectral equilibrium** — phase transitions in α coincide with reasoning-step boundaries ("\n\n", "Step 2:", "therefore"). Reframes F-1 breathing as discrete jumps at meaningful tokens, not smooth oscillation. Direct connection to H-18 (post-answer-newline activation predictor).

- **Instruction tuning *reverses* spectral signature for reasoning** — base models: reasoning α < factual α (compression); instruct models: reasoning α > factual α (concentration). Reframes the project's "reasoning helps" narrative as architecture- and training-paradigm-dependent. DeepSeek-R1 equilibrium is a specific prediction for reasoning-distilled architectures.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **21-task spectral phase benchmark** (13 reasoning + 6 factual + 2 random, paper Appendix A Table 5) — small synthetic benchmark, not on HF, paper-internal. Applicable: marginal for refutation tests because task distribution differs from MATH-500.

- **40-problem OOD validation** (4 categories × 10 problems × {direct-answer, CoT}, code tracing / commonsense / multi-hop math / logical elimination) — synthetic, paper-internal, not released. Applicable: marginal — too small to be a serious external benchmark.

- **200 reasoning problems / model for correctness prediction** — drawn from the 13 reasoning tasks above, sampled per model. Applicable: not directly — too small and heterogeneous compared to our MATH-500/500-problem setup.

- **No real public benchmarks** (GSM8K, MATH-500, BBH, MMLU) used. This is a notable limitation: paper does not validate against any standard reasoning benchmark.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Hidden-state matrix H^(ℓ) ∈ R^(T×d), one SVD per layer per inference (~3% inference overhead on 7B).
- T=200 tokens for phase analysis, T=500 for token-level dynamics, sliding window w=10.
- Power-law fit by OLS on log-log singular values (no regularization, no MP correction); mean R²>0.85 across models and layers.
- Phase buckets keyed to layer index: Early=first 25%, Mid=25–50%, Late=50–75%, Response=last 25% (during generation, distinct slice).
- Logistic regression on phase-aggregated features; 5-fold *stratified* CV (matters with imbalanced labels).
- Greedy decoding (T=0) throughout — reproducibility guarantee.
- Statistical: Welch two-sample t-test, OLS for scaling law, 1000-permutation test for AUC>0.5.
- Randomized SVD (Halko 2011) cited for streaming on large d.
- Code: paper does not link a public repo (single-author, lylewis@outlook.com) — replication is from-scratch.

### Replicable intermediates

- Compute α on cached pathway11_h100 Stage-2 prefill NPZs (1.5B: T_prefill × d=1536; 7B: T_prefill × d=4096) — script: ~50 lines numpy, 30min CPU for both models on all 500 problems × all layers.
- Use existing 1024-tok MATH-500 correctness labels (`pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json`) — 5min CPU for logistic regression per layer.
- Compare best-layer α-AUROC head-to-head against L19 DoM-AUROC=0.7731 (1.5B) and the published 7B prefill DoM number (same `results.json`).
- For F-10 refutation (P11-FE750): generate Marchenko-Pastur baselines via per-question-shuffled residuals at the same T×d aspect ratio, fit α, run Welch t-test per layer.
- For length confound (P11-FE751): bin by `len(generation_tokens)` tercile from `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json`, recompute α-AUROC per bin.
- For breathing replication (P11-FE752): cached per-token L19 NPZs at `pathway11_h100/per_token/*.npz`; sliding-window α at w=10.

### Cross-paper signals

- 2410.13640 — already in graph (status: graphed). CoE shares "trajectory of hidden states predicts correctness" framing; α is a complementary single-scalar version. Paper does *not* cite CoE — independent convergence.
- 2509.11569 — already in graph (status: graphed). D²HScore is the closest comparable label-free hidden-state hallucination detector (depth/breadth ratio of activation eigenspectrum). Paper does *not* cite or compare; we should run α + D²HScore + DoM head-to-head.
- 2604.18805 — already in graph (status: graphed). Confirmation-bias warning is directly relevant: paper claims "perfect" prediction with 40-problem OOD validation that drops to AUC=0.6, exactly the failure mode Ríos-García flags (in-distribution success not generalizing).
- 2501.12948 — already in graph (status: graphed). Paper makes specific spectral-equilibrium claims about R1 (∆α_P→R≈0) that should inform our P11-FE5 (R1-Distill comparison).
- 2412.15115 — already in graph (status: graphed). Qwen2.5 reference; paper uses Qwen2.5-0.5B/3B/7B base and 1.5B/3B-Instruct.
- 2402.17762 — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Sun et al. "Massive activations in LLMs" — outlier dimensions directly affect α (a few massive singular values dominate the power-law tail). Paper does not cite Sun, but α is sensitive to exactly the phenomenon Sun characterized.
- 2207.05221 — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Kadavath "LLMs (mostly) know what they know" — foundational reference for self-confidence-from-internals literature; paper cites it as motivation for Finding 7.

## 2604.16217 — Beyond Surface Statistics: Robust Conformal Prediction for LLMs via Internal Representations (Wang, Kuang, Han, Xu, Wang; 2026)

**Relevance:** Methodologically the most direct competitor to our F-2 /
F-9 framing we've seen. Proposes "Layer-Wise Information (LI) scores"
— per-layer LM-head-lens entropy reduction summed across all
transformer layers — as a label-free, probe-free conformal nonconformity
score, and claims it strictly improves conformal efficiency (APSS) by
~17% relative under cross-domain shift on MMLU-Pro / MedMCQA, and ~16%
on TriviaQA / CoQA vs semantic-entropy. The non-monotonic-across-depth
theoretical motivation (Kim et al. 2025a) is in direct tension with our
F-9 single-layer-suffices result on CoE-60.

**Key claim we tested:** Aggregating per-layer LM-head-lens entropy
reduction across all transformer layers strictly outperforms any
single-layer correctness signal on factoid QA and cross-domain MCQA.

**Our result:** **TO TEST** — they did not run on math reasoning, only
factoid/closed-ended QA. Direct test (P11-FE753 / H-592) is
feasible on cached Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500 residuals in ~1 day CPU. The
test specifically discriminates F-9 (single-layer suffices) from the
Layerwise CP framing.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE753 (LI-L19 vs LI-all on MATH-500),
P11-FE754 (LI layer sweep), P11-FE755 (LI vs semantic-entropy on
MATH-500), P11-FE756 (LI on D-bucket vs A-bucket), P11-FE757
(conformal restatement of F-8); H-592, H-593; relates to F-2,
F-7, F-8, F-9, H-12.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies extracted

- **LM-head logit-lens per-layer entropy** — project residual stream at
  layer ℓ through the pretrained LM head to get a next-token distribution
  p_ℓ(y_t | y_<t, x), compute average negative log-likelihood of a sampled
  response y as H_ℓ(y|x). Same trick as logit-lens / tuned-lens but used as
  a calibration signal rather than for interpretability.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU on cached residuals (need per-layer
  hidden states and the model's `lm_head` matrix; both available for
  Qwen-2.5-1.5B).
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — directly comparable to L19 DoM
  AUROC on cached MATH-500 prefill data, and lets us put F-2 on a
  probe-free footing.

- **Per-layer V-usable-information score (I_ℓ)** — null-conditioned vs
  question-conditioned entropy difference, I_ℓ(x→y) = H_ℓ(y|∅) − H_ℓ(y|x).
  Empirical instantiation of Xu et al. 2020 / Ethayarajh et al. 2022's
  V-usable info, restricted to a single layer's "view" of the LM head.
  *Replication cost*: 30 min CPU; needs an extra null-prompt forward pass
  per (model, sample) pair. The authors are vague about what ∅ means
  exactly — "absence of question context" — likely the few-shot template
  with the question slot blanked. Worth pinning down before replication.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — pairs well with our existing prefill
  vs final-token contrast (F-2 / F-3).

- **LI score** — sum I_ℓ over a chosen layer subset, default = all layers.
  *Replication cost*: trivial once I_ℓ is computed.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — single-layer vs all-layer LI is the
  clean test of F-9.

- **Within-pool min-max normalization** (eq 9) — normalize LI scores within
  each candidate-pool {y_m^(i)} per question to remove cross-question
  scale variation.
  *Replication cost*: trivial.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — if we ever extend our K=8/K=16
  sampling pipeline to a conformal frame, this is the right preprocessing.

- **Answer-frequency aggregation** (eq 12) — average normalized LI scores
  over all candidate responses parsing to the same answer unit; equivalent
  to the within-question voting score from Jiang et al. 2025.
  *Replication cost*: trivial.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **maybe** — only matters once we have
  multi-sample MATH-500 generations with semantic equivalence classes,
  which we don't currently use.

- **Convex combination with answer-frequency** (eq 13) F^LW = w_LI F_LI +
  w_f F_freq with w_LI = w_f = 0.5. Internal score regularized by
  cross-sample consensus (self-consistency).
  *Replication cost*: trivial.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — direct comparator to our
  selective-prediction at K=2.5 (F-8); we currently use only DoM cosine.

- **Split conformal prediction (SCP) wrapper** with EMR / APSS / SSM
  metrics — empirical miscoverage rate, average prediction set size,
  size-stratified miscoverage. Standard CP plumbing from Angelopoulos &
  Bates 2022.
  *Replication cost*: 1 day CPU to build a clean SCP harness over our
  existing K=8 generations.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **yes** — would let us state F-8 with
  finite-sample validity guarantees.

- **Sentence-similarity correctness protocol** for open-domain QA
  (Su et al. 2024 / Wang et al. 2025b) — we don't currently need this
  because MATH-500 has exact-match.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: **no** — not relevant to MATH-500.

### Approaches & framings

- **"The bottleneck is the uncertainty *signal*, not how CP is adapted to
  shift."** This reframes the conformal-prediction literature: instead of
  fancier reweighting tricks (Tibshirani 2020, Barber 2023), use a
  better-quality scalar score. Maps cleanly onto our F-2 framing where
  the *signal* (prefill L19 DoM) carries the action and the wrapper
  (logistic regression OOF) is interchangeable.

- **"Internal layer-wise information evolves non-monotonically across
  depth"** (Kim et al. 2025a, cited approvingly). Direct theoretical
  competitor to F-9's single-layer-suffices framing — see refutation 1.

- **Information-theoretic interpretation of conformal prediction** (their
  Appendix E, claimed): "prediction-set size at controlled risk reflects
  residual uncertainty." Bridges CP efficiency (APSS) with V-usable
  information. Useful framing for putting F-8 on conformal footing.

- **Empirical-not-validity contribution.** They explicitly say: "we do not
  claim that internal representations remove the need for conformal
  assumptions or restore formal validity under domain shift. Our claim is
  narrower and empirical." Healthy scientific posture; matches the
  refutations-first style we want to import into our own writeups.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **MMLU-Pro** (Wang et al. 2024a) — 10-option closed-ended QA, 14 subject
  domains, M=50 candidate samples per question. HF gated (license: MIT
  per HF). **Applicable: no** — closed-ended, not free-form math; our
  setup is single-best-answer numeric.

- **MedMCQA** (Pal et al. 2022) — medical 4-option MCQA, M=20 samples per
  question. HF, MIT-equivalent. **Applicable: no** — same closed-ended
  format mismatch.

- **TriviaQA** (Joshi et al. 2017) — open-domain QA, 4000-example subset,
  M=10 samples per prompt. HF, Apache 2.0. **Applicable: no** —
  factoid-recall benchmark, very different signal from multi-step math.

- **CoQA** (Reddy et al. 2019) — conversational QA, 4000-example subset,
  M=10. HF, mixed licenses. **Applicable: no** — same as TriviaQA.

The paper does **not** test on MATH, GSM8K, or any reasoning benchmark.
This is a non-trivial gap: their claim is about closed-ended factuality
QA, while our regime is multi-step reasoning where breathing (F-1) and
asymmetric collapse (F-4) operate. Their cross-domain story is among
**MMLU-Pro subjects**, not across task types. Replicating their gain on
MATH-500 cross-difficulty (e.g., calibrate on Algebra, deploy on
Counting & Probability) is novel.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Calibration/test split ratio: 0.5, repeated 100 random trials.
- Risk budgets evaluated: β ∈ {0.1, 0.2, 0.3} (i.e., target miscoverage).
- Generation: `do_sample=True, num_beams=1, top_p=0.9, temperature=1.0`,
  max length 1 token for MCQA, 36 tokens for open-domain.
- Model suite: Qwen-2.5-3B/7B/14B-Instruct, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct,
  Vicuna-13B-v1.5. White-box (need hidden states + LM head). No
  fine-tuning.
- Prompt strategy: 3-shot for MMLU-Pro/MedMCQA, few-shot for
  TriviaQA/CoQA.
- Strongest backbone: Qwen-2.5-14B (EMR 0.110, APSS 1.68, SSM 0.178).
- Standard deviations of EMR/APSS are smaller for Layerwise CP than for
  SConU-Pro across all five models — a stability gain on top of the
  efficiency gain. Worth noting if we replicate.
- Default layer subset L_s = L (all transformer layers). Authors do not
  ablate single-layer vs all-layer LI, which is exactly the gap our
  refutation 1 fills.
- Gotcha: their I_ℓ(x→y) requires a "null context" forward pass
  p_ℓ(y_t|y_<t, ∅), and the paper is loose about what ∅ is
  (presumably few-shot template with question slot blanked, but not
  pinned down in the main text — Appendix B may help).
- No code/repository link in the v1 PDF (preprint, under review).

### Replicable intermediates

- **LI-at-L19 vs LI-all-layers on MATH-500.** Cached residuals at
  `pathway11_h100/.../residuals_qwen15b_*.npz` already contain per-layer
  prefill hidden states for 500 MATH-500 problems. Implementing the
  LM-head-lens entropy + I_ℓ + sum is ~150 LOC of numpy. Compare AUROC
  vs correctness labels at L19 alone vs all 28 layers. Settles
  refutation 1 in <1 day CPU.
- **LI vs L19 DoM on the same problems.** Same harness; report both
  AUROC and Pearson correlation between LI and DoM scores. Direct
  method-independent corroboration / refutation of F-2.
- **LI on F-7 D-bucket vs A-bucket.** 36 vs 207 problems already
  bucketed in `scratch/pathway10_temporal_and_verifier_results.json` (or
  the F-7 source JSON). Compute mean LI per bucket; Welch's t-test.
  Settles refutation 4.

### Cross-paper signals

- **2410.13640 — Chain-of-Embedding (Wang ICLR 2025)** — already in graph
  (status: graphed, PARTIALLY CONFIRMED in PAPER_INDEX). Direct

- **2402.03744 — INSIDE / EigenScore (Chen et al., ICLR 2024)** — already

## 2604.19018 — Local Linearity of LLMs Enables Activation Steering via Model-Based Linear Optimal Control (Skifstad, Yang, Chou, 2026)

**Relevance:** Closed-loop activation steering via LQR with formal tracking guarantees,
plus a novel empirical claim that within-layer Jacobians are highly correlated across
reachable activations (subspace similarity ~0.5–0.8 on Gemma-2-2B, Qwen-2.5-3B,
Llama-3-8B). Directly relevant to (a) H-1 as the strongest available steering baseline
that turns the open-loop ActAdd / ITI plan into a feedback controller with formal
guarantees, and (b) F-3 / F-5 / H-17 by reframing layer-wise dynamics as nearly
content-independent — which, if it replicates on Qwen-2.5-1.5B at L19, has corollaries for
the project's "content-dependent breathing" and "two functionally distinct directions"
claims.

**Key claim we tested:** Closed-loop LQR with adaptive layer-norm-scaled setpoint (LFS,
β_k* = λ μ_k) yields SOTA semantic-feature steering with formally bounded tracking error.
Layer-wise transformer Jacobians within a fixed layer are ~0.5–0.8 aligned across
reachable activations.

**Our result:** **TO TEST**. We have not yet run their A-LQR machinery on MATH-500 with
prefill L19 DoM, nor reproduced their Jacobian-coupling result on Qwen-2.5-1.5B at L19.
H-600 / H-601 / H-602 are the three replication checks.

**Related experiments:** P10-FE39 (A-LQR on MATH-500), P11-FE766 (Jacobian alignment at
L19), P11-FE767 (linearized-cascade PR), H-600, H-601, H-602, F-2, F-3, F-5, H-1, H-17.

**Status:** TO TEST

### Methodologies
- A-LQR closed-loop steerer (Riccati-precomputed K_k, online u_k* = K_k (β_k* - v_k^T z_k) v_k).
- Linear feature setpoint (LFS): β_k* = λ μ_k (per-layer-norm-scaled adaptive target).
- Top-m subspace similarity score (Eq. 24): nuclear-norm-weighted alignment metric for Jacobians.
- Closed-loop tracking error bound (Thm 4.2 / Cor 4.3): formal guarantees with empirical L_i.
- A-LQR+ all-token-position variant.
- S-PID baseline (PID over LFS) as light-weight alternative.

### Approaches
- LLM as LTV dynamical system; layer Jacobians as local descriptors.
- Within-layer Jacobian content-coupling complements Aubry et al. 2025's across-layer coupling.
- Closed-loop feedback steering vs open-loop activation addition.

### Datasets
- RealToxicityPrompts (1000 sampled), TruthfulQA generation split, AdvBench (80/20),
  Jigsaw Toxic Comment, OneSeC concept dataset, HarmBench classifier. None directly
  applicable to MATH-500.

### Implementation
- Code: https://github.com/trustworthyrobotics/lqr-activation-steering
- Models: Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Gemma-2-2B/9B, Qwen-2.5-3B/14B/32B, Llama-3-8B,
  Llama-3.1-8B/70B.
- Last-token-only intervention at all layers (Karnik & Bansal 2025; Hedstrom 2025
  conventions).
- Riccati precomputed offline; K_k storage is the VRAM bottleneck.

### Replicable intermediates
- Layer-19 Jacobian alignment test on cached Qwen-2.5-1.5B prefill activations.
- Linearized-cascade PR test on cached Stage 2 activations.
- A-LQR steering on the 257 incorrect MATH-500 problems with prefill L19 DoM as v_k.

### Cross-paper signals
- Builds directly on 2406.11717 (Arditi single-direction refusal), 2308.10248 (ActAdd),
  2306.03341 (ITI, our CONTRADICTED), 2410.23054 (Linear-AcT), 2510.04309 (PID-AcT),
  2410.02707 (LLMs Know More), 2311.03658 (Park linear-rep-geometry).
- Recommends admission of 2510.26243 (Vu & Nguyen Angular Steering, AAS), 2510.13285
  (Vogels et al. In-distribution steering), 2406.05954 (Kong et al. control perspective),
  2509.21528 (Karnik & Bansal latent reachability), 2310.04444 (Bhargava magic word
  control), 2405.15454 (Cheng & Alonso linearly controlled), 2305.18449 (Soatto taming AI
  bots).

### Methodologies extracted

- **A-LQR (Activation-LQR closed-loop steering)** — solve LTV-LQR Riccati recursion `S_k =
  A_k^T (S_{k+1} - S_{k+1} B_k Γ_k B_k^T S_{k+1}) A_k + Q_k`; apply `u_k* = K_k (β_k* - v_k^T
  z_k) v_k` online. Q, R are hyperparameters (App. E).
  *Replication cost*: ~1 day H100 to run on Qwen-2.5-1.5B with a contrastive set; offline
  Jacobian computation is VRAM-heavy.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — closed-loop steerer with prefill DoM as v is the right test
  for H-1 / F-2 causality.

- **Linear Feature Setpoint (LFS, β_k* = λ μ_k)** — adapts setpoint to per-layer activation
  norm μ_k = ‖e_k‖ where e_k = z_{k,+} - z_{k,-}.
  *Replication cost*: 20 min CPU once Jacobians and contrastive activations are cached.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — drop-in replacement for fixed-α ActAdd in any steering trial.

- **Top-m subspace similarity score (Eq. 24)** — `sim_m(W,X) = ‖A‖_* / (‖Σ(W_m)‖_F · ‖Σ(X_m)‖_F)`,
  with `A = (U_W^(m) Σ_W^(m))^T U_X^(m) Σ_X^(m)` and ‖·‖_* = nuclear norm. Generalises
  Aubry et al. 2025's matrix coupling to weight by singular values.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU on cached Jacobian samples per layer.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct test for refutations R2, R3.

- **Closed-loop tracking error bound (Thm 4.2 / Cor 4.3)** — bounds `|ε_k| ≤ Δ_1^v + Σ ‖v_k^T
  Φ̂_{k,i+1}‖ (‖ε_i‖ + L_i/2 ‖δz_i‖^2)`, with empirical `L̂_i = 2‖r_i‖/‖δz_i‖^2`.
  *Replication cost*: 1h CPU once L_i is empirically estimated from rollouts.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — useful only if we adopt A-LQR as a tool, then this gives
  formal guarantees on prefill-DoM tracking under our F-2 setup.

- **A-LQR+ (per-token-position variant)** — same K_k applied at every token position, with
  per-position online error signals; more invasive but lifts jailbreaking ASR (e.g.
  Gemma-2-9B 0.144 → 0.769).
  *Replication cost*: 1 day H100.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: no — jailbreaking is out of scope; flagging because intervention
  spread across positions is the most relevant variant if H-1 fails on last-token-only.

- **S-PID baseline** — drop-in PID controller tracking the LFS setpoint. Cheap, useful as
  intermediate step before full LQR.
  *Replication cost*: 4h CPU.
  *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — sanity-check before A-LQR.

### Approaches & framings

- **LLM inference as a linear time-varying (LTV) dynamical system** with `z_{k+1} = A_k z_k +
  B_k u_k + w_k`. Recasts hidden-state geometry as a control problem; complements our
  geometry-as-prediction framing. Direct intersection with H-17 (rotation as a mechanical
  cascade rather than RoPE).
- **Layer-Jacobian content-coupling** — within a fixed layer, Jacobians at different reachable
  activations are highly correlated (~0.5–0.8 nuclear-weighted top-m subspace similarity).
  Complements Aubry et al. 2025's *across-layer* coupling. Direct intersection with F-1, F-3,
  F-5, F-10.
- **Closed-loop vs open-loop steering** — feedback control on online error vs precomputed
  vector addition. Reframes ActAdd / ITI / Linear-AcT as the open-loop limit, A-LQR as the
  closed-loop limit. Direct intersection with H-1.
- **Adaptive layer-norm-scaled setpoint (LFS)** — encodes the prior fact that per-layer DoM
  magnitudes vary substantially (Vu & Nguyen 2025). Direct intersection with the
  per-position DoM bank concept underneath H-1.

### Datasets & benchmarks

- **RealToxicityPrompts (RTP)** — Gehman 2020, ~100K prompts (paper uses 1000 sampled).
  HuggingFace, openly accessible. Applicable? **no** for MATH-500 / 1024-tok regime; flagged
  only if we ever re-run A-LQR on RTP for sanity.
- **TruthfulQA generation split** — Lin 2021, 817 questions, generation split. HuggingFace,
  open. Applicable? **no** for MATH but **yes** as a non-MATH probe of whether prefill DoM is
  task-general (could test H-5 framing, problem familiarity vs decomposability).
- **AdvBench** — Zou 2023, 520 harmful prompts. HF, open. Applicable? **no** — jailbreaking out
  of scope.
- **Jigsaw Toxic Comment** — Kaggle, gated by Kaggle ToS. Applicable? **no**.
- **OneSeC concept dataset** — Scarlini 2019, multilingual sense-annotated. HF, open.
  Applicable? **no** for MATH-500 directly; could provide contrastive sets if we ever
  generalise H-1 to non-math concepts.
- **HarmBench classifier** — Mazeika 2024, evaluator model. Open. Applicable? **no**.

### Implementation details worth capturing

- Code release: https://github.com/trustworthyrobotics/lqr-activation-steering
- Models tested: Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Gemma-2-2B/9B, Qwen-2.5-3B/14B/32B, Llama-3-8B,
  Llama-3.1-8B/70B. **Qwen-2.5-3B is in their evaluation grid** — closest sibling to our
  Qwen-2.5-1.5B and 7B, so transfer to our setup is plausible.
- Intervention: additive perturbation to last-token residual stream at all 28 layers
  (Karnik & Bansal 2025 convention; Hedstrom et al. 2025 confirms across-all-layers is best).
- Contrastive sets: D+, D− with mean-difference vector `e_k = z_{k,+} - z_{k,−}`, unit
  direction `v_k = e_k / μ_k`.
- A_k Jacobian = `∂φ_k/∂z|_(z̄_k=z_{k,+}, ū_k=0)`. B_k = I.
- Riccati gains computed *offline* once per (model, contrastive set, Q, R, λ) tuple;
  reused online without recomputation. K_k storage is the bottleneck (paper notes VRAM
  overhead in App. F.3).
- Compute complexity: O(ℓ d^3) on CPU, O(log ℓ · log^2 d) on GPU via Fang & Chou 2026.
- LQR Q, R, λ tuned empirically to maximise toxicity reduction subject to PPL/MMLU floor;
  per-model tuning needed (App. E.2).
- Limitation explicitly flagged in §9: Q, R, λ sensitivity; Jacobian VRAM cost; conformal
  prediction (Srinivasan et al. 2026) listed as future direction for low-rank K compression.

### Replicable intermediates

- **L19 single-layer Jacobian alignment test (refutation R2/R3)**: cache 50 prefill
  activations from `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute/results.json` (we have B/D/A bucket
  labels per problem). Compute `∂φ_19/∂z` at each (PyTorch `torch.autograd.functional.jacobian`
  on a frozen Qwen-2.5-1.5B). Compute pairwise top-m=64 subspace similarity (Eq. 24). Stratify
  by bucket. **Cost**: ~4h H100 for Jacobian extraction + 1h CPU for subspace similarity.
- **Linearized PR test (refutation R3)**: from cached Jacobians at L1…L28, apply LTI cascade
  `A_28 ∘ … ∘ A_1` to an initial-condition `z_0 = z_{embedding}` for 50 high-peak-PR and 50
  low-peak-PR Stage 2 prompts. Compute PR of linearized trajectory; compare to actual PR. If
  curves overlap to ε<0.05, F-5 is refuted. **Cost**: 2h CPU once Jacobians are cached.
- **Closed-loop A-LQR steering test for H-1**: install
  https://github.com/trustworthyrobotics/lqr-activation-steering, instantiate with
  Qwen-2.5-1.5B and v_k = our prefill L19 DoM (already cached, cosine-normalized). Run on the
  243 incorrect MATH-500 problems with λ ∈ {0.5, 1, 2, 5}. Measure (a) downstream K=1 accuracy
  delta, (b) PPL drift, (c) MMLU drift. **Cost**: ~1 day H100.
- **S-PID precursor**: reuse the same v_k as A-LQR; PID is dramatically cheaper. If S-PID
  fails to flip any incorrect→correct, A-LQR is unlikely to either. **Cost**: 4h CPU.
